name: 3-minute Diagnostic Interview for CAM-defined Delirium (3D-CAM)
description: Brief structured bedside diagnostic interview operationalising the CAM algorithm for delirium in hospitalised patients

en.name: 3-minute Diagnostic Interview for CAM-defined Delirium (3D-CAM)
en.shortDescription: Brief structured bedside diagnostic interview operationalising the CAM algorithm for delirium in hospitalised patients
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context The 3D-CAM (3-Minute Diagnostic Assessment for CAM-defined Delirium) is a brief, structured bedside diagnostic instrument that operationalises the Confusion Assessment Method (CAM) algorithm for identifying delirium in hospitalised patients. It takes a median of 3 minutes to administer (IQR 2–5 minutes) and does not require special training [1]. The instrument comprises 20 items organised into the four CAM diagnostic features: - acute onset and fluctuating course - inattention - disorganised thinking - altered level of consciousness A feature is considered present if any single item within that category is positive. Delirium is diagnosed when features 1 and 2 are both present, along with feature 3 and/or feature 4. ## Included Concepts This concept set contains a single custom concept, as no equivalent exists in standard terminologies (SNOMED, LOINC). ## References [1] Marcantonio ER, Ngo LH, O'Connor M, et al. 3D-CAM: Derivation and Validation of a 3-Minute Diagnostic Interview for CAM-Defined Delirium. *Ann Intern Med*. 2014;161(8):554-561. doi:10.7326/M14-0865. PMID: 25329203

fr.name: 3-minute Diagnostic Interview for CAM-defined Delirium (3D-CAM)
fr.shortDescription: Entretien diagnostique structuré court au lit du patient, opérationnalisant l'algorithme CAM pour le delirium chez les patients hospitalisés
fr.longDescription: ## Définition et contexte clinique Le 3D-CAM (3-Minute Diagnostic Assessment for CAM-defined Delirium) est un instrument diagnostique structuré et bref, réalisable au lit du patient, basé sur l'algorithme de la Confusion Assessment Method (CAM) pour identifier le délirium chez les patients hospitalisés. Son administration prend en médiane 3 minutes (IQR 2–5 minutes) et ne nécessite pas de formation spécifique [1]. L'instrument comprend 20 items organisés selon les quatre critères diagnostiques du CAM : - début aigu et évolution fluctuante - inattention - désorganisation de la pensée - altération du niveau de conscience Un critère est considéré comme présent si au moins un item de cette catégorie est positif. Le délirium est diagnostiqué lorsque les critères 1 et 2 sont tous deux présents, accompagnés du critère 3 et/ou du critère 4. ## Concepts inclus Ce concept set contient un seul concept custom, aucun équivalent n'existant dans les terminologies standard (SNOMED, LOINC). ## Références [1] Marcantonio ER, Ngo LH, O'Connor M, et al. 3D-CAM: Derivation and Validation of a 3-Minute Diagnostic Interview for CAM-Defined Delirium. *Ann Intern Med*. 2014;161(8):554-561. doi:10.7326/M14-0865. PMID: 25329203

name: 4 A's Test for Delirium Screening
description: Rapid four-item bedside screening tool for delirium, designed for routine use without special training

en.name: 4 A's Test for Delirium Screening
en.shortDescription: Rapid four-item bedside screening tool for delirium, designed for routine use without special training
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context The 4AT (4 'A's Test) is a rapid screening tool for delirium, designed for use in routine clinical practice without special training. It takes less than 2 minutes to administer and can be used with patients who have visual or hearing impairment, or who are too drowsy or agitated to undergo formal cognitive testing [1]. The instrument comprises four items: - alertness - AMT4 (Abbreviated Mental Test-4, a brief orientation screen) - attention (months of the year backwards) - acute change or fluctuating course The total score ranges from 0 to 12. A score of 0 suggests delirium is unlikely, 1–3 indicates possible cognitive impairment warranting further investigation, and ≥ 4 suggests possible delirium. ## Included Concepts This concept set contains the OMOP-standard SNOMED concept for the scale: - `3662219` — 4AT - 4 A's Test (`1239191000000102`, Staging / Scales, Standard) The non-standard SNOMED Observable Entity `3662221` (4AT (4 A's Test) score, `1239211000000103`) maps to this standard concept (OMOP `Maps to`), so recorded score values stored against the source code are captured through standard-concept resolution. ## References [1] Bellelli G, Morandi A, Davis D, et al. Validation of the 4AT, a new instrument for rapid delirium screening: a study in 234 hospitalised older people. *Age Ageing*. 2014;43(4):496-502. doi:10.1093/ageing/afu021. PMID: 24590568

fr.name: 4 A's Test for Delirium Screening score
fr.shortDescription: Outil de dépistage rapide du delirium à quatre items, conçu pour un usage en routine sans formation spécifique
fr.longDescription: ## Définition et contexte clinique Le 4AT (4 'A's Test) est un outil de dépistage rapide du délirium, conçu pour être utilisé en pratique clinique courante sans formation spécifique. Son administration prend moins de 2 minutes et il peut être utilisé chez les patients présentant une déficience visuelle ou auditive, ou trop somnolents ou agités pour réaliser une évaluation cognitive formelle [1]. L'instrument comprend quatre items : - vigilance - AMT4 (Abbreviated Mental Test-4, un test bref d'orientation) - attention (mois de l'année à l'envers) - changement aigu ou évolution fluctuante Le score total varie de 0 à 12. Un score de 0 suggère que le délirium est peu probable, 1–3 indique un trouble cognitif possible nécessitant des investigations complémentaires, et ≥ 4 suggère un délirium possible. ## Concepts inclus Ce concept set contient le concept SNOMED standard OMOP de l'échelle : - `3662219` — 4AT - 4 A's Test (`1239191000000102`, Staging / Scales, Standard) Le concept SNOMED Observable Entity non-standard `3662221` (4AT (4 A's Test) score, `1239211000000103`) se mappe vers ce concept standard (`Maps to` OMOP) ; les valeurs de score enregistrées sous le code source sont donc capturées via la résolution vers le concept standard. ## Références [1] Bellelli G, Morandi A, Davis D, et al. Validation of the 4AT, a new instrument for rapid delirium screening: a study in 234 hospitalised older people. *Age Ageing*. 2014;43(4):496-502. doi:10.1093/ageing/afu021. PMID: 24590568

name: Behavioral Pain Scale (BPS)
description: Behavioural observational tool for assessing pain in sedated, mechanically ventilated patients unable to self-report

en.name: Behavioral Pain Scale (BPS)
en.shortDescription: Behavioural observational tool for assessing pain in sedated, mechanically ventilated patients unable to self-report
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context The BPS (Behavioral Pain Scale) is a bedside observational tool for assessing pain in sedated, mechanically ventilated patients who cannot self-report. It takes less than 2 minutes to administer and does not require special training [1]. The instrument comprises three items, each scored from 1 to 4: - facial expression - upper limb movements - compliance with mechanical ventilation The total score ranges from 3 (no pain) to 12 (maximum pain). A score > 5 is generally considered indicative of unacceptable pain requiring analgesic adjustment. ## Included Concepts This concept set contains a single custom concept, as no equivalent exists in standard terminologies (SNOMED, LOINC). ## References [1] Payen JF, Bru O, Bosson JL, et al. Assessing pain in critically ill sedated patients by using a behavioral pain scale. *Crit Care Med*. 2001;29(12):2258-2263. doi:10.1097/00003246-200112000-00004. PMID: 11801819

fr.name: Échelle comportementale de douleur
fr.shortDescription: Outil d'évaluation comportementale de la douleur chez les patients sédatés et ventilés mécaniquement, incapables de s'auto-évaluer
fr.longDescription: ## Définition et contexte clinique Le BPS (Behavioral Pain Scale) est un outil d'évaluation comportementale de la douleur au lit du patient, destiné aux patients sédatés sous ventilation mécanique ne pouvant pas s'auto-évaluer. Son administration prend moins de 2 minutes et ne nécessite pas de formation spécifique [1]. L'instrument comprend trois items, chacun coté de 1 à 4 : - expression faciale - mouvements des membres supérieurs - adaptation à la ventilation mécanique Le score total varie de 3 (absence de douleur) à 12 (douleur maximale). Un score > 5 est généralement considéré comme indicatif d'une douleur inacceptable nécessitant une adaptation de l'analgésie. ## Concepts inclus Ce concept set contient un seul concept custom, aucun équivalent n'existant dans les terminologies standard (SNOMED, LOINC). ## Références [1] Payen JF, Bru O, Bosson JL, et al. Assessing pain in critically ill sedated patients by using a behavioral pain scale. *Crit Care Med*. 2001;29(12):2258-2263. doi:10.1097/00003246-200112000-00004. PMID: 11801819

name: Confusion Assessment Method for the Intensive Care Unit (CAM-ICU)
description: Bedside delirium diagnostic instrument adapted from the CAM for use in critically ill, including ventilated, patients

concept.conceptName: Confusion Assessment Method for the Intensive Care Unit (CAM-ICU)

en.name: Confusion Assessment Method for the Intensive Care Unit (CAM-ICU)
en.shortDescription: Bedside delirium diagnostic instrument adapted from the CAM for use in critically ill, including ventilated, patients
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context The CAM-ICU (Confusion Assessment Method for the Intensive Care Unit) is a bedside delirium diagnostic instrument adapted from the original CAM for use in critically ill patients, including those who are mechanically ventilated. It takes approximately 2 minutes to administer and does not require special training [1]. The instrument uses a two-step process. The level of consciousness is first assessed using the RASS; patients with RASS −4 or −5 (coma) cannot be evaluated. For assessable patients, four features are evaluated: - acute onset or fluctuating course - inattention - altered level of consciousness - disorganised thinking The CAM-ICU is positive for delirium when features 1 and 2 are both present, together with feature 3 and/or feature 4. ## Included Concepts This concept set contains a single custom concept, as no equivalent exists in standard terminologies (SNOMED, LOINC). ## References [1] Ely EW, Inouye SK, Bernard GR, et al. Delirium in mechanically ventilated patients: validity and reliability of the confusion assessment method for the intensive care unit (CAM-ICU). *JAMA*. 2001;286(21):2703-2710. doi:10.1001/jama.286.21.2703. PMID: 11730446

fr.name: Confusion Assessment Method for the Intensive Care Unit (CAM-ICU)
fr.shortDescription: Outil diagnostique du delirium au lit du patient, adapté du CAM pour les patients de réanimation, y compris ventilés
fr.longDescription: ## Définition et contexte clinique Le CAM-ICU (Confusion Assessment Method for the Intensive Care Unit) est un instrument diagnostique du délirium au lit du patient, adapté du CAM original pour une utilisation chez les patients de réanimation, y compris ceux sous ventilation mécanique. Son administration prend environ 2 minutes et ne nécessite pas de formation spécifique [1]. L'instrument utilise un processus en deux étapes. Le niveau de conscience est d'abord évalué à l'aide du RASS ; les patients avec un RASS de −4 ou −5 (coma) ne peuvent pas être évalués. Pour les patients évaluables, quatre critères sont recherchés : - début aigu ou évolution fluctuante - inattention - altération du niveau de conscience - désorganisation de la pensée Le CAM-ICU est positif pour le délirium lorsque les critères 1 et 2 sont tous deux présents, accompagnés du critère 3 et/ou du critère 4. ## Concepts inclus Ce concept set contient un seul concept custom, aucun équivalent n'existant dans les terminologies standard (SNOMED, LOINC). ## Références [1] Ely EW, Inouye SK, Bernard GR, et al. Delirium in mechanically ventilated patients: validity and reliability of the confusion assessment method for the intensive care unit (CAM-ICU). *JAMA*. 2001;286(21):2703-2710. doi:10.1001/jama.286.21.2703. PMID: 11730446

name: Delirium Detection Score (DDS)
description: Bedside ICU assessment tool to monitor and quantify delirium severity through eight clinical criteria

en.name: Delirium Detection Score (DDS)
en.shortDescription: Bedside ICU assessment tool to monitor and quantify delirium severity through eight clinical criteria
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context The DDS (Delirium Detection Score) is a bedside assessment tool designed to monitor and quantify delirium severity in ICU patients. It was originally developed and validated in surgical ICU patients [1]. The instrument comprises eight clinical criteria: - orientation - hallucinations - agitation - anxiety - seizures - tremor - paroxysmal sweating - altered sleep-wake rhythm The DDS score increases with delirium severity. ## Included Concepts This concept set contains a single custom concept, as no equivalent exists in standard terminologies (SNOMED, LOINC). ## References [1] Otter H, Martin J, Bäsell K, et al. Validity and reliability of the DDS for severity of delirium in the ICU. *Neurocrit Care*. 2005;2(2):150-154. doi:10.1385/NCC:2:2:150. PMID: 16159057

fr.name: Delirium Detection Score (DDS)
fr.shortDescription: Outil d'évaluation au lit du patient en réanimation, mesurant la sévérité du delirium à partir de huit critères cliniques
fr.longDescription: ## Définition et contexte clinique Le DDS (Delirium Detection Score) est un outil d'évaluation au lit du patient conçu pour surveiller et quantifier la sévérité du délirium chez les patients de réanimation. Il a été initialement développé et validé chez des patients de réanimation chirurgicale [1]. L'instrument comprend huit critères cliniques : - orientation - hallucinations - agitation - anxiété - convulsions - tremblements - sudation paroxystique - altération du rythme veille-sommeil Le score DDS augmente avec la sévérité du délirium. ## Concepts inclus Ce concept set contient un seul concept custom, aucun équivalent n'existant dans les terminologies standard (SNOMED, LOINC). ## Références [1] Otter H, Martin J, Bäsell K, et al. Validity and reliability of the DDS for severity of delirium in the ICU. *Neurocrit Care*. 2005;2(2):150-154. doi:10.1385/NCC:2:2:150. PMID: 16159057

name: Delirium Observation Screening (DOS) Scale
description: Nursing observation-based screening instrument for early recognition of delirium, completed each shift

en.name: Delirium Observation Screening (DOS) Scale
en.shortDescription: Nursing observation-based screening instrument for early recognition of delirium, completed each shift
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context The DOS (Delirium Observation Screening Scale) is a nursing observation-based screening instrument for early recognition of delirium based on DSM-IV criteria [1]. The instrument comprises 13 items covering behaviours such as: - dozing off during conversation - distractibility and inattention - disorientation in time or place - slow response to instructions - restlessness or picking behaviour - hallucinations Each item is scored 0 (normal) or 1 (abnormal behaviour observed). The total score ranges from 0 to 13. A score ≥ 3 suggests delirium. The scale is completed once per nursing shift (up to three times per 24 hours). ## Included Concepts This concept set contains a single custom concept, as no equivalent exists in standard terminologies (SNOMED, LOINC). ## References [1] Schuurmans MJ, Shortridge-Baggett LM, Duursma SA. The Delirium Observation Screening Scale: a screening instrument for delirium. *Res Theory Nurs Pract*. 2003;17(1):31-50. PMID: 12751884

fr.name: Delirium Observation Screening (DOS) Scale
fr.shortDescription: Outil de dépistage du delirium par l'observation infirmière, complété à chaque vacation pour une détection précoce
fr.longDescription: ## Définition et contexte clinique Le DOS (Delirium Observation Screening Scale) est un instrument de dépistage du délirium basé sur l'observation infirmière, fondé sur les critères du DSM-IV [1]. L'instrument comprend 13 items couvrant des comportements tels que : - assoupissement pendant la conversation - distractibilité et inattention - désorientation dans le temps ou l'espace - lenteur de réponse aux instructions - agitation ou comportement de préhension - hallucinations Chaque item est coté 0 (normal) ou 1 (comportement anormal observé). Le score total varie de 0 à 13. Un score ≥ 3 suggère un délirium. L'échelle est complétée une fois par poste infirmier (jusqu'à trois fois par 24 heures). ## Concepts inclus Ce concept set contient un seul concept custom, aucun équivalent n'existant dans les terminologies standard (SNOMED, LOINC). ## Références [1] Schuurmans MJ, Shortridge-Baggett LM, Duursma SA. The Delirium Observation Screening Scale: a screening instrument for delirium. *Res Theory Nurs Pract*. 2003;17(1):31-50. PMID: 12751884

name: Delirium Rating Scale-revised-98 (DRS-R-98)
description: Clinician-rated 16-item scale for assessing delirium severity and assisting in differential diagnosis

en.name: Delirium Rating Scale-revised-98 (DRS-R-98)
en.shortDescription: Clinician-rated 16-item scale for assessing delirium severity and assisting in differential diagnosis
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context The DRS-R-98 (Delirium Rating Scale – Revised-98) is a clinician-rated scale for assessing delirium severity and assisting in differential diagnosis. It is a substantial revision of the original DRS (Trzepacz et al., 1988), designed for repeated measurements and phenomenological research [1]. The instrument comprises 16 items divided into two sections. The 13-item severity section (scored 0–3 each, total 0–39) can be used separately for repeated measurements: - sleep-wake cycle disturbance - perceptual disturbances and hallucinations - delusions - lability of affect - language - thought process abnormalities - motor agitation - motor retardation - orientation - attention - short-term memory - long-term memory - visuospatial ability Three additional diagnostic items (temporal onset of symptoms, fluctuation of symptom severity, physical disorder) are added for the total scale score (0–46). ## Included Concepts This concept set contains a single custom concept, as no equivalent exists in standard terminologies (SNOMED, LOINC). ## References [1] Trzepacz PT, Mittal D, Torres R, Kanary K, Norton J, Jimerson N. Validation of the Delirium Rating Scale-Revised-98: comparison with the Delirium Rating Scale and the Cognitive Test for Delirium. *J Neuropsychiatry Clin Neurosci*. 2001;13(2):229-242. doi:10.1176/jnp.13.2.229. PMID: 11449030

fr.name: Delirium Rating Scale (DRS)
fr.shortDescription: Échelle à 16 items cotée par le clinicien pour évaluer la sévérité du delirium et aider au diagnostic différentiel
fr.longDescription: ## Définition et contexte clinique Le DRS-R-98 (Delirium Rating Scale – Revised-98) est une échelle d'évaluation du délirium cotée par le clinicien, permettant d'en mesurer la sévérité et d'en établir le diagnostic. Il s'agit d'une révision substantielle de la Delirium Rating Scale originale (Trzepacz et al., 1988), conçue pour des mesures répétées et une utilisation élargie en contexte clinique et de recherche [1]. L'instrument comprend 16 items répartis en deux sections : - échelle de sévérité (13 items, score 0–39) : perturbation du cycle veille-sommeil, troubles perceptifs et hallucinations, idées délirantes, labilité de l'affect, langage, anomalies du cours de la pensée, agitation motrice, ralentissement moteur, orientation, attention, mémoire à court terme, mémoire à long terme, capacités visuospatiales - échelle diagnostique (3 items, score 0–7) : début temporel des symptômes, fluctuation de la sévérité des symptômes, trouble physique Le score total (0–46) est utilisé pour l'évaluation initiale ; le score de sévérité seul est recommandé pour les mesures répétées. ## Concepts inclus Ce concept set contient un seul concept custom, aucun équivalent n'existant dans les terminologies standard (SNOMED, LOINC). ## Références [1] Trzepacz PT, Mittal D, Torres R, Kanary K, Norton J, Jimerson N. Validation of the Delirium Rating Scale–Revised-98: comparison with the Delirium Rating Scale and the Cognitive Test for Delirium. *J Neuropsychiatry Clin Neurosci*. 2001;13(2):229-242. doi:10.1176/jnp.13.2.229. PMID: 11449030

name: Glasgow coma scale total
description: Single integer GCS total score (3–15), summing the eye, verbal and motor components

en.name: Glasgow coma scale total
en.shortDescription: Single integer GCS total score (3–15), summing the eye, verbal and motor components
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context The Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) total score is the sum of the three component scores — eye opening (E), verbal response (V) and motor response (M) — yielding a single integer between 3 (deep unresponsive coma) and 15 (fully alert and oriented). The scale was originally developed by Teasdale and Jennett in 1974 for the standardised evaluation of patients with acute brain injury [1]. A total score ≤ 8 is conventionally used to define coma and is a common threshold for intubation in trauma settings. The total alone should be interpreted with caution: clinically very different patterns can yield the same sum (e.g. E1 V1 M6 vs E4 V4 M3), which is why the three component scores are recorded as separate variables (see the dedicated concept sets for eye opening, verbal response and motor response). When any component cannot be assessed (e.g. periorbital oedema, intubation, sedation), the total score is not meaningful and should not be reported — only the assessable component scores should be recorded. ## Included Concepts This concept set contains the single LOINC concept representing the recorded GCS total score: - `3007194` — Glasgow coma score total (`9269-2`, Clinical Observation) ## Related Concept Sets The three component scores are captured separately: - Glasgow coma scale eye opening - Glasgow coma scale verbal response - Glasgow coma scale motor response ## References [1] Teasdale G, Jennett B. Assessment of coma and impaired consciousness: a practical scale. *Lancet*. 1974;2(7872):81-84. doi:10.1016/s0140-6736(74)91639-0. PMID: 4136544

fr.name: Glasgow coma scale total
fr.shortDescription: Score total GCS unique (3–15), somme des sous-scores d'ouverture des yeux, verbal et moteur
fr.longDescription: ## Définition et contexte clinique Le score total du Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) est la somme des trois sous-scores — ouverture des yeux (E), réponse verbale (V) et réponse motrice (M) — donnant un entier compris entre 3 (coma profond aréactif) et 15 (patient parfaitement éveillé et orienté). L'échelle a été initialement développée par Teasdale et Jennett en 1974 pour l'évaluation standardisée des patients présentant un traumatisme crânien aigu [1]. Un score total ≤ 8 définit conventionnellement le coma et constitue un seuil fréquent d'indication d'intubation en traumatologie. Le total seul doit être interprété avec prudence : des situations cliniques très différentes peuvent donner la même somme (par ex. E1 V1 M6 vs E4 V4 M3), raison pour laquelle les trois sous-scores sont enregistrés comme des variables séparées (voir les concept sets dédiés à l'ouverture des yeux, la réponse verbale et la réponse motrice). Lorsqu'une composante ne peut pas être évaluée (par ex. œdème périorbitaire, intubation, sédation), le score total perd son sens et ne doit pas être rapporté — seuls les sous-scores évaluables doivent être enregistrés. ## Concepts inclus Ce concept set contient l'unique concept LOINC représentant le score total GCS enregistré : - `3007194` — Glasgow coma score total (`9269-2`, Clinical Observation) ## Concept sets associés Les trois sous-scores sont capturés séparément : - Glasgow coma scale eye opening - Glasgow coma scale verbal response - Glasgow coma scale motor response ## Références [1] Teasdale G, Jennett B. Assessment of coma and impaired consciousness: a practical scale. *Lancet*. 1974;2(7872):81-84. doi:10.1016/s0140-6736(74)91639-0. PMID: 4136544

name: Intensive Care Delirium Screening Checklist (ICDSC)
description: Eight-item screening checklist for delirium based on DSM criteria, completed each nursing shift

en.name: Intensive Care Delirium Screening Checklist (ICDSC)
en.shortDescription: Eight-item screening checklist for delirium based on DSM criteria, completed each nursing shift
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context The ICDSC (Intensive Care Delirium Screening Checklist) is a screening tool for delirium based on DSM (Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders) criteria, designed to be completed by clinicians or nurses at the bedside using information from each 8-hour nursing shift or the previous 24 hours [1]. The checklist comprises eight items, each scored 0 or 1: - altered level of consciousness - inattention - disorientation - hallucination, delusion, or psychosis - psychomotor agitation or retardation - inappropriate speech or mood - sleep/wake cycle disturbance - symptom fluctuation The total score ranges from 0 to 8. A score ≥ 4 suggests delirium. ## Included Concepts This concept set contains the OMOP-standard SNOMED concept for the scale: - `1447893` — Intensive Care Delirium Screening Checklist (`1351993001`, Staging / Scales, Standard) The non-standard SNOMED Observable Entity `1450965` (Intensive Care Delirium Screening Checklist score, `1351995008`) maps to this standard concept (OMOP `Maps to`), so recorded score values stored against the source code are captured through standard-concept resolution. ## References [1] Bergeron N, Dubois MJ, Dumont M, Dial S, Skrobik Y. Intensive Care Delirium Screening Checklist: evaluation of a new screening tool. *Intensive Care Med*. 2001;27(5):859-864. doi:10.1007/s001340100909. PMID: 11430542

fr.name: Intensive Care Delirium Screening Checklist (ICDSC)
fr.shortDescription: Liste de contrôle à huit items pour le dépistage du delirium selon les critères DSM, complétée à chaque vacation infirmière
fr.longDescription: ## Définition et contexte clinique L'ICDSC (Intensive Care Delirium Screening Checklist) est un outil de dépistage du délirium basé sur les critères du DSM (Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders), conçu pour être rempli par des cliniciens ou des infirmiers au lit du patient à partir des informations recueillies sur chaque période de 8 heures ou les 24 heures précédentes [1]. La checklist comprend huit items, chacun coté 0 ou 1 : - altération du niveau de conscience - inattention - désorientation - hallucination, délire ou psychose - agitation ou ralentissement psychomoteur - discours ou humeur inappropriés - perturbation du cycle veille-sommeil - fluctuation des symptômes Le score total varie de 0 à 8. Un score ≥ 4 suggère un délirium. ## Concepts inclus Ce concept set contient le concept SNOMED standard OMOP de l'échelle : - `1447893` — Intensive Care Delirium Screening Checklist (`1351993001`, Staging / Scales, Standard) Le concept SNOMED Observable Entity non-standard `1450965` (Intensive Care Delirium Screening Checklist score, `1351995008`) se mappe vers ce concept standard (`Maps to` OMOP) ; les valeurs de score enregistrées sous le code source sont donc capturées via la résolution vers le concept standard. ## Références [1] Bergeron N, Dubois MJ, Dumont M, Dial S, Skrobik Y. Intensive Care Delirium Screening Checklist: evaluation of a new screening tool. *Intensive Care Med*. 2001;27(5):859-864. doi:10.1007/s001340100909. PMID: 11430542

name: Numeric Pain Rating Scale
description: 11-point (0–10) self-reported numeric scale on which the patient rates the intensity of their pain

en.name: Numeric Pain Rating Scale
en.shortDescription: 11-point (0–10) self-reported numeric scale on which the patient rates the intensity of their pain
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context The Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS, also Numeric Rating Scale or NRS) is an 11-point (0–10) self-reported scale on which the patient rates the intensity of their pain, where 0 corresponds to "no pain" and 10 to the "worst pain imaginable" [1]. The scale is widely used in clinical practice because of its simplicity, brevity, and applicability to a wide range of populations including patients unable to use a continuous visual analogue scale. The original validation study compared the NRS with a simple descriptive scale and the visual analogue scale, and demonstrated that the 11-point NRS performs better than both alternatives [1]. ## Included Concepts This concept set contains the OMOP-standard SNOMED concept for the scale: - `37151627` — Numeric Pain Rating Scale (`1284852002`, Staging / Scales, Standard) The non-standard SNOMED Observable Entity `37151630` (Numeric Pain Rating Scale score, `1284857008`) maps to this standard concept (OMOP `Maps to`), so recorded score values stored against the source code are captured through standard-concept resolution. ## Excluded Concepts The following SNOMED concept is intentionally **not** included: - `37174733` — Assessment using Numeric Pain Rating Scale (`1284856004`, Procedure) — represents the act of assessment, not the recorded score value ## References [1] Downie WW, Leatham PA, Rhind VM, Wright V, Branco JA, Anderson JA. Studies with pain rating scales. *Ann Rheum Dis*. 1978;37(4):378-381. doi:10.1136/ard.37.4.378. PMID: 686873

fr.name: Numeric Pain Rating Scale
fr.shortDescription: Échelle numérique auto-rapportée à 11 points (0–10) sur laquelle le patient cote l'intensité de sa douleur
fr.longDescription: ## Définition et contexte clinique La NPRS (Numeric Pain Rating Scale, ou échelle numérique NRS) est une échelle d'auto-évaluation à 11 points (0–10) sur laquelle le patient cote l'intensité de sa douleur, où 0 correspond à « aucune douleur » et 10 à la « pire douleur imaginable » [1]. Elle est largement utilisée en pratique clinique du fait de sa simplicité, de sa brièveté et de son applicabilité à un large éventail de populations, y compris les patients ne pouvant pas utiliser une échelle visuelle analogique continue. L'étude princeps de validation a comparé la NRS à une échelle descriptive simple et à l'échelle visuelle analogique, et a montré que la NRS à 11 points est plus performante que ces deux alternatives [1]. ## Concepts inclus Ce concept set contient le concept SNOMED standard OMOP de l'échelle : - `37151627` — Numeric Pain Rating Scale (`1284852002`, Staging / Scales, Standard) Le concept SNOMED Observable Entity non-standard `37151630` (Numeric Pain Rating Scale score, `1284857008`) se mappe vers ce concept standard (`Maps to` OMOP) ; les valeurs de score enregistrées sous le code source sont donc capturées via la résolution vers le concept standard. ## Concepts exclus Le concept SNOMED suivant est intentionnellement **non inclus** : - `37174733` — Assessment using Numeric Pain Rating Scale (`1284856004`, Procedure) — représente l'acte d'évaluation, non la valeur du score enregistré ## Références [1] Downie WW, Leatham PA, Rhind VM, Wright V, Branco JA, Anderson JA. Studies with pain rating scales. *Ann Rheum Dis*. 1978;37(4):378-381. doi:10.1136/ard.37.4.378. PMID: 686873

en.name: Nursing Delirium Screening Scale (Nu-DESC)
en.shortDescription: Five-item observational scale for delirium completed by bedside nurses during routine care, once per shift
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context The Nu-DESC (Nursing Delirium Screening Scale) is an observational five-item screening scale for delirium, designed to be completed by bedside nurses during routine care. It takes on average one minute per patient and is completed three times per day (once per nursing shift) [1]. The instrument comprises five items, each rated from 0 to 2 based on symptom presence and intensity: - disorientation - inappropriate behaviour - inappropriate communication - illusions/hallucinations - psychomotor retardation The total score ranges from 0 to 10. A score ≥ 2 suggests delirium. ## Included Concepts This concept set contains a single custom concept, as no equivalent exists in standard terminologies (SNOMED, LOINC). ## References [1] Gaudreau JD, Gagnon P, Harel F, Tremblay A, Roy MA. Fast, systematic, and continuous delirium assessment in hospitalized patients: the Nursing Delirium Screening Scale. *J Pain Symptom Manage*. 2005;29(4):368-375. doi:10.1016/j.jpainsymman.2004.07.009. PMID: 15857740

fr.name: Nursing Delirium Screening Scale (Nu-DESC)
fr.shortDescription: Échelle d'observation du delirium à cinq items, complétée par les infirmières au lit du patient une fois par vacation
fr.longDescription: ## Définition et contexte clinique Le Nu-DESC (Nursing Delirium Screening Scale) est une échelle observationnelle de dépistage du délirium en cinq items, conçue pour être remplie par les infirmiers au lit du patient lors des soins courants. Son administration prend en moyenne une minute par patient et est réalisée trois fois par jour (une fois par poste infirmier) [1]. L'instrument comprend cinq items, chacun coté de 0 à 2 selon la présence et l'intensité du symptôme : - désorientation - comportement inapproprié - communication inappropriée - illusions/hallucinations - ralentissement psychomoteur Le score total varie de 0 à 10. Un score ≥ 2 suggère un délirium. ## Concepts inclus Ce concept set contient un seul concept custom, aucun équivalent n'existant dans les terminologies standard (SNOMED, LOINC). ## Références [1] Gaudreau JD, Gagnon P, Harel F, Tremblay A, Roy MA. Fast, systematic, and continuous delirium assessment in hospitalized patients: the Nursing Delirium Screening Scale. *J Pain Symptom Manage*. 2005;29(4):368-375. doi:10.1016/j.jpainsymman.2004.07.009. PMID: 15857740

name: Pupil diameter
description: Bedside manual measurement of pupil resting diameter in millimetres, recorded separately for each eye

en.name: Pupil diameter
en.shortDescription: Bedside manual measurement of pupil resting diameter in millimetres, recorded separately for each eye
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Pupil diameter is the resting size of the pupil, measured at the bedside in millimetres, separately for each eye. The normal range under typical ambient lighting is approximately 2–6 mm; sizes outside this range are described as miosis (< 2 mm) or mydriasis (> 6 mm) and may signal toxidromes, brainstem pathology or pharmacological effects [1].

The two pupils are always recorded independently because pupillary innervation is asymmetric (the parasympathetic fibres travel with cranial nerve III). Anisocoria — a difference of more than 1 mm between the two pupils — is a red flag for ipsilateral mass effect or uncal herniation in patients with altered consciousness, although small physiological anisocoria is common in healthy individuals.

This concept set captures the manual bedside measurement (visually or with a millimetre rule). Pupillometer-derived diameters from automated infrared devices are mapped to the same LOINC concepts in many implementations, but the source of the measurement should be documented as a separate variable when both are available.

## Included Concepts

This concept set contains the two LOINC concepts representing the manually recorded pupil diameter, separately for each eye:
- `3010321` — Right eye Pupil diameter Manual (`8643-9`, Clinical Observation)
- `3026611` — Left eye Pupil diameter Manual (`8641-3`, Clinical Observation)

## Related Concept Sets

Pupillary reactivity to light is captured in a separate concept set (Pupillary response), since the two measurements have different scales and units and cannot be combined or compared.

## References

[1] Posner JB, Saper CB, Schiff ND, Claassen J. *Plum and Posner's Diagnosis and Treatment of Stupor and Coma*. 5th ed. Oxford University Press; 2019. Chapter 2: Examination of the comatose patient.

fr.name: Diamètre pupillaire
fr.shortDescription: Mesure manuelle au lit du patient du diamètre pupillaire de repos en millimètres, séparément pour chaque œil
fr.longDescription:
## Définition et contexte clinique

Le diamètre pupillaire est la taille de repos de la pupille, mesurée au lit du patient en millimètres, séparément pour chaque œil. L'intervalle normal sous lumière ambiante typique est d'environ 2–6 mm ; les valeurs en dehors de cet intervalle sont qualifiées de myosis (< 2 mm) ou de mydriase (> 6 mm) et peuvent évoquer des toxidromes, une pathologie du tronc cérébral ou un effet pharmacologique [1].

Les deux pupilles sont toujours enregistrées indépendamment car l'innervation pupillaire est asymétrique (les fibres parasympathiques cheminent avec le nerf crânien III). L'anisocorie — une différence de plus de 1 mm entre les deux pupilles — est un signe d'alerte évoquant un effet de masse ipsilatéral ou un engagement uncal chez un patient avec trouble de la conscience, bien qu'une petite anisocorie physiologique soit fréquente chez les sujets sains.

Ce concept set ne couvre que la mesure manuelle au lit (visuelle ou à la règle millimétrique). Les diamètres issus d'un pupillomètre infrarouge automatisé sont mappés sur les mêmes concepts LOINC dans de nombreuses implémentations, mais la source de la mesure devrait être documentée comme une variable distincte lorsque les deux sont disponibles.

## Concepts inclus

Ce concept set contient les deux concepts LOINC représentant le diamètre pupillaire mesuré manuellement, séparément pour chaque œil :
- `3010321` — Right eye Pupil diameter Manual (`8643-9`, Clinical Observation)
- `3026611` — Left eye Pupil diameter Manual (`8641-3`, Clinical Observation)

## Concept sets associés

La réactivité pupillaire à la lumière est capturée dans un concept set séparé (Pupillary response), les deux mesures ayant des échelles et des unités différentes et ne pouvant pas être combinées ou comparées.

## Références

[1] Posner JB, Saper CB, Schiff ND, Claassen J. *Plum and Posner's Diagnosis and Treatment of Stupor and Coma*. 5e éd. Oxford University Press ; 2019. Chapitre 2 : Examen du patient comateux.

name: Ramsay sedation scale
description: Six-level clinician-rated scale for assessing sedation depth in adult ICU patients

en.name: Ramsay sedation scale
en.shortDescription: Six-level clinician-rated scale for assessing sedation depth in adult ICU patients
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context The Ramsay Sedation Scale (RSS) is a six-level clinician-rated scale for assessing the depth of sedation in adult intensive care unit patients. It was originally developed in the context of a clinical trial of alphaxalone–alphadolone sedation and is one of the earliest and most widely used sedation scales [1]. The scale assigns a single score from 1 to 6 based on bedside observation and response to stimulation: - 1 anxious, agitated or restless - 2 cooperative, oriented and tranquil - 3 responsive to commands only - 4 brisk response to a light glabellar tap or loud auditory stimulus - 5 sluggish response to a light glabellar tap or loud auditory stimulus - 6 no response Levels 1–3 describe awake states (with level 2 considered the target for most sedated patients), while levels 4–6 describe progressively deeper sedation. The RSS has since been largely superseded in research and modern critical-care practice by the RASS and SAS, which offer better discrimination at lighter levels of sedation, but it remains in widespread clinical use and is frequently referenced in legacy ICU datasets. ## Included Concepts This concept set contains the LOINC Survey concept representing the recorded Ramsay total score: - `1091379` — Ramsay sedation scale total score [Reported.RSS] (`105044-2`, Survey) ## Excluded Concepts The following SNOMED concept is intentionally **not** included, as it represents the assessment tool rather than the recorded score value: - `4105091` — Ramsay sedation scale (`281400004`, Staging / Scales) ## References [1] Ramsay MA, Savege TM, Simpson BR, Goodwin R. Controlled sedation with alphaxalone-alphadolone. *Br Med J*. 1974;2(5920):656-659. doi:10.1136/bmj.2.5920.656. PMID: 4835444

fr.name: Ramsay sedation scale
fr.shortDescription: Échelle à six niveaux cotée par le clinicien pour évaluer la profondeur de la sédation chez les patients adultes de réanimation
fr.longDescription: ## Définition et contexte clinique La Ramsay Sedation Scale (RSS) est une échelle à six niveaux cotée par le clinicien pour évaluer la profondeur de la sédation chez les patients adultes de réanimation. Elle a été initialement développée dans le cadre d'un essai clinique évaluant la sédation par alphaxalone–alphadolone et constitue l'une des premières et des plus largement utilisées des échelles de sédation [1]. L'échelle attribue un score unique de 1 à 6 à partir de l'observation au lit du patient et de sa réponse à la stimulation : - 1 anxieux, agité ou nerveux - 2 coopérant, orienté et tranquille - 3 répond uniquement aux ordres - 4 réponse vive à un tapotement glabellaire léger ou à un stimulus auditif fort - 5 réponse lente à un tapotement glabellaire léger ou à un stimulus auditif fort - 6 aucune réponse Les niveaux 1 à 3 décrivent un patient éveillé (le niveau 2 étant la cible recherchée chez la plupart des patients sédatés), tandis que les niveaux 4 à 6 décrivent une sédation de plus en plus profonde. La RSS a depuis été largement supplantée en recherche et en pratique de réanimation moderne par les échelles RASS et SAS, qui offrent une meilleure discrimination aux niveaux de sédation légère, mais elle reste largement utilisée en clinique et fréquemment retrouvée dans les jeux de données de réanimation anciens. ## Concepts inclus Ce concept set contient le concept LOINC Survey représentant le score total Ramsay enregistré : - `1091379` — Ramsay sedation scale total score [Reported.RSS] (`105044-2`, Survey) ## Concepts exclus Le concept SNOMED suivant est intentionnellement **non inclus**, car il représente l'outil d'évaluation et non la valeur du score enregistré : - `4105091` — Ramsay sedation scale (`281400004`, Staging / Scales) ## Références [1] Ramsay MA, Savege TM, Simpson BR, Goodwin R. Controlled sedation with alphaxalone-alphadolone. *Br Med J*. 1974;2(5920):656-659. doi:10.1136/bmj.2.5920.656. PMID: 4835444

name: Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale (RASS)
description: 10-level clinician-rated scale for assessing level of consciousness, sedation and agitation in adult ICU patients

en.name: Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale (RASS)
en.shortDescription: 10-level clinician-rated scale for assessing level of consciousness, sedation and agitation in adult ICU patients
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context The RASS (Richmond Agitation–Sedation Scale) is a 10-level clinician-rated scale for assessing the level of consciousness, sedation, and agitation in adult intensive care unit patients. It can be administered in 30–60 seconds and does not require special training [1]. The scale uses three sequential assessment steps — observation, response to auditory stimulation, and response to physical stimulation — to assign a single score: - +4 combative - +3 very agitated - +2 agitated - +1 restless - 0 alert and calm - −1 drowsy - −2 light sedation - −3 moderate sedation - −4 deep sedation - −5 unarousable Positive scores denote agitation, zero denotes a calm and alert state, and negative scores denote sedation. ## Included Concepts This concept set contains the OMOP-standard SNOMED concept for the scale: - `1447532` — Richmond Agitation Sedation Scale (`1345048008`, Staging / Scales, Standard) The non-standard SNOMED Observable Entity `1450955` (Richmond Agitation Sedation Scale score, `1345050000`) maps to this standard concept (OMOP `Maps to`), so recorded score values stored against the source code are captured through standard-concept resolution. ## References [1] Sessler CN, Gosnell MS, Grap MJ, et al. The Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale: validity and reliability in adult intensive care unit patients. *Am J Respir Crit Care Med*. 2002;166(10):1338-1344. doi:10.1164/rccm.2107138. PMID: 12421743

fr.name: Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale (RASS)
fr.shortDescription: Échelle à 10 niveaux cotée par le clinicien pour évaluer le niveau de conscience, de sédation et d'agitation chez les patients adultes de réanimation
fr.longDescription: ## Définition et contexte clinique Le RASS (Richmond Agitation–Sedation Scale) est une échelle à 10 niveaux cotée par le clinicien pour évaluer le niveau de conscience, de sédation et d'agitation chez les patients adultes de réanimation. Son administration prend 30 à 60 secondes et ne nécessite pas de formation spécifique [1]. L'échelle utilise trois étapes séquentielles d'évaluation — observation, réponse à la stimulation auditive et réponse à la stimulation physique — pour attribuer un score unique : - +4 combatif - +3 très agité - +2 agité - +1 nerveux - 0 éveillé et calme - −1 somnolent - −2 sédation légère - −3 sédation modérée - −4 sédation profonde - −5 non éveillable Les scores positifs indiquent une agitation, zéro correspond à un état calme et éveillé, et les scores négatifs indiquent une sédation. ## Concepts inclus Ce concept set contient le concept SNOMED standard OMOP de l'échelle : - `1447532` — Richmond Agitation Sedation Scale (`1345048008`, Staging / Scales, Standard) Le concept SNOMED Observable Entity non-standard `1450955` (Richmond Agitation Sedation Scale score, `1345050000`) se mappe vers ce concept standard (`Maps to` OMOP) ; les valeurs de score enregistrées sous le code source sont donc capturées via la résolution vers le concept standard. ## Références [1] Sessler CN, Gosnell MS, Grap MJ, et al. The Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale: validity and reliability in adult intensive care unit patients. *Am J Respir Crit Care Med*. 2002;166(10):1338-1344. doi:10.1164/rccm.2107138. PMID: 12421743

name: Visual analog pain scale
description: Unidimensional self-reported scale on which the patient marks pain intensity on a continuous 100 mm line

en.name: Visual analog pain scale
en.shortDescription: Unidimensional self-reported scale on which the patient marks pain intensity on a continuous 100 mm line
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context The Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) for pain is a unidimensional self-reported scale on which the patient marks the intensity of their pain on a continuous line, conventionally 100 mm long, anchored at one end by "no pain" and at the other by "worst pain imaginable" or equivalent wording [1]. The score corresponds to the distance in millimetres from the "no pain" anchor to the patient's mark, yielding a continuous value between 0 and 100. The VAS was popularised for the clinical assessment of pain by Huskisson, who established its sensitivity to change and its applicability across a range of clinical contexts [1]. ## Included Concepts This concept set contains the OMOP-standard SNOMED concept for the scale: - `4165600` — Visual analog pain scale (`273904000`, Staging / Scales, Standard) The non-standard SNOMED Observable Entity `40481449` (Visual analog scale pain score, `443394008`) maps to this standard concept (OMOP `Maps to`), so recorded score values stored against the source code are captured through standard-concept resolution. ## Excluded Concepts The following SNOMED concept is intentionally **not** included: - `40492247` — Assessment using visual analog pain scale (`445719003`, Procedure) — represents the act of assessment, not the recorded score value ## References [1] Huskisson EC. Measurement of pain. *Lancet*. 1974;2(7889):1127-1131. doi:10.1016/s0140-6736(74)90884-8. PMID: 4139420

fr.name: Visual analog pain scale
fr.shortDescription: Échelle unidimensionnelle auto-rapportée sur laquelle le patient marque l'intensité de sa douleur sur une ligne continue de 100 mm
fr.longDescription: ## Définition et contexte clinique La VAS (Visual Analogue Scale, échelle visuelle analogique) pour la douleur est une échelle unidimensionnelle d'auto-évaluation sur laquelle le patient marque l'intensité de sa douleur sur une ligne continue, conventionnellement de 100 mm, ancrée à une extrémité par « aucune douleur » et à l'autre par « la pire douleur imaginable » ou un libellé équivalent [1]. Le score correspond à la distance en millimètres entre l'ancrage « aucune douleur » et la marque du patient, produisant une valeur continue entre 0 et 100. La VAS a été popularisée pour l'évaluation clinique de la douleur par Huskisson, qui en a établi la sensibilité au changement et l'applicabilité dans divers contextes cliniques [1]. ## Concepts inclus Ce concept set contient le concept SNOMED standard OMOP de l'échelle : - `4165600` — Visual analog pain scale (`273904000`, Staging / Scales, Standard) Le concept SNOMED Observable Entity non-standard `40481449` (Visual analog scale pain score, `443394008`) se mappe vers ce concept standard (`Maps to` OMOP) ; les valeurs de score enregistrées sous le code source sont donc capturées via la résolution vers le concept standard. ## Concepts exclus Le concept SNOMED suivant est intentionnellement **non inclus** : - `40492247` — Assessment using visual analog pain scale (`445719003`, Procedure) — représente l'acte d'évaluation, non la valeur du score enregistré ## Références [1] Huskisson EC. Measurement of pain. *Lancet*. 1974;2(7889):1127-1131. doi:10.1016/s0140-6736(74)90884-8. PMID: 4139420

name: Acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS)
description: Acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS) — advanced HIV infection with profound immunosuppression.

en.name: Acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS)
en.shortDescription: Acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS) — advanced HIV infection with profound immunosuppression.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS) is the advanced stage of HIV infection, defined by profound immunosuppression and the occurrence of opportunistic infections or AIDS-defining illnesses. In intensive care it is relevant both as a cause of admission (opportunistic infection, severe immunosuppression) and as a comorbidity affecting prognosis. AIDS is one of the chronic health items in the APACHE IV severity model.

## Scope

The set captures the documented diagnosis of AIDS and AIDS-related conditions. It represents established AIDS, distinct from asymptomatic HIV infection.

## Mapping Notes

- Map a documented diagnosis of AIDS (or an AIDS-defining condition recorded as such) to this set.
- Asymptomatic HIV infection without progression to AIDS is conceptually distinct; map it only if the intent is to capture AIDS specifically.

name: Alcoholic liver disease
description: Alcoholic liver disease — liver damage caused by chronic alcohol use, from fatty liver to alcoholic hepatitis and alcoholic cirrhosis.

en.name: Alcoholic liver disease
en.shortDescription: Alcoholic liver disease — liver damage caused by chronic alcohol use, from fatty liver to alcoholic hepatitis and alcoholic cirrhosis.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Alcoholic liver disease is the spectrum of liver damage caused by chronic alcohol use, ranging from reversible fatty liver (steatosis) through alcoholic hepatitis to alcoholic cirrhosis and alcoholic hepatic failure. In intensive care it is relevant as a comorbidity affecting coagulation, drug metabolism, infection risk and prognosis, and as a cause of admission (e.g. severe alcoholic hepatitis, decompensated alcoholic cirrhosis).

## Scope

The set is anchored on the SNOMED concept *201612 / 41309000 — Alcoholic liver damage* with all descendants included, so it captures the full spectrum: alcoholic fatty liver, alcoholic hepatitis (acute and chronic), alcoholic fibrosis, alcoholic cirrhosis, and alcoholic hepatic failure.

## Mapping Notes

- This set overlaps the Cirrhosis of liver set by a single concept (alcoholic cirrhosis): a patient with alcoholic cirrhosis maps to both sets, which is expected since the two variables answer different questions (alcohol as a cause vs. cirrhosis as an outcome).
- Non-alcoholic liver disease (e.g. viral hepatitis, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease) is **not** part of this set.

name: Chronic kidney disease
description: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) — long-standing reduction in kidney function; all stages and causes.

en.name: Chronic kidney disease
en.shortDescription: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) — long-standing reduction in kidney function; all stages and causes.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a long-standing reduction in kidney function (low glomerular filtration rate and/or kidney damage) persisting over months. In intensive care it is a pre-existing comorbidity that influences fluid and drug handling, the risk of acute-on-chronic kidney injury, and prognosis. In the APACHE IV severity model, severe chronic renal failure / dialysis dependence is one of the chronic health items; this set is broader (see Scope).

## Scope

The set is anchored on the SNOMED concept *46271022 / 709044004 — Chronic kidney disease* with all descendants included. It therefore captures **all stages** (stage 1 through stage 5 / end-stage renal disease) and **all causes** (hypertensive, diabetic, obstructive, etc.). It is the general "has CKD" variable, not restricted to the dialysis-dependent or end-stage form.

## Mapping Notes

- Map any documented stage or cause of CKD to this set.
- CKD caused by diabetes is included here **and** the diabetes diagnosis would map to the Diabetes mellitus set — the two are recorded independently.
- Acute kidney injury (a reversible, short-term event) is a distinct condition and is **not** part of this set.

name: Cirrhosis of liver
description: Cirrhosis of liver — advanced scarring of the liver, all causes; one of the APACHE IV chronic health conditions.

en.name: Cirrhosis of liver
en.shortDescription: Cirrhosis of liver — advanced scarring of the liver, all causes; one of the APACHE IV chronic health conditions.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Cirrhosis is advanced, diffuse scarring (fibrosis) of the liver with nodular regeneration, the common end-stage of many chronic liver diseases. In intensive care it is a major comorbidity affecting coagulation, fluid balance, infection risk, drug handling and prognosis. Cirrhosis is one of the chronic health items in the APACHE IV severity model.

## Scope

The set is anchored on the SNOMED concept *4064161 / 19943007 — Cirrhosis of liver* with all descendants included, so it captures cirrhosis of **all causes** (biliary, viral, cardiac, non-alcoholic, alcoholic, cryptogenic, etc.), including advanced and decompensated forms.

## Mapping Notes

- All aetiologies of cirrhosis map here. Alcoholic cirrhosis maps both here and to the Alcoholic liver disease set (the two variables answer different questions).
- Hepatic failure (loss of liver function) is captured by its own set; a cirrhotic patient who develops hepatic failure maps to both.

name: Hepatic failure
description: Hepatic failure — loss of the liver's synthetic and detoxifying function; one of the APACHE IV chronic health conditions.

en.name: Hepatic failure
en.shortDescription: Hepatic failure — loss of the liver's synthetic and detoxifying function; one of the APACHE IV chronic health conditions.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Hepatic failure is the loss of the liver's synthetic and detoxifying function, presenting with jaundice, coagulopathy and hepatic encephalopathy. It may be acute (in a previously normal liver) or occur on a background of chronic liver disease (acute-on-chronic). In intensive care it is both a reason for admission and a severe comorbidity. Hepatic failure is one of the chronic health items in the APACHE IV severity model.

## Scope

The set is anchored on the SNOMED concept *4245975 / 59927004 — Hepatic failure* with all descendants included, capturing acute, chronic and acute-on-chronic hepatic failure and related decompensation states.

## Mapping Notes

- Cirrhosis (structural scarring) and hepatic failure (functional loss) are distinct variables with their own sets; a patient may map to both.
- Hepatic encephalopathy is part of the hepatic-failure picture within this tree.

name: Immunosuppression
description: Immunosuppression — suppressed resistance to infection from therapy or disease; one of the APACHE IV chronic health conditions.

en.name: Immunosuppression
en.shortDescription: Immunosuppression — suppressed resistance to infection from therapy or disease; one of the APACHE IV chronic health conditions.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Immunosuppression is a state in which the body's resistance to infection is reduced, either by therapy (immunosuppressive drugs, chemotherapy, radiotherapy, transplantation) or by an underlying disease. In intensive care it markedly raises the risk and severity of infection and affects prognosis. Immunosuppression is one of the chronic health items in the APACHE IV severity model (where AIDS, lymphoma, leukemia and myeloma are counted as separate items).

## Scope

The set is anchored on two SNOMED concepts with their descendants: *4242843 / 38013005 — Immunosuppression* and *4140977 / 33286000 — Secondary immune deficiency disorder*. It therefore captures acquired immunosuppression: drug-induced and iatrogenic immunodeficiency, immunodeficiency secondary to chemotherapy, radiotherapy or neoplasm, and age-related immunodeficiency.

## Mapping Notes

- This set intentionally focuses on **acquired/secondary** immunosuppression rather than primary (congenital) immunodeficiency disorders.
- Because AIDS sits under secondary immune deficiency in SNOMED, an AIDS patient may resolve into both this set and the AIDS set; in the APACHE IV model these are scored as separate chronic health items.

name: Leukemia
description: Leukemia — malignancy of blood-forming cells; one of the APACHE IV chronic health conditions.

en.name: Leukemia
en.shortDescription: Leukemia — malignancy of blood-forming cells; one of the APACHE IV chronic health conditions.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Leukemia is a malignancy of the blood-forming (haematopoietic) cells, producing abnormal white cells in the blood and bone marrow. In intensive care it is a major comorbidity (cytopenias, immunosuppression, complications of chemotherapy) and a cause of admission. Leukemia is one of the chronic health items in the APACHE IV severity model.

## Scope

The set is anchored on the SNOMED concept *317510 / 93143009 — Leukemia* with all descendants included, capturing acute and chronic leukemias, lymphoid and myeloid lineages, and their subtypes (including leukemia in remission).

## Mapping Notes

- Lymphoma and multiple myeloma are related haematologic malignancies captured by their own sets.
- Leukemia in remission is included in this tree; the set records the diagnosis, not the disease activity status.

name: Malignant lymphoma
description: Malignant lymphoma — malignancy of the lymphatic system (Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin); one of the APACHE IV chronic health conditions.

en.name: Malignant lymphoma
en.shortDescription: Malignant lymphoma — malignancy of the lymphatic system (Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin); one of the APACHE IV chronic health conditions.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Malignant lymphoma is a malignancy of the lymphatic system, comprising Hodgkin lymphoma and the many non-Hodgkin lymphomas. In intensive care it is a comorbidity associated with immunosuppression and chemotherapy complications, and a cause of admission. Lymphoma is one of the chronic health items in the APACHE IV severity model.

## Scope

The set is anchored on the SNOMED concept *432571 / 118600007 — Malignant lymphoma* with all descendants included, so it captures Hodgkin and the full range of non-Hodgkin lymphoma subtypes.

## Mapping Notes

- Leukemia and multiple myeloma are distinct haematologic malignancies captured by their own sets.

name: Metastatic malignant neoplasm
description: Metastatic malignant neoplasm — cancer that has spread to distant sites; one of the APACHE IV chronic health conditions.

en.name: Metastatic malignant neoplasm
en.shortDescription: Metastatic malignant neoplasm — cancer that has spread to distant sites; one of the APACHE IV chronic health conditions.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

A metastatic malignant neoplasm is a cancer that has spread (metastasised) from its primary site to distant organs. In intensive care, metastatic disease is a major prognostic comorbidity and informs goals-of-care discussions. Metastatic cancer is one of the chronic health items in the APACHE IV severity model.

## Scope

The set is anchored on the SNOMED concept *432851 / 128462008 — Metastatic malignant neoplasm* with all descendants included, capturing secondary/metastatic malignant neoplasms across sites.

## Mapping Notes

- This set captures the **metastatic** state. A localised (non-metastatic) primary cancer is conceptually distinct and does not, by itself, map here.
- Haematologic malignancies (leukemia, lymphoma, myeloma) have their own sets and are not "metastatic solid tumours".

name: Multiple myeloma
description: Multiple myeloma — malignancy of plasma cells; one of the APACHE IV chronic health conditions.

en.name: Multiple myeloma
en.shortDescription: Multiple myeloma — malignancy of plasma cells; one of the APACHE IV chronic health conditions.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Multiple myeloma is a malignancy of plasma cells (a type of white blood cell) in the bone marrow, associated with bone disease, renal impairment, anaemia and immunosuppression. In intensive care it is a comorbidity affecting infection risk, renal function and prognosis. Myeloma is one of the chronic health items in the APACHE IV severity model (grouped with leukemia).

## Scope

The set is anchored on the SNOMED concept *437233 / 109989006 — Multiple myeloma* with all descendants included, capturing multiple myeloma and its variants.

## Mapping Notes

- Leukemia and lymphoma are distinct haematologic malignancies captured by their own sets.

name: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS)
description: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) — acute, severe, diffuse lung injury causing hypoxaemic respiratory failure.

en.name: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS)
en.shortDescription: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) — acute, severe, diffuse lung injury causing hypoxaemic respiratory failure.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is acute, diffuse inflammatory lung injury causing severe hypoxaemic respiratory failure with bilateral pulmonary infiltrates not fully explained by cardiac failure. It is a defining condition of intensive care, typically requiring mechanical ventilation, and is triggered by pneumonia, sepsis, aspiration, trauma and other insults.

## Scope

The set is anchored on the SNOMED concept *4195694 / 67782005 — Acute respiratory distress syndrome*. It captures the diagnosis of ARDS as an acute critical-illness condition.

## Mapping Notes

- ARDS is an acute syndrome, distinct from chronic respiratory comorbidities such as COPD.
- The older term "adult respiratory distress syndrome" refers to the same condition; the current term is "acute respiratory distress syndrome".

name: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
description: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) — chronic airflow limitation from chronic bronchitis and/or emphysema.

en.name: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
en.shortDescription: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) — chronic airflow limitation from chronic bronchitis and/or emphysema.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a chronic respiratory condition characterised by persistent airflow limitation, usually from a mix of small-airway disease (chronic bronchitis) and parenchymal destruction (emphysema). In intensive care it matters as a pre-existing comorbidity that affects respiratory reserve, weaning from mechanical ventilation, and prognosis.

## Scope

The set is anchored on the SNOMED concept *255573 / 13645005 — Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease* with all descendants included, so it captures the documented diagnosis of COPD and its sub-types (including chronic bronchitis and emphysema variants and COPD with acute exacerbation). It represents the presence of the diagnosis, not its severity grade (e.g. GOLD stage), which is not encoded at the concept level.

## Mapping Notes

- Map a documented diagnosis of COPD, chronic bronchitis, or emphysema to this set.
- Asthma is a distinct diagnosis and is **not** part of this set, even though both cause airflow obstruction.
- An acute exacerbation of COPD is included here as a COPD sub-type; if the source separately needs the acute event, that is captured by the exacerbation concept within this tree.

en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Chronic heart failure is a long-standing impairment of the heart's ability to pump blood, causing breathlessness, fatigue and fluid retention. In intensive care it is a comorbidity affecting fluid management, weaning and prognosis, and a cause of admission when decompensated.

## Scope

The set is anchored on the SNOMED concept *444031 / 48447003 — Chronic heart failure* with all descendants included, capturing chronic heart failure and its subtypes.

## Mapping Notes

- Acute heart failure / acute decompensation is a distinct clinical event; this set captures the chronic condition.
- Heart failure with preserved versus reduced ejection fraction is not distinguished at the set level.

en.shortDescription: Dependence on home ventilator — chronic reliance on home mechanical ventilation.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Dependence on a home ventilator indicates that a patient chronically relies on mechanical ventilation provided at home (for example for chronic respiratory failure or a neuromuscular disorder). In intensive care this baseline status is important for interpreting respiratory support, weaning targets and prognosis.

## Scope

The set is anchored on the SNOMED concept *46273524 / 60631000119109 — Dependence on home ventilator*. It captures the patient's chronic ventilator-dependent status, not an acute episode of mechanical ventilation.

## Mapping Notes

- This is a baseline dependence/status, distinct from receiving mechanical ventilation during the current ICU stay (a procedure captured elsewhere).

name: Diabetes mellitus
description: Diabetes mellitus — chronic disorder of high blood glucose; all types.

en.name: Diabetes mellitus
en.shortDescription: Diabetes mellitus — chronic disorder of high blood glucose; all types.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Diabetes mellitus is a chronic metabolic disorder of persistently high blood glucose, from absolute insulin deficiency (type 1) or insulin resistance with relative deficiency (type 2), among other forms. In intensive care it is a common comorbidity that affects glucose control, infection risk, and the management of many acute illnesses.

## Scope

The set is anchored on the SNOMED concept *201820 / 73211009 — Diabetes mellitus* with all descendants included, so it captures **all types** (type 1, type 2, secondary, gestational, and others) and diabetes with complications.

## Mapping Notes

- All documented types of diabetes map here; the set records the presence of diabetes, not its type or control.
- Diabetes that has caused chronic kidney disease maps here **and** to the Chronic kidney disease set (the two variables are recorded independently).
- Transient stress hyperglycaemia without a diabetes diagnosis is not part of this set.

name: Catheter infection
description: Catheter infection — infection related to an intravascular catheter (line infection, catheter-related bloodstream infection).

en.name: Catheter infection
en.shortDescription: Catheter infection — infection related to an intravascular catheter (line infection, catheter-related bloodstream infection).
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Catheter infection covers infections related to an intravascular catheter or vascular access device — from local exit-site or tunnel infection to catheter-related bloodstream infection (CRBSI) / central line-associated bloodstream infection (CLABSI). These are common, preventable hospitalisation complications in intensive care, where central venous and haemodialysis catheters are frequent.

## Scope

The set is anchored on the SNOMED concept *43021283 / 473083009 — Infection associated with vascular device* with all descendants included. It therefore captures infections of intravenous and central venous catheters (including exit-site and tunnel-site infections), totally implantable venous access devices, and haemodialysis catheters (tunnelled and temporary), as well as catheter-related/central-line-associated bloodstream infection and intravascular-line candidaemia.

## Mapping Notes

- This set captures infections **of/related to** a vascular catheter or device, not the presence of the catheter itself or its mechanical complications.
- Urinary catheter infection (CAUTI) and peritoneal dialysis catheter infection are intentionally **not** part of this set — the anchor is restricted to vascular devices.

name: Ventilator-associated pneumonia
description: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) — pneumonia developing during mechanical ventilation.

en.name: Ventilator-associated pneumonia
en.shortDescription: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) — pneumonia developing during mechanical ventilation.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is pneumonia that develops in a patient who has been mechanically ventilated (typically beyond 48 hours of intubation). It is a key hospitalisation complication in intensive care, associated with prolonged ventilation, longer ICU stay and increased mortality, and is widely tracked as a quality indicator.

## Scope

The set is anchored on the SNOMED concept *259992 / 429271009 — Ventilator associated pneumonia*. It captures the VAP diagnosis specifically.

## Mapping Notes

- VAP is distinct from community-acquired or non-ventilator hospital-acquired pneumonia; map only pneumonia identified as ventilator-associated.

versions.author: Boris Delange
versions.message: Add the RxNorm Extension ingredient Heparin Sodium (35884360) with its descendants. RxNorm Extension carries it as a standard Ingredient separate from the RxNorm ingredient heparin (1367571), so its 177 descendants, mostly European products (e.g. Novo-Heparin, Hepaflush), were not reached by the heparin anchor and a site mapping its heparin products to them was counted as not covered. Low molecular weight heparins (RxNorm Extension 35884361, 35884372) stay out of this set, which covers unfractionated heparin.

versions.author: Boris Delange
versions.message: Deprecated. The source RxNorm Extension ingredient 'insulin aspart' (35198096) was deprecated in OMOP (RxNorm Extension 2026-01-14) and now maps to the standard RxNorm ingredient 'insulin aspart, human' (1567198). As a result this set became equivalent to concept set 123 'Insulin Aspart, Human', which already uses 1567198. Use concept set 123 instead.

reviews.comments:
## Summary
**Approved.** Used in QI03 via the ingredient hierarchy (dose derived from DrugStrength).

## Use in our quality indicators
- Used in QI03 (Feeding).
- CQL: covered as a whole via the anchor concept 1567198 insulin aspart, human with descendants (OMOP hierarchy codesystem) in [`InsulinDrugs.cql`](https://github.com/umg-minai/cql-indicate-qi/blob/d63eb84a308d5586fcede0b7e3fa73abf6b6761c/cql/InsulinDrugs.cql?plain=1), [`InsulinIngredients.cql`](https://github.com/umg-minai/cql-indicate-qi/blob/d63eb84a308d5586fcede0b7e3fa73abf6b6761c/cql/InsulinIngredients.cql?plain=1); the 803 resolved concepts were not reviewed one by one.

## Suggestions
- None.

en.name: Base excess in blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Base excess (BE) is a marker of the metabolic component of acid-base balance, computed by blood gas analysers from pH, PCO2 and haemoglobin. Routine values lie within ±2 mmol/L; negative values mean metabolic acidosis, positive values metabolic alkalosis [1, 2]. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, expressed in mmol/L. **Note: arterial vs venous.** BE is constructed to be insensitive to the venous-to-arterial PCO2 difference, so arterial, venous, mixed venous and central venous BE are clinically very close and used interchangeably (except in shock or local hypoperfusion). This concept set covers all common blood specimens. **Note: BE vs standard BE.** LOINC distinguishes `Base excess` (in vivo) from `Base excess standard` (with haemoglobin normalised to 5 g/dL). The two are produced together by modern blood gas analysers and differ by 1-2 mmol/L on average. Both are included here; analyses that need to distinguish them must use the LOINC code, not the value. ## Included Concepts The set is anchored on six LOINC Hierarchy concepts (scoped to `Chemistry - non-challenge`), each expanded to include all their descendants. The set resolves to 11 LOINC "Lab Test" concepts. ### Whole blood - *3012501 / 11555-0 — Base excess in Blood by calculation (LOINC)*: generic blood specimen. ### Arterial blood - *3003396 / 1925-7 — Base excess in Arterial blood by calculation (LOINC)*: most widely used. - *3021421 / 19235-1 — Base excess standard in Arterial blood by calculation (LOINC)*: standardised form. ### Venous blood - *3002032 / 1927-3 — Base excess in Venous blood by calculation (LOINC)* - *3027215 / 19237-7 — Base excess standard in Venous blood by calculation (LOINC)* ### Mixed venous blood - *3023001 / 19234-4 — Base excess in Mixed venous blood by calculation (LOINC)* - *3010329 / 19238-5 — Base excess standard in Mixed venous blood by calculation (LOINC)* ### Central venous blood - *1616922 / 97546-6 — Base excess in Central venous blood by calculation (LOINC)* - *1616406 / 97547-4 — Base excess standard in Central venous blood by calculation (LOINC)* ### Capillary blood - *3003129 / 1926-5 — Base excess in Capillary blood by calculation (LOINC)* - *3026613 / 19236-9 — Base excess standard in Capillary blood by calculation (LOINC)* **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS`: **`mmol/L`** (concept 8753 — millimole per litre). ## Excluded Concepts No concepts are explicitly excluded by name. The set deliberately omits the following LOINC concepts: - **Cord blood and fetus specimens**: physiologically distinct from post-natal blood. - **Base excess.100% oxygenated variants**: special calculation under hyperoxic assumption, rarely used outside research. - **Extracellular fluid, nonbiological fluid specimens**: out of scope. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports a base excess value without specifying specimen: `3003396 / 1925-7 — Base excess in Arterial blood by calculation`, by far the most common. - **Source reports "BE" or "BE(B)" without distinguishing standard vs in vivo**: in clinical practice this is treated as in vivo (Siggaard-Andersen) BE; map to the `Base excess in X blood` LOINC code rather than the `Base excess standard` one. - **Source explicitly reports SBE (standard base excess)**: map to the matching `Base excess standard in X blood` LOINC code. - **Do not confuse with**: bicarbonate (separate concept set, "Bicarbonate in blood"), anion gap, strong ion difference (different acid-base parameters). ## References [1] Siggaard-Andersen O. The Van Slyke equation. *Scand J Clin Lab Invest Suppl*. 1977;146:15-20. Available: https://doi.org/10.3109/00365517709098927 [2] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 1925-7 — Base excess in Arterial blood by calculation. Available: https://loinc.org/1925-7/
