en.name: Carbon dioxide partial pressure in arterial blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context The arterial partial pressure of carbon dioxide (PaCO2) is the pressure of CO2 dissolved in arterial blood. It is the main marker of alveolar ventilation: PaCO2 rises in hypoventilation and falls in hyperventilation [1]. Together with pH and bicarbonate, it characterises the respiratory component of acid-base balance. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a blood gas analyser on an arterial sample. Results are reported in mmHg (US convention) or kPa (SI / European convention) [2]. **Note: arterial vs venous.** Arterial and venous PCO2 differ substantially (venous PCO2 is typically 4-6 mmHg higher); the arterio-venous gradient is itself a clinical signal of perfusion. This concept set covers **arterial PCO2 only**. Venous, mixed venous, central venous and capillary PCO2 are captured by the separate concept set "Carbon dioxide partial pressure in venous blood". **Note: temperature-corrected variant.** Modern blood gas analysers measure at 37 °C. A separate LOINC code exists for PCO2 corrected to the patient's actual temperature (relevant in hypothermia). Both forms are included here; analyses that need to distinguish them must use the LOINC code, not the value. **Note: do not confuse with total CO2.** LOINC distinguishes `Carbon dioxide [Partial pressure]` (PaCO2, dissolved gas, mmHg or kPa) from `Carbon dioxide, total [Moles/volume]` (total CO2 content, mmol/L). The latter is essentially the bicarbonate plus dissolved CO2 and belongs with the separate concept set "Bicarbonate in blood". Only `[Partial pressure]` codes are included here. ## Included Concepts The set is anchored on the LOINC Hierarchy `Carbon dioxide | Blood arterial | Chemistry - non-challenge`, expanded to include all its descendants, with total-CO2 codes excluded by name. The set resolves to two LOINC "Lab Test" concepts: - *3027946 / 2019-8 — Carbon dioxide [Partial pressure] in Arterial blood (LOINC)*: most widely used. - *3045156 / 32771-8 — Carbon dioxide [Partial pressure] adjusted to patient's actual temperature in Arterial blood (LOINC)*: temperature-corrected variant. **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS`: **`mm[Hg]`** (concept 8876 — millimetre of mercury). Conversion: `1 kPa ≈ 7.50 mmHg`. ## Excluded Concepts The following LOINC concepts that exist for CO2 in arterial blood are deliberately not part of this set, grouped by reason for exclusion. ### Total CO2 — different measurand (bicarbonate equivalent) - *3009609 / 2026-3 — Carbon dioxide, total [Moles/volume] in Arterial blood* - *3037663 / 41647-9 — Carbon dioxide, total [Moles/volume] in Arterial blood by calculation* ### Cord blood specimens — physiologically distinct - *3003932 / 28644-3 — Carbon dioxide [Partial pressure] in Arterial cord blood* - *3032759 / 49694-3 — Carbon dioxide [Partial pressure] adjusted to patient's actual temperature in Arterial cord blood* - *3043950 / 39466-8 — Carbon dioxide, total [Moles/volume] in Arterial cord blood* - *40761030 / 57921-9 — Carbon dioxide, total [Moles/volume] in Arterial cord blood by calculation* ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports an arterial PCO2 (e.g. blood gas analyser): `3027946 / 2019-8 — Carbon dioxide [Partial pressure] in Arterial blood`. - **Source reports PCO2 from venous, mixed venous or central venous blood**: do **not** map. Use "Carbon dioxide partial pressure in venous blood" instead. - **Source reports "total CO2" or "TCO2" (mmol/L)**: do **not** map. Use the "Bicarbonate in blood" concept set. - **Do not confuse with**: venous PCO2 (separate concept set), bicarbonate (separate concept set), end-tidal CO2 (EtCO2, exhaled gas — different measurand). ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 2019-8 — Carbon dioxide [Partial pressure] in Arterial blood. Available: https://loinc.org/2019-8/ [2] Nomenclature for Properties and Units (NPU). IFCC/IUPAC. NPU codes (current release). Available: https://npu-terminology.org/npu-database/

en.name: Oxygen partial pressure in arterial blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context The arterial partial pressure of oxygen (PaO2) is the pressure of O2 dissolved in arterial blood. It reflects the efficiency of pulmonary gas exchange and falls in respiratory failure, shunt, ventilation/perfusion mismatch, and diffusion impairment. Together with the inspired oxygen fraction (FiO2), it forms the PaO2/FiO2 ratio used to grade hypoxaemia severity (ARDS Berlin criteria) [1, 2]. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a blood gas analyser on an arterial sample. Results are reported in mmHg (US convention) or kPa (SI / European convention) [3]. **Note: arterial vs venous.** Arterial PO2 (~80-100 mmHg under room air in healthy adults) is much higher than venous PO2 (~40 mmHg). They are fundamentally different measurands and must not be merged. This concept set covers **arterial PO2 only**. Venous, mixed venous, central venous and capillary PO2 are captured by the separate concept set "Oxygen partial pressure in venous blood". **Note: temperature-corrected variant.** Modern blood gas analysers measure at 37 °C. A separate LOINC code exists for PO2 corrected to the patient's actual temperature (relevant in hypothermia). Both forms are included here; analyses that need to distinguish them must use the LOINC code, not the value. **Note: do not confuse with P50.** LOINC has a separate code `Oxygen [Partial pressure] saturation adjusted to 0.5` (P50, the PO2 at which haemoglobin is 50% saturated — a marker of haemoglobin oxygen affinity, not the routine PaO2). It is excluded from this concept set. ## Included Concepts The set is anchored on the LOINC Hierarchy `Oxygen | Blood arterial | Chemistry - non-challenge`, expanded to include all its descendants, with the P50 code excluded by name. The set resolves to two LOINC "Lab Test" concepts: - *3027801 / 2703-7 — Oxygen [Partial pressure] in Arterial blood (LOINC)*: most widely used. - *3022803 / 19255-9 — Oxygen [Partial pressure] adjusted to patient's actual temperature in Arterial blood (LOINC)*: temperature-corrected variant. **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS`: **`mm[Hg]`** (concept 8876 — millimetre of mercury). Conversion: `1 kPa ≈ 7.50 mmHg`. ## Excluded Concepts The following LOINC concepts that exist for O2 in arterial blood are deliberately not part of this set, grouped by reason for exclusion. ### P50 — different measurand - *3015968 / 19214-6 — Oxygen [Partial pressure] saturation adjusted to 0.5 in Arterial blood*: P50, haemoglobin oxygen affinity marker, not routine PaO2. ### Cord blood specimens — physiologically distinct - *3021706 / 28648-4 — Oxygen [Partial pressure] in Arterial cord blood* - *3033254 / 49696-8 — Oxygen [Partial pressure] adjusted to patient's actual temperature in Arterial cord blood* ### Oxygen saturation — different measurand - All `Oxygen saturation` codes: covered by the separate "Oxygen saturation in arterial blood" concept set. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports an arterial PO2 (e.g. blood gas analyser): `3027801 / 2703-7 — Oxygen [Partial pressure] in Arterial blood`. - **Source reports PO2 from venous, mixed venous or central venous blood**: do **not** map. Use "Oxygen partial pressure in venous blood" instead. - **Source reports oxygen saturation (SaO2/SpO2/%)**: do **not** map. Use "Oxygen saturation in arterial blood" (different measurand). - **Source reports P50** (haemoglobin oxygen affinity): out of scope of this concept set. - **Do not confuse with**: venous PO2 (separate concept set), oxygen saturation (separate concept set), inspired oxygen fraction (FiO2, ventilator setting). ## References [1] ARDS Definition Task Force, Ranieri VM, Rubenfeld GD, Thompson BT, Ferguson ND, Caldwell E, et al. Acute respiratory distress syndrome: the Berlin Definition. *JAMA*. 2012;307(23):2526-33. Available: https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2012.5669 [2] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 2703-7 — Oxygen [Partial pressure] in Arterial blood. Available: https://loinc.org/2703-7/ [3] Nomenclature for Properties and Units (NPU). IFCC/IUPAC. NPU codes (current release). Available: https://npu-terminology.org/npu-database/

en.name: Oxygen saturation in arterial blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Arterial oxygen saturation (SaO2) is the fraction of haemoglobin in arterial blood bound to oxygen, expressed as a percentage. It is measured on an arterial blood sample by a CO-oximeter (multi-wavelength spectrophotometer in the blood gas analyser), which directly distinguishes oxyhaemoglobin from deoxy-, carboxy- and methaemoglobin [1]. SaO2 is the reference for arterial oxygenation and reflects the position on the haemoglobin-oxygen dissociation curve at the patient's PaO2. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, reported as a percentage (0-100%). **Note: SaO2 vs SpO2.** This concept set covers **SaO2 measured by CO-oximetry on an arterial blood sample only** — a one-shot laboratory measurement. It does **not** cover pulse oximetry (SpO2), which is a continuous, transcutaneous estimate produced by a pulse oximeter at the fingertip or earlobe. SpO2 is biased upward of SaO2 in carbon monoxide intoxication, methemoglobinemia, severe anaemia or low perfusion, and is captured by a separate concept set ("Oxygen saturation by pulse oximetry", if defined; LOINC class is `Clinical Observation`). **Note: arterial vs venous.** Arterial saturation (SaO2 ~ 95-100% in healthy adults at sea level) and venous saturation (SvO2 ~ 65-75%) are different measurands and must not be merged. Venous and central venous saturation are captured by the separate concept set "Oxygen saturation in venous blood". **Note: directly measured vs calculated.** LOINC distinguishes `Oxygen saturation in Arterial blood` (direct CO-oximetry, code 2708-6) from `Oxygen saturation Calculated from oxygen partial pressure in Arterial blood` (computed from PaO2 via the haemoglobin dissociation curve, code 51733-4). Both forms are included here; the calculated variant is less reliable when dyshaemoglobinaemias are present. ## Included Concepts The set lists four LOINC "Lab Test" concepts for SaO2 (cord blood excluded), grouped by representation. ### Volume fraction (%, traditional) - *3016502 / 2708-6 — Oxygen saturation in Arterial blood (LOINC)*: most widely used. - *3039426 / 51733-4 — Oxygen saturation Calculated from oxygen partial pressure in Arterial blood (LOINC)*: derived from PaO2. ### Pure mass fraction (UCUM variants) - *42869607 / 71852-8 — Oxygen saturation [Pure mass fraction] in Arterial blood (LOINC)* - *42869598 / 71843-7 — Oxygen saturation [Pure mass fraction] Calculated from oxygen partial pressure in Arterial blood (LOINC)* **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS`: **`%`** (concept 8554 — percent). The `[Pure mass fraction]` variants are dimensionless ratios between 0 and 1. ## Excluded Concepts The following LOINC concepts that exist for arterial oxygen saturation are deliberately not part of this set, grouped by reason for exclusion. ### Pulse oximetry (SpO2) — different measurement principle - All `Oxygen saturation in Arterial blood by Pulse oximetry` codes (LOINC class is mostly `Clinical Observation`): different measurement principle (transcutaneous, non-invasive, continuous), with different biases. ### Cord blood — physiologically distinct - *3014295 / 28642-7 — Oxygen saturation in Arterial cord blood* - *42869603 / 71848-6 — Oxygen saturation [Pure mass fraction] in Arterial cord blood* ### Other specimens - All venous, mixed venous, central venous codes: captured by the separate "Oxygen saturation in venous blood" concept set. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports SaO2 measured on an arterial blood gas (CO-oximetry): `3016502 / 2708-6 — Oxygen saturation in Arterial blood`. - **Source is a pulse oximetry reading (SpO2)**: do **not** map to this concept set. Use the dedicated pulse oximetry concept set. - **Source explicitly says "calculated from PaO2"**: map to the `Calculated from oxygen partial pressure` variant. - **Source reports SvO2 / ScvO2 (venous saturation)**: do **not** map. Use "Oxygen saturation in venous blood" instead. - **Do not confuse with**: SpO2 (pulse oximetry, different concept set), SvO2/ScvO2 (venous saturation, separate concept set), PaO2 (oxygen partial pressure, separate concept set). ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 2708-6 — Oxygen saturation in Arterial blood. Available: https://loinc.org/2708-6/

en.name: Ionized calcium in blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Ionized (free) calcium is the biologically active fraction of total calcium — typically ~50 % of total calcium in plasma. It is measured directly by ion-selective membrane electrodes on blood gas analysers and on dedicated biochemistry platforms. It is the variable of interest in critical care (hypocalcaemia, transfusion-related hypocalcaemia, post-cardiac-surgery monitoring) where rapid acid-base disturbances or hypoalbuminaemia make total calcium misleading [1]. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp. Results are reported as a substance concentration in mmol/L (SI unit) or as a mass concentration in mg/dL [2]. This concept set aggregates **ionized calcium** measurements across blood specimens (serum, plasma, arterial, venous, mixed venous, capillary and unspecified blood). Cord blood and fetus specimens are excluded. **Note: ionized vs total calcium.** This concept set covers **ionized (free) calcium** only. Total calcium (including the protein-bound and complexed fractions) is captured by a separate concept set, "Calcium in blood". The two are different measurands with different reference ranges and clinical interpretation; they must not be merged. **Note: actual vs. pH-adjusted ionized calcium.** LOINC distinguishes two forms: - **Ionized calcium** — measured at the patient's actual pH. - **Ionized calcium adjusted to pH 7.4** — recalculated as if pH were 7.4, to neutralise the effect of acid-base status on calcium binding. In the absence of acid-base disturbance the two values are nearly identical, but they can diverge in acidosis or alkalosis. **Both forms are included in this concept set** because most clinical sources and studies aggregate them under "ionized calcium". Study designs that explicitly compare actual vs. pH-adjusted ionized calcium should preserve the distinction at the source value level. ## Included Concepts The set is anchored on six LOINC Hierarchy concepts (one per blood specimen, scoped to `Chemistry - non-challenge`), with their descendants pulled in. After exclusions, the set resolves to 22 LOINC "Lab Test" concepts, grouped here by specimen. ### Serum or plasma - *3021347 / 1995-0 — Calcium.ionized [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: most widely used substance-concentration form. - *3027694 / 17863-2 — Calcium.ionized [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: same measurand expressed as mass concentration. - *3013784 / 12180-6 — Calcium.ionized [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma by Ion-selective membrane electrode (ISE) (LOINC)*: ISE method explicit. - *3024250 / 17864-0 — Calcium.ionized [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma by Ion-selective membrane electrode (ISE) (LOINC)*: ISE method explicit, mass form. - *3015774 / 13959-2 — Calcium.ionized [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma by calculation (LOINC)*: derived by calculation (rather than directly measured). - *3016431 / 19072-8 — Calcium.ionized [Moles/volume] adjusted to pH 7.4 in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: pH-adjusted form. - *40760451 / 57333-7 — Calcium.ionized [Mass/volume] adjusted to pH 7.4 in Serum or Plasma by Ion-selective membrane electrode (ISE) (LOINC)*: pH-adjusted form, mass, ISE. ### Generic blood (specimen unspecified) - *3021119 / 1994-3 — Calcium.ionized [Moles/volume] in Blood (LOINC)*: typically reported by a blood gas analyser. - *3036426 / 38230-9 — Calcium.ionized [Mass/volume] in Blood (LOINC)*: same measurand expressed as mass concentration. - *3050068 / 47596-2 — Calcium.ionized [Moles/volume] in Blood by Ion-selective membrane electrode (ISE) (LOINC)*: ISE method explicit. - *3048816 / 47598-8 — Calcium.ionized [Moles/volume] adjusted to pH 7.4 in Blood (LOINC)*: pH-adjusted form. ### Arterial blood - *3044331 / 34581-9 — Calcium.ionized [Moles/volume] in Arterial blood (LOINC)* - *40762532 / 59470-5 — Calcium.ionized [Mass/volume] in Arterial blood (LOINC)* - *3041706 / 53138-4 — Calcium.ionized [Moles/volume] adjusted to pH 7.4 in Arterial blood (LOINC)*: pH-adjusted form. - *40762534 / 59472-1 — Calcium.ionized [Mass/volume] adjusted to pH 7.4 in Arterial blood by Ion-selective membrane electrode (ISE) (LOINC)*: pH-adjusted form, mass, ISE. ### Venous blood - *3033705 / 41645-3 — Calcium.ionized [Moles/volume] in Venous blood (LOINC)* - *40762533 / 59471-3 — Calcium.ionized [Mass/volume] in Venous blood (LOINC)* - *3041671 / 53140-0 — Calcium.ionized [Moles/volume] adjusted to pH 7.4 in Venous blood (LOINC)*: pH-adjusted form. - *40762535 / 59473-9 — Calcium.ionized [Mass/volume] adjusted to pH 7.4 in Venous blood by Ion-selective membrane electrode (ISE) (LOINC)*: pH-adjusted form, mass, ISE. ### Mixed venous blood - *3032271 / 41646-1 — Calcium.ionized [Moles/volume] in Mixed venous blood (LOINC)*: typically from a Swan-Ganz catheter. ### Capillary blood - *3035279 / 41644-6 — Calcium.ionized [Moles/volume] in Capillary blood (LOINC)* - *3039602 / 53139-2 — Calcium.ionized [Moles/volume] adjusted to pH 7.4 in Capillary blood (LOINC)*: pH-adjusted form. **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS`: **`mmol/L`** (concept 8753 — millimole per litre) for `[Moles/volume]` codes and **`mg/dL`** (concept 8840) for `[Mass/volume]` codes. Conversion: `1 mmol/L ≈ 4.01 mg/dL`. ## Excluded Concepts The hierarchies above pull in two LOINC concepts that are explicitly excluded: ### Ratios — different measurand (ratio to total calcium) - *3032710 / 49936-8 — Calcium.ionized/Calcium.total corrected for albumin in Blood* - *3032782 / 49935-0 — Calcium.ionized/Calcium.total corrected for albumin in Serum or Plasma* The set also deliberately omits the following LOINC concepts: - **Cord blood specimens** (e.g. `40757498 / 54367-8 — Calcium.ionized [Moles/volume] in Cord blood`, `40757497 / 54366-0 — Calcium.ionized [Moles/volume] adjusted to pH 7.4 in Cord blood`): physiologically distinct from post-natal blood. - **Blood drawn from CRRT circuit** (e.g. via `LP385977-6` hierarchy): specialised intra-circuit monitoring, not a routine patient measurement. - **Body fluid, CSF, dialysis fluid, nonbiological fluid specimens**: out of scope for a "blood" concept set. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports "ionized calcium", "iCa", "free calcium", "Ca++" without further specification: `3021347 / 1995-0 — Calcium.ionized [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma`. If the source comes from a blood gas analyser, prefer `3021119 / 1994-3 — Calcium.ionized [Moles/volume] in Blood` or the arterial variant. - **Source explicitly labels the value as "adjusted to pH 7.4"** (or "pH-corrected ionized calcium"): map to the corresponding `adjusted to pH 7.4` LOINC code for the specimen. Do **not** merge with the actual ionized calcium without checking the study design. - **Source reports "calcium" or "Ca" without specifying ionized/total**: by default, total calcium is the routine biochemistry measurement; map to the "Calcium in blood" concept set unless the source unambiguously labels the result as ionized. - **Do not confuse with**: total calcium (separate concept set), corrected calcium (separate concept set, "Corrected calcium in blood"). ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 1995-0 — Calcium.ionized [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma. Available: https://loinc.org/1995-0/ [2] Nomenclature for Properties and Units (NPU). IFCC/IUPAC. NPU codes (current release). Available: https://npu-terminology.org/npu-database/

en.name: Lactate in arterial blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Lactate is the end-product of anaerobic glucose metabolism; its concentration in arterial blood is a key marker of tissue hypoperfusion and is widely used in shock, sepsis, and critical care [1]. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a blood gas analyser or a point-of-care device on arterial blood. Results are reported as a substance concentration in mmol/L (SI unit) or as a mass concentration in mg/dL [2]. **Note: arterial vs venous lactate.** Lactate concentrations in arterial and venous blood are **not numerically equivalent** — the arterio-venous difference reflects tissue lactate production/clearance and is clinically meaningful. This concept set covers **arterial lactate** only. Venous lactate (including capillary, mixed venous, central venous, serum/plasma generic) is captured by a separate concept set, "Lactate in venous blood". Cord blood and fetus specimens are excluded. ## Included Concepts The set is anchored on two LOINC Hierarchy concepts (scoped to `Chemistry - non-challenge`), with their descendants pulled in. The set resolves to three LOINC "Lab Test" concepts. ### Arterial blood - *3018405 / 2518-9 — Lactate [Moles/volume] in Arterial blood (LOINC)*: most widely used LOINC code for arterial lactate. - *3035561 / 30242-2 — Lactate [Mass/volume] in Arterial blood (LOINC)*: same measurand expressed as mass concentration. - *3020410 / 32132-3 — Lactate [Moles/volume] in Arterial plasma (LOINC)*: less common variant where the specimen is explicitly arterial plasma rather than whole arterial blood. **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS`: **`mmol/L`** (concept 8753 — millimole per litre) for `[Moles/volume]` codes and **`mg/dL`** (concept 8840) for `[Mass/volume]` codes. Conversion: `1 mg/dL ≈ 0.111 mmol/L` (molar mass of lactate = 89.07 g/mol). ## Excluded Concepts No concepts are explicitly excluded by name. The set deliberately omits the following LOINC concepts: - **Venous, mixed venous, capillary, central venous, generic Blood, Serum or Plasma specimens**: captured by the separate concept set "Lactate in venous blood". - **Cord blood and fetus specimens**: physiologically distinct from post-natal blood. - **Lactate/Pyruvate ratio**: different measurand. - **Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH)**: different analyte, captured by the separate "Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) in blood" concept set. - **CSF, body fluid, dialysis fluid and other specimens**: out of scope for a "blood" concept set. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports a lactate value explicitly from arterial blood (e.g. blood gas analyser, arterial sample): `3018405 / 2518-9 — Lactate [Moles/volume] in Arterial blood`. - **Source reports a lactate value without specifying arterial origin**: do **not** map to this concept set. Use the separate "Lactate in venous blood" concept set, which aggregates venous, capillary, mixed venous and generic specimens. - **Do not confuse with**: venous lactate (separate concept set, arterio-venous difference is clinically meaningful), lactate dehydrogenase (LDH, different analyte), lactate/pyruvate ratio. ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 2518-9 — Lactate [Moles/volume] in Arterial blood. Available: https://loinc.org/2518-9/ [2] Nomenclature for Properties and Units (NPU). IFCC/IUPAC. NPU codes (current release). Available: https://npu-terminology.org/npu-database/

en.name: pH in arterial blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Arterial pH (pHa) is the negative log of the hydrogen ion activity in arterial blood, normally between 7.35 and 7.45. It is the primary descriptor of acid-base balance: pHa < 7.35 defines acidaemia, pHa > 7.45 defines alkalaemia [1]. Together with PaCO2 and bicarbonate, it allows the distinction of respiratory vs metabolic disorders and their compensation. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a blood gas analyser on an arterial sample. pH is dimensionless. **Note: arterial vs venous.** Arterial and venous pH differ by ~ 0.02-0.04 (venous pH is lower because of CO2 production by tissues). The difference widens in low-flow states. Although venous pH is sometimes used as a surrogate for arterial pH in non-critical settings, the two are not strictly interchangeable. This concept set covers **arterial** pH only. Venous, mixed venous, central venous and capillary pH are captured by the separate concept set "pH in venous blood". **Note: temperature-corrected variant.** Modern blood gas analysers measure at 37 °C. A separate LOINC code exists for pH corrected to the patient's actual temperature (relevant in hypothermia, e.g. therapeutic hypothermia post-cardiac arrest). The two approaches — keeping pH constant at the measured (37 °C) value (α-stat) versus keeping it constant at the temperature-corrected value (pH-stat) — yield different management decisions and reflect distinct CO2 management strategies [2]. Both LOINC codes are included here; analyses that need to distinguish them must use the LOINC code, not the value. ## Included Concepts The set lists two LOINC "Lab Test" concepts for pH in arterial blood (cord blood excluded): - *3019977 / 2744-1 — pH of Arterial blood (LOINC)*: most widely used. - *3029473 / 33254-4 — pH of Arterial blood adjusted to patient's actual temperature (LOINC)*: temperature-corrected (pH-stat) variant. **Note on units.** pH is dimensionless. LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS` is **`[pH]`**; the OMOP vocabulary spells the same unit **`pH`** (OMOP concept 8482), which is the code used in this dictionary. ## Excluded Concepts The following LOINC concepts are deliberately not part of this set: ### Cord blood specimens — physiologically distinct - *3006598 / 28646-8 — pH of Arterial cord blood* - *3030109 / 49698-4 — pH of Arterial cord blood adjusted to patient's actual temperature* ### Other specimens - All venous, mixed venous, central venous, capillary, generic blood codes: captured by the separate "pH in venous blood" concept set or generic-blood concept set if defined. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports an arterial pH (e.g. blood gas analyser): `3019977 / 2744-1 — pH of Arterial blood`. - **Source reports pH from venous, mixed venous or central venous blood**: do **not** map to this concept set. Use "pH in venous blood" instead. - **Source explicitly says "temperature-corrected" or "pH-stat"**: map to `3029473 / 33254-4 — pH of Arterial blood adjusted to patient's actual temperature`. - **Do not confuse with**: venous pH (separate concept set), urinary pH, gastric pH (different specimens). ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 2744-1 — pH of Arterial blood. Available: https://loinc.org/2744-1/ [2] Bacher A. Effects of body temperature on blood gases. *Intensive Care Med*. 2005;31(1):24-7. Available: https://doi.org/10.1007/s00134-004-2369-3

en.name: Arterial blood specimen
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Arterial blood specimen is a sample of blood obtained by puncture or catheterisation of a systemic artery (radial, femoral, brachial). It is used primarily for blood gas analysis (PaO2, PaCO2, pH, SaO2, lactate) and reflects the oxygen and carbon-dioxide status of blood after gas exchange in the lungs and before tissue extraction. Arterial sampling is more painful and carries a higher risk of complications than venous sampling, so it is reserved for clinical questions where the arterial-venous difference matters.

**OMOP CDM usage.** This concept set targets the `SPECIMEN.specimen_concept_id` field. See the [Mapping Recommendations](#/mapping-recommendations) — *Lab Mapping → Specimen* section for how MEASUREMENT and SPECIMEN are linked in CDM v5.4.

## Included Concepts

The set is anchored on the SNOMED Specimen concept `Arterial blood specimen`, expanded to include all its descendants. The set resolves to one specimen:

- *4047496 / 122552005 — Arterial blood specimen (SNOMED)*

## Excluded Concepts

The following SNOMED Specimen descendant is deliberately excluded by name:

- *45766301 / 703430008 — Arterial cord blood specimen*: cord blood is physiologically distinct from post-natal arterial blood (placental circulation, oxygenation pattern).

## Mapping Notes

- **Default mapping** when the source data records a sample collected from an artery (radial line, femoral puncture, arterial blood gas): `4047496 / 122552005 — Arterial blood specimen`.
- **Source records umbilical / cord sampling**: do **not** map. Out of scope.
- **Source records a venous or capillary sample**: use the appropriate venous / peripheral / whole blood specimen concept set.

en.name: Peripheral blood specimen
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Peripheral blood specimen is a sample of blood obtained from a peripheral vessel (typically a peripheral vein), as opposed to a central catheter, an artery, or umbilical / cord blood. It is the most common source of blood samples for routine laboratory testing. In SNOMED CT, this concept is sibling to `Arterial blood specimen` and is positioned to encode the **anatomical site** of the draw, complementary to the specimen-type concepts (whole blood, plasma, serum).

**OMOP CDM usage.** This concept set targets the `SPECIMEN.specimen_concept_id` field. See the [Mapping Recommendations](#/mapping-recommendations) — *Lab Mapping → Specimen* section for how MEASUREMENT and SPECIMEN are linked in CDM v5.4.

## Included Concepts

The set is anchored on the SNOMED Specimen concept `Peripheral blood specimen`, expanded to include all its descendants. The set resolves to one specimen:

- *4047495 / 122551003 — Peripheral blood specimen (SNOMED)*

## Excluded Concepts

No concepts are explicitly excluded by name. The set deliberately omits:

- **Cord, umbilical, fetal blood specimens**: physiologically distinct from post-natal peripheral blood.
- **Central venous, arterial samples**: covered by the separate "Venous blood specimen" or "Arterial blood specimen" concept sets.

## Mapping Notes

- **Default mapping** when the source data records a peripheral venipuncture (e.g. routine biology draw, antecubital vein): `4047495 / 122551003 — Peripheral blood specimen`.
- **Source records a sample drawn from an artery, central line, umbilicus or cord**: do **not** map. Use the appropriate dedicated concept set.
- **Do not confuse with**: `Whole blood specimen` (specimen type, anticoagulant-related), which describes the **physical state** of the sample, not the **anatomical site**.

en.name: Venous blood specimen
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Venous blood specimen is a sample of blood obtained by venipuncture or from a venous catheter. It includes peripheral venous samples (routine biology), central venous samples (drawn from a central venous catheter) and mixed venous samples (drawn from a pulmonary artery catheter). Compared with arterial blood, venous blood has lower PO2 and SO2, higher PCO2, and slightly lower pH, reflecting tissue oxygen extraction and CO2 production.

**OMOP CDM usage.** This concept set targets the `SPECIMEN.specimen_concept_id` field. See the [Mapping Recommendations](#/mapping-recommendations) — *Lab Mapping → Specimen* section for how MEASUREMENT and SPECIMEN are linked in CDM v5.4.

**Note: SNOMED does not provide a separate "Central venous blood specimen" code.** Central venous samples are recorded as `Venous blood specimen` at the specimen level; the central-venous distinction is captured by the analyte-side LOINC code (`... in Central venous blood`).

## Included Concepts

The set is anchored on the SNOMED Specimen concept `Venous blood specimen`, expanded to include all its descendants. The set resolves to two specimens:

- *4045667 / 122555007 — Venous blood specimen (SNOMED)*
- *4001226 / 119298005 — Mixed venous blood specimen (SNOMED)*

## Excluded Concepts

The following SNOMED Specimen descendant is deliberately excluded by name:

- *45766302 / 703431007 — Venous cord blood specimen*: cord blood is physiologically distinct from post-natal venous blood.

## Mapping Notes

- **Default mapping** when the source data records a sample drawn from a peripheral or central vein: `4045667 / 122555007 — Venous blood specimen`.
- **Source explicitly records a pulmonary artery catheter / Swan-Ganz sample**: map to `4001226 / 119298005 — Mixed venous blood specimen`.
- **Source records umbilical / cord sampling**: do **not** map. Out of scope.
- **Source records an arterial sample**: use "Arterial blood specimen" instead.

en.name: Whole blood specimen
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Whole blood specimen is a blood sample that has not been separated into its components (plasma, serum, cells). It is the source from which plasma and serum are derived, and is itself used directly for several assays — blood gas analysis, point-of-care glucose, lactate, haemoglobin (CO-oximetry), haematology (CBC), and molecular tests. The choice of anticoagulant in the collection tube influences which downstream tests can be performed: EDTA for haematology, lithium heparin for plasma chemistry on certain analysers, sodium fluoride / potassium oxalate for glucose preservation, citrate for coagulation studies.

**OMOP CDM usage.** This concept set targets the `SPECIMEN.specimen_concept_id` field. See the [Mapping Recommendations](#/mapping-recommendations) — *Lab Mapping → Specimen* section for how MEASUREMENT and SPECIMEN are linked in CDM v5.4.

**Note: anticoagulant variants.** The SNOMED hierarchy under `Whole blood specimen` distinguishes the anticoagulant present in the collection tube. The current set captures all of them via the descendant relationship.

## Included Concepts

The set is anchored on the SNOMED Specimen concept `Whole blood specimen`, expanded to include all its descendants. The set resolves to eight specimens:

- *4122283 / 258580003 — Whole blood specimen (SNOMED)*: parent / unspecified anticoagulant.
- *37155361 / 57921000052103 — Whole blood specimen with edetic acid (SNOMED)*: EDTA tube.
- *44808076 / 838971000000104 — Whole blood specimen with heparin (SNOMED)*
- *1447858 / 1351815005 — Whole blood specimen with lithium heparin (SNOMED)*
- *1447859 / 1351816006 — Whole blood specimen with citrate (SNOMED)*
- *44808077 / 838981000000102 — Whole blood specimen with fluoride oxalate (SNOMED)*
- *1447857 / 1351813003 — Whole blood specimen with hirudin (SNOMED)*
- *44808078 / 838991000000100 — Whole blood specimen with perchlorate (SNOMED)*

## Excluded Concepts

No concepts are explicitly excluded by name. The set deliberately omits:

- **Plasma / Serum specimens**: these are processed derivatives of whole blood, covered by their own SNOMED concepts.
- **Cord, fetal blood specimens**: physiologically distinct from post-natal blood.
- **Dried blood spot (DBS), blood culture bottles, smears**: out of scope for routine clinical biology.

## Mapping Notes

- **Default mapping** when the source data records a whole-blood sample without specifying the anticoagulant: `4122283 / 258580003 — Whole blood specimen`.
- **Source specifies an EDTA / heparin / citrate / fluoride / lithium heparin / hirudin tube**: map to the matching `... with X` LOINC code.
- **Source records plasma or serum (i.e. the sample has been centrifuged)**: do **not** map. Use the dedicated plasma or serum concept set.
- **Do not confuse with**: `Peripheral blood specimen` (anatomical site), `Plasma specimen` and `Serum specimen` (processed derivatives).

en.name: Coagulation factor V activity
en.shortDescription: Functional clotting activity of factor V ; distinct from factor V antigen (immunological quantity)
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Coagulation factor V is a clotting protein synthesised mainly by the liver [1]. Its **activity** — what this concept set measures — reflects the functional capacity of the protein in the clotting cascade [1]. The result is a single numeric value per patient-timestamp, produced by a coagulation analyser on platelet-poor plasma using a one-stage clot-based assay [1, 2]. Results are reported as a percentage of normal plasma activity — the representation this concept set covers. A separate LOINC code expresses the same assay as a concentration in IU/mL; it is excluded here because that unit is not convertible to a percentage [3]. **Note: activity vs antigen.** This concept set covers **functional activity** only — what the factor V protein actually does in the clotting cascade. The antigenic concentration of factor V (immunological measurement of protein mass irrespective of activity) is captured by a separate concept set, "Coagulation factor V antigen". The two values can diverge in qualitative deficits where antigen is normal but activity is reduced — they are different study variables and must not be merged. ## Included Concepts The set contains a single LOINC "Lab Test" concept, measuring functional factor V activity in platelet-poor plasma by clot-based coagulation assay: - *3005757 / 3193-0 — Coagulation factor V activity actual/normal in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay (LOINC)*: result expressed as a **percentage** of pooled normal plasma activity (e.g. 75 %). This is the representation returned by routine coagulation analysers. **Note on units.** The recommended unit is **`%`** (OMOP concept 8554 — percent), the proportion of pooled normal plasma activity. Sources reporting factor V activity in `U/mL` or `IU/mL` are measuring the concentration variant excluded from this set — see *Excluded Concepts* below. ## Excluded Concepts One concept is explicitly excluded by name (see the note on units below). The following LOINC concepts that exist for factor V are also not part of this set: - **Factor V antigen** (`3027396 / 3194-8 — Coagulation factor V Ag [Units/volume]`, `3023945 / 3195-5 — Coagulation factor V Ag actual/normal`): captured by the separate concept set "Coagulation factor V antigen". - **Factor V activated, expressed as a concentration** (`3006924 / 3192-2 — Coagulation factor V activated [Units/volume] in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay`): excluded — see the note below. The activated form measured here is the assay readout, not factor Va in vivo. - **Factor V inhibitor** (`3004057 / 3191-4 — Coagulation factor V inhibitor [Units/volume]`, `21494686 / 81124-0 — Coagulation factor V inhibitor [Presence]`): out of scope; describes acquired antibodies against factor V (rare bleeding disorder), not the factor V activity itself. - **Factor V activity and inhibitor panel** (`36031832 / 96458-5 — Coagulation factor V activity and inhibitor panel - Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay`): a panel grouping concept, not a measurement result. - **Factor V Leiden mutation** (a separate genetic test): not a coagulation measurement; out of scope. **Note on excluded units.** Concept 3006924 / 3192-2 — Coagulation factor V activated [Units/volume] in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay (LOINC) is excluded from this set. It reports an *activity concentration* in arbitrary units (`[arb'U]/mL`) rather than a proportion of normal plasma, and the two are not interchangeable: UCUM defines arbitrary units as non-dimensional and non-convertible, while IUPAC/IFCC call the same thing a *procedure-defined unit* — a unit whose reference is set by the individual laboratory or measuring device. No conversion factor to `%` can therefore be stated with confidence. In practice laboratories report factor V as a percentage of normal (typically 50–200 % in adults [2]), and no published source documents reference values in `[arb'U]/mL`. Should a data provider actually report this concept, it warrants its own concept set rather than being merged here. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports "factor V", "FV", "facteur V" or "factor V activity" without further specification, with the value expressed as a percentage of normal: `3005757 / 3193-0 — Coagulation factor V activity actual/normal in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay`. By far the most common LOINC code. - **Source reports IU/mL or U/mL**: do **not** map here. That representation corresponds to `3006924 / 3192-2 — Coagulation factor V activated [Units/volume] in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay`, which is excluded from this set because its arbitrary unit cannot be converted to a percentage of normal. - **Do not confuse with**: factor V antigen (different concept set), factor V Leiden genotype (genetic test, not coagulation), factor V inhibitor (autoantibody titer), factor V deficient plasma reagent (laboratory reagent, not a patient measurement). - **Method preservation**: when the source records the assay method (one-stage clot vs chromogenic, deficient plasma reagent supplier, etc.), preserve it in the measurement source value — it does not change the target concept. ## References [1] Mann KG, Kalafatis M. Factor V: a combination of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde. *Blood*. 2003;101(1):20-30. Available: https://doi.org/10.1182/blood-2002-01-0290 [2] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 3193-0 — Coagulation factor V activity actual/normal in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay (Part description for "Coagulation factor V activity"). Available: https://loinc.org/3193-0/ [3] Nomenclature for Properties and Units (NPU). IFCC/IUPAC. NPU codes (current release). Available: https://npu-terminology.org/npu-database/

en.name: Fibrin D-dimer in blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Fibrin D-dimer is a degradation product of cross-linked fibrin, formed by the sequential action of three enzymes — thrombin, factor XIIIa, and plasmin — and is a specific marker of fibrin formation and fibrinolysis [1]. The main clinical use is the exclusion of venous thromboembolism (VTE): a normal D-dimer in a patient with a low or intermediate clinical pretest probability has a high negative predictive value and rules out VTE without imaging [1, 2]. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by an immunoassay on platelet-poor plasma or, for some point-of-care devices, whole blood. **Note on units — D-dimer units (DDU) vs fibrinogen-equivalent units (FEU).** D-dimer can be reported in two distinct unit systems — **DDU** (mass of the D-dimer fragment) and **FEU** (mass expressed as the parent fibrinogen molecule) — and **the two are not numerically equivalent**. Conversion between systems is assay-dependent and not standardised across manufacturers [3]. The same patient sample run on a DDU-reporting assay vs. an FEU-reporting assay will yield different numerical values. **Always preserve the unit (DDU or FEU) when mapping** — never strip or convert silently. The LOINC code itself encodes which unit system is used (suffix `.DDU` vs `.FEU` in the LOINC long name). ## Included Concepts The set is built around two LOINC Hierarchy concepts, each expanded to include all their descendants. Together they pull in nine LOINC "Lab Test" concepts covering quantitative D-dimer measurements in platelet poor plasma (PPP) and in whole blood. **Platelet poor plasma**, anchored on *37072890 / LP394010-5 — Fibrin D-dimer | Platelet poor plasma | Coagulation*: - *3051714 / 48065-7 — Fibrin D-dimer FEU [Mass/volume] in Platelet poor plasma*: most widely used FEU code worldwide; default for FEU sources that do not specify the assay method. - *3052648 / 48067-3 — Fibrin D-dimer [Mass/volume] in Platelet poor plasma by Immunoassay.FEU*: same quantity as `48065-7`, with the immunoassay method explicit. - *3048530 / 48066-5 — Fibrin D-dimer DDU [Mass/volume] in Platelet poor plasma*: default for DDU sources that do not specify the assay method. - *3052716 / 48058-2 — Fibrin D-dimer [Mass/volume] in Platelet poor plasma by Immunoassay.DDU*: same quantity as `48066-5`, with the immunoassay method explicit. **Whole blood** (point-of-care assays), anchored on *1470777 / LP443381-1 — Fibrin D-dimer | Blood | Coagulation*: - *42870366 / 71427-9 — Fibrin D-dimer [Mass/volume] in Blood by Rapid immunoassay*: most common LOINC code for whole-blood point-of-care D-dimer devices. - *37021210 / 91556-1 — Fibrin D-dimer [Mass/volume] in Blood by Immunoassay.DDU*: whole-blood D-dimer reported in DDU. **Note on units.** D-dimer is reported on **two different scales that are not interchangeable**: *D-dimer units* (DDU), the mass of the D-dimer itself, and *fibrinogen-equivalent units* (FEU), the mass referred to the fibrinogen it derives from. **1 FEU = 2 DDU**, so a value read on the wrong scale is off by a factor of two — enough to move a result across a pulmonary-embolism rule-out threshold. LOINC documents the distinction in a dedicated technical brief, and the ISTH has never succeeded in standardising the two. The recommended units therefore differ by concept: **`ug/L`** (OMOP concept 8748) for the DDU codes, and **`mg{FEU}/L`** (OMOP concept 44777663) for the FEU codes. LOINC writes the DDU unit `ug/L{DDU}`, which has no OMOP concept — the annotation carries no dimension, so plain `ug/L` is used, the scale being carried by the concept itself. A conversion is provided between the two (`mg{FEU}/L` → `ug/L` = ×500, i.e. ×1000 for mg→ug then ÷2 for FEU→DDU), but **prefer keeping the source scale and the matching LOINC code** over converting: assays are calibrated against manufacturer-specific standards and a converted value is not equivalent to one measured on that scale. Source systems may report `mg/L`, `ug/mL`, `mg/L FEU`, `ng/mL DDU`, etc. — the unit string and the LOINC code together unambiguously specify the result. Conversion between DDU and FEU is assay-dependent [3]; do not assume a fixed factor without consulting the assay package insert. ## Excluded Concepts The two hierarchy anchors above also pull in three qualitative LOINC concepts that are explicitly excluded: - *3015823 / 15179-5 — Fibrin D-dimer [Presence] in Platelet poor plasma*: qualitative result (present / absent), not a quantitative measurement. Cannot be merged with numerical mg/L values. - *3033464 / 29280-5 — Fibrin D-dimer [Presence] in Platelet poor plasma by Latex agglutination*: same as above, with a method specification. - *3038383 / 38898-3 — Fibrin D-dimer [Titer] in Platelet poor plasma*: titer (e.g. 1:8, 1:16) is a dilution-based result of historical assays — different unit system, different statistical handling. The set also deliberately omits the following LOINC concepts that exist for D-dimer: - **Cerebrospinal fluid** specimens (e.g. `40777694 / LP52466-7 — Fibrin D-dimer | Cerebral spinal fluid`): out of scope for a "blood" concept set. - **Panel concepts** (e.g. `37032186 / LP394459-4 — Short Fibrin D-dimer FEU and DDU panel`): grouping concepts, not measurement results. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports "D-dimer", "DDi", "DD", "D-dimères" without further specification, on platelet-poor plasma, in **mg/L FEU** or **ng/mL FEU** (the most common reporting convention worldwide): `3051714 / 48065-7 — Fibrin D-dimer FEU [Mass/volume] in Platelet poor plasma`. - **Source reports DDU**: map to `3048530 / 48066-5 — Fibrin D-dimer DDU [Mass/volume] in Platelet poor plasma` (or `3052716 / 48058-2 — Fibrin D-dimer [Mass/volume] in Platelet poor plasma by Immunoassay.DDU` if the source explicitly mentions immunoassay method). - **Source uses a whole-blood point-of-care assay** (Cardiac Reader, Triage, etc.): map to `42870366 / 71427-9 — Fibrin D-dimer [Mass/volume] in Blood by Rapid immunoassay`. - **DDU vs FEU disambiguation**: when the source unit string is ambiguous (e.g. just `mg/L` without DDU/FEU annotation), check the assay manufacturer documentation. - **Do not convert units silently**: if a source reports DDU and the recommended unit in the data dictionary is FEU (or vice-versa), preserve the original value and unit; conversion is assay-dependent. - **Do not confuse with**: fibrinogen degradation products (FDP — broader pool of fibrin/fibrinogen breakdown products, different LOINC concepts), soluble fibrin monomer (different marker), or thrombin-antithrombin complex. ## References [1] Adam SS, Key NS, Greenberg CS. D-dimer antigen: current concepts and future prospects. *Blood*. 2009;113(13):2878-87. Available: https://doi.org/10.1182/blood-2008-06-165845 [2] Konstantinides SV, Meyer G, Becattini C, et al. 2019 ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of acute pulmonary embolism. *Eur Heart J*. 2020;41(4):543-603. Available: https://doi.org/10.1093/eurheartj/ehz405 [3] Longstaff C, Adcock D, Olson JD, et al. Harmonisation of D-dimer — A call for action. *Thromb Res*. 2016;137:219-220. Available: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.thromres.2015.11.031

en.name: Fibrinogen in blood
en.shortDescription: Functional (clottable) fibrinogen, Clauss method ; distinct from fibrinogen antigen (immunoassay)
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Fibrinogen is a clotting protein that is the substrate of thrombin in the final step of coagulation: thrombin cleaves fibrinogen into fibrin monomers, which polymerise and are then cross-linked by activated factor XIII (XIIIa) to form a stable clot [1]. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced on platelet poor plasma (PPP) by a clot-based coagulation assay or, on whole blood, by a viscoelastic test [2]. Results are reported as a mass concentration in g/L or mg/dL [3]. Clinically, fibrinogen is part of the standard coagulation monitoring in trauma resuscitation, alongside the prothrombin time and platelet count [2]. **Note: "fibrinogen" vs "fibrinogen antigen".** This concept set covers **fibrinogen measured by clot-based or viscoelastic assays** — these assays only detect fibrinogen that is functionally able to be clotted by thrombin. The antigenic concentration of fibrinogen (immunoassay measurement of protein mass, irrespective of clottability) is captured by a separate concept set, "Fibrinogen antigen". The two values can diverge in dysfibrinogenaemia, where antigen is normal but the clot-based result is reduced — they are different study variables and must not be merged. ## Included Concepts The set is built around two LOINC Hierarchy concepts, each expanded to include all their descendants. After applying the exclusions below, the set resolves to four LOINC "Lab Test" concepts. **Platelet poor plasma**, anchored on *37032427 / LP394019-6 — Fibrinogen | Platelet poor plasma | Coagulation*: - *3016407 / 3255-7 — Fibrinogen [Mass/volume] in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay*: the **Clauss method** — the reference clinical assay [2]. Most widely used LOINC code worldwide for routine fibrinogen measurement. - *3052964 / 48664-7 — Fibrinogen [Mass/volume] in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation.derived*: **PT-derived fibrinogen** — fibrinogen estimated indirectly from the optical density change during the prothrombin time test. Some labs report it as a screening proxy. - *3018928 / 30902-1 — Fibrinogen [Mass/volume] in Platelet poor plasma by Heat denaturation*: historical method (heat precipitation), rarely used today; preserved for legacy datasets. **Whole blood**, anchored on *1618662 / LP422984-7 — Fibrinogen | Blood | Coagulation*: - *1616312 / 97016-0 — Fibrinogen [Mass/volume] in Blood by calculation*: fibrinogen estimated from a whole-blood viscoelastic test (FIBTEM in ROTEM, FF in TEG); used in trauma and cardiac-surgery resuscitation when a rapid bedside estimate is needed [2]. **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS`: **`g/L`** (concept 8636) for all four codes. Source systems may report `g/L`, `mg/dL`, or `mg/L`. Conversions: `1 g/L = 100 mg/dL = 1000 mg/L`. ## Excluded Concepts The two hierarchy anchors above also pull in five LOINC concepts that are explicitly excluded: - *3002937 / 16859-1 — Fibrinogen [Presence] in Platelet poor plasma*: qualitative result, not a quantitative measurement. - *3008766 / 21002-1 — Fibrinogen [Interpretation] in Platelet poor plasma*: text interpretation, not a numerical result. - *3026131 / 31158-9 — Fibrinogen Ag/Fibrinogen [Mass Ratio] in Platelet poor plasma*: derived ratio, not a fibrinogen concentration. - *3016628 / 3256-5 — Fibrinogen Ag [Mass/volume] in Platelet poor plasma by Immunoassay*: antigenic concentration — captured by the separate concept set "Fibrinogen antigen". - *3037950 / 42772-4 — Fibrinogen Ag [Mass/volume] in Platelet poor plasma by Nephelometry*: same as above, with a method specification — also captured by "Fibrinogen antigen". The set also deliberately omits the following LOINC concepts that exist for fibrinogen: - **Fibrinogen fragments** (degradation products) and **Fibrin+Fibrinogen fragments** (FDP): different measurands, captured by D-dimer or FDP concept sets when relevant. - **Cryofibrinogen**: a different assay measuring cold-precipitable fibrinogen — different clinical context (cryofibrinogenaemia workup). - **Tissue, Smears, and Urine** specimens: out of scope. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports "fibrinogen", "Fg", "FGN", "fibrinogène" without further specification, on platelet poor plasma: `3016407 / 3255-7 — Fibrinogen [Mass/volume] in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay` (Clauss method). By far the most common LOINC code. - **PT-derived fibrinogen**: if the source explicitly states "PT-derived", "fibrinogen derived", or reports the value alongside the PT result without a separate Clauss measurement, map to `3052964 / 48664-7 — Fibrinogen [Mass/volume] in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation.derived`. - **Viscoelastic-derived fibrinogen** (FIBTEM in ROTEM, FF in TEG): map to `1616312 / 97016-0 — Fibrinogen [Mass/volume] in Blood by calculation`. Note: viscoelastic devices report fibrinogen-equivalent values that correlate with but do not numerically equal the Clauss result. - **Do not confuse with**: fibrinogen antigen (separate concept set), fibrin degradation products (FDP), D-dimer, fibrin monomer, cryofibrinogen, factor XIII activity. ## References [1] Mosesson MW. Fibrinogen and fibrin structure and functions. *J Thromb Haemost*. 2005;3(8):1894-904. Available: https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1538-7836.2005.01365.x [2] Spahn DR, Bouillon B, Cerny V, et al. The European guideline on management of major bleeding and coagulopathy following trauma: fifth edition. *Crit Care*. 2019;23(1):98. Available: https://doi.org/10.1186/s13054-019-2347-3 [3] Nomenclature for Properties and Units (NPU). IFCC/IUPAC. NPU codes (current release). Available: https://npu-terminology.org/npu-database/

en.name: INR in blood
en.shortDescription: Standardised ratio derived from prothrombin time ; comparable across laboratories
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context The International Normalized Ratio (INR) is a standardised, dimensionless transformation of the prothrombin time (PT) [1]. By construction, it is independent of the thromboplastin reagent used by the laboratory, which makes INR values comparable across labs — unlike PT in seconds. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a coagulation analyser on platelet poor plasma (PPP), or by a point-of-care device on capillary fingerstick blood. Results are reported as a dimensionless ratio (e.g. 2.4) [2]. **Note: relationship with PT.** The INR is derived from the PT but is *not* the same measurement. PT is reported in seconds and depends on the laboratory's reagent; INR is reported as a dimensionless ratio and is reagent-independent by construction. The data dictionary keeps them as separate concept sets ("Prothrombin time" and this set). ## Included Concepts The set is built around four LOINC Hierarchy concepts, each expanded to include all their descendants. Together they pull in five LOINC "Lab Test" concepts covering INR measurements across all relevant specimens. **Platelet poor plasma**, anchored on *37057823 / LP394061-8 — INR | Platelet poor plasma | Coagulation*: - *3022217 / 6301-6 — INR in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay*: the standard hospital lab measurement. Most widely used LOINC code worldwide. - *3039326 / 52129-4 — INR in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay --post heparin neutralization*: same numerical interpretation as the standard INR; produced when a heparinised sample is treated with polybrene/heparinase before measurement. **Whole blood**, anchored on *37074906 / LP394058-4 — INR | Blood | Coagulation*: - *3032080 / 34714-6 — INR in Blood by Coagulation assay*: INR measured on whole blood (non-capillary). **Capillary blood (point-of-care)**, anchored on *37042344 / LP394059-2 — INR | Blood capillary | Coagulation*: - *3051593 / 46418-0 — INR in Capillary blood by Coagulation assay*: point-of-care fingerstick INR (CoaguChek and others), used for vitamin K antagonist (VKA) self-monitoring. **Specimen-agnostic**, anchored on *37072728 / LP394062-6 — INR | Platelet poor plasma or blood | Coagulation*: - *3042605 / 38875-1 — INR in Platelet poor plasma or blood by Coagulation assay*: used when the source aggregates results without a specimen tag. **Note on units.** The INR is dimensionless by construction. LOINC lists `{INR}` as its example UCUM unit — an annotation-only marker carrying no dimension — but the OMOP vocabulary has no concept for `{INR}`, so the recommended unit used here is the generic **`{ratio}`** (OMOP concept 8523), already used elsewhere in this dictionary for dimensionless ratios. Source systems variously report no unit at all, `1`, `{INR}` or `INR`: all denote the same dimensionless quantity and none requires a numeric conversion. Concept 3051593 (INR in capillary blood) carries no `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS` in LOINC but is given the same unit, since it measures the same quantity as the other INR concepts. ## Excluded Concepts No concepts are explicitly excluded by name. The following LOINC concepts that exist for INR-related quantities are deliberately not part of this set: - **INR goal** (`37071262 / LP407479-7 — INR goal | Platelet poor plasma | Coagulation`): the *target* INR for a patient under VKA therapy, not a measurement of the actual INR. - **Reverse INR** (`40774777 / LP64562-9 — reverse INR | Platelet poor plasma`): a reciprocal-scale derivative used in some research contexts, not the routine INR. - **Fetus** specimens (e.g. `37035036 / LP394064-2 — INR | Fetus | Coagulation`): out of scope for routine adult/paediatric care. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports "INR", "International Normalized Ratio", "ratio normalisé international" without further specification: `3022217 / 6301-6 — INR in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay`. By far the most common LOINC code (routine hospital lab on citrated plasma). - **Point-of-care INR** (CoaguChek, fingerstick): map to `3051593 / 46418-0 — INR in Capillary blood by Coagulation assay`. - **Specimen unspecified**: map to `3042605 / 38875-1 — INR in Platelet poor plasma or blood by Coagulation assay`. - **Whole blood** (non-capillary): map to `3032080 / 34714-6 — INR in Blood by Coagulation assay`. - **Heparinised sample treated for INR measurement**: map to `3039326 / 52129-4 — INR in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay --post heparin neutralization`. The result is equivalent to a standard INR. - **Do not confuse with**: prothrombin time in seconds (separate concept set), or the French "TP" (taux de prothrombine), reported in % — TP is a different transformation of the PT and must never be mapped to INR. ## References [1] World Health Organization. Guidelines for thromboplastins and plasma used to control oral anticoagulant therapy. WHO Technical Report Series, No. 889, Annex 3, 1999. Available: https://www.who.int/publications/m/item/who-trs-889-annex-3 [2] Nomenclature for Properties and Units (NPU). IFCC/IUPAC. NPU codes (current release). Available: https://npu-terminology.org/npu-database/

en.name: Prothrombin time in blood
en.shortDescription: Raw clotting time (seconds) from which the INR is computed
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context The prothrombin time (PT) measures the time, in seconds, required for plasma to form a clot after addition of thromboplastin and calcium [1]. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a coagulation analyser on platelet poor plasma (PPP), or by a point-of-care device on capillary fingerstick blood. Results are reported in seconds [2]. **Note: PT vs INR vs prothrombin ratio.** The PT (this concept set), the INR, and the prothrombin ratio are three different representations of the same underlying physical measurement, with different normalisations: - **PT (seconds)** — raw measurement; depends on the laboratory's thromboplastin reagent. - **INR** — dimensionless, reagent-independent transformation. Used for vitamin K antagonist (VKA) monitoring. Captured by a separate concept set, "INR in blood". - **Prothrombin ratio** — percentage of pooled normal plasma activity. Captured by a separate concept set, "Prothrombin ratio in blood". The three representations are **not interconvertible** without the laboratory's local calibration curve. The data dictionary keeps them addressable independently — analyses needing a homogeneous variable should pick one representation rather than merging across. ## Included Concepts The set is built around three LOINC Hierarchy concepts, each expanded to include all their descendants. After applying the exclusions below, the set resolves to four LOINC "Lab Test" concepts. **Platelet poor plasma**, anchored on *37041470 / LP394044-4 — Prothrombin time (PT) | Platelet poor plasma | Coagulation*: - *3034426 / 5902-2 — Prothrombin time (PT)*: generic PT concept used when the LOINC code in the source does not specify the specimen — a "wildcard" for systems that do not differentiate. en.name: aPTT in blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context The activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) measures the time, in seconds, required for plasma to form a clot after addition of an activator, a phospholipid emulsion, and calcium [1]. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a coagulation analyser on platelet poor plasma (PPP). Results are reported in seconds [2]. **Note: aPTT vs aPTT ratio.** The aPTT (this concept set) and the aPTT ratio are two different representations of the same underlying physical measurement, with different normalisations: - **aPTT (seconds)** — raw measurement; depends on the laboratory's reagent. - **aPTT ratio** — patient time divided by the laboratory's normal control time. Captured by a separate concept set, "aPTT ratio in blood". The two representations are **not interconvertible** without the laboratory's local normal control. The data dictionary keeps them addressable independently — analyses needing a homogeneous variable should pick one representation rather than merging across. ## Included Concepts The set is built around two LOINC Hierarchy concepts, each expanded to include all their descendants. After applying the exclusions below, the set resolves to three LOINC "Lab Test" concepts. **Platelet poor plasma**, anchored on *37041593 / LP393946-1 — aPTT | Platelet poor plasma | Coagulation*: - *3018677 / 14979-9 — aPTT in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay*: the standard hospital lab measurement. Most widely used LOINC code worldwide. - *3041232 / 52123-7 — aPTT in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay --post heparin neutralization*: clinically equivalent to a standard aPTT — produced when a heparinised sample is treated with polybrene/heparinase before measurement. **Whole blood**, anchored on *37037324 / LP393943-8 — aPTT | Blood | Coagulation*: - *3013466 / 3173-2 — aPTT in Blood by Coagulation assay*: aPTT measured on whole blood (rare; some point-of-care devices). Not to be confused with the activated clotting time (ACT), which is a distinct point-of-care test. **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS`: **`s`** (concept 8555 — second) for all three codes. Source systems may report aPTT in `s` or `sec`; conversion is identity. ## Excluded Concepts The two hierarchy anchors above pull in 22 LOINC concepts that are explicitly excluded: **aPTT ratio**: - *40766287 / 63561-5 — aPTT actual/normal in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay*: dimensionless ratio (patient/normal control). Captured by the separate concept set "aPTT ratio in blood". **Sequential specimen series (3 codes)** — successive aPTT measurements on a series of timed specimens during a thrombolysis or anticoagulation protocol (research/protocol context): - *3040743 / 40108-3* — aPTT in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay --8 hours post XXX challenge - *3042449 / 40109-1* — aPTT in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay --12 hours post XXX challenge - *3038668 / 40110-9* — aPTT in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay --1 day post XXX challenge - *3042634 / 40111-7* — aPTT in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay --18 hours post XXX challenge **1:1 saline mixing studies (2 codes)** — patient plasma diluted 1:1 with saline to investigate the cause of a prolonged aPTT: - en.name: Alkaline phosphatase (ALP) in blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Alkaline phosphatase (ALP) is a hydrolase enzyme that catalyses the removal of phosphate groups from various molecules. It is present throughout body tissues but is concentrated in the liver, bile ducts, kidney, bone, and placenta [1]. Elevated activity in blood is most often seen in cholestatic liver disease (bile duct obstruction) and in conditions with increased bone turnover (growth in children, Paget's disease, bone metastases); it is also physiologically increased in pregnancy [1]. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a biochemistry analyser on serum or plasma. It is collected in routine biochemistry as part of a liver panel. Results are reported as catalytic activity concentration; NPU recognises both **U/L** (the conventional unit, used by virtually all clinical labs) and **µkat/L** (the SI unit) [2]. The IFCC reference measurement procedure for alkaline phosphatase at 37 °C, listed by JCTLM, gives the conversion factor `1 U/L = 0.01667 µkat/L` [3]. **Note on isoenzymes.** ALP exists as several tissue-specific isoenzymes (liver, bone, intestinal, placental). This concept set covers the **total** ALP activity assayed in routine biochemistry — not the individual isoenzymes, which have their own LOINC concepts and are out of scope. ## Included Concepts The set contains three LOINC "Lab Test" concepts, all measuring total alkaline phosphatase catalytic activity in blood, differing only by specimen specification. - *3035995 / 6768-6 — Alkaline phosphatase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: the most widely used LOINC code for ALP, returned by routine biochemistry analysers. - *3001110 / 1783-0 — Alkaline phosphatase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Blood (LOINC)*: used when the source reports ALP on whole blood without specifying serum/plasma. - *46235077 / 77141-0 — Alkaline phosphatase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum, Plasma or Blood (LOINC)*: generic concept used when the matrix is not differentiated between serum/plasma and whole blood (e.g. aggregated multi-source feeds). **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows LOINC: **`[U]/L`** (concept 8645). The notations `U/L` and `IU/L` are used interchangeably in clinical practice and represent the same value mathematically — no conversion is needed between them. ## Excluded Concepts No concepts are explicitly excluded. The set is defined by anchoring on the LOINC group for total alkaline phosphatase catalytic activity in blood/serum/plasma and pulling in all its descendants. This naturally excludes: - **ALP isoenzymes**: liver-, bone-, intestinal-, placental-, renal-, regan-specific concepts (e.g. `1779-8 — Alkaline phosphatase.liver`, `1777-2 — Alkaline phosphatase.bone`). These are separate measurands. - **Isoenzyme ratios** like `Alkaline phosphatase.liver/Alkaline phosphatase.total` (`15015-1`) — out of scope. - **Heat stability tests** (`32351-9`, `32352-7`) — historical method-specific tests. - **Other specimens** such as cord blood (`55971-6`), body fluids, urine, dialysis fluid — out of scope for a "blood" concept set. - **Macromolecular ALP** (`100737-6`) — qualitative test for macro-ALP complexes. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports "ALP", "alkaline phosphatase", "PAL" or similar without further specification (typical of routine biochemistry analysers): `3035995 / 6768-6 — Alkaline phosphatase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum or Plasma`. By far the most common specimen for this assay. - **Whole blood without matrix tag**: if the source explicitly says "blood" (not serum/plasma), map to `3001110 / 1783-0 — Alkaline phosphatase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Blood`. If the source aggregates results from both biochemistry and other workflows without a matrix tag, use `46235077 / 77141-0 — Alkaline phosphatase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum, Plasma or Blood` as a generic fallback. - **Do not confuse with**: ALP isoenzymes (liver, bone, intestinal, etc.), isoenzyme ratios, or ALP in non-blood specimens — all belong to other concept sets. - **Method is not part of the mapping target**: when the source records the assay method (kinetic colorimetric, IFCC reference at 37 °C, etc.), preserve it in the measurement source value — it does not change the target concept. - **Unit naming**: source systems may report `U/L` or `IU/L`. Both correspond to the same physical quantity. Map them all to the recommended unit `[U]/L` (concept 8645). Values reported in `µkat/L` should be converted using `1 U/L = 0.01667 µkat/L` (i.e. multiply µkat/L by ~60 to get U/L) [3]. ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 6768-6 — Alkaline phosphatase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum or Plasma (Part description for "Alkaline phosphatase"). Available: https://loinc.org/6768-6/ [2] Nomenclature for Properties and Units (NPU). IFCC/IUPAC. NPU codes (current release). Available: https://npu-terminology.org/npu-database/ [3] Joint Committee for Traceability in Laboratory Medicine (JCTLM). Database of higher-order reference measurement procedures, reference materials and reference measurement services. BIPM/IFCC/ILAC. Available: https://www.jctlmdb.org/#/app/home

en.name: Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) in blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Alanine aminotransferase (ALT, also called SGPT — serum glutamic pyruvic transaminase) is an enzyme produced primarily in the liver, with smaller amounts in the heart, skeletal muscle, kidney and pancreas [1]. When hepatocytes are damaged, ALT leaks into the bloodstream and its serum activity rises — making it the most specific routine marker of hepatocellular injury (viral hepatitis, drug-induced liver injury, ischaemic hepatitis, etc.) [1]. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a biochemistry analyser on serum or plasma. It is collected in routine biochemistry as part of every liver panel. Results are reported as catalytic activity concentration; NPU recognises both **U/L** (the conventional unit, used by virtually all clinical labs) and **µkat/L** (the SI unit) [2]. The IFCC reference measurement procedure for ALT at 37 °C, listed by JCTLM, gives the conversion factor `1 U/L = 0.01667 µkat/L` [3]. **Note on assay method (with vs without P-5'-P).** Pyridoxal-5'-phosphate (P-5'-P) is the cofactor of ALT. The IFCC primary reference procedure adds P-5'-P to the reagent to activate the enzyme that is otherwise present as inactive apo-ALT, giving the total ALT activity [4]. Assays run without added P-5'-P measure only the holo-fraction already saturated in the sample, which can underestimate total activity (especially in patients deficient in vitamin B6). Both methods produce results expressed in U/L; values are not strictly interchangeable across the two methods, but LOINC treats them as the same measurand under different method specifications. ## Included Concepts The set contains five LOINC "Lab Test" concepts, all measuring ALT catalytic activity in blood, differing by specimen and by whether P-5'-P is added. ### Generic (method not specified) The default when the source does not state which method is used. - *3006923 / 1742-6 — Alanine aminotransferase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: most widely used LOINC code, returned by routine biochemistry analysers when the method is not detailed. ### Method-specific (with or without P-5'-P) Use these only when the source explicitly identifies the assay method. - *3005755 / 1743-4 — Alanine aminotransferase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum or Plasma by With P-5'-P (LOINC)*: IFCC-recommended method. - *3027388 / 1744-2 — Alanine aminotransferase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum or Plasma by No addition of P-5'-P (LOINC)*: economy method, still common in practice. ### Other specimen specifications - *46235106 / 76625-3 — Alanine aminotransferase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Blood (LOINC)*: used when the source reports ALT on whole blood without specifying serum/plasma. - *46236949 / 77144-4 — Alanine aminotransferase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum, Plasma or Blood (LOINC)*: generic concept used when the matrix is not differentiated between serum/plasma and whole blood (e.g. aggregated multi-source feeds). **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows LOINC: **`[U]/L`** (concept 8645). The notations `U/L` and `IU/L` are used interchangeably in clinical practice. ## Excluded Concepts No concepts are explicitly excluded. The set is defined by anchoring on the LOINC group for ALT catalytic activity in blood/serum/plasma and pulling in all its descendants. This naturally excludes: - **Aggregations** like `Alanine aminotransferase ... (Maximum value during study)` (`44785-4`) — out of scope. - **Non-blood specimens** such as red blood cells (`16324-6`). - **Macromolecular ALT** (`48134-1`, `100738-4`) — qualitative or research test for macro-ALT complexes. - **ALT/AST ratios** (`16325-3`, `1916-6`) — out of scope. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports "ALT", "SGPT", "ALAT" or similar without further specification (most routine biochemistry analysers): `3006923 / 1742-6 — Alanine aminotransferase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum or Plasma`. By far the most common. - **Source explicitly states P-5'-P method**: map to `3005755 / 1743-4 — Alanine aminotransferase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum or Plasma by With P-5'-P` (with P-5'-P) or `3027388 / 1744-2 — Alanine aminotransferase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum or Plasma by No addition of P-5'-P` (without P-5'-P) accordingly. Otherwise, default to `1742-6` — do **not** infer the method from the analyser brand or the country. - **Whole blood without matrix tag**: map to `46235106 / 76625-3 — Alanine aminotransferase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Blood`. If the source aggregates serum/plasma and whole-blood results without a matrix tag, use `46236949 / 77144-4 — Alanine aminotransferase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum, Plasma or Blood` as a generic fallback. - **Do not confuse with**: AST (aspartate aminotransferase, a related but distinct enzyme), ALT/AST ratios, macromolecular ALT, or ALT in non-blood specimens — all belong to other concept sets. - **Method is not part of the mapping target beyond P-5'-P**: when the source records additional method details (kinetic, Tris buffer, etc.), preserve them in the measurement source value — they do not change the target concept. - **Unit naming**: source systems may report `U/L` or `IU/L`. Both correspond to the same physical quantity. Map them all to the recommended unit `[U]/L` (concept 8645). Values reported in `µkat/L` should be converted using `1 U/L = 0.01667 µkat/L` (i.e. multiply µkat/L by ~60 to get U/L) [3]. ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute.
