en.name: Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) in blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Aspartate aminotransferase (AST, also called SGOT — serum glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase) is an enzyme released by injured muscle cells and liver cells, predominantly found in the liver and the heart [1]. AST is part of every liver panel, typically measured together with ALT to assess hepatocellular injury; an AST/ALT ratio above 2 is a classical pattern of alcoholic liver disease, but AST is less liver-specific than ALT (also rises in muscle damage, myocardial infarction, haemolysis) [1]. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a biochemistry analyser on serum or plasma. Results are reported as catalytic activity concentration; NPU recognises both **U/L** (the conventional unit, used by virtually all clinical labs) and **µkat/L** (the SI unit) [2]. The IFCC reference measurement procedure for AST at 37 °C, listed by JCTLM, gives the conversion factor `1 U/L = 0.01667 µkat/L` [3]. **Note on assay method (with vs without P-5'-P).** Pyridoxal-5'-phosphate (P-5'-P) is the cofactor of AST. The IFCC primary reference procedure adds P-5'-P to the reagent to activate the enzyme that is otherwise present as inactive apo-AST, giving the total AST activity [4]. Assays run without added P-5'-P measure only the holo-fraction already saturated in the sample, which can underestimate total activity (especially in patients deficient in vitamin B6). Both methods produce results expressed in U/L; values are not strictly interchangeable across the two methods, but LOINC treats them as the same measurand under different method specifications. ## Included Concepts The set contains three LOINC "Lab Test" concepts, all measuring AST catalytic activity in serum or plasma, differing only by whether P-5'-P is added. ### Generic (method not specified) The default when the source does not state which method is used. - *3013721 / 1920-8 — Aspartate aminotransferase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: most widely used LOINC code, returned by routine biochemistry analysers when the method is not detailed. ### Method-specific (with or without P-5'-P) Use these only when the source explicitly identifies the assay method. - *3037081 / 30239-8 — Aspartate aminotransferase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum or Plasma by With P-5'-P (LOINC)*: IFCC-recommended method. - *36305398 / 88112-8 — Aspartate aminotransferase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum or Plasma by No addition of P-5'-P (LOINC)*: economy method, still common in practice. **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows LOINC: **`[U]/L`** (concept 8645). The notations `U/L` and `IU/L` are used interchangeably in clinical practice. ## Excluded Concepts No concepts are explicitly excluded. The set is defined by anchoring on the LOINC group for AST catalytic activity in blood/serum/plasma and pulling in all its descendants. This naturally excludes: - **Aggregations** like `Aspartate aminotransferase ... (Maximum value during study)` (`44786-2`) — out of scope. - **Non-blood specimens** such as red blood cells (`16412-9`). - **Macromolecular AST** (`48136-6`, `100739-2`, `54500-4`) — qualitative or research test for macro-AST complexes. - **Presence-only test** (`27344-1`) — qualitative, not a quantitative activity measurement. - **Ratios** such as AST/ALT (`1916-6`), ALT/AST (`16325-3`), GGT/AST (`2325-9`) — out of scope. Notably, no LOINC concepts exist for `AST in Blood` or `AST in Serum, Plasma or Blood` (unlike ALT and ALP), because AST is essentially never reported on whole blood in routine practice. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports "AST", "SGOT", "ASAT" or similar without further specification (most routine biochemistry analysers): `3013721 / 1920-8 — Aspartate aminotransferase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum or Plasma`. By far the most common. - **Source explicitly states P-5'-P method**: map to `3037081 / 30239-8 — Aspartate aminotransferase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum or Plasma by With P-5'-P` (with P-5'-P) or `36305398 / 88112-8 — Aspartate aminotransferase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum or Plasma by No addition of P-5'-P` (without P-5'-P) accordingly. Otherwise, default to `1920-8` — do **not** infer the method from the analyser brand or the country. - **Do not confuse with**: ALT (alanine aminotransferase, a related but distinct enzyme), AST/ALT and ALT/AST ratios, macromolecular AST, or AST in non-blood specimens (e.g. red blood cells) — all belong to other concept sets. - **Method is not part of the mapping target beyond P-5'-P**: when the source records additional method details (kinetic, malate dehydrogenase coupling, etc.), preserve them in the measurement source value — they do not change the target concept. - **Unit naming**: source systems may report `U/L` or `IU/L`. Both correspond to the same physical quantity. Map them all to the recommended unit `[U]/L` (concept 8645). Values reported in `µkat/L` should be converted using `1 U/L = 0.01667 µkat/L` (i.e. multiply µkat/L by ~60 to get U/L) [3]. ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 1920-8 — Aspartate aminotransferase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum or Plasma (Part description for "Aspartate aminotransferase"). Available: https://loinc.org/1920-8/ [2] Nomenclature for Properties and Units (NPU). IFCC/IUPAC. NPU codes (current release). Available: https://npu-terminology.org/npu-database/ [3] Joint Committee for Traceability in Laboratory Medicine (JCTLM). Database of higher-order reference measurement procedures, reference materials and reference measurement services. BIPM/IFCC/ILAC. Available: https://www.jctlmdb.org/#/app/home [4] Schumann G, Bonora R, Ceriotti F, Férard G, Ferrero CA, Franck PFH, Gella FJ, Hoelzel W, Jørgensen PJ, Kanno T, Kessner A, Klauke R, Kristiansen N, Lessinger JM, Linsinger TPJ, Misaki H, Panteghini M, Pauwels J, Schiele F, Schimmel HG, Weidemann G, Siekmann L. IFCC primary reference procedures for the measurement of catalytic activity concentrations of enzymes at 37 °C. Part 5. Reference procedure for the measurement of catalytic concentration of aspartate aminotransferase. Clin Chem Lab Med. 2002;40(7):725-733. Available: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12241022/

en.name: Ammonia in blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Ammonia (NH3) is produced in the body as a by-product of amino-acid metabolism and processed in the liver into urea, which is eliminated in the urine [1]. Elevated blood ammonia is toxic to the central nervous system and is most often measured in suspected hepatic encephalopathy (severe liver disease), Reye syndrome, urea-cycle disorders, and other inborn errors of metabolism [1]. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a biochemistry analyser on plasma or whole blood — and increasingly by point-of-care blood-gas devices on arterial blood. Results are reported either in mass units (**µg/dL**) or in SI units (**µmol/L**, the unit recognised by NPU as the standard for substance concentration of ammonia/ammonium [2]). ## Included Concepts The set contains five LOINC "Lab Test" concepts, all measuring ammonia in blood, grouped here by specimen. ### Plasma (default specimen for routine biochemistry) The most common specimen for routine ammonia measurement. EDTA or heparin plasma is preferred over serum because clotting introduces additional ammonia. - *3036887 / 22763-7 — Ammonia [Mass/volume] in Plasma (LOINC)*: reported in µg/dL. - *3011958 / 16362-6 — Ammonia [Moles/volume] in Plasma (LOINC)*: reported in µmol/L. ### Blood (whole blood, unspecified) Used when the source reports ammonia on whole blood without specifying arterial origin — typically a co-oximetry or dedicated blood-gas channel on a point-of-care device. - *3030942 / 32664-5 — Ammonia [Mass/volume] in Blood (LOINC)*: reported in µg/dL. - *3005347 / 1839-0 — Ammonia [Moles/volume] in Blood (LOINC)*: reported in µmol/L. ### Arterial blood Used when the specimen is explicitly an arterial blood sample. Only the SI variant exists in LOINC. - *1002144 / 93684-9 — Ammonia [Moles/volume] in Arterial blood (LOINC)*: reported in µmol/L. **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows the LOINC property: mass-concentration concepts use **µg/dL** (concept 8837), substance-concentration concepts use **µmol/L** (concept 8749). Conversion: 1 µg/dL ≈ 0.587 µmol/L; 1 µmol/L ≈ 1.703 µg/dL (molar mass of NH3 = 17.031 g/mol). ## Excluded Concepts No concepts are explicitly excluded. The set is defined by anchoring on the two LOINC groups for ammonia in blood/serum/plasma (mass concentration and substance concentration) and pulling in all their descendants. This naturally excludes: - **Ammonium ion (NH4+)** concepts (`1844-0`, `1845-7`). LOINC distinguishes these from `Ammonia` even though clinical labs measure them as the same physical quantity. Map ammonia results to the `Ammonia` concepts above; if a source labels the test specifically as "ammonium ion", consider whether a separate concept set is needed. - **Other specimens** such as urine, dialysis fluid, amniotic fluid — out of scope for a "blood" concept set. - **Unrelated panels** like `Gas and ammonia panel - Arterial blood` (`100847-3`) or histidine ammonia lyase activity — out of scope. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports "ammonia", "NH3" or similar without further specification: `3036887 / 22763-7 — Ammonia [Mass/volume] in Plasma` if the value is in µg/dL, `3011958 / 16362-6 — Ammonia [Moles/volume] in Plasma` if the value is in µmol/L. Plasma is the default specimen for routine biochemistry analysers. - **Whole blood (point-of-care)**: if the source explicitly reports "blood ammonia" from a point-of-care device, map to `3030942 / 32664-5 — Ammonia [Mass/volume] in Blood` (mg-equivalent in µg/dL) or `3005347 / 1839-0` (µmol/L). - **Arterial blood** (e.g. blood-gas analyser): map to `1002144 / 93684-9 — Ammonia [Moles/volume] in Arterial blood`. LOINC has no mass-concentration variant for arterial blood, so a source reporting µg/dL still maps here — the µg/dL to µmol/L conversion is registered. - **Do not confuse with**: ammonium ion concepts (`1844-0`, `1845-7`) — these are sematically distinct in LOINC even though clinically equivalent — or ammonia in non-blood specimens. - **Method is not part of the mapping target**: the source lab's measurement method (enzymatic glutamate dehydrogenase, ion-selective electrode, dry chemistry, etc.) can be preserved in the measurement source value but does not change which concept to map to. ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 1839-0 — Ammonia [Moles/volume] in Blood (Part description for "Ammonia"). Available: https://loinc.org/1839-0/ [2] Nomenclature for Properties and Units (NPU). IFCC/IUPAC. NPU codes (current release). Available: https://npu-terminology.org/npu-database/

en.name: Conjugated bilirubin in blood
en.shortDescription: Bilirubin fraction processed by the liver (direct) ; distinct from indirect and total bilirubin
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Bilirubin is an orange-yellow pigment produced by the normal breakdown of heme, a component of the haemoglobin found in red blood cells [1]. **Conjugated (or "direct") bilirubin** is the fraction that has been processed by the liver: glucuronidated bilirubin is water-soluble and ready for excretion in bile, while delta bilirubin is the fraction covalently bound to albumin that accumulates in prolonged cholestasis [1]. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a biochemistry analyser on serum or plasma. It is collected in routine biochemistry as part of a liver panel, especially when investigating jaundice or cholestasis. Results are reported either in mass units (**mg/dL**) or in SI units (**µmol/L**, the unit recognised by NPU as the standard for substance concentration of bilirubin [2]). Both units are in active use in practice; the choice varies by lab and by country. **Important — "conjugated" vs "direct".** In LOINC, two distinct terms coexist: - **"Bilirubin.conjugated"** (LOINC component `Bilirubin.glucuronidated`) — the strictly glucuronidated fraction, typically measured by HPLC (high-performance liquid chromatography). - **"Bilirubin.direct"** (LOINC component `Bilirubin.glucuronidated+Bilirubin.albumin bound`) — the fraction that reacts with diazo reagents without an accelerator. This includes both glucuronidated bilirubin **and delta-bilirubin**. This is the routine assay used in most clinical laboratories and is what is usually reported on a liver panel under "direct bilirubin" or, somewhat loosely, "conjugated bilirubin". Both are included in this concept set because, in real-world data, the two terms are used interchangeably and the clinical interpretation is the same. Downstream analyses that need to distinguish the two (e.g. studies restricted to HPLC measurements) can filter on the specific concept. ## Included Concepts The set contains four LOINC "Lab Test" concepts, all measured in serum or plasma. Each measurand (conjugated and direct) has a mass-concentration variant (mg/dL) and a substance-concentration variant (µmol/L). ### Bilirubin.conjugated (HPLC, strictly glucuronidated) - *3019676 / 15152-2 — Bilirubin.conjugated [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: reported in mg/dL. - *3005772 / 29760-6 — Bilirubin.conjugated [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: reported in µmol/L. ### Bilirubin.direct (diazo reaction, conjugated + delta) - *3027597 / 1968-7 — Bilirubin.direct [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: reported in mg/dL. This is the most widely used LOINC code in routine US laboratory practice. - *3028638 / 14629-0 — Bilirubin.direct [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: reported in µmol/L. The standard SI code used in Europe. **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows the LOINC property: the mass-concentration concepts use **mg/dL** (concept 8840), the substance-concentration concepts use **µmol/L** (concept 8749). Conversion: 1 mg/dL = 17.1 µmol/L; 1 µmol/L = 0.0585 mg/dL (molar mass of bilirubin ≈ 584.66 g/mol). ## Excluded Concepts No concepts are explicitly excluded. The set is defined by anchoring on the two LOINC groups for conjugated bilirubin in serum or plasma (one for the strictly glucuronidated fraction, one for glucuronidated + albumin-bound) and pulling in all their descendants. This naturally excludes: - **Total bilirubin** (covered by a separate concept set). - **Indirect / unconjugated bilirubin** (covered by a separate concept set). - **Other specimens** such as cord blood, body fluids (peritoneal, pleural, dialysis), and urine — direct/conjugated bilirubin variants exist for these but are out of scope for this set. - **Ratios and qualitative tests** such as `Bilirubin.direct/Bilirubin.total`, `Bilirubin.conjugated+indirect`, or `Bilirubin.direct [Presence]`. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports "direct bilirubin" or "conjugated bilirubin" without further specification (typical of routine biochemistry analysers): `3027597 / 1968-7 — Bilirubin.direct [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma` if the value is in mg/dL, `3028638 / 14629-0 — Bilirubin.direct [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma` if the value is in µmol/L. Routine clinical assays use the diazo method, which corresponds to the `Bilirubin.direct` concepts even when the source labels them "conjugated". - **Source labelled "HPLC" or explicitly "glucuronidated"**: prefer `3019676 / 15152-2 — Bilirubin.conjugated [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma` (mg/dL) or `3005772 / 29760-6 — Bilirubin.conjugated [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma` (µmol/L). These are appropriate when the lab uses an HPLC method that resolves the strictly glucuronidated fraction. - **Do not confuse with**: total bilirubin, indirect/unconjugated bilirubin, neonatal transcutaneous bilirubin, delta bilirubin (when measured separately), bilirubin in urine, or bilirubin in cord blood — all belong to other concept sets. - **Method is not part of the mapping target**: when the source records the assay method (Jendrassik–Grof, vanadate, dry chemistry, HPLC, etc.), preserve it in the measurement source value but do not let it change the target concept beyond the "direct vs conjugated" choice above. ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 1968-7 — Bilirubin.direct [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma (Part description for "Bilirubin.glucuronidated+Bilirubin.albumin bound"). Available: https://loinc.org/1968-7/ [2] Nomenclature for Properties and Units (NPU). IFCC/IUPAC. NPU codes (current release). Available: https://npu-terminology.org/npu-database/

en.name: Gamma glutamyl transferase (GGT) in blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Gamma glutamyl transferase (GGT, also written GGTP or Gamma-GT) is a liver enzyme involved in the transfer of amino acids across the cellular membrane and in glutathione metabolism [1]. Its activity in blood rises in cholestatic and biliary conditions, and is also a sensitive (though not specific) marker of alcohol-related liver injury. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a biochemistry analyser on serum or plasma. It is collected in routine biochemistry as part of a liver panel, especially when investigating cholestasis, monitoring chronic liver disease, or following alcohol use. Results are reported as catalytic activity concentration; NPU recognises both **U/L** (the conventional unit, used by virtually all clinical labs) and **µkat/L** (the SI unit) [2]. The IFCC reference measurement procedure for gamma-GT at 37 °C, listed by JCTLM, gives the conversion factor `1 U/L = 0.01667 µkat/L` [3]. ## Included Concepts The set contains a single LOINC "Lab Test" concept, measured in serum or plasma — by far the only specimen used in routine practice for this assay. - *3026910 / 2324-2 — Gamma glutamyl transferase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: reported in U/L. **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows LOINC: **`[U]/L`** (concept 8645). The notations `U/L` and `IU/L` are used interchangeably in clinical practice and represent the same value mathematically — no conversion is needed between them. ## Excluded Concepts No concepts are explicitly excluded by name, but the following LOINC concepts that exist for GGT are deliberately not part of this set: - **DBS (Dried Blood Spot)** — `36032012 / 96593-9 — Gamma glutamyl transferase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in DBS`. GGT measured on dried blood spot is not interchangeable with serum/plasma values (whole-blood matrix dilutes plasma enzymes by the haematocrit fraction, ≈ 40-45%). It is rarely used in clinical practice and could be added to a separate concept set in the future if needed. - **Other specimens**: amniotic fluid, body fluid, dialysis fluid, semen, urine, 24-hour urine — out of scope for a "blood" concept set. - **Macromolecular GGT presence** (`100741-8`) — a qualitative test for macro-GGT complexes, not a quantitative activity measurement. - **Ratios** like `Gamma glutamyl transferase/Aspartate aminotransferase` (`2325-9`) — out of scope. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports "GGT", "gamma-GT", "γ-GT", "GGTP" or similar without further specification: `3026910 / 2324-2 — Gamma glutamyl transferase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum or Plasma`. This is by far the most widely used LOINC code for this test. - **Do not confuse with**: GGT/AST ratio, macromolecular GGT presence, or GGT in non-blood specimens (urine, body fluid, etc.) — all belong to other concept sets or are out of scope. - **Method is not part of the mapping target**: when the source records the assay method (kinetic colorimetric, IFCC reference at 37 °C, etc.), preserve it in the measurement source value — it does not change the target concept. - **Unit naming**: source systems may report `U/L` or `IU/L` (sometimes `iU/L`). All correspond to the same physical quantity. Map them all to the recommended unit `[U]/L` (concept 8645). Values reported in `µkat/L` should be converted using `1 U/L = 0.01667 µkat/L` (i.e. multiply µkat/L by ~60 to get U/L) [3]. ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 2324-2 — Gamma glutamyl transferase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum or Plasma (Part description for "Gamma glutamyl transferase"). Available: https://loinc.org/2324-2/ [2] Nomenclature for Properties and Units (NPU). IFCC/IUPAC. NPU codes (current release). Available: https://npu-terminology.org/npu-database/ [3] Joint Committee for Traceability in Laboratory Medicine (JCTLM). Database of higher-order reference measurement procedures, reference materials and reference measurement services. BIPM/IFCC/ILAC. Available: https://www.jctlmdb.org/#/app/home

en.name: Indirect bilirubin in blood
en.shortDescription: Bilirubin fraction not yet processed by the liver (unconjugated) ; distinct from conjugated and total bilirubin
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Bilirubin is an orange-yellow pigment produced by the normal breakdown of heme, a component of the haemoglobin found in red blood cells [1]. **Indirect (or "unconjugated", or "non-glucuronidated") bilirubin** is the fraction that has **not** been processed by the liver yet — it is the initial breakdown product of heme that lacks water solubility and circulates bound to albumin [1]. In real-world data, this value is **almost never measured directly** — it is typically **calculated** as `total bilirubin − direct bilirubin` (or, less commonly, by HPLC or specific photometric methods). Most laboratory information systems still output it as a separate result line, which is why a dedicated LOINC code exists. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, on serum or plasma. It is collected in routine biochemistry as part of a liver panel, especially when investigating jaundice. Results are reported either in mass units (**mg/dL**) or in SI units (**µmol/L**, the unit recognised by NPU as the standard for substance concentration of bilirubin [2]). Both units are in active use in practice; the choice varies by lab and by country. ## Included Concepts The set contains two LOINC "Lab Test" concepts, both measured in serum or plasma. Each measurand has a mass-concentration variant (mg/dL) and a substance-concentration variant (µmol/L). - *3007359 / 1971-1 — Bilirubin.indirect [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: reported in mg/dL. - *3007242 / 14630-8 — Bilirubin.indirect [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: reported in µmol/L. **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows the LOINC property: the mass-concentration concept uses **mg/dL** (concept 8840), the substance-concentration concept uses **µmol/L** (concept 8749). Conversion: 1 mg/dL = 17.1 µmol/L; 1 µmol/L = 0.0585 mg/dL (molar mass of bilirubin ≈ 584.66 g/mol). ## Excluded Concepts No concepts are explicitly excluded. The set is defined by anchoring on the LOINC group for non-glucuronidated bilirubin in serum or plasma and pulling in all its descendants. This naturally excludes: - **Total bilirubin** (covered by a separate concept set). - **Conjugated / direct bilirubin** (covered by a separate concept set). - **Other specimens** such as cord blood, body fluids, and peritoneal fluid — indirect bilirubin variants exist for these but are out of scope for this set. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports "indirect bilirubin" or "unconjugated bilirubin" without further specification: `3007359 / 1971-1 — Bilirubin.indirect [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma` if the value is in mg/dL, `3007242 / 14630-8 — Bilirubin.indirect [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma` if the value is in µmol/L. - **Calculated vs measured**: in most clinical workflows the indirect bilirubin value is derived from total − direct, not directly measured. Both the calculated and the directly measured values map to the same LOINC concepts above — there is no LOINC distinction between calculated and measured. If the source system flags the result as calculated, preserve that flag in the measurement source value but do not change the target concept. - **Do not confuse with**: total bilirubin, conjugated/direct bilirubin, delta bilirubin, neonatal transcutaneous bilirubin, or bilirubin in urine — all belong to other concept sets. ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 14630-8 — Bilirubin.indirect [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma (Part description for "Bilirubin.non-glucuronidated"). Available: https://loinc.org/14630-8/ [2] Nomenclature for Properties and Units (NPU). IFCC/IUPAC. NPU codes (current release). Available: https://npu-terminology.org/npu-database/

en.name: Total bilirubin in blood
en.shortDescription: Total bilirubin = conjugated + unconjugated ; distinct from each fraction individually
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Bilirubin is an orange-yellow pigment produced by the normal breakdown of heme, a component of the haemoglobin found in red blood cells [1]. **Total bilirubin** is the sum of all its forms (conjugated + unconjugated + delta) in a single blood sample. It is a standard laboratory test — the source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a biochemistry analyser (most commonly on serum or plasma) or, especially in neonatal settings, by a blood-gas analyser via co-oximetry on whole blood [2]. It is collected in routine biochemistry, in intensive care (typically on venous samples, occasionally on arterial), and in neonatal units (often on capillary samples). Results are reported either in mass units (**mg/dL**) or in SI units (**µmol/L**, the unit recognised by NPU as the standard for substance concentration of bilirubin [3]). Both units are in active use in practice; the choice varies by lab and by country. ## Included Concepts The set contains ten LOINC "Lab Test" concepts, grouped here by specimen type. Each specimen usually has two variants: a mass-concentration variant (mg/dL) and a substance-concentration variant (µmol/L). ### Serum or plasma (default specimen) Most common specimen for this test in hospital biochemistry; use these when the source does not specify a more precise specimen. - *3024128 / 1975-2 — Bilirubin.total [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: reported in mg/dL. - *3006140 / 14631-6 — Bilirubin.total [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: reported in µmol/L. ### Whole blood (unspecified) Used when the source reports total bilirubin on whole blood without specifying arterial, venous or capillary origin — typically a co-oximetry result from a blood-gas analyser when the specimen origin is not recorded. - *3028833 / 42719-5 — Bilirubin.total [Mass/volume] in Blood (LOINC)*: mg/dL. - *40757494 / 54363-7 — Bilirubin.total [Moles/volume] in Blood (LOINC)*: µmol/L. ### Arterial blood Used when the specimen is explicitly an arterial sample — most often an arterial blood-gas run on a point-of-care analyser that includes a co-oximetry bilirubin channel [2]. Less common than venous in most adult ICU workflows. - *40762888 / 59827-6 — Bilirubin.total [Mass/volume] in Arterial blood (LOINC)*: mg/dL. - *1175183 / 89872-6 — Bilirubin.total [Moles/volume] in Arterial blood (LOINC)*: µmol/L. ### Venous blood Used when the specimen is explicitly venous whole blood — the most common whole-blood specimen in adult ICU and ward settings, including venous blood-gas runs. - *40762889 / 59828-4 — Bilirubin.total [Mass/volume] in Venous blood (LOINC)*: mg/dL. - *1175191 / 89871-8 — Bilirubin.total [Moles/volume] in Venous blood (LOINC)*: µmol/L. ### Capillary blood Primarily used in neonatal screening (heel-prick) and point-of-care testing. Only the SI variant exists in LOINC. - *1616780 / 97770-2 — Bilirubin.total [Moles/volume] in Capillary blood (LOINC)*: µmol/L. ### Serum, plasma or blood (unspecified, generic) Generic concept when the specimen is not differentiated between serum/plasma and whole blood. Only the SI variant exists. - *46235782 / 77137-8 — Bilirubin.total [Moles/volume] in Serum, Plasma or Blood (LOINC)*: µmol/L. **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows the LOINC property: all mass-concentration concepts use **mg/dL** (concept 8840), all substance-concentration concepts use **µmol/L** (concept 8749). Conversion: 1 mg/dL = 17.1 µmol/L; 1 µmol/L = 0.0585 mg/dL. ## Excluded Concepts No concepts are explicitly excluded. The set is defined by anchoring on the two LOINC groups for total bilirubin (mass concentration and substance concentration) and pulling in all their descendants, which naturally excludes related but distinct bilirubin measurements: conjugated (direct) bilirubin, unconjugated (indirect) bilirubin, neonatal transcutaneous bilirubin, delta bilirubin, bilirubin.glucuronidated, and bilirubin in urine or amniotic fluid. These belong to separate concept sets. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports "total bilirubin" without specifying a specimen but is known to come from a routine biochemistry analyser: `3024128 / 1975-2 — Bilirubin.total [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma` if the value is in mg/dL, `3006140 / 14631-6 — Bilirubin.total [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma` if the value is in µmol/L. Serum or plasma is by far the most common specimen for this test. - **Serum/plasma vs serum/plasma/blood**: use `46235782 / 77137-8 — Bilirubin.total [Moles/volume] in Serum, Plasma or Blood` only when the source genuinely cannot tell whether the matrix is serum/plasma or whole blood (e.g. a column aggregating results from both biochemistry and blood-gas analysers without a matrix tag). When the workflow is a routine biochemistry analyser, prefer `3024128 / 1975-2 — Bilirubin.total [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma` (or `3006140 / 14631-6 — Bilirubin.total [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma` in µmol/L), even if the matrix is not explicitly labelled in the source — `77137-8` is a generic fallback, not the default. - **Blood-gas / ICU context**: if the result comes from a venous blood-gas analyser, map to `40762889 / 59828-4 — Bilirubin.total [Mass/volume] in Venous blood` (mg/dL) or `1175191 / 89871-8 — Bilirubin.total [Moles/volume] in Venous blood` (µmol/L). For an arterial blood-gas analyser, use `40762888 / 59827-6 — Bilirubin.total [Mass/volume] in Arterial blood` or `1175183 / 89872-6 — Bilirubin.total [Moles/volume] in Arterial blood`. - **Capillary / neonatal heel-prick**: map to `1616780 / 97770-2 — Bilirubin.total [Moles/volume] in Capillary blood`. LOINC has no mg/dL variant for capillary blood, so a source reporting mg/dL still maps here — the mg/dL to µmol/L conversion is registered. - **Do not confuse with**: direct/conjugated bilirubin, indirect/unconjugated bilirubin, delta bilirubin, transcutaneous (skin, non-invasive) bilirubin, neonatal bilirubin panels, or bilirubin in urine — all belong to other concept sets. - **Method is not part of the mapping target**: the source lab's measurement method (diazo, spectrophotometric, dry chemistry, co-oximetry, etc.) can be preserved in the measurement source value but does not change which concept to map to. ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 1975-2 — Bilirubin.total [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma (Part description for "Bilirubin"). Available: https://loinc.org/1975-2/ [2] Liu J, Dai Y, Li R, Yuan J, Wang Q, Wang L. Accuracy and Reliability of Whole Blood Bilirubin Measurements Using a Roche Blood Gas Analyzer for Neonatal Hyperbilirubinemia Screening and Risk Stratification. Front Pediatr. 2022;10:910566. Available: https://www.frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/fped.2022.910566/full [3] Nomenclature for Properties and Units (NPU). IFCC/IUPAC. NPU codes (current release). en.name: B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) in blood
en.shortDescription: Biologically active form of B-type natriuretic peptide ; not numerically interchangeable with NT-proBNP
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) is a 32-amino-acid peptide hormone produced by ventricular cardiomyocytes. Plasma BNP rises in heart failure and is widely used to rule out the diagnosis in patients presenting with dyspnoea [1]. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by immunoassay. Results are reported as a mass concentration in pg/mL [2]. **Note: BNP vs NT-proBNP.** ProBNP is cleaved into equimolar amounts of the biologically active **BNP** and the biologically inactive **NT-proBNP** [1]. In plasma, NT-proBNP concentrations are roughly 6 times higher than BNP because their clearance mechanisms differ [1]. The two are **not numerically interchangeable** and use different cut-offs. This concept set covers **BNP only** ; NT-proBNP is captured by the separate concept set "N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) in blood". ## Included Concepts The set is anchored on two LOINC Hierarchy concepts (scoped to `Chemistry - non-challenge`), each expanded to include all their descendants. The set resolves to three LOINC "Lab Test" concepts: - *3011960 / 30934-4 — Natriuretic peptide B [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: most widely used. - *3052295 / 47092-2 — Natriuretic peptide B [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: SI form. - *3031569 / 42637-9 — Natriuretic peptide B [Mass/volume] in Blood (LOINC)* **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS`: **`pg/mL`** (concept 8845 — picogram per millilitre) for `[Mass/volume]` codes and **`pmol/L`** (concept 8729 — picomole per litre) for `[Moles/volume]` codes. The stoichiometric conversion factor is `1 pg/mL ≈ 0.288 pmol/L`, derived from the BNP-32 molecular weight of 3472 Da [1] (`pg/mL` and `ng/L` are numerically identical, as are the corresponding factors). **BNP and NT-proBNP are distinct molecules with different molecular weights (3472 vs ~8500 Da); their conversion factors must not be swapped.** Assays are standardised differently between manufacturers, so converted values remain method-dependent. ## Excluded Concepts The following LOINC concept is deliberately excluded by name: - *1469998 / 107231-3 — Natriuretic peptide B [Mass/volume] adjusted for eGFR in Serum or Plasma*: derived measurement (eGFR-adjusted), not the raw BNP concentration. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports a BNP value: `3011960 / 30934-4 — Natriuretic peptide B [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma`. - **Source reports NT-proBNP**: do **not** map to this concept set. Use "N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) in blood" instead. - **Do not confuse with**: NT-proBNP (separate concept set, different molecule and cut-offs), ANP/proANP (atrial natriuretic peptide, different analyte), CNP (C-type natriuretic peptide). ## References [1] Novack ML, Zubair M. Natriuretic Peptide B Type Test. In: *StatPearls*. Treasure Island (FL): StatPearls Publishing. Available: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK556136/ [2] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 30934-4 — Natriuretic peptide B [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma. Available: https://loinc.org/30934-4/

en.name: C reactive protein (CRP) in blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context C reactive protein (CRP) is an acute-phase plasma protein produced by hepatocytes under transcriptional control by interleukin-6, in response to inflammation, infection or tissue damage. After a single stimulus, serum CRP rises above 5 mg/L by about 6 hours, peaks around 48 hours, and falls rapidly (plasma half-life ~ 19 hours) once the stimulus resolves [1]. Following an acute-phase stimulus, values may increase 10,000-fold (from < 50 µg/L up to > 500 mg/L) [1]. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by immunoassay. Results are reported as a mass concentration in mg/L (SI / European convention) or mg/dL (US convention), or less commonly as a substance concentration in nmol/L [2]. **Note: standard CRP vs high-sensitivity CRP (hsCRP).** The analyte is the **same** in both cases — only the assay sensitivity differs [1]. The 'regular' CRP assay is reported in mg/L (or mg/dL) and is adequate for monitoring infection and clinically evident inflammation. The hsCRP assay has a lower detection limit (typically < 1 mg/L) and is used for cardiovascular risk stratification, where values < 1, 1-3, and > 3 mg/L correspond to lower, average, and higher relative risk respectively; values > 10 mg/L probably reflect an acute-phase response and should be repeated 2-3 weeks later before being used for cardiovascular risk assessment [3]. Both LOINC code variants are included in this concept set; downstream analyses that distinguish them must use the LOINC code, not the value. ## Included Concepts The set is anchored on four LOINC Hierarchy concepts (scoped to `Chemistry - non-challenge`), each expanded to include all their descendants. The set resolves to nine LOINC "Lab Test" concepts, grouped here by specimen. ### Serum or plasma - *3020460 / 1988-5 — C reactive protein [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: most widely used. - *3010156 / 30522-7 — C reactive protein [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma by High sensitivity method (LOINC)*: hsCRP. - *46234770 / 76485-2 — C reactive protein [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: SI form. - *46234771 / 76486-0 — C reactive protein [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma by High sensitivity method (LOINC)*: SI form, hsCRP. ### Whole blood - *42870365 / 71426-1 — C reactive protein [Mass/volume] in Blood by High sensitivity method (LOINC)* - *1091617 / 105126-7 — C reactive protein [Mass/volume] in Serum, Plasma or Blood (LOINC)* - *1469985 / 106736-2 — C reactive protein [Mass/volume] in Serum, Plasma or Blood by Rapid immunoassay (LOINC)* ### Capillary blood - *3051387 / 48421-2 — C reactive protein [Mass/volume] in Capillary blood (LOINC)* **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS`: **`mg/L`** (OMOP concept 8751 — milligram per litre) for `[Mass/volume]` codes and **`nmol/L`** (OMOP concept 8736 — nanomole per litre) for `[Moles/volume]` codes. **No mass-to-molar conversion is provided**, deliberately. The factor depends on which molecular form is assumed — the native pentamer (five ~23 kDa subunits, ≈115 kDa) or the monomer — and the two differ fivefold. Serum proteins are standardised and reported as mass concentrations (the IFCC/BCR reference material ERM-DA470k carries certified mass values), and CRP is reported in `mg/L` (sometimes `mg/dL`) by essentially all laboratories, so the molar LOINC codes are seldom populated. Prefer `mg/L`; a source reporting `nmol/L` should be converted upstream using the molar mass of the form its assay actually calibrates against. ## Excluded Concepts The following LOINC concepts in Serum or Plasma are deliberately excluded by name: - *3000965 / 11039-5 — C reactive protein [Presence] in Serum or Plasma*: qualitative, not a concentration. - *3034254 / 35648-5 — C reactive protein [Quintile] in Serum or Plasma by High sensitivity method*: categorical (quintile bin), not a concentration. - *3028766 / 14634-0 — C reactive protein [Titer] in Serum or Plasma*: dilution titre, not a concentration. In addition, the set deliberately omits: - **Body fluid, CSF specimens**: out of scope for a "blood" concept set. - **Cord blood and fetus specimens**: physiologically distinct from post-natal blood. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports a CRP value without specifying assay sensitivity: `3020460 / 1988-5 — C reactive protein [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma`. The most common LOINC code. - **Source explicitly says "hsCRP" or "high sensitivity"**: map to the matching `by High sensitivity method` LOINC code. - **Source reports a qualitative result (positive/negative, titre)**: do **not** map. Qualitative results are out of scope. - **Source reports CRP from CSF or body fluid**: do **not** map. Out of scope. - **Do not confuse with**: procalcitonin (PCT, separate concept set), interleukin-6 (IL-6, separate concept set), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR, separate concept set if defined). ## References [1] Pepys MB, Hirschfield GM. C-reactive protein: a critical update. *J Clin Invest*. 2003;111(12):1805-12. Available: https://doi.org/10.1172/JCI18921 [2] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 1988-5 — C reactive protein [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma. Available: https://loinc.org/1988-5/ [3] Ridker PM. A test in context: high-sensitivity C-reactive protein. *J Am Coll Cardiol*. 2016;67(6):712-23. Available: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jacc.2015.11.037

en.name: Glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) in blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) is the fraction of haemoglobin non-enzymatically glycated by glucose, used as the reference biomarker for long-term glycaemic control and as an accepted criterion for the diagnosis of diabetes mellitus (HbA1c ≥ 6.5% / ≥ 48 mmol/mol) [1]. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by HPLC, immunoassay or capillary electrophoresis on a whole blood sample. Results are reported in two unit systems: **NGSP (%)**, the historical US/DCCT convention, and **IFCC (mmol/mol)**, the SI / European convention. The two are related by the NGSP-IFCC Master Equation `NGSP% = (0.915 × IFCC%) + 2.152` [1]. ## Included Concepts The set lists eight LOINC "Lab Test" concepts for HbA1c in blood (no LOINC Hierarchy with descendants is available in the loaded vocabulary), grouped by representation. ### HbA1c / total haemoglobin ratio - *3004410 / 4548-4 — Hemoglobin A1c/Hemoglobin.total in Blood (LOINC)*: most widely used. - *3003309 / 4549-2 — Hemoglobin A1c/Hemoglobin.total in Blood by Electrophoresis (LOINC)* - *3005673 / 17856-6 — Hemoglobin A1c/Hemoglobin.total in Blood by HPLC (LOINC)* - *3007263 / 17855-8 — Hemoglobin A1c/Hemoglobin.total in Blood by calculation (LOINC)* - *40762352 / 59261-8 — Hemoglobin A1c/Hemoglobin.total in Blood by IFCC protocol (LOINC)*: IFCC-standardised, reported in mmol/mol. - *40765129 / 62388-4 — Hemoglobin A1c/Hemoglobin.total in Blood by JDS/JSCC protocol (LOINC)*: Japanese protocol. - *42869630 / 71875-9 — Hemoglobin A1c/Hemoglobin.total [Pure mass fraction] in Blood (LOINC)*: dimensionless ratio variant. ### Mass concentration - *3034639 / 41995-2 — Hemoglobin A1c [Mass/volume] in Blood (LOINC)*: rarely used. **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS`. For the ratio codes, NGSP reports use **`%`** (concept 8554 — percent), IFCC reports use **`mmol/mol`** (concept 9579 — millimole per mole). The `NGSP% ↔ IFCC mmol/mol` conversion is **affine, not multiplicative** (`IFCC [mmol/mol] ≈ 10.929 × NGSP[%] − 23.50`, with the reverse `NGSP[%] ≈ 0.09148 × IFCC[mmol/mol] + 2.152`, derived from the master equation [1]). It is recorded in `unit_conversions.json` using the optional `offset` field (`target = factor × source + offset`) for the four NGSP-% ratio concepts, so downstream tooling (including the OMOP SQL export) applies it automatically. ## Excluded Concepts No concepts are explicitly excluded by name. The set deliberately omits: - *36032094 / 96595-4 — Hemoglobin A1c/Hemoglobin.total in DBS*: dried blood spot, different specimen. - **Cord blood and fetus specimens**: physiologically distinct from post-natal blood. - **HbA1c goal / target codes**: clinical observation, not a measurement. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports an HbA1c value without specifying method: `3004410 / 4548-4 — Hemoglobin A1c/Hemoglobin.total in Blood`. - **Source explicitly mentions HPLC, electrophoresis or another method**: map to the method-specific LOINC code if available. - **Source reports estimated average glucose (eAG)**: derived measurement, do **not** map to HbA1c. Out of scope. - **Do not confuse with**: fasting glucose, oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT), fructosamine (shorter-term glycation marker), glycated albumin. ## References [1] Sacks DB, Arnold M, Bakris GL, Bruns DE, Horvath AR, Lernmark Å, et al. Guidelines and recommendations for laboratory analysis in the diagnosis and management of diabetes mellitus. *Clin Chem*. 2023;69(8):808-68. Available: https://doi.org/10.1093/clinchem/hvad080 [2] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 4548-4 — Hemoglobin A1c/Hemoglobin.total in Blood. Available: https://loinc.org/4548-4/

en.name: Interleukin-6 (IL-6) in blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Interleukin-6 (IL-6) is a cytokine promptly and transiently produced in response to infections and tissue injuries, by monocytes/macrophages, endothelial cells, fibroblasts and many other cell types [1]. Once released, IL-6 reaches the liver through the bloodstream and induces a wide range of acute-phase proteins, including C-reactive protein (CRP), serum amyloid A (SAA), fibrinogen and haptoglobin [1]. The rise in serum IL-6 precedes the rise in serum acute-phase proteins (in sterile surgical models) [1], so it can be informative earlier than CRP, although routine clinical use of IL-6 outside specialised contexts (e.g. monitoring of cytokine release syndrome after CAR T-cell therapy [2]) remains limited. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by immunoassay. Results are reported as a mass concentration in pg/mL — the representation this concept set covers. Some assays instead report an arbitrary-unit concentration in U/mL or IU/mL; that variant is excluded here, because the pg/mL ↔ IU/mL relationship depends on the calibration of the kit against the NIBSC reference standard and is not portable between assays [3]. ## Included Concepts The set is anchored on the LOINC Hierarchy `Interleukin 6 | Serum or Plasma | Chemistry - non-challenge`, expanded to include all its descendants. After exclusions, it resolves to a single LOINC "Lab Test" concept: - *3023091 / 26881-3 — Interleukin 6 [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: the mass concentration, and by far the most widely used representation. **Note on units.** The recommended unit is **`pg/mL`** (OMOP concept 8845 — picogram per millilitre), as listed by LOINC for `26881-3`. ## Excluded Concepts The following LOINC concepts in Serum or Plasma are deliberately excluded by name: - *3044155 / 44322-6 — Interleukin 6 [Presence] in Serum or Plasma*: qualitative, not a concentration. - *3009104 / 4655-7 — Interleukin 6 [Units/volume] in Serum or Plasma*: arbitrary-unit concentration — see the note below. In addition, the set deliberately omits: - **Body fluid, CSF specimens**: out of scope for a "blood" concept set. - **Cord blood and fetus specimens**: physiologically distinct from post-natal blood. **Note on excluded units.** Concept 3009104 / 4655-7 — Interleukin 6 [Units/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC) is excluded from this set. It reports an activity concentration in arbitrary units, which UCUM defines as non-dimensional and non-convertible, so it cannot be harmonised with the mass concentration in `pg/mL` used by the rest of the set. LOINC additionally marks this code DISCOURAGED, on the grounds that no units are associated with the term and its validity cannot be verified. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports an IL-6 value: `3023091 / 26881-3 — Interleukin 6 [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma`. - **Source reports IL-6 from CSF or body fluid**: do **not** map. Out of scope. - **Source reports a qualitative result (positive/negative)**: do **not** map. - **Do not confuse with**: other interleukins (IL-1, IL-8, IL-10 — different cytokines), procalcitonin (PCT, separate concept set), C reactive protein (CRP, separate concept set). ## References [1] Tanaka T, Narazaki M, Kishimoto T. IL-6 in inflammation, immunity, and disease. *Cold Spring Harb Perspect Biol*. 2014;6(10):a016295. Available: https://doi.org/10.1101/cshperspect.a016295 [2] Hay KA, Hanafi LA, Li D, Gust J, Liles WC, Wurfel MM, et al. Kinetics and biomarkers of severe cytokine release syndrome after CD19 chimeric antigen receptor-modified T-cell therapy. *Blood*. 2017;130(21):2295-2306. Available: https://doi.org/10.1182/blood-2017-06-793141 [3] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 26881-3 — Interleukin 6 [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma. Available: https://loinc.org/26881-3/

en.name: Lipase in blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Pancreatic lipase is a digestive enzyme secreted by the exocrine pancreas that hydrolyses dietary triglycerides. Serum lipase activity ≥ 3 × the upper limit of normal is one of the three diagnostic criteria for acute pancreatitis under the revised Atlanta classification [1] and the IAP/APA guidelines [2]. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a colorimetric or turbidimetric assay. Results are reported as an enzyme-activity concentration in `U/L` (international units per litre) or, in SI, in `µkat/L` [3]. ## Included Concepts The set is anchored on one LOINC Hierarchy concept (scoped to `Chemistry - non-challenge`), expanded to include all its descendants. The set resolves to one LOINC "Lab Test" concept: - *3004905 / 3040-3 — Lipase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)* **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS`: **`[iU]/L`** (concept 8923 — international unit per litre, written `U/L` in clinical reports). SI conversion: `1 U/L = 0.01667 µkat/L` (derived from the katal SI definition, see NPU03612 vs NPU57165 [3]). Reference ranges are highly method-dependent (no international standard for lipase activity measurement); preserve the upper limit of normal from the source lab. ## Excluded Concepts The following LOINC concept in Serum or Plasma is deliberately excluded by name: - *1761825 / 100743-4 — Lipase.macromolecular [Presence] in Serum or Plasma*: qualitative test for macrolipasaemia, not a routine activity measurement. In addition, the set deliberately omits: - **Lipase in urine, amniotic fluid, body fluid, peritoneal fluid, pleural fluid, dialysis fluid specimens**: out of scope for a "blood" concept set. - **Sincalide challenge codes (`--Nth specimen post Sincalide`)**: challenge tests, out of scope. - **Cord blood and fetus specimens**: physiologically distinct from post-natal blood. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports a lipase value: `3004905 / 3040-3 — Lipase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum or Plasma`. - **Source reports lipase from ascitic fluid, peritoneal fluid, pleural fluid**: do **not** map. Out of scope. - **Do not confuse with**: amylase (separate concept set, different enzyme), lipoprotein lipase (different enzyme, lipid metabolism). ## References [1] Banks PA, Bollen TL, Dervenis C, Gooszen HG, Johnson CD, Sarr MG, et al. Classification of acute pancreatitis—2012: revision of the Atlanta classification and definitions by international consensus. *Gut*. 2013;62(1):102-11. Available: https://doi.org/10.1136/gutjnl-2012-302779 [2] Working Group IAP/APA Acute Pancreatitis Guidelines. IAP/APA evidence-based guidelines for the management of acute pancreatitis. *Pancreatology*. 2013;13(4 Suppl 2):e1-15. Available: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.pan.2013.07.063 [3] Nomenclature for Properties and Units (NPU). IFCC/IUPAC. NPU codes (current release). Available: https://npu-terminology.org/npu-database/

en.name: N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) in blood
en.shortDescription: Biologically inactive N-terminal fragment of proBNP ; not numerically interchangeable with BNP
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) is the biologically inactive 76-amino-acid N-terminal fragment of proBNP, produced by ventricular cardiomyocytes. Plasma NT-proBNP rises in heart failure and is widely used to rule out the diagnosis in patients presenting with dyspnoea [1]. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by immunoassay. Results are reported as a mass concentration in pg/mL (or ng/L — numerically identical) [2]. **Note: NT-proBNP vs BNP.** ProBNP is cleaved into equimolar amounts of the biologically active **BNP** and the biologically inactive **NT-proBNP** [1]. In plasma, NT-proBNP concentrations are roughly 6 times higher than BNP because their clearance mechanisms differ [1]. The two are **not numerically interchangeable** and use different cut-offs. This concept set covers **NT-proBNP only** ; BNP is captured by the separate concept set "B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) in blood". ## Included Concepts The set is anchored on three LOINC Hierarchy concepts (scoped to `Chemistry - non-challenge`), each expanded to include all their descendants. The set resolves to five LOINC "Lab Test" concepts, grouped here by specimen. ### Serum or plasma - *3029187 / 33762-6 — Natriuretic peptide.B prohormone N-Terminal [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: most widely used. - *42529224 / 83107-3 — Natriuretic peptide.B prohormone N-Terminal [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma by Immunoassay (LOINC)* - *3029435 / 33763-4 — Natriuretic peptide.B prohormone N-Terminal [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: SI form. - *42529225 / 83108-1 — Natriuretic peptide.B prohormone N-Terminal [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma by Immunoassay (LOINC)*: SI form, immunoassay. ### Whole blood - *42870364 / 71425-3 — Natriuretic peptide.B prohormone N-Terminal [Mass/volume] in Blood by Immunoassay (LOINC)* - *1469712 / 106735-4 — Natriuretic peptide.B prohormone N-Terminal [Mass/volume] in Serum, Plasma or Blood by Rapid immunoassay (LOINC)* **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS`: **`pg/mL`** (concept 8845 — picogram per millilitre) for `[Mass/volume]` codes and **`pmol/L`** (concept 8729 — picomole per litre) for `[Moles/volume]` codes. `1 pg/mL = 1 ng/L` (numerically equal). The stoichiometric conversion factor is `1 pg/mL ≈ 0.118 pmol/L`, derived from the NT-proBNP molecular weight of ~ 8500 Da (the 76-amino-acid N-terminal fragment of proBNP — sequence from UniProt P16860). **NT-proBNP and BNP are distinct molecules with different molecular weights (~8500 vs 3472 Da); their conversion factors must not be swapped.** Assays are standardised differently between manufacturers, so converted values remain method-dependent. ## Excluded Concepts No concepts are explicitly excluded by name. The set deliberately omits: - **Pleural fluid, peritoneal dialysis fluid specimens**: out of scope for a "blood" concept set. - **Cord blood and fetus specimens**: physiologically distinct from post-natal blood. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports an NT-proBNP value: `3029187 / 33762-6 — Natriuretic peptide.B prohormone N-Terminal [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma`. - **Source reports BNP**: do **not** map. Use "B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) in blood" instead. - **Do not confuse with**: BNP (separate concept set, different molecule and cut-offs), MR-proANP (mid-regional pro-atrial natriuretic peptide). ## References [1] Novack ML, Zubair M. Natriuretic Peptide B Type Test. In: *StatPearls*. Treasure Island (FL): StatPearls Publishing. Available: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK556136/ [2] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 33762-6 — Natriuretic peptide.B prohormone N-Terminal [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma. Available: https://loinc.org/33762-6/

concept.conceptName: Procalcitonin | Serum or Plasma | Chemistry - non-challenge

en.name: Procalcitonin (PCT) in blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Procalcitonin (PCT) is the precursor peptide of calcitonin. In healthy individuals, plasma PCT is low (< 0.1 ng/mL) [2]. In response to bacterial infection, circulating PCT rises within a few hours and peaks earlier than C reactive protein (CRP) [2]. Bacterial infection is a strong stimulus for PCT production, whereas viral infection induces little or no PCT rise [1, 2], so PCT is used clinically to discriminate bacterial from viral or non-infectious inflammation, and to guide antibiotic discontinuation in critically ill patients [3]. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by immunoassay (most commonly the Brahms / Kryptor assay). Results are reported as a mass concentration in ng/mL or µg/L (numerically identical), or less commonly as a substance concentration in pmol/L [4]. ## Included Concepts The set is anchored on the LOINC Hierarchy `Procalcitonin | Serum or Plasma | Chemistry - non-challenge`, expanded to include all its descendants. The set resolves to three LOINC "Lab Test" concepts: - *3046279 / 33959-8 — Procalcitonin [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: most widely used. - *44817130 / 75241-0 — Procalcitonin [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma by Immunoassay (LOINC)*: method-specific variant. - *1988947 / 99099-4 — Procalcitonin [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: SI form. **Note on units.** Recommended unit: **`8748 / ug/L — microgram per liter`** (UCUM) for the `[Mass/volume]` codes, and **`8736 / nmol/L — nanomole per liter`** (UCUM) for the `[Moles/volume]` code. `1 ng/mL = 1 µg/L` (numerically equal), and a `8842 / ng/mL — nanogram per milliliter` → `ug/L` conversion is registered. **No conversion bridges the mass and molar codes**, deliberately. Procalcitonin is the 116-amino-acid precursor of calcitonin [5], giving a theoretical mass of ≈12.8 kDa and hence `1 ng/mL ≈ 78 pmol/L`; that factor is registered on *1988947 / 99099-4 — Procalcitonin [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)* for sources reporting molar values against that code, but it is **not** used to merge the two families into a single column. Two reasons. First, the circulating analyte in septic patients is not the full-length form: mass spectrometry of patient serum gives 12,640 Da, matching the N-terminally truncated 114-amino-acid form, so any factor derived from the 116-residue mass is off by ~1 % and the literature scatters further [6]. Second, commercial PCT immunoassays are calibrated and reported in mass concentration, all published decision thresholds (0.25, 0.5, 2 µg/L) are mass-based [3], and the molar LOINC code is seldom populated. Prefer the mass form; treat a molar result as a separate quantity rather than converting it silently. ## Excluded Concepts No concepts are explicitly excluded by name. The set deliberately omits: - **Body fluid, CSF specimens**: out of scope for a "blood" concept set. - **Cord blood and fetus specimens**: physiologically distinct from post-natal blood. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports a procalcitonin value: `3046279 / 33959-8 — Procalcitonin [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma`. - **Source reports PCT from CSF or body fluid**: do **not** map. Out of scope. - **Do not confuse with**: calcitonin (thyroid hormone, different analyte and indication), C reactive protein (CRP, separate concept set), interleukin-6 (IL-6, separate concept set). ## References [1] Assicot M, Gendrel D, Carsin H, Raymond J, Guilbaud J, Bohuon C. High serum procalcitonin concentrations in patients with sepsis and infection. *Lancet*. 1993;341(8844):515-8. Available: https://doi.org/10.1016/0140-6736(93)90277-N [2] Meisner M. Update on procalcitonin measurements. *Ann Lab Med*. 2014;34(4):263-73. Available: https://doi.org/10.3343/alm.2014.34.4.263 [3] de Jong E, van Oers JA, Beishuizen A, Vos P, Vermeijden WJ, Haas LE, et al. Efficacy and safety of procalcitonin guidance in reducing the duration of antibiotic treatment in critically ill patients: a randomised, controlled, open-label trial. *Lancet Infect Dis*. 2016;16(7):819-27. Available: https://doi.org/10.1016/S1473-3099(16)00053-0 [4] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 33959-8 — Procalcitonin [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma. Available: https://loinc.org/33959-8/ [5] Le Moullec JM, Jullienne A, Chenais J, Lasmoles F, Guliana JM, Milhaud G, et al. The complete sequence of human preprocalcitonin. *FEBS Lett*. 1984;167(1):93-7. Available: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/6546550/ [6] Weglöhner W, Struck J, Fischer-Schulz C, Morgenthaler NG, Otto A, Bohuon C, et al. Isolation and characterization of serum procalcitonin from patients with sepsis. *Peptides*. 2001;22(12):2099-103. Available: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11786196/

en.name: Troponin T in blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Cardiac troponin T (cTnT) is a regulatory protein of the cardiac muscle thin filament, released into the circulation when cardiomyocytes are damaged. Together with cardiac troponin I (cTnI), it is the central biomarker for the diagnosis of myocardial injury and acute myocardial infarction [1]. cTnT may also be elevated in many other settings of cardiomyocyte stress (heart failure, pulmonary embolism, sepsis, chronic kidney disease). The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by immunoassay. Results are reported as a mass concentration, conventionally in ng/L for high-sensitivity assays and ng/mL for older contemporary assays. `1 ng/mL = 1000 ng/L`. **Note: high-sensitivity cTnT (hs-cTnT) vs contemporary cTnT.** High-sensitivity assays measure detectable cTn values in > 50% of healthy individuals, where contemporary assays cannot ; the 99th-percentile URL is assay-specific and must be looked up in the manufacturer documentation [1]. Values from different assays are not interchangeable. Both contemporary and hs-cTnT codes are included in this concept set ; analyses that distinguish them must use the LOINC code and the source unit (ng/L vs ng/mL), not the value alone. **Note: cTnT vs cTnI.** Cardiac troponin T (cTnT) and cardiac troponin I (cTnI) are two distinct gene products. Both are cardiac-specific and clinically equivalent for the diagnosis of myocardial injury, but they are **not numerically interchangeable** and use different cut-offs. Most institutions use one or the other. This concept set covers **cTnT only**. ## Included Concepts The set is anchored on four LOINC Hierarchy concepts (scoped to `Chemistry - non-challenge`), each expanded to include all their descendants. The set resolves to six LOINC "Lab Test" concepts, grouped here by specimen. ### Serum or plasma - *3019800 / 6598-7 — Troponin T.cardiac [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: most widely used (older standard assays). - *40769783 / 67151-1 — Troponin T.cardiac [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma by High sensitivity method (LOINC)*: hs-cTnT, current standard. ### Whole blood - *3048529 / 48425-3 — Troponin T.cardiac [Mass/volume] in Blood (LOINC)* - *1469858 / 106734-7 — Troponin T.cardiac [Mass/volume] in Serum, Plasma or Blood by Rapid immunoassay (LOINC)*: point-of-care. ### Venous blood - *3019572 / 6597-9 — Troponin T.cardiac [Mass/volume] in Venous blood (LOINC)* **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS`: **`ng/L`** (OMOP concept 8725 — nanogram per litre) for high-sensitivity assays and **`ng/mL`** (OMOP concept 8842 — nanogram per millilitre) for standard assays. `1 ng/mL = 1000 ng/L`. The concepts in this set carry `ug/L` (OMOP concept 8748) or `pg/mL` (OMOP concept 8845) as their recommended unit; `ug/L` is numerically identical to `ng/mL`, and `pg/mL` to `ng/L`. ## Excluded Concepts The following LOINC concepts in Blood / Serum or Plasma are deliberately excluded by name: - *3052931 / 48426-1 — Troponin T.cardiac [Presence] in Blood*: qualitative, not a concentration. - *3042837 / 33204-9 — Troponin T.cardiac [Presence] in Serum or Plasma*: qualitative, not a concentration. - *36304662 / 89575-5 — Troponin T.cardiac [Interpretation] in Serum or Plasma Qualitative by High sensitivity method*: qualitative interpretation, not a concentration. - *3965306 / 101915-7 — Troponin T.cardiac [Mass/volume] in 6 hour Serum or Plasma*: timed-protocol variant (Δ-troponin at 6 h), out of scope for a raw-concentration concept set. In addition, the set deliberately omits: - **Cord blood and fetus specimens**: physiologically distinct from post-natal blood. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports a troponin T value: `3019800 / 6598-7 — Troponin T.cardiac [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma`. - **Source explicitly says "high sensitivity" or unit is ng/L**: map to `40769783 / 67151-1 — Troponin T.cardiac [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma by High sensitivity method`. - **Source reports a qualitative result (positive/negative)**: do **not** map. Qualitative results are out of scope. - **Source reports troponin I (cTnI)**: do **not** map to this concept set. Use a dedicated cTnI concept set instead (if defined). - **Source reports a Δ-troponin (change at 1 h, 3 h, 6 h)**: do **not** map. Δ-troponin is a derived measurement. - **Do not confuse with**: troponin I (cTnI, different molecule and cut-offs), CK-MB, myoglobin (different cardiac markers). ## References [1] Thygesen K, Alpert JS, Jaffe AS, Chaitman BR, Bax JJ, Morrow DA, et al. Fourth Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction (2018). *Circulation*. 2018;138(20):e618-51. Available: https://doi.org/10.1161/CIR.0000000000000617 [2] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 67151-1 — Troponin T.cardiac [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma by High sensitivity method. Available: https://loinc.org/67151-1/

en.name: Hematocrit in blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context The hematocrit is the volume fraction of red blood cells (erythrocytes) in whole blood — i.e. the proportion of the blood volume occupied by erythrocytes [1]. It is part of every routine complete blood count (CBC) and is used to assess anaemia, polycythaemia, hydration status, and to follow blood loss or transfusion. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a haematology analyser on whole blood (EDTA tube). It is collected in routine biochemistry and intensive care, including on point-of-care blood-gas analysers that compute hematocrit from haemoglobin or measure it directly by impedance. Results are reported as a fraction, either as a percentage (e.g. **42 %**) or as a unitless ratio (e.g. **0.42** or `0.42 L/L`); the two are mathematically equivalent. ## Included Concepts The set contains fifteen LOINC "Lab Test" concepts. LOINC distinguishes two property variants for the same physical quantity: - **`[Volume Fraction]` (VFr)** — historical convention, reported in `%` or `L/L` (e.g. 42 % or 0.42 L/L). - **`[Pure volume fraction]` (VFr.DF)** — IUPAC-aligned convention introduced in 2017, reported as a dimensionless number (e.g. 0.42 with no unit). Mathematically identical to VFr. Both conventions are included because real-world datasets may use either. Within each convention, concepts vary by specimen and by measurement method. ### Volume Fraction (historical, reported in % or L/L) #### Generic blood (method not specified) - *3009542 / 20570-8 — Hematocrit [Volume Fraction] of Blood (LOINC)*: most widely used LOINC code, returned by haematology analysers when the method is not detailed. #### Method-specific - *3023314 / 4544-3 — Hematocrit [Volume Fraction] of Blood by Automated count (LOINC)*: automated impedance or optical method (most common). - *3019909 / 4545-0 — Hematocrit [Volume Fraction] of Blood by Centrifugation (LOINC)*: micro-haematocrit reference method, manual centrifugation. - *3013752 / 31100-1 — Hematocrit [Volume Fraction] of Blood by Impedance (LOINC)*: impedance-based count. - *3050746 / 48703-3 — Hematocrit [Volume Fraction] of Blood by Estimated (LOINC)*: estimated from haemoglobin (typically Hct ≈ 3 × Hb), used by some point-of-care devices. #### Specimen-specific - *3023230 / 32354-3 — Hematocrit [Volume Fraction] of Arterial blood (LOINC)*: explicit arterial sample (often from a blood-gas analyser). - *3034976 / 41654-5 — Hematocrit [Volume Fraction] of Venous blood (LOINC)*: explicit venous sample. - *3028813 / 42908-4 — Hematocrit [Volume Fraction] of Capillary blood (LOINC)*: capillary heel-prick or fingerstick (neonatal, point-of-care). - *3034037 / 41655-2 — Hematocrit [Volume Fraction] of Mixed venous blood (LOINC)*: mixed venous sample (typically from a Swan-Ganz catheter). ### Pure volume fraction (IUPAC, reported as a dimensionless number) - *1092441 / 104826-3 — Hematocrit [Pure volume fraction] of Blood (LOINC)* - *42869588 / 71833-8 — Hematocrit [Pure volume fraction] of Blood by Automated count (LOINC)* - *42869587 / 71832-0 — Hematocrit [Pure volume fraction] of Arterial blood (LOINC)* - *42869584 / 71829-6 — Hematocrit [Pure volume fraction] of Venous blood (LOINC)* - *42869585 / 71830-4 — Hematocrit [Pure volume fraction] of Mixed venous blood (LOINC)* - *42869586 / 71831-2 — Hematocrit [Pure volume fraction] of Capillary blood (LOINC)* **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows the LOINC property: - For `[Volume Fraction]` concepts: **`%`** (`8554 / % — percent (UCUM)`). LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS` is `%` for all variants. - For `[Pure volume fraction]` concepts: **`1`** (`32912 / 1 — Generic unit for indivisible thing (UCUM)`, dimensionless), aligned with NPU [2]. - `L/L` (`44777604 / L/L — liter per liter (UCUM)`) is mathematically equivalent and may be used as an alternative source unit. Conversions: `1 L/L = 100 %`, `1 % = 0.01 L/L`, `1 (dimensionless) = 100 %`. ## Excluded Concepts No concepts are explicitly excluded by name. The following LOINC concepts that exist for hematocrit are deliberately not part of this set: - **Other specimens**: cord blood, body fluid, bone marrow, CSF, dialysis fluid, pleural fluid, synovial fluid, urine, stem cell product, fetal blood — out of scope for a "blood" concept set. - **Glucose tolerance test series** — hematocrit measured at fixed time points during an oral glucose challenge (research/study context, not routine care): - `1091805 / 104874-3 — Hematocrit [Volume Fraction] of Blood --baseline` (pre-dose, t=0) - `1092140 / 104875-0 — Hematocrit [Volume Fraction] of Blood --30 minutes post dose glucose` - `1091711 / 104876-8 — Hematocrit [Volume Fraction] of Blood --1 hour post dose glucose` - `1091224 / 104877-6 — Hematocrit [Volume Fraction] of Blood --1.5 hours post dose glucose` - `1091140 / 104878-4 — Hematocrit [Volume Fraction] of Blood --2 hours post dose glucose` - `1091362 / 104879-2 — Hematocrit [Volume Fraction] of Blood --2.5 hours post dose glucose` - `1092370 / 104880-0 — Hematocrit [Volume Fraction] of Blood --3 hours post dose glucose` - **Test status / panel concepts** — these are panel grouping or test-status codes, not measurement results: - `3039251 / 39227-4 — Hematocrit test status CPHS` - `3001643 / 24360-0 — Hemoglobin and Hematocrit panel - Blood` - `3964676 / 101655-9 — Basic metabolic and hematocrit panel - Blood` - `1260092 / 104076-5 — Basic metabolic with hemoglobin and hematocrit panel - Blood` - **Ratios** like `3010748 / 16931-8 — Hematocrit/Hemoglobin [Ratio] of Blood by Automated count` — a derived ratio, not a hematocrit value. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports "hematocrit", "Ht", "Hct", "PCV" (packed cell volume) or similar without further specification: `3009542 / 20570-8 — Hematocrit [Volume Fraction] of Blood`. By far the most common LOINC code. - **Method-specific source**: if the source explicitly states the method (impedance, centrifugation, estimated), map to the corresponding method-specific concept. Otherwise, default to the generic `3009542 / 20570-8 — Hematocrit [Volume Fraction] of Blood`. - **Specimen-specific source**: if the source explicitly states "arterial", "venous", "capillary", or "mixed venous" blood, map to the corresponding specimen concept. - **Source uses the dimensionless representation** (e.g. value `0.42` without `%` or `L/L`): if the LOINC code in the source is one of the `[Pure volume fraction]` codes (e.g. `1092441 / 104826-3 — Hematocrit [Pure volume fraction] of Blood`), map to that concept. If the source uses the historical `[Volume Fraction]` codes but reports `0.42` as a fraction, map to the `[Volume Fraction]` concept and store the value with the unit `L/L` (which is the alternative supported by the unit conversions). - **Do not confuse with**: erythrocyte count (cells per volume, different concept set), haemoglobin concentration, mean corpuscular volume (MCV), or hematocrit on non-blood specimens. ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 20570-8 — Hematocrit [Volume Fraction] of Blood (Part description for "Erythrocyte"). Available: https://loinc.org/20570-8/ [2] Nomenclature for Properties and Units (NPU). IFCC/IUPAC. NPU codes (current release). Available: https://npu-terminology.org/npu-database/

en.name: Basophils in blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Basophils are the rarest type of circulating white blood cell (typically <1 % of leukocytes), characterised by dense basophilic granules containing histamine and heparin [1]. They are involved in allergic and inflammatory responses, and an elevated absolute count may be seen in chronic myeloid leukaemia and some other myeloproliferative disorders. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a haematology analyser as part of the differential white-cell count, on whole blood (EDTA tube). It is collected in routine biochemistry and intensive care. Results are reported as an absolute number concentration, typically in **`10*9/L`** (NPU SI convention, equivalent to `G/L`) or in the US notation **`10*3/uL`** (numerically identical: `1 ×10⁹/L = 1 ×10³/µL`). ## Included Concepts The set is anchored on the LOINC Group `40653984 / LG32848-0 — Basophils|Number Concentration (count/vol)|Moment in time|Blood (LOINC Group)` and pulls in all its descendants. This resolves to three standard concepts, which differ only by counting method. ### Generic (method not specified) - *3006315 / 26444-0 — Basophils [#/volume] in Blood (LOINC)*: most widely used LOINC code, returned by haematology analysers when the method is not detailed. ### Method-specific - *3013429 / 704-7 — Basophils [#/volume] in Blood by Automated count (LOINC)*: automated impedance, optical or flow-cytometric count (most common in routine practice). - *3027651 / 705-4 — Basophils [#/volume] in Blood by Manual count (LOINC)*: manual differential on a stained smear under microscope (used as a confirmation when the analyser flags the result, or in low-resource settings). **Note on units.** Recommended unit: **`10*9/L`** (`9444 / 10*9/L — billion per liter (UCUM)`), aligned with NPU [2]. LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS` is `10*3/uL` (`8848 / 10*3/uL — thousand per microliter (UCUM)`), which is the same physical quantity in US notation. Conversion: `1 ×10⁹/L = 1 ×10³/µL` (factor 1). ## Excluded Concepts No concepts are explicitly excluded. The set is defined by anchoring on the LOINC Group for basophil number concentration in blood and pulling in all its descendants. This naturally excludes: - **Percentage / fraction variants** — basophils as a fraction of total leukocytes, not an absolute count: - `3022096 / 30180-4 — Basophils/Leukocytes in Blood` - `3013869 / 706-2 — Basophils/Leukocytes in Blood by Automated count` - `3009797 / 707-0 — Basophils/Leukocytes in Blood by Manual count` - `43055368 / 71675-3 — Basophils/Leukocytes [Pure number fraction] in Blood by Manual count` - `43055373 / 71680-3 — Basophils/Leukocytes [Pure number fraction] in Blood by Automated count` - **Aggregated counts** — basophils combined with other cell types, not a basophil-specific count: - `3005836 / 32349-3 — Basophils+Eosinophils+Monocytes [#/volume] in Blood` - `3013950 / 32154-7 — Basophils+Eosinophils+Monocytes [#/volume] in Blood by Automated count` - **Other specimens**: cord blood (e.g. `44787049 / 74406-0 — Basophils [#/volume] in Cord blood`), fetal blood, body fluid, bone marrow, CSF, dialysis fluid, pleural/synovial/peritoneal fluid — out of scope for a "blood" concept set. - **Immature / band-form variants** and basophil/mast-cell aggregations — out of scope for a routine differential count. - **Allergy-panel concepts** (`X basophil bound Ab` series) — these measure IgE bound to basophils for allergen-specific testing, a different measurand. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports "basophils", "Baso", "BA#" or similar absolute count without specifying the method: `3006315 / 26444-0 — Basophils [#/volume] in Blood`. en.name: Eosinophils in blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Eosinophils are a type of granulocyte (typically 1–4 % of circulating leukocytes) characterised by eosinophilic granules containing major basic protein and other cytotoxic mediators [1]. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a haematology analyser as part of the differential white-cell count, on whole blood (EDTA tube). It is collected in routine biochemistry and intensive care. Conversion: `1 ×10⁹/L = 1 ×10³/µL` (factor 1). ## Excluded Concepts No concepts are explicitly excluded.
