en.name: Erythrocytes in blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Erythrocytes (red blood cells, RBCs) are the most abundant cells in blood; they carry haemoglobin and transport oxygen from the lungs to peripheral tissues [1]. The absolute red-cell count is a core component of the complete blood count (CBC). It is altered in anaemia (decreased), polycythaemia (increased), bleeding, dehydration, and many haematological disorders. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a haematology analyser as part of the CBC, on whole blood (EDTA tube). It is collected in routine biochemistry and intensive care. Results are reported as a number concentration, typically in **`10*12/L`** (NPU SI convention, equivalent to `T/L`) or in the US notation **`10*6/uL`** (numerically identical: `1 ×10¹²/L = 1 ×10⁶/µL`). ## Included Concepts The set is anchored on the LOINC Group `40654005 / LG32850-6 — Erythrocytes|Number Concentration (count/vol)|Moment in time|Blood (LOINC Group)` and pulls in all its descendants. This resolves to three standard concepts, which differ only by counting method. ### Generic (method not specified) - *3026361 / 26453-1 — Erythrocytes [#/volume] in Blood (LOINC)*: most widely used LOINC code, returned by haematology analysers when the method is not detailed. ### Method-specific - *3020416 / 789-8 — Erythrocytes [#/volume] in Blood by Automated count (LOINC)*: automated impedance, optical or flow-cytometric count (most common in routine practice). - *3027017 / 790-6 — Erythrocytes [#/volume] in Blood by Manual count (LOINC)*: manual counting on a haemocytometer (rare in modern practice; mostly historical or research). **Note on units.** Recommended unit: **`10*12/L`** (`8734 / 10*12/L — trillion per liter (UCUM)`), aligned with NPU [2]. LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS` is `10*6/uL` (`8815 / 10*6/uL — million per microliter (UCUM)`), which is the same physical quantity in US notation. Conversion: `1 ×10¹²/L = 1 ×10⁶/µL` (factor 1). ## Excluded Concepts No concepts are explicitly excluded. The set is defined by anchoring on the LOINC Group for erythrocyte number concentration in blood and pulling in all its descendants. This naturally excludes: - **Other specimens**: cord blood (e.g. `45888181 / 71663-9 — Erythrocytes [#/volume] in Cord blood`), fetal blood, body fluid, CSF, dialysis fluid, peritoneal/pleural fluid, urine — out of scope for a "blood" concept set. - **Derived measurements**: mean corpuscular volume (MCV), mean corpuscular haemoglobin (MCH), red cell distribution width (RDW), nucleated red cells, reticulocyte counts — these are separate measurands. - **Volume fraction of erythrocytes** (i.e. hematocrit) — a different quantity, captured in the dedicated "Hematocrit in blood" concept set. - **Aggregations** like `(Maximum value during study)` — out of scope. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports "RBC", "Erythrocytes", "GR" (globules rouges) or similar without specifying the method: `3026361 / 26453-1 — Erythrocytes [#/volume] in Blood`. en.name: Hemoglobin in blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Haemoglobin (Hb) is the iron-containing oxygen-transport protein contained in erythrocytes [1]. The concentration of haemoglobin in blood is the primary laboratory marker of anaemia (decreased) and polycythaemia (increased). It is part of every routine complete blood count (CBC) and is also measured directly on point-of-care blood-gas analysers via co-oximetry. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a haematology analyser on whole blood (EDTA tube), or by a blood-gas/co-oximetry channel on arterial, venous, capillary or mixed venous blood. Results are reported either as a **mass concentration** (`g/L` or `g/dL`, the dominant convention worldwide) or as a **substance concentration** (`mmol/L`, an SI variant explicitly recognised by ICSH/IFCC/WASP [3] and by NPU [2]; less commonly used in routine practice but encountered in some labs). ## Included Concepts The set is anchored on four LOINC Groups (one per blood specimen — generic, arterial, venous, mixed venous), with their descendants pulled in. Each Group resolves to both the mass-concentration (`[Mass/volume]`) and the substance-concentration (`[Moles/volume]`) variant for that specimen — both are kept in the set because they describe the same measurand reported in different units (see "Note on units" below). Seven additional standard concepts that no Group covers (by-Oximetry, by-calculation, and Capillary blood variants) are added explicitly. Within the set, concepts vary by specimen, method (analyser vs co-oximetry vs calculation), and clinical context. ### Generic blood (method not specified) - *3000963 / 718-7 — Hemoglobin [Mass/volume] in Blood (LOINC)*: most widely used LOINC code for the mass-concentration form, returned by haematology analysers when the method is not detailed. - *40762351 / 59260-0 — Hemoglobin [Moles/volume] in Blood (LOINC)*: substance-concentration form, used by labs that report haemoglobin in `mmol/L` (the SI alternative recognised by ICSH/IFCC/WASP [3]). ### Method-specific - *40758903 / 55782-7 — Hemoglobin [Mass/volume] in Blood by Oximetry (LOINC)*: co-oximetry on a blood-gas analyser (typical of point-of-care devices). - *3027484 / 20509-6 — Hemoglobin [Mass/volume] in Blood by calculation (LOINC)*: derived from other measurements (e.g. from hematocrit), rather than directly measured. ### Specimen-specific (mass concentration) - *3002173 / 30313-1 — Hemoglobin [Mass/volume] in Arterial blood (LOINC)*: explicit arterial sample (often from a blood-gas analyser). - *3004119 / 30350-3 — Hemoglobin [Mass/volume] in Venous blood (LOINC)*: explicit venous sample. - *3006184 / 30352-9 — Hemoglobin [Mass/volume] in Capillary blood (LOINC)*: capillary heel-prick or fingerstick (neonatal, point-of-care). - *3007302 / 30351-1 — Hemoglobin [Mass/volume] in Mixed venous blood (LOINC)*: mixed venous sample (typically from a Swan-Ganz catheter). ### Specimen-specific (substance concentration) - *21490721 / 75928-2 — Hemoglobin [Moles/volume] in Arterial blood (LOINC)* - *1002216 / 93846-4 — Hemoglobin [Moles/volume] in Venous blood (LOINC)* - *1092194 / 105300-8 — Hemoglobin [Moles/volume] in Mixed venous blood (LOINC)* ### Specimen + method combinations (oximetry on a specific specimen) - *3006239 / 14775-1 — Hemoglobin [Mass/volume] in Arterial blood by Oximetry (LOINC)* - *46235392 / 76769-9 — Hemoglobin [Mass/volume] in Venous blood by Oximetry (LOINC)* - *46235391 / 76768-1 — Hemoglobin [Mass/volume] in Mixed venous blood by Oximetry (LOINC)* - *1616317 / 97556-5 — Hemoglobin [Mass/volume] in Capillary blood by Oximetry (LOINC)* **Note on units.** - **Recommended unit for `[Mass/volume]` concepts**: **`g/L`** (`8636 / g/L — gram per liter (UCUM)`), aligned with NPU [2] and ICSH 1995 [3]. LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS` is `g/dL` for the older non-oximetry concepts and `g/L` for the more recent oximetry concepts; the project standardises on `g/L`. - **Recommended unit for `[Moles/volume]` concepts**: **`mmol/L`** (`8753 / mmol/L — millimole per liter (UCUM)`), per LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS`. - **Conversion between mass and substance concentration**: ICSH 1995 [3] establishes the convention: when haemoglobin is reported in `mmol/L` it is, by international agreement (ICSH/IFCC/WASP), the substance concentration **per haem group / per Fe atom / per globin monomer** (notation `Hb(Fe)`), not per haemoglobin tetramer (`Hb(4Fe)`). The relative molecular mass of the haemoglobin monomer is **16,114.5 g/mol** (= 64,458 / 4) [3]. The resulting conversion factors are: `1 mmol/L = 16.1145 g/L`, `1 g/L = 0.06206 mmol/L` (and `1 mmol/L ≈ 1.6114 g/dL`, `1 g/dL ≈ 0.6206 mmol/L`). These factors are recorded in `units/unit_conversions.json` so that source values reported in `mmol/L` are converted to the recommended `g/L` at storage time. Pure-unit conversions for the mass form (`g/dL ↔ g/L`, factor 10) are also recorded. ## Excluded Concepts No concepts are explicitly excluded. The following LOINC concepts that exist for haemoglobin in blood are deliberately not part of this set: - **Cord/fetal blood and blood-product specimens**: - `40757420 / 54289-4 — Hemoglobin [Mass/volume] in Blood from Blood product unit` - `40763941 / 61180-6 — Hemoglobin [Mass/volume] in Blood from Fetus` - cord blood variants — out of scope for a routine "blood" concept set. - **Pre-therapeutic phlebotomy** (`3048275 / 48725-6 — Hemoglobin [Mass/volume] in Blood --pre therapeutic phlebotomy`) — research/protocol context. - **Calculated specimen-specific variants** (`1091111 / 105040-0 — Hemoglobin [Mass/volume] in Mixed venous blood by calculation`, `1091321 / 105274-5 — Hemoglobin [Mass/volume] in Venous blood by calculation`) — recently introduced LOINC codes; rare in real-world data. Not currently included; consider adding if a source uses them. - **Central venous variants** (`1617122 / 97550-8 — Hemoglobin [Mass/volume] in Central venous blood by calculation`, `1617021 / 97555-7 — Hemoglobin [Mass/volume] in Central venous blood by Oximetry`) — niche, rarely reported separately. Treat central venous as venous. - **Free haemoglobin** (`Hemoglobin.free`), haemoglobin variants (HbA1c, HbA2, HbF, HbS), methaemoglobin, carboxyhaemoglobin — these are separate measurands captured in other concept sets. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports "Hb", "Hgb", "haemoglobin" or similar without further specification: `3000963 / 718-7 — Hemoglobin [Mass/volume] in Blood`. By far the most common LOINC code. - **Specimen-specific source**: if the source explicitly states "arterial", "venous", "capillary", or "mixed venous" blood, map to the corresponding specimen concept (`3002173 / 30313-1 — Hemoglobin [Mass/volume] in Arterial blood`, etc.). If the source is a blood-gas analyser and explicitly co-oximetry, prefer the specimen + oximetry combination (e.g. `3006239 / 14775-1 — Hemoglobin [Mass/volume] in Arterial blood by Oximetry`). - **Method-specific source**: map "co-oximetry" results to `40758903 / 55782-7 — Hemoglobin [Mass/volume] in Blood by Oximetry` if no specimen is stated, or to the specimen + Oximetry variant if both are known. Map calculated results (Hb derived from hematocrit) to `3027484 / 20509-6 — Hemoglobin [Mass/volume] in Blood by calculation`. Otherwise, default to `3000963 / 718-7 — Hemoglobin [Mass/volume] in Blood` — do **not** infer the method from the analyser brand. - **Source reports `mmol/L`**: map to the corresponding `[Moles/volume]` concept (`40762351 / 59260-0 — Hemoglobin [Moles/volume] in Blood` for the generic case, or the specimen-specific variant if applicable). Do **not** convert manually to `g/L` — the unit conversions in `units/unit_conversions.json` handle this automatically using the ICSH `Hb(Fe)` convention. - **Do not confuse with**: hematocrit (volume fraction of erythrocytes), erythrocyte count, MCH, MCHC, free haemoglobin, glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c), methaemoglobin, carboxyhaemoglobin, or haemoglobin on non-blood specimens — all belong to other concept sets. ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 718-7 — Hemoglobin [Mass/volume] in Blood (Part description for "Hemoglobin"). Available: https://loinc.org/718-7/ [2] Nomenclature for Properties and Units (NPU). IFCC/IUPAC. NPU codes (current release). Available: https://npu-terminology.org/npu-database/ [3] International Council for Standardisation in Haematology (ICSH), Expert Panel on Haemoglobinometry. Recommendations for reference method for haemoglobinometry in human blood (ICSH standard 1995) and specifications for international haemiglobincyanide standard (4th edition). J Clin Pathol. 1996;49(4):271-274. Available: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8655699/

LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS` is `10*3/uL` (`8848 / 10*3/uL — thousand per microliter (UCUM)`), which is the same physical quantity in US notation. Conversion: `1 ×10⁹/L = 1 ×10³/µL` (factor 1). ## Excluded Concepts No concepts are explicitly excluded. This naturally excludes: - **Lymphocyte subsets** — T cells (CD3, CD4, CD8), B cells (CD19, CD20), NK cells (CD56), regulatory T cells, etc. — out of scope. All correspond to the same physical quantity and can be converted to the recommended `10*9/L` (factor 1 with `10*3/uL`, factor 0.001 with `/uL`). - **Do not confuse with**: lymphocyte percentage, T/B/NK subset counts, atypical lymphocytes, or lymphocytes on non-blood specimens — all belong to other concept sets. ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. en.name: Monocytes in blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Monocytes are circulating mononuclear phagocytes (typically 2–10 % of leukocytes) that differentiate into tissue macrophages and dendritic cells [1]. The absolute monocyte count is part of the CBC differential and is used to assess chronic inflammation, infection, and haematological disorders (notably chronic myelomonocytic leukaemia, where monocytes are persistently elevated). The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a haematology analyser as part of the differential white-cell count, on whole blood (EDTA tube). It is collected in routine biochemistry and intensive care. Results are reported as an absolute number concentration, typically in **`10*9/L`** (NPU SI convention, equivalent to `G/L`) or in the US notation **`10*3/uL`** (numerically identical: `1 ×10⁹/L = 1 ×10³/µL`). ## Included Concepts The set is anchored on the LOINC Group `40654069 / LG32885-2 — Monocytes|Number Concentration (count/vol)|Moment in time|Blood (LOINC Group)` and pulls in all its descendants. This resolves to four standard concepts, which differ by counting method. ### Generic (method not specified) - *3001604 / 26484-6 — Monocytes [#/volume] in Blood (LOINC)*: most widely used LOINC code, returned by haematology analysers when the method is not detailed. ### Method-specific - *3033575 / 742-7 — Monocytes [#/volume] in Blood by Automated count (LOINC)*: automated impedance, optical or flow-cytometric count (most common in routine practice). - *3034107 / 743-5 — Monocytes [#/volume] in Blood by Manual count (LOINC)*: manual differential on a stained smear under microscope. - *1092234 / 104548-3 — Monocytes [#/volume] in Blood by Flow cytometry (FC) (LOINC)*: dedicated flow-cytometry assay (e.g. for CMML diagnostic workup, where monocyte subsets are quantified). Recently introduced LOINC code; rare in routine data. **Note on units.** Recommended unit: **`10*9/L`** (`9444 / 10*9/L — billion per liter (UCUM)`), aligned with NPU [2]. LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS` is `10*3/uL` (`8848 / 10*3/uL — thousand per microliter (UCUM)`), which is the same physical quantity in US notation. Conversion: `1 ×10⁹/L = 1 ×10³/µL` (factor 1). ## Excluded Concepts No concepts are explicitly excluded. The set is defined by anchoring on the LOINC Group for monocyte number concentration in blood and pulling in all its descendants. This naturally excludes: - **Percentage / fraction variants** — monocytes as a fraction of total leukocytes (`Monocytes/100 leukocytes`, `Monocytes/Leukocytes [Pure number fraction]`) — out of scope, separate measurand. - **Aggregated counts** — monocytes combined with other cell types, e.g. `3005836 / 32349-3 — Basophils+Eosinophils+Monocytes [#/volume] in Blood`, are not monocyte-specific. - **Monocyte subsets** (classical / intermediate / non-classical, defined by CD14/CD16) — out of scope, captured under flow-cytometry concept sets if needed. - **Other specimens**: cord blood, fetal blood, body fluid, bone marrow, CSF, dialysis fluid, peritoneal/pleural/synovial fluid — out of scope for a "blood" concept set. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports "Monocytes", "Mono", "MO#" or similar absolute count without specifying the method: `3001604 / 26484-6 — Monocytes [#/volume] in Blood`. By far the most common. - **Method-specific source**: if the source explicitly states "automated", "manual" or "flow cytometry", map to the corresponding method-specific concept. Otherwise, default to `3001604 / 26484-6 — Monocytes [#/volume] in Blood`. - **Source reports a percentage** (e.g. `8 %` of leukocytes): this is **not** the same measurand. It belongs to a different concept set (monocyte percentage). - **Unit notation**: source systems may report `10*9/L`, `G/L`, `10*3/uL`, `K/uL`, or `/uL` (×1000). All correspond to the same physical quantity and can be converted to the recommended `10*9/L` (factor 1 with `10*3/uL`, factor 0.001 with `/uL`). - **Do not confuse with**: monocyte percentage, monocyte subsets (classical/intermediate/non-classical), aggregations like Basophils+Eosinophils+Monocytes, or monocytes on non-blood specimens — all belong to other concept sets. ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 26484-6 — Monocytes [#/volume] in Blood (Part description for "Monocytes"). Available: https://loinc.org/26484-6/ [2] Nomenclature for Properties and Units (NPU). IFCC/IUPAC. en.name: Neutrophils in blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Neutrophils are the most abundant circulating leukocytes (typically 50–70 % of leukocytes), and the front-line responders of the innate immune system against bacterial and fungal infections [1]. The absolute neutrophil count (ANC) is part of the CBC differential and is critical for assessing risk of bacterial infection: severe neutropenia (ANC < 0.5 ×10⁹/L) is the threshold for febrile-neutropenia management in oncology and intensive care. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a haematology analyser as part of the differential white-cell count, on whole blood (EDTA tube). It is collected in routine biochemistry and intensive care. Results are reported as an absolute number concentration, typically in **`10*9/L`** (NPU SI convention, equivalent to `G/L`) or in the US notation **`10*3/uL`** (numerically identical: `1 ×10⁹/L = 1 ×10³/µL`). ## Included Concepts The set is anchored on the LOINC Group `40654088 / LG32886-0 — Neutrophils|Number Concentration (count/vol)|Moment in time|Blood (LOINC Group)` and pulls in all its descendants. This resolves to three standard concepts, which differ only by counting method. ### Generic (method not specified) - *3017732 / 26499-4 — Neutrophils [#/volume] in Blood (LOINC)*: most widely used LOINC code, returned by haematology analysers when the method is not detailed. ### Method-specific - *3013650 / 751-8 — Neutrophils [#/volume] in Blood by Automated count (LOINC)*: automated impedance, optical or flow-cytometric count (most common in routine practice). - *3017501 / 753-4 — Neutrophils [#/volume] in Blood by Manual count (LOINC)*: manual differential on a stained smear under microscope (used as a confirmation when the analyser flags the result, or in low-resource settings). **Note on units.** Recommended unit: **`10*9/L`** (`9444 / 10*9/L — billion per liter (UCUM)`), aligned with NPU [2]. LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS` is `10*3/uL` (`8848 / 10*3/uL — thousand per microliter (UCUM)`), which is the same physical quantity in US notation. Conversion: `1 ×10⁹/L = 1 ×10³/µL` (factor 1). ## Excluded Concepts No concepts are explicitly excluded. The set is defined by anchoring on the LOINC Group for neutrophil number concentration in blood and pulling in all its descendants. This naturally excludes: - **Percentage / fraction variants** — neutrophils as a fraction of total leukocytes (`Neutrophils/100 leukocytes`, `Neutrophils/Leukocytes [Pure number fraction]`) — out of scope, separate measurand. - **Maturation-stage variants** — segmented neutrophils (`Neutrophils.segmented`), band-form neutrophils (`Neutrophils.band form`), immature granulocytes, hyper-/hyposegmented neutrophils — these are subpopulation counts, captured separately if needed. - **Other specimens**: cord blood, fetal blood, body fluid, bone marrow, CSF, dialysis fluid, peritoneal/pleural/synovial fluid — out of scope for a "blood" concept set. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports "Neutrophils", "Neutro", "PNN" (polynucléaires neutrophiles), "ANC" (absolute neutrophil count) or similar absolute count without specifying the method: `3017732 / 26499-4 — Neutrophils [#/volume] in Blood`. By far the most common. - **Method-specific source**: if the source explicitly states "automated" or "manual", map to the corresponding method-specific concept. Otherwise, default to `3017732 / 26499-4 — Neutrophils [#/volume] in Blood`. - **Source reports segmented + band counts separately**: those belong to subpopulation concept sets, not to the total neutrophil count. If only a total is needed, sum them upstream of mapping or use the total field directly when available. - **Source reports a percentage** (e.g. `65 %` of leukocytes): this is **not** the same measurand. It belongs to a different concept set (neutrophil percentage). - **Unit notation**: source systems may report `10*9/L`, `G/L`, `10*3/uL`, `K/uL`, or `/uL` (×1000). All correspond to the same physical quantity and can be converted to the recommended `10*9/L` (factor 1 with `10*3/uL`, factor 0.001 with `/uL`). - **Do not confuse with**: neutrophil percentage, segmented/band neutrophil subpopulations, immature granulocytes, or neutrophils on non-blood specimens — all belong to other concept sets. ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 26499-4 — Neutrophils [#/volume] in Blood (Part description for "Neutrophils"). Available: https://loinc.org/26499-4/ [2] Nomenclature for Properties and Units (NPU). IFCC/IUPAC. en.name: Platelets in blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Platelets (thrombocytes) are small anuclear blood cell fragments produced by megakaryocytes that mediate primary haemostasis [1]. The platelet count is part of the complete blood count (CBC) and is used to assess bleeding risk (thrombocytopenia, e.g. < 50 ×10⁹/L for surgical risk, < 10 ×10⁹/L for spontaneous bleeding) and thrombotic risk (thrombocytosis). The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a haematology analyser as part of the CBC, on whole blood (EDTA tube) or, less commonly, on platelet-rich plasma. It is collected in routine biochemistry and intensive care. Results are reported as a number concentration, typically in **`10*9/L`** (NPU SI convention, equivalent to `G/L`) or in the US notation **`10*3/uL`** (numerically identical: `1 ×10⁹/L = 1 ×10³/µL`). ## Included Concepts The set is anchored on **two** LOINC Groups, one for whole blood and one for plasma — real-world data uses either matrix: - `40654106 / LG32892-8 — Platelets|Number Concentration (count/vol)|Moment in time|Blood (LOINC Group)` - `40654108 / LG32776-3 — Platelets|Number Concentration (count/vol)|Moment in time|Plasma (LOINC Group)` Both pull in their descendants. The set resolves to seven standard concepts, grouped here by specimen and method. ### Whole blood (default) #### Generic (method not specified) - *3007461 / 26515-7 — Platelets [#/volume] in Blood (LOINC)*: most widely used LOINC code for platelet count on whole blood. #### Method-specific - *3024929 / 777-3 — Platelets [#/volume] in Blood by Automated count (LOINC)*: automated impedance or optical count (most common in routine practice). - *1616298 / 97995-5 — Platelets [#/volume] in Blood by Automated count.optical (LOINC)*: explicit optical (laser/fluorescence) count, used by some analysers when impedance results are unreliable (e.g. platelet clumping, fragmented red cells). - *3010834 / 778-1 — Platelets [#/volume] in Blood by Manual count (LOINC)*: manual count on a haemocytometer. - *3031586 / 49497-1 — Platelets [#/volume] in Blood by Estimate (LOINC)*: visually estimated from a stained smear (rare, used as a sanity check when the analyser flags the result). ### Plasma - *3006297 / 26516-5 — Platelets [#/volume] in Plasma (LOINC)*: generic platelet count on plasma. - *3016682 / 13056-7 — Platelets [#/volume] in Plasma by Automated count (LOINC)*: automated count on plasma. **Note on units.** Recommended unit: **`10*9/L`** (`9444 / 10*9/L — billion per liter (UCUM)`), aligned with NPU [2]. LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS` is `10*3/uL` (`8848 / 10*3/uL — thousand per microliter (UCUM)`), which is the same physical quantity in US notation. Conversion: `1 ×10⁹/L = 1 ×10³/µL` (factor 1). ## Excluded Concepts No concepts are explicitly excluded. The set is defined by anchoring on the LOINC Groups for platelet number concentration in blood and in plasma and pulling in all their descendants. This naturally excludes: - **Cord blood** (`Platelets|Number Concentration (count/vol)|Moment in time|Blood - cord` group) — out of scope for a routine "blood" concept set. - **Mean platelet volume (MPV)**, **platelet distribution width (PDW)**, **immature platelet fraction (IPF)**, **plateletcrit (PCT)** — different measurands captured under their own concept sets if needed. - **Platelet aggregation tests**, **platelet activation markers** (e.g. CD62P), **platelet function assays** — separate measurands. - **Other specimens**: body fluid, ascites, peritoneal/pleural fluid, dialysis fluid — out of scope. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports "Platelets", "PLT" or similar without further specification: `3007461 / 26515-7 — Platelets [#/volume] in Blood`. By far the most common LOINC code, used for whole-blood EDTA samples on a haematology analyser. - **Method-specific source**: if the source explicitly states "automated", "manual" or "estimate", map to the corresponding method-specific blood concept (`3024929 / 777-3 — Platelets [#/volume] in Blood by Automated count`, `3010834 / 778-1 — Platelets [#/volume] in Blood by Manual count`, `3031586 / 49497-1 — Platelets [#/volume] in Blood by Estimate`). If the source explicitly states "optical count" (e.g. CD61 fluorescence-based count for thrombocytopenia confirmation), map to `1616298 / 97995-5 — Platelets [#/volume] in Blood by Automated count.optical`. Otherwise, default to `3007461 / 26515-7 — Platelets [#/volume] in Blood` — do **not** infer the method from the analyser brand. - **Source explicitly reports plasma matrix** (e.g. citrated plasma): map to `3006297 / 26516-5 — Platelets [#/volume] in Plasma` (generic) or `3016682 / 13056-7 — Platelets [#/volume] in Plasma by Automated count` (if automated). Plasma platelet counts are uncommon in routine biochemistry — a typical EDTA CBC reports the whole-blood concept. - **Unit notation**: source systems may report `10*9/L`, `G/L`, `10*3/uL`, `K/uL`, or `/uL` (×1000). All correspond to the same physical quantity and can be converted to the recommended `10*9/L` (factor 1 with `10*3/uL`, factor 0.001 with `/uL`). - **Do not confuse with**: mean platelet volume (MPV), platelet distribution width (PDW), immature platelet fraction (IPF), plateletcrit, platelet aggregation/function tests, or platelets on non-blood/plasma specimens — all belong to other concept sets. ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 26515-7 — Platelets [#/volume] in Blood (Part description for "Platelets"). Available: https://loinc.org/26515-7/ [2] Nomenclature for Properties and Units (NPU). IFCC/IUPAC. NPU codes (current release). Available: https://npu-terminology.org/npu-database/

en.name: Reticulocytes in blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Reticulocytes are immature, anucleate red blood cells that have just been released from the bone marrow and still contain residual ribosomal RNA, visible as a reticulum after supravital staining [1]. The reticulocyte count reflects bone-marrow erythropoietic activity: it is elevated in regenerative anaemias (haemolysis, blood loss) and depressed in non-regenerative anaemias (aplasia, iron/B12/folate deficiency, chemotherapy). The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a haematology analyser using fluorescent staining of nucleic acids, on whole blood (EDTA tube). It is collected when an unexplained anaemia or a bone-marrow recovery is being investigated. Results are reported as a number concentration, typically in **`10*9/L`** (NPU SI convention, equivalent to `G/L`) or in the US notation **`10*3/uL`** (numerically identical: `1 ×10⁹/L = 1 ×10³/µL`). ## Included Concepts The set is anchored on the LOINC Group `40654117 / LG32882-9 — Reticulocytes|Number Concentration (count/vol)|Moment in time|Blood (LOINC Group)` and pulls in all its descendants. This resolves to four standard concepts, which differ by counting method. ### Generic (method not specified) - *3023520 / 14196-0 — Reticulocytes [#/volume] in Blood (LOINC)*: most widely used LOINC code, returned by haematology analysers when the method is not detailed. ### Method-specific - *40763528 / 60474-4 — Reticulocytes [#/volume] in Blood by Automated count (LOINC)*: automated flow-cytometric count using fluorescent nucleic-acid stains (most common in modern practice). - *3041154 / 40665-2 — Reticulocytes [#/volume] in Blood by Manual count (LOINC)*: manual count on a stained smear (e.g. new methylene blue), historical method. - *3037637 / 42758-3 — Reticulocytes [#/volume] in Blood by calculation (LOINC)*: derived from the reticulocyte percentage and the absolute red-cell count, rather than directly counted. **Note on units.** Recommended unit: **`10*9/L`** (`9444 / 10*9/L — billion per liter (UCUM)`), aligned with NPU [2]. LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS` is `10*3/uL` (`8848 / 10*3/uL — thousand per microliter (UCUM)`) for the absolute count, which is the same physical quantity in US notation. Conversion: `1 ×10⁹/L = 1 ×10³/µL` (factor 1). Note: LOINC lists `10*3/L` as the example unit for `42758-3`, which is almost certainly a typographical inconsistency in the LOINC distribution; the value is the same physical quantity as `10*3/uL`. Map accordingly. ## Excluded Concepts No concepts are explicitly excluded. The set is defined by anchoring on the LOINC Group for reticulocyte number concentration in blood and pulling in all its descendants. This naturally excludes: - **Reticulocyte percentage / fraction variants** — `Reticulocytes/100 erythrocytes`, `Reticulocytes/Erythrocytes [Pure number fraction]` — these describe a relative composition, not an absolute count, and are a separate measurand. - **Reticulocyte indices** — mean reticulocyte volume (MRV), reticulocyte haemoglobin content (CHr / Ret-He), immature reticulocyte fraction (IRF), high/medium/low fluorescence ratios — these are derived parameters captured under their own concept sets if needed. - **Other specimens**: cord blood, fetal blood, body fluid, bone marrow — out of scope for a "blood" concept set. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports "Reticulocytes", "Retic", "Ret#" or similar absolute count without specifying the method: `3023520 / 14196-0 — Reticulocytes [#/volume] in Blood`. By far the most common. - **Method-specific source**: if the source explicitly states "automated", "manual" or "calculation", map to the corresponding method-specific concept. Otherwise, default to `3023520 / 14196-0 — Reticulocytes [#/volume] in Blood`. - **Source reports a percentage** (e.g. `1.5 %` of erythrocytes): this is **not** the same measurand. It belongs to a different concept set (reticulocyte percentage). Many older datasets report only the percentage. - **Unit notation**: source systems may report `10*9/L`, `G/L`, `10*3/uL`, `K/uL`, or `/uL` (×1000). All correspond to the same physical quantity and can be converted to the recommended `10*9/L` (factor 1 with `10*3/uL`, factor 0.001 with `/uL`). - **Do not confuse with**: reticulocyte percentage, mean reticulocyte volume (MRV), reticulocyte haemoglobin content (CHr / Ret-He), immature reticulocyte fraction (IRF), or reticulocytes on non-blood specimens — all belong to other concept sets. ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 14196-0 — Reticulocytes [#/volume] in Blood (Part description for "Reticulocytes"). Available: https://loinc.org/14196-0/ [2] Nomenclature for Properties and Units (NPU). IFCC/IUPAC. en.name: Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) in blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) is a cytoplasmic enzyme present in most tissues; its release into the blood follows cellular damage. The serum or plasma activity is measured as a non-specific marker of tissue injury (haemolysis, liver, muscle, malignancy) [1]. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a biochemistry analyser. Results are reported as an enzymatic activity in U/L (international units per litre) [2]. ## Included Concepts The set is anchored on one LOINC Hierarchy concept (scoped to `Chemistry - non-challenge`), with its descendants pulled in. The set resolves to three LOINC "Lab Test" concepts in serum or plasma. ### Serum or plasma (default specimen) - *3016436 / 2532-0 — Lactate dehydrogenase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: generic LOINC code, method-agnostic. Most widely used. - *3022250 / 14804-9 — Lactate dehydrogenase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum or Plasma by Lactate to pyruvate reaction (LOINC)*: same measurand, with the assay direction explicit. - *3005225 / 14805-6 — Lactate dehydrogenase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum or Plasma by Pyruvate to lactate reaction (LOINC)*: same measurand, with the assay direction explicit. The two reaction directions yield different absolute values (lactate→pyruvate is conventionally ~2× higher than pyruvate→lactate); the LOINC code preserves this method information. **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS`: **`U/L`**, spelled **`[U]/L`** in UCUM and in the OMOP vocabulary (OMOP concept 8645 — unit per litre). Source systems may report `U/L` or `IU/L`; the two are numerically equal. ## Excluded Concepts No concepts are explicitly excluded by name. The set deliberately omits the following LOINC concepts: - **Red Blood Cells specimens**: intra-erythrocytic LDH, specialised research measurement. - **Urine, CSF, body fluid and other specimens**: out of scope for a "blood" concept set. - **LDH isoenzymes** (LDH-1 through LDH-5): different measurands, captured by dedicated concept sets when needed. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports "LDH", "lactate dehydrogenase", "lactic acid dehydrogenase" without further specification: `3016436 / 2532-0 — Lactate dehydrogenase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum or Plasma`. By far the most common LOINC code. - **Source explicitly mentions the assay direction**: map to the corresponding `14804-9` (lactate-to-pyruvate) or `14805-6` (pyruvate-to-lactate) code. The two are **not numerically equivalent** — preserve the source method. - **Do not confuse with**: LDH isoenzymes (LDH-1 to LDH-5), lactate (the metabolite, a different concept set), pyruvate. ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 2532-0 — Lactate dehydrogenase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum or Plasma. Available: https://loinc.org/2532-0/ [2] Nomenclature for Properties and Units (NPU). IFCC/IUPAC. NPU codes (current release). Available: https://npu-terminology.org/npu-database/

en.name: Albumin in blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Albumin is the main protein synthesised by the liver, accounting for ~60 % of total plasma protein. Its concentration in blood reflects the long-term nutritional and synthetic status, and is decreased in chronic liver disease, malnutrition, nephrotic syndrome, and systemic inflammation [1]. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a biochemistry analyser. Results are reported as a mass concentration in g/L (SI unit) or g/dL [2]. This concept set aggregates albumin measurements across blood specimens (serum, plasma and unspecified blood). ## Included Concepts The set is anchored on four LOINC Hierarchy concepts (one per blood specimen, scoped to `Chemistry - non-challenge`), with their descendants pulled in. After exclusions, the set resolves to 11 LOINC "Lab Test" concepts, grouped here by specimen. ### Serum or plasma (default specimen for routine biochemistry) - *3024561 / 1751-7 — Albumin [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: generic LOINC code, method-agnostic. Most widely used. - *3028286 / 2862-1 — Albumin [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma by Electrophoresis (LOINC)*: same measurand, with electrophoresis explicit. - *3965752 / 101198-0 — Albumin [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma by Nephelometry (LOINC)*: same measurand, with nephelometry explicit. - *40763912 / 61151-7 — Albumin [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma by Bromocresol green (BCG) dye binding method (LOINC)*: same measurand, with BCG dye method explicit. - *40763913 / 61152-5 — Albumin [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma by Bromocresol purple (BCP) dye binding method (LOINC)*: same measurand, with BCP dye method explicit. - *40757478 / 54347-0 — Albumin [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: substance concentration form. - *40764995 / 62234-0 — Albumin [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma by Bromocresol purple (BCP) dye binding method (LOINC)*: substance concentration form, BCP method. - *40764996 / 62235-7 — Albumin [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma by Bromocresol green (BCG) dye binding method (LOINC)*: substance concentration form, BCG method. ### Serum - *1260115 / 103577-3 — Albumin [Mass/volume] in Serum by Immunoassay (LOINC)* ### Generic blood (specimen unspecified) - *46235170 / 76631-1 — Albumin [Mass/volume] in Blood by Bromocresol purple (BCP) dye binding method (LOINC)* - *46236953 / 77148-5 — Albumin [Mass/volume] in Serum, Plasma or Blood by Bromocresol purple (BCP) dye binding method (LOINC)*: specimen-agnostic. **Note on units.** Recommended unit: **`8636 / g/L — gram per liter`** (UCUM) for the `[Mass/volume]` codes, and **`8749 / umol/L — micromole per liter`** (UCUM) for the `[Moles/volume]` codes. Both are listed by NPU as accepted forms for plasma albumin (`NPU19673` mass concentration, `NPU01132` substance concentration) [3]. Conversion: `1 g/dL = 10 g/L`. **No conversion bridges the mass and molar codes**, deliberately. Mature human serum albumin (UniProt P02768, chain 25-609) has a molar mass of ≈66.4 kg/mol [4], which would give `1 g/L ≈ 15 µmol/L`. That factor is not registered, for three reasons. First, albumin is standardised and reported as a **mass** concentration — the IFCC/BCR certified reference material ERM-DA470k/IFCC carries certified values in g/L (albumin: 37.2 g/L) [5]. Second, essentially all laboratories report `g/L` or `g/dL`, and the molar LOINC codes are seldom populated. Third, a nominal molar mass would silently propagate the BCG/BCP method bias described below into what looks like an exact unit conversion. Prefer `g/L`; treat a molar result as a separate quantity rather than converting it. **Note on BCG vs. BCP methods.** The bromocresol green (BCG) and bromocresol purple (BCP) dye-binding methods are the two most common laboratory assays for albumin, but they are **not numerically equivalent**: BCG tends to give slightly higher values than BCP, especially at low albumin concentrations, due to differential cross-reactivity with non-albumin plasma proteins. The LOINC code preserves the method when known. Study designs that compare albumin across centres should consider the assay method. ## Excluded Concepts The Serum/Plasma hierarchy above pulls in seven LOINC concepts that are explicitly excluded: ### Ratios — different measurand (ratio to another analyte) - *3020509 / 1759-0 — Albumin/Globulin [Mass Ratio] in Serum or Plasma* - *3046948 / 44429-9 — Albumin/Globulin [Mass Ratio] in Serum or Plasma by Electrophoresis* - *3007424 / 13980-8 — Albumin/Protein.total in Serum or Plasma by Electrophoresis* - *3035472 / 35706-1 — Albumin/Protein.total in Serum or Plasma* - *43055432 / 72598-6 — Albumin/Protein.total [Pure mass fraction] in Serum or Plasma by Electrophoresis* ### Qualitative — different measurand (presence, not a concentration) - *3043798 / 43712-9 — Albumin [Presence] in Serum or Plasma* ### Timed dialysis protocol — protocol-specific timepoint, out of scope - *3018721 / 21058-3 — Albumin [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma --2 hours post peritoneal dialysis* The set also deliberately omits the following LOINC concepts: - **Urine specimens** (e.g. microalbuminuria): captured by a separate concept set when relevant. - **CSF, body fluid, ascites, peritoneal fluid, pleural fluid and other specimens**: out of scope for a "blood" concept set. - **Fetus specimens**: out of scope. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports "albumin", "Alb", "albuminémie" without further specification: `3024561 / 1751-7 — Albumin [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma`. By far the most common LOINC code. - **Source mentions BCG or BCP method**: map to the corresponding `61151-7` (BCG) or `61152-5` (BCP) code. The two are **not numerically equivalent** — preserve the source method when known. - **Source reports microalbuminuria**: do **not** map to this concept set. Urinary albumin is a different measurand, captured by a separate concept set when relevant. - **Source reports albumin/globulin ratio or albumin/total protein ratio**: do **not** map. These are different measurands. - **Do not confuse with**: urinary albumin (microalbuminuria), total protein, prealbumin (transthyretin, a different protein). ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 1751-7 — Albumin [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma. Available: https://loinc.org/1751-7/ [2] Nomenclature for Properties and Units (NPU). IFCC/IUPAC. NPU codes (current release). Available: https://npu-terminology.org/npu-database/ [3] Nomenclature for Properties and Units (NPU). NPU19673 (P—Albumin; mass conc.) and NPU01132 (P—Albumin; subst. conc.). Available: https://npu-terminology.org/npu-database/ [4] UniProt Consortium. P02768 (ALBU_HUMAN) — Albumin, Homo sapiens. Available: https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P02768/entry [5] European Commission, Joint Research Centre, IRMM. Certification of proteins in the human serum reference material ERM-DA470k/IFCC. EUR 23431 EN. 2008. Available: https://publications.jrc.ec.europa.eu/repository/handle/JRC46604

en.name: Bicarbonate in blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Bicarbonate (HCO3⁻) is the main extracellular buffer and a key component of acid-base balance [1]. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a biochemistry analyser, a blood gas analyser, or a point-of-care device. Results are reported as a substance concentration in mmol/L (SI unit) or mEq/L; the two are numerically equivalent for bicarbonate [2]. This concept set aggregates bicarbonate measurements across blood specimens (serum, plasma, arterial, venous, capillary, mixed venous, central venous and unspecified blood). Cord blood specimens are excluded — they reflect the foetal-placental circulation at birth and are not physiologically equivalent to post-natal blood from the same neonate. **Note: actual vs. standard bicarbonate.** LOINC distinguishes two forms: - **Actual bicarbonate** — calculated from the patient's measured pH and PaCO2 at the time of sampling. - **Standard bicarbonate** — recalculated as if PaCO2 were 40 mmHg at 37 °C, to isolate the metabolic component independently of the respiratory status. In the absence of respiratory disturbance the two values are nearly identical, but they can diverge substantially in respiratory acidosis or alkalosis. **Both forms are included in this concept set** because most clinical sources and studies aggregate them under "bicarbonate". Study designs that explicitly compare actual vs. standard bicarbonate should preserve the distinction at the source value level. ## Included Concepts The set is anchored on nine LOINC Hierarchy concepts (one per blood specimen, scoped to `Chemistry - non-challenge`), with their descendants pulled in. It resolves to 13 LOINC "Lab Test" concepts, grouped here by specimen. ### Serum or plasma (default specimen for routine biochemistry) - *3016293 / 1963-8 — Bicarbonate [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: most widely used LOINC code worldwide. - *42868453 / 69964-5 — Bicarbonate [Moles/volume] standard in Plasma (LOINC)*: standard form. - *40757490 / 54359-5 — Bicarbonate [Moles/volume] in Plasma --post dialysis (LOINC)*: point-in-time measurement immediately after a haemodialysis session. - *3050416 / 48631-6 — Bicarbonate [Moles/volume] in Serum --post dialysis (LOINC)*: point-in-time measurement immediately after a haemodialysis session. ### Generic blood (specimen unspecified) - *3006576 / 1959-6 — Bicarbonate [Moles/volume] in Blood (LOINC)* ### Arterial blood - *3008152 / 1960-4 — Bicarbonate [Moles/volume] in Arterial blood (LOINC)*: typically reported by a blood gas analyser. - *3014218 / 19230-2 — Bicarbonate [Moles/volume] standard in Arterial blood (LOINC)*: standard form. ### Venous blood - *3027273 / 14627-4 — Bicarbonate [Moles/volume] in Venous blood (LOINC)* - *3007628 / 19232-8 — Bicarbonate [Moles/volume] standard in Venous blood (LOINC)*: standard form. ### Central venous blood - *1616794 / 97543-3 — Bicarbonate [Moles/volume] in Central venous blood (LOINC)*: from a central venous catheter. - *1617100 / 97544-1 — Bicarbonate [Moles/volume] standard in Central venous blood (LOINC)*: standard form. ### Mixed venous blood - *3025817 / 19229-4 — Bicarbonate [Moles/volume] in Mixed venous blood (LOINC)*: typically from a Swan-Ganz catheter. - *3006538 / 19233-6 — Bicarbonate [Moles/volume] standard in Mixed venous blood (LOINC)*: standard form. ### Capillary blood - *3015235 / 1961-2 — Bicarbonate [Moles/volume] in Capillary blood (LOINC)*: capillary heel-prick or fingerstick (neonatal, point-of-care). - *3004490 / 19231-0 — Bicarbonate [Moles/volume] standard in Capillary blood (LOINC)*: standard form. **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS`: **`mmol/L`** (concept 8753 — millimole per litre). Source systems may report `mmol/L` or `mEq/L`; for bicarbonate (a monovalent anion) the two are numerically equal. ## Excluded Concepts No concepts are explicitly excluded by name. The set deliberately omits the following LOINC concepts: - **Cord blood specimens** (e.g. `3037749 / 14151-5 — Bicarbonate [Moles/volume] in Cord blood`, `3017809 / 28640-1 — Bicarbonate [Moles/volume] in Arterial cord blood`, `3018650 / 28641-9 — Bicarbonate [Moles/volume] in Venous cord blood`, plus their `standard` variants): physiologically distinct from post-natal blood (foetal-placental circulation at birth). - **Red Blood Cells specimens**: intra-erythrocytic bicarbonate, specialised research measurement. - **Body fluid, CSF, dialysis fluid, peritoneal fluid, pleural fluid, amniotic fluid, water, nonbiological fluid specimens**: out of scope for a "blood" concept set. - **Urine specimens**: out of scope (captured by the separate "Urinary bicarbonate" concept set). ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports "bicarbonate", "HCO3", "total CO2", "tCO2" without further specification: `3016293 / 1963-8 — Bicarbonate [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma`. By far the most common LOINC code. - **Source reports a bicarbonate value from a blood gas analyser** (typically arterial): map to `3008152 / 1960-4 — Bicarbonate [Moles/volume] in Arterial blood`. - **Source explicitly labels the value as "standard bicarbonate"** (or "sHCO3", "sBic"): map to the corresponding `standard` LOINC code for the specimen. Do **not** merge with the actual bicarbonate without checking the study design — the two values can diverge in respiratory disturbances. - **Do not confuse with**: urinary bicarbonate (separate concept set), base excess (different measurand), carbon dioxide partial pressure (PaCO2 — different measurand, separate concept set). ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 1963-8 — Bicarbonate [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma. Available: https://loinc.org/1963-8/ [2] Nomenclature for Properties and Units (NPU). IFCC/IUPAC. NPU codes (current release). Available: https://npu-terminology.org/npu-database/

en.name: Calcium in blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Total calcium in blood includes the protein-bound fraction (mostly to albumin), the complexed fraction (bound to phosphate, citrate, bicarbonate), and the ionized (free, biologically active) fraction. It is the routine biochemistry measurement [1]. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a biochemistry analyser. Results are reported as a substance concentration in mmol/L (SI unit) or as a mass concentration in mg/dL [2]. This concept set aggregates **total calcium** measurements across blood specimens (serum, plasma, arterial, venous, capillary and unspecified blood). Cord blood and fetus specimens are excluded. **Note: total vs ionized vs corrected calcium.** This concept set covers **total calcium** only. The ionized (free) fraction — the biologically active form, sensitive to pH and albumin — is captured by a separate concept set, "Ionized calcium in blood". The total calcium mathematically adjusted for albumin or total protein is captured by another separate concept set, "Corrected calcium in blood". The three are different measurands with different reference ranges and clinical interpretation; they must not be merged. ## Included Concepts The set is anchored on five LOINC Hierarchy concepts (one per blood specimen, scoped to `Chemistry - non-challenge`), with their descendants pulled in. After exclusions, the set resolves to seven LOINC "Lab Test" concepts, grouped here by specimen. ### Serum or plasma (default specimen for routine biochemistry) - *3015377 / 2000-8 — Calcium [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: most widely used LOINC code worldwide. - *3006906 / 17861-6 — Calcium [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: same measurand expressed as mass concentration. - *3042419 / 51950-4 — Calcium [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma --post dialysis (LOINC)*: point-in-time measurement immediately after a haemodialysis session. - *40762241 / 59148-7 — Calcium [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma --post dialysis (LOINC)*: same as `51950-4` expressed as substance concentration. ### Generic blood (specimen unspecified) - *3005162 / 1996-8 — Calcium [Moles/volume] in Blood (LOINC)* - *3032503 / 49765-1 — Calcium [Mass/volume] in Blood (LOINC)*: same measurand expressed as mass concentration. ### Arterial blood - *1092214 / 104654-9 — Calcium [Moles/volume] in Arterial blood (LOINC)* ### Venous blood - *3032543 / 42857-3 — Calcium [Moles/volume] in Venous blood (LOINC)* ### Capillary blood - *3034988 / 42593-4 — Calcium [Moles/volume] in Capillary blood (LOINC)* **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS`: **`mmol/L`** (concept 8753 — millimole per litre) for `[Moles/volume]` codes and **`mg/dL`** (concept 8840) for `[Mass/volume]` codes. Conversion: `1 mmol/L ≈ 4.01 mg/dL` (molar mass of Ca = 40.078 g/mol); `1 mEq/L = 0.5 mmol/L` (calcium is divalent). ## Excluded Concepts The hierarchies above pull in 11 LOINC concepts that are explicitly excluded, grouped by reason for exclusion. ### Corrected for albumin or total protein — derived value, not the raw measurement - *3049461 / 47597-0 — Calcium [Moles/volume] corrected for total protein in Blood* - *3004064 / 18281-6 — Calcium [Moles/volume] corrected for total protein in Serum or Plasma* - *3020059 / 29265-6 — Calcium [Moles/volume] corrected for albumin in Serum or Plasma* - *3030597 / 34907-6 — Calcium [Mass/volume] corrected for total protein in Serum or Plasma* - *3047107 / 46099-8 — Calcium [Mass/volume] corrected for albumin in Serum or Plasma* ### Ratios — different measurand (ratio to another analyte) - *3007393 / 13444-5 — Calcium/Albumin [Mass Ratio] in Serum or Plasma* - *3025742 / 13448-6 — Calcium/Osmolality [Ratio] in Serum or Plasma* - *3007264 / 16525-8 — Calcium/Phosphate [Mass Ratio] in Serum or Plasma* - *3005674 / 16526-6 — Calcium/Protein [Mass Ratio] in Serum or Plasma* - *3026798 / 16527-4 — Calcium/Sodium [Mass Ratio] in Serum or Plasma* ### Qualitative — different measurand (presence, not a concentration) - *3027495 / 27182-5 — Calcium [Presence] in Blood* The set also deliberately omits the following LOINC concepts: - **Ionized (free) calcium**: different measurand, captured by the separate concept set "Ionized calcium in blood". - **Cord blood and fetus specimens**: physiologically distinct from post-natal blood. - **Red Blood Cells specimens**: intra-erythrocytic calcium, specialised research measurement. - **Urine specimens**: out of scope (captured by the separate "Urinary calcium" concept set). - **Body fluid, CSF, calculus (stone), dialysis fluid, peritoneal fluid, pleural fluid, gastric fluid, hair, saliva, semen, stool, synovial fluid, amniotic fluid, water, nonbiological fluid, sweat specimens**: out of scope for a "blood" concept set. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports "calcium", "Ca", "calcaemia" without further specification: `3015377 / 2000-8 — Calcium [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma`. By far the most common LOINC code. - **Source explicitly labels the value as "ionized", "iCa", "free calcium"**: do **not** map to this concept set. Use the separate "Ionized calcium in blood" concept set. - **Source reports a corrected calcium** (corrected for albumin or total protein): do **not** map to this concept set. Use the separate "Corrected calcium in blood" concept set. - **Do not confuse with**: ionized calcium (separate concept set, "Ionized calcium in blood"), corrected calcium (separate concept set, "Corrected calcium in blood"), urinary calcium. ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 2000-8 — Calcium [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma. Available: https://loinc.org/2000-8/ [2] Nomenclature for Properties and Units (NPU). IFCC/IUPAC. NPU codes (current release). Available: https://npu-terminology.org/npu-database/

en.name: Chloride in blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Chloride is the principal extracellular anion. Its concentration in blood is one of the routine electrolyte measurements [1]. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a biochemistry analyser or a point-of-care device. Results are reported as a substance concentration in mmol/L (SI unit) or mEq/L; the two are numerically equivalent for chloride [2]. This concept set aggregates chloride measurements across blood specimens (serum, plasma, arterial, venous, capillary, mixed venous and unspecified blood), because the chloride concentration does not depend meaningfully on the sampling site. ## Included Concepts The set is anchored on seven LOINC Hierarchy concepts (one per blood specimen, scoped to `Chemistry - non-challenge`), with their descendants pulled in. Source systems may report `mmol/L` or `mEq/L`; for chloride (a monovalent anion) the two are numerically equal. ## Excluded Concepts No concepts are explicitly excluded by name. The set deliberately omits the following LOINC concepts: - **Red Blood Cells specimens**: intra-erythrocytic chloride, specialised research measurement. - **Body fluid, CSF, dialysis fluid, gastric fluid, peritoneal fluid, pleural fluid, sweat, saliva, stool, urine, amniotic fluid, vitreous fluid, water, mother's milk specimens**: out of scope for a "blood" concept set. - **Fetus specimens**: out of scope. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports "chloride", "Cl", "chloraemia" without further specification: `3014576 / 2075-0 — Chloride [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma`. By far the most common LOINC code. - **Source reports a chloride value from a blood gas analyser** (typically arterial): map to `3031248 / 41650-3 — Chloride [Moles/volume] in Arterial blood`. - **Specimen unspecified**: map to `46235783 / 77138-6 — Chloride [Moles/volume] in Serum, Plasma or Blood`. - **Do not confuse with**: urinary chloride (different measurand, separate concept set when relevant). ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. en.name: Creatinine in blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Creatinine is a waste product of muscle metabolism, freely filtered by the glomerulus; its concentration in blood is the routine marker of glomerular filtration rate (GFR) and renal function [1]. This concept set aggregates creatinine measurements across blood specimens (serum, plasma, arterial, venous and unspecified blood). Cord blood and fetus specimens are excluded. ## Included Concepts The set is anchored on five LOINC Hierarchy concepts (one per blood specimen, scoped to `Chemistry - non-challenge`), with their descendants pulled in. *3032720 / 50380-5 — Creatinine renal clearance/1.73 sq M.predicted among females by Cockcroft-Gault formula, BSA formula* - *3029545 / 50381-3 — Creatinine renal clearance/1.73 sq M.predicted among males by Cockcroft-Gault formula, BSA formula* ### Timed specimen series — protocol-specific timepoints, out of scope for routine creatinine - *3019397 / 16188-5 — Creatinine [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma --2 hour specimen* - *3035090 / 16189-3 — Creatinine [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma --4 hour specimen* - *43055236 / 72271-0 — Creatinine [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma --pre contrast* ### Ratios — different measurand (ratio to another analyte) - en.name: Glucose in blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Glucose in blood is one of the most frequently ordered laboratory measurements, monitored in diabetes mellitus, critical care, perioperative care, and many other contexts [1]. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a biochemistry analyser, a blood gas analyser, or a point-of-care glucometer. Results are reported as a substance concentration in mmol/L (SI unit, used in Europe) or as a mass concentration in mg/dL (used in the US) [2]. This concept set aggregates glucose measurements across blood specimens (serum, plasma, arterial, venous, capillary, mixed venous and unspecified blood). Cord blood and fetus specimens are excluded. **Note on capillary glucose (glucometer / POCT).** Capillary glucose measured by a glucometer (point-of-care test) is included in this concept set, but data scientists should be aware that: - Capillary glucose can differ from venous/plasma glucose by 10–15 % in the post-prandial state. - Glucometers calibrated to plasma-equivalent values are now standard, but legacy devices may report whole-blood values that are ~10–15 % lower. Study designs that require strict comparability across specimens should preserve the LOINC code and the measurement source value. ## Included Concepts The set is anchored on seven LOINC Hierarchy concepts (one per blood specimen, scoped to `Chemistry - non-challenge`), with their descendants pulled in. After exclusions, the set resolves to 21 LOINC "Lab Test" concepts, grouped here by specimen. ### Serum or plasma (default specimen for routine biochemistry) - *3013826 / 14749-6 — Glucose [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: most widely used LOINC code worldwide (SI form). - *3004501 / 2345-7 — Glucose [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: same measurand expressed as mass concentration (US form). - *40757626 / 54495-7 — Glucose [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma --post dialysis (LOINC)*: point-in-time measurement immediately after a haemodialysis session. ### Generic blood (specimen unspecified) - *3020491 / 15074-8 — Glucose [Moles/volume] in Blood (LOINC)* - *3000483 / 2339-0 — Glucose [Mass/volume] in Blood (LOINC)*: same measurand expressed as mass concentration. - *3011424 / 2340-8 — Glucose [Mass/volume] in Blood by Automated test strip (LOINC)* - *3014053 / 2341-6 — Glucose [Mass/volume] in Blood by Test strip manual (LOINC)* - *43055143 / 72516-8 — Glucose [Moles/volume] in Blood by Automated test strip (LOINC)* - *46235168 / 76629-5 — Fasting glucose [Moles/volume] in Blood (LOINC)*: fasting variant. - *44816672 / 74774-1 — Glucose [Mass/volume] in Serum, Plasma or Blood (LOINC)*: specimen-agnostic. - *46236948 / 77135-2 — Glucose [Moles/volume] in Serum, Plasma or Blood (LOINC)*: specimen-agnostic. - *46236950 / 77145-1 — Fasting glucose [Moles/volume] in Serum, Plasma or Blood (LOINC)*: specimen-agnostic fasting variant. ### Arterial blood - *3044242 / 39481-7 — Glucose [Moles/volume] in Arterial blood (LOINC)* - *3031266 / 41651-1 — Glucose [Mass/volume] in Arterial blood (LOINC)*: same measurand expressed as mass concentration. - *1091312 / 104598-8 — Glucose [Mass/volume] in Arterial blood by Glucometer (LOINC)* ### Venous blood - *3038515 / 39480-9 — Glucose [Moles/volume] in Venous blood (LOINC)* - *3033408 / 41652-9 — Glucose [Mass/volume] in Venous blood (LOINC)*: same measurand expressed as mass concentration. - *1092005 / 104597-0 — Glucose [Mass/volume] in Venous blood by Glucometer (LOINC)* ### Capillary blood (glucometer / POCT) - *3040151 / 51596-5 — Glucose [Moles/volume] in Capillary blood (LOINC)* - *3004077 / 32016-8 — Glucose [Mass/volume] in Capillary blood (LOINC)* - *3001501 / 14743-9 — Glucose [Moles/volume] in Capillary blood by Glucometer (LOINC)*: point-of-care glucometer. - *3034962 / 41653-7 — Glucose [Mass/volume] in Capillary blood by Glucometer (LOINC)*: point-of-care glucometer. ### Mixed venous blood - *1761753 / 100746-7 — Glucose [Moles/volume] in Mixed venous blood (LOINC)* - *1092148 / 104655-6 — Glucose [Mass/volume] in Mixed venous blood (LOINC)* **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS`: **`mmol/L`** (concept 8753 — millimole per litre) for `[Moles/volume]` codes and **`mg/dL`** (concept 8840) for `[Mass/volume]` codes. Conversion: `1 mg/dL ≈ 0.0555 mmol/L` (molar mass of glucose = 180.16 g/mol); `1 mmol/L ≈ 18.02 mg/dL`. ## Excluded Concepts The hierarchies above pull in 15 LOINC concepts that are explicitly excluded, grouped by reason for exclusion. ### Sequential specimen series — protocol-specific (e.g. oral glucose tolerance test, OGTT) - *3032986 / 50206-2 — Glucose [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma --1st specimen* - *3032779 / 50212-0 — Glucose [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma --2nd specimen* - *3030416 / 50213-8 — Glucose [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma --3rd specimen* - *3032719 / 50214-6 — Glucose [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma --4th specimen* - *3028944 / 50215-3 — Glucose [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma --5th specimen* - *3032230 / 50216-1 — Glucose [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma --6th specimen* - *3031928 / 50207-0 — Glucose [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma --7th specimen* - *3029014 / 50217-9 — Glucose [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma --8th specimen* - *3031929 / 50218-7 — Glucose [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma --9th specimen* - *3032780 / 50208-8 — Glucose [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma --10th specimen* - *3003541 / 12611-0 — Glucose [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma --4 hour specimen* ### Ratios — different measurand - *3046715 / 43740-0 — Glucose/Insulin [Mass Ratio] in Serum or Plasma* - *40765155 / 62418-9 — Glucose/Insulin [Ratio] in Serum or Plasma* ### Aggregated value — not a point-in-time measurement - *1002230 / 93791-2 — Glucose [Mass/volume] mean in Serum or Plasma* ### Qualitative — different measurand (presence, not a concentration) - *3014305 / 5914-7 — Glucose [Presence] in Blood by Test strip* The set also deliberately omits the following LOINC concepts: - **Cord blood and fetus specimens**: physiologically distinct from post-natal blood. - **Urine specimens**: out of scope (captured by the separate "Urinary glucose" concept set). - **CSF, body fluid, dialysis fluid, peritoneal fluid and other specimens**: out of scope for a "blood" concept set. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports "glucose", "glycaemia", "sugar" without further specification: `3013826 / 14749-6 — Glucose [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma` (SI form). If the source uses US conventional units, prefer `3004501 / 2345-7 — Glucose [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma`. - **Source reports a fingerstick / capillary / glucometer / POCT glucose**: map to the corresponding Capillary blood code (`14743-9`, `41653-7`, `32016-8`, `51596-5`). - **Source reports a fasting glucose**: map to `46235168 / 76629-5 — Fasting glucose [Moles/volume] in Blood` or `46236950 / 77145-1 — Fasting glucose [Moles/volume] in Serum, Plasma or Blood`. - **Source reports an OGTT (oral glucose tolerance test) series** (e.g. 0, 30, 60, 90, 120 min after 75 g oral glucose): do **not** map to this concept set. OGTT timepoints are out of scope. - **Do not confuse with**: HbA1c (different measurand, separate concept set), urinary glucose, glucose/insulin ratio, mean glucose. ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 14749-6 — Glucose [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma. Available: https://loinc.org/14749-6/ [2] Nomenclature for Properties and Units (NPU). IFCC/IUPAC. NPU codes (current release). en.name: Lactate in venous blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Lactate is the end-product of anaerobic glucose metabolism; its concentration in venous blood is widely used as a marker of tissue hypoperfusion when arterial sampling is not available [1]. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a biochemistry analyser, a blood gas analyser, or a point-of-care device. Results are reported as a substance concentration in mmol/L (SI unit) or as a mass concentration in mg/dL [2]. This concept set aggregates lactate measurements across **non-arterial** blood specimens: venous, mixed venous, capillary, serum/plasma generic, and unspecified blood. Cord blood and fetus specimens are excluded. **Note: arterial vs venous lactate.** Lactate concentrations in arterial and venous blood are **not numerically equivalent** — the arterio-venous difference reflects tissue lactate production/clearance and is clinically meaningful. Arterial lactate is captured by a separate concept set, "Lactate in arterial blood". Study designs that require strict comparability should preserve the LOINC code (which encodes the specimen). ## Included Concepts The set is anchored on six LOINC Hierarchy concepts (one per non-arterial blood specimen, scoped to `Chemistry - non-challenge`), with their descendants pulled in. After exclusions, the set resolves to 12 LOINC "Lab Test" concepts, grouped here by specimen. ### Serum or plasma (default specimen for routine biochemistry) - *3014111 / 2524-7 — Lactate [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: most widely used LOINC code for venous/plasma lactate. - *3020138 / 14118-4 — Lactate [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: same measurand expressed as mass concentration. ### Generic blood (specimen unspecified) - *3047181 / 32693-4 — Lactate [Moles/volume] in Blood (LOINC)* - *40762125 / 59032-3 — Lactate [Mass/volume] in Blood (LOINC)*: same measurand expressed as mass concentration. ### Venous blood - *3008037 / 2519-7 — Lactate [Moles/volume] in Venous blood (LOINC)* - *3002106 / 30241-4 — Lactate [Mass/volume] in Venous blood (LOINC)*: same measurand expressed as mass concentration. - *3005491 / 32133-1 — Lactate [Moles/volume] in Plasma venous (LOINC)*: less common variant where the specimen is explicitly venous plasma. ### Capillary blood - *3028271 / 19239-3 — Lactate [Moles/volume] in Capillary blood (LOINC)* - *3040968 / 51829-0 — Lactate [Mass/volume] in Capillary blood (LOINC)*: same measurand expressed as mass concentration. ### Mixed venous blood - *3005949 / 19240-1 — Lactate [Moles/volume] in Mixed venous blood (LOINC)*: typically from a Swan-Ganz catheter. **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS`: **`mmol/L`** (concept 8753 — millimole per litre) for `[Moles/volume]` codes and **`mg/dL`** (concept 8840) for `[Mass/volume]` codes. Conversion: `1 mg/dL ≈ 0.111 mmol/L` (molar mass of lactate = 89.07 g/mol). ## Excluded Concepts The hierarchies above pull in two LOINC concepts that are explicitly excluded: ### Ratios — different measurand (ratio to another analyte) - *3022085 / 2550-2 — Lactate/Pyruvate [Molar ratio] in Blood* - *40762141 / 59048-9 — Lactate/Pyruvate [Mass Ratio] in Blood* The set also deliberately omits the following LOINC concepts: - **Arterial blood specimens**: captured by the separate concept set "Lactate in arterial blood". - **Cord blood and fetus specimens**: physiologically distinct from post-natal blood. - **Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) and LDH isoenzymes**: different analytes, captured by the separate "Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) in blood" concept set. - **CSF, body fluid, dialysis fluid, gastric fluid, peritoneal fluid, pleural fluid, stool, synovial fluid, urine specimens**: out of scope for a "blood" concept set. - **Lactate and pyruvate panel**: panel grouping concept, not a measurement result. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports a lactate value without specifying arterial origin (e.g. routine biochemistry, peripheral venous draw): `3014111 / 2524-7 — Lactate [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma`. By far the most common LOINC code. - **Source explicitly mentions arterial sampling** (e.g. "arterial lactate", blood gas analyser): do **not** map to this concept set. Use the separate "Lactate in arterial blood" concept set. - **Source reports a lactate-to-pyruvate ratio**: do **not** map. Different measurand. - **Do not confuse with**: arterial lactate (separate concept set, arterio-venous difference is clinically meaningful), lactate dehydrogenase (LDH, different analyte), lactate/pyruvate ratio. ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 2524-7 — Lactate [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma. Available: https://loinc.org/2524-7/ [2] Nomenclature for Properties and Units (NPU). IFCC/IUPAC. NPU codes (current release). Available: https://npu-terminology.org/npu-database/

en.name: Magnesium in blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Magnesium is an intracellular cation involved in many enzymatic reactions. Its concentration in blood is measured to investigate hypo- or hypermagnesaemia [1]. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a biochemistry analyser. Results are reported as a substance concentration in mmol/L (SI unit), as a mass concentration in mg/dL, or in mEq/L [2]. ## Included Concepts The set is anchored on two LOINC Hierarchy concepts (one per blood specimen, scoped to `Chemistry - non-challenge`), with their descendants pulled in. After exclusions, the set resolves to five LOINC "Lab Test" concepts, grouped here by specimen. ### Serum or plasma (default specimen for routine biochemistry) - *3012095 / 2601-3 — Magnesium [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: most widely used LOINC code worldwide. - *3001420 / 19123-9 — Magnesium [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: same measurand expressed as mass concentration. - *40759058 / 55937-7 — Magnesium [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma --post dialysis (LOINC)*: point-in-time measurement immediately after a haemodialysis session. ### Generic blood (specimen unspecified) - *3033836 / 2593-2 — Magnesium [Moles/volume] in Blood (LOINC)* - *3006916 / 21377-7 — Magnesium [Mass/volume] in Blood (LOINC)*: same measurand expressed as mass concentration. **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS`: **`mmol/L`** (concept 8753 — millimole per litre) for `[Moles/volume]` codes and **`mg/dL`** (concept 8840) for `[Mass/volume]` codes. Conversion: `1 mmol/L ≈ 2.43 mg/dL` (molar mass of Mg = 24.305 g/mol); `1 mEq/L = 0.5 mmol/L` (magnesium is divalent). ## Excluded Concepts The hierarchies above pull in two LOINC concepts that are explicitly excluded: - *3003341 / 27210-4 — Magnesium [Presence] in Blood*: qualitative result (present / absent), not a quantitative measurement. - *40768058 / 65362-6 — Magnesium [Moles/volume] corrected for albumin in Serum or Plasma*: derived value (corrected for albumin), not the raw measurement. The set also deliberately omits the following LOINC concepts: - **Red Blood Cells specimens** (e.g. `3021770 / 26746-8 — Magnesium [Mass/volume] in Red Blood Cells`): intra-erythrocytic magnesium, specialised research measurement. - **White blood cells specimens**: specialised research measurement. - **Urine, CSF, body fluid and other specimens**: out of scope for a "blood" concept set. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports "magnesium", "Mg", "magnesaemia" without further specification: `3012095 / 2601-3 — Magnesium [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma`. By far the most common LOINC code. - **Do not confuse with**: corrected magnesium (for albumin, separate measurand), intra-erythrocytic magnesium, urinary magnesium. ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 2601-3 — Magnesium [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma. Available: https://loinc.org/2601-3/ [2] Nomenclature for Properties and Units (NPU). IFCC/IUPAC. NPU codes (current release). Results are reported as a substance concentration in mmol/L (SI unit) or as a mass concentration in mg/dL [2]. ## Included Concepts The set is anchored on two LOINC Hierarchy concepts (one per blood specimen, scoped to `Chemistry - non-challenge`), with their descendants pulled in. en.name: Potassium in blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Potassium is the principal intracellular cation; its concentration in blood is one of the most frequently ordered laboratory measurements [1]. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a biochemistry analyser, a blood gas analyser, or a point-of-care device. Results are reported as a substance concentration in mmol/L (SI unit) or mEq/L; the two are numerically equivalent for potassium [2]. This concept set aggregates potassium measurements across blood specimens (serum, plasma, arterial, venous, capillary, mixed venous and unspecified blood). ## Included Concepts The set is anchored on eight LOINC Hierarchy concepts (one per blood specimen, scoped to `Chemistry - non-challenge`), with their descendants pulled in. After exclusions, the set resolves to nine LOINC "Lab Test" concepts, grouped here by specimen. ### Serum or plasma (default specimen for routine biochemistry) - *3023103 / 2823-3 — Potassium [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: most widely used LOINC code worldwide. - *3015066 / 29349-8 — Potassium [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma --post dialysis (LOINC)*: point-in-time measurement immediately after a haemodialysis session. - *3039651 / 51618-7 — Potassium [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma --pre dialysis (LOINC)*: point-in-time measurement immediately before a haemodialysis session. ### Generic blood (specimen unspecified) - *3005456 / 6298-4 — Potassium [Moles/volume] in Blood (LOINC)*: used when the source reports potassium on whole blood without further specification. - *21490733 / 75940-7 — Potassium [Mass/volume] in Blood (LOINC)*: same measurand expressed as mass concentration. - *46235078 / 77142-8 — Potassium [Moles/volume] in Serum, Plasma or Blood (LOINC)*: specimen-agnostic. ### Arterial blood - *3043409 / 32713-0 — Potassium [Moles/volume] in Arterial blood (LOINC)*: typically reported by a blood gas analyser. ### Venous blood - *3041354 / 39789-3 — Potassium [Moles/volume] in Venous blood (LOINC)* ### Capillary blood - *3040893 / 39790-1 — Potassium [Moles/volume] in Capillary blood (LOINC)*: capillary heel-prick or fingerstick (neonatal, point-of-care). ### Mixed venous blood - *3031219 / 41656-0 — Potassium [Moles/volume] in Mixed venous blood (LOINC)*: typically from a Swan-Ganz catheter. **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS`: **`mmol/L`** (concept 8753 — millimole per litre). Source systems may report `mmol/L` or `mEq/L`; for potassium (a monovalent cation) the two are numerically equal. **Note on haemolysis.** Potassium concentration is highly sensitive to haemolysis: red blood cells contain ~30-fold more potassium than plasma, so a haemolysed sample yields a falsely elevated result.
