en.name: Sodium in blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Sodium is the principal extracellular cation. Its concentration in blood is one of the most frequently ordered laboratory measurements [1]. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a biochemistry analyser or a point-of-care device. Results are reported as a substance concentration in mmol/L (SI unit) or mEq/L; the two are numerically equivalent for sodium [2]. This concept set aggregates sodium measurements across blood specimens (serum, plasma, arterial, venous, capillary, mixed venous and unspecified blood), because the sodium concentration does not depend meaningfully on the sampling site. ## Included Concepts The set is anchored on seven LOINC Hierarchy concepts (one per blood specimen, scoped to `Chemistry - non-challenge`), with their descendants pulled in. After exclusions, the set resolves to seven LOINC "Lab Test" concepts, grouped here by specimen. ### Serum or plasma (default specimen for routine biochemistry) - *3019550 / 2951-2 — Sodium [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: most widely used LOINC code worldwide. - *44816586 / 74688-3 — Sodium [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma --post dialysis (LOINC)*: point-in-time measurement immediately after a haemodialysis session. ### Generic blood (specimen unspecified) - *3000285 / 2947-0 — Sodium [Moles/volume] in Blood (LOINC)*: used when the source reports sodium on whole blood without further specification. - *46235784 / 77139-4 — Sodium [Moles/volume] in Serum, Plasma or Blood (LOINC)*: specimen-agnostic. ### Arterial blood - *3043706 / 32717-1 — Sodium [Moles/volume] in Arterial blood (LOINC)*: typically reported by a blood gas analyser. ### Venous blood - *3041473 / 39791-9 — Sodium [Moles/volume] in Venous blood (LOINC)* ### Capillary blood - *3038702 / 39792-7 — Sodium [Moles/volume] in Capillary blood (LOINC)*: capillary heel-prick or fingerstick (neonatal, point-of-care). ### Mixed venous blood - *3031579 / 41657-8 — Sodium [Moles/volume] in Mixed venous blood (LOINC)*: typically from a Swan-Ganz catheter. **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS`: **`mmol/L`** (concept 8753 — millimole per litre). Source systems may report `mmol/L` or `mEq/L`; for sodium (a monovalent cation) the two are numerically equal. ## Excluded Concepts The Serum/Plasma hierarchy above pulls in three LOINC concepts that are explicitly excluded: - *3000288 / 28003-2 — Sodium/Potassium [Molar ratio] in Serum or Plasma*: derived ratio, not a sodium concentration. - *3044738 / 44783-9 — Sodium [Moles/volume] (Maximum value during study) in Serum or Plasma*: aggregated value over a study window, not a point-in-time measurement. - *3032987 / 51419-0 — Sodium [Moles/volume] corrected for glucose in Serum or Plasma*: derived value (corrected for hyperglycaemia), not the raw measurement. The set also deliberately omits the following LOINC concepts: - **Red Blood Cells specimens** (`3001838 / 12907-2 — Sodium [Moles/volume] in Red Blood Cells`, `42528959 / 82812-9 — Sodium [Mass/volume] in Red Blood Cells`): intra-erythrocytic sodium, specialised research measurement. - **Vasopressin challenge tests** (`1001778 / 93997-5 — Sodium [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma --1 hour post dose vasopressin`, `1002415 / 94006-4 — Sodium [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma --2 hours post dose vasopressin`): research protocols. - **Sodium and Potassium panels** (`3045783 / 34548-8 — Sodium and Potassium panel [Moles/volume] - Serum or Plasma`, `44786996 / 74353-4 — Sodium and Potassium panel [Moles/volume] - Blood`): panel grouping concepts, not measurement results. - **Sodium nitrite / sodium benzoate IgE** (`40759830 / 56711-5 — Sodium benzoate IgE Ab [Units/volume] in Serum`, `36031761 / 96293-6 — Sodium nitrite IgE Ab [Units/volume] in Serum`): allergology tests, different measurand. - **Urine, CSF, sweat, dialysate, and other body fluid specimens**: out of scope for a "blood" concept set. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports "sodium", "Na", "natraemia" without further specification: `3019550 / 2951-2 — Sodium [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma`. By far the most common LOINC code. - **Source reports a sodium value from a blood gas analyser** (typically arterial): map to `3043706 / 32717-1 — Sodium [Moles/volume] in Arterial blood`. - **Specimen unspecified**: map to `46235784 / 77139-4 — Sodium [Moles/volume] in Serum, Plasma or Blood`. - **Do not confuse with**: urinary sodium (different measurand, separate concept set when relevant), corrected sodium for hyperglycaemia (a derived value), Na/K ratio. ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. en.name: Urea in blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Urea is the main nitrogenous end-product of protein catabolism; its concentration in blood is used to assess renal function and the protein catabolic state [1]. In US sources it is often reported as **blood urea nitrogen (BUN)** — the nitrogen content of urea, which is **not numerically equal** to urea itself (see Mapping Notes below). The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a biochemistry analyser. Results are reported as a substance concentration in mmol/L (SI unit) or as a mass concentration in mg/dL [2]. This concept set aggregates urea measurements across blood specimens (serum, plasma, arterial, venous and unspecified blood). ## Included Concepts The set is anchored on five LOINC Hierarchy concepts (one per blood specimen, scoped to `Chemistry - non-challenge`), with their descendants pulled in. After exclusions, the set resolves to eight LOINC "Lab Test" concepts, grouped here by specimen. ### Serum or plasma (default specimen for routine biochemistry) - *3020779 / 22664-7 — Urea [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: most widely used LOINC code worldwide. - *3034204 / 3091-6 — Urea [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: same measurand expressed as mass concentration. - *3042602 / 39776-0 — Urea [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma --post dialysis (LOINC)*: point-in-time measurement immediately after a haemodialysis session. - *3039815 / 39777-8 — Urea [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma --pre dialysis (LOINC)*: point-in-time measurement immediately before a haemodialysis session. ### Generic blood (specimen unspecified) - *43534077 / 72903-8 — Urea [Moles/volume] in Blood (LOINC)* - *3009810 / 20977-5 — Urea [Mass/volume] in Blood (LOINC)*: same measurand expressed as mass concentration. - *46235781 / 77136-0 — Urea [Moles/volume] in Serum, Plasma or Blood (LOINC)*: specimen-agnostic. ### Arterial blood - *43534101 / 72927-7 — Urea [Moles/volume] in Arterial blood (LOINC)* ### Venous blood - *43534100 / 72926-9 — Urea [Moles/volume] in Venous blood (LOINC)* **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS`: **`mmol/L`** (concept 8753 — millimole per litre) for `[Moles/volume]` codes and **`mg/dL`** (concept 8840) for `[Mass/volume]` codes. Conversion: `1 mmol/L urea ≈ 6.01 mg/dL urea` (molar mass of urea = 60.06 g/mol). ## Excluded Concepts The Serum/Plasma hierarchy above pulls in two LOINC concepts that are explicitly excluded: - *3040431 / 39783-6 — Urea/Creatinine [Molar ratio] in Serum or Plasma*: derived ratio, not a urea concentration. - *40760116 / 56997-0 — Urea/Creatinine [Mass Ratio] in Serum or Plasma*: derived ratio, not a urea concentration. The set also deliberately omits the following LOINC concepts: - **Urine specimens**: out of scope (captured by the separate "Urinary urea" concept set). - **Body fluid, CSF and other specimens**: out of scope for a "blood" concept set. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports "urea", "urée" without further specification: `3020779 / 22664-7 — Urea [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma`. By far the most common LOINC code. - **Source reports BUN (blood urea nitrogen)**: BUN measures only the nitrogen content of urea (2 N atoms × 14 g/mol = 28 g/mol). Stoichiometric conversion: `1 mg/dL BUN ≈ 0.357 mmol/L urea` and `1 mmol/L urea ≈ 2.8 mg/dL BUN` [3]. **Do not map a BUN value directly to a urea LOINC code without converting**, otherwise the value will be off by a factor of ~2.14. - **Do not confuse with**: urea nitrogen / BUN (uses different LOINC codes, conversion factor required), urinary urea, urea/creatinine ratio. ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 22664-7 — Urea [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma. Available: https://loinc.org/22664-7/ [2] Nomenclature for Properties and Units (NPU). IFCC/IUPAC. NPU codes (current release). Available: https://npu-terminology.org/npu-database/ [3] Hosten AO. BUN and Creatinine. In: Walker HK, Hall WD, Hurst JW, editors. *Clinical Methods: The History, Physical, and Laboratory Examinations*. 3rd ed. Boston: Butterworths; 1990. Chapter 193. Available: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK305/

en.name: Urinary glucose
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Urinary glucose is the concentration of glucose in a urine specimen — typically a spot (random) urine sample. It is commonly assessed by urine dipstick and is elevated when blood glucose exceeds the renal threshold for glucose reabsorption (~10 mmol/L in adults) [1]. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a biochemistry analyser or a urine test strip. Results are reported as a substance concentration in mmol/L (SI unit) or as a mass concentration in mg/dL [2]. ## Included Concepts The set lists four LOINC "Lab Test" concepts measuring the glucose concentration in a spot urine specimen: - *3005570 / 15076-3 — Glucose [Moles/volume] in Urine (LOINC)*: spot (random) urine sample, SI form. Most widely used LOINC code. - *3020399 / 2350-7 — Glucose [Mass/volume] in Urine (LOINC)*: spot urine sample, mass concentration form. - *44786994 / 74351-8 — Glucose [Moles/volume] in Urine collected for unspecified duration (LOINC)*: used when the source does not specify whether the sample is spot or timed. - *3035214 / 35662-6 — Glucose [Mass/volume] in Urine collected for unspecified duration (LOINC)*: same measurand expressed as mass concentration. **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS`: **`mmol/L`** (concept 8753 — millimole per litre) for `[Moles/volume]` codes and **`mg/dL`** (concept 8840) for `[Mass/volume]` codes. Conversion: `1 mg/dL ≈ 0.0555 mmol/L`. ## Excluded Concepts The following LOINC concepts that exist for urinary glucose are deliberately not part of this set, grouped by reason for exclusion. ### Timed urine collections — different specimen (timed vs. spot) - *3007034 / 21305-8 — Glucose [Mass/volume] in 24 hour Urine* - *3035381 / 25916-8 — Glucose [Moles/volume] in 24 hour Urine* - *44816585 / 74687-5 — Glucose [Moles/volume] in 12 hour Urine* ### Excretion rates — different measurand (amount per unit time, not a concentration) - *3000361 / 15077-1 — Glucose [Moles/time] in 24 hour Urine* - *3005478 / 2351-5 — Glucose [Mass/time] in 24 hour Urine* - *3023544 / 18227-9 — Glucose [Mass/time] in 6 hour Urine* - *3005943 / 21306-6 — Glucose [Mass/time] in 8 hour Urine* - *3025893 / 21307-4 — Glucose [Mass/time] in 10 hour Urine* - *44816584 / 74686-7 — Glucose [Moles/time] in 12 hour Urine* - *40762090 / 58997-8 — Glucose [Mass/time] in 18 hour Urine* ### Ratios — different measurand (ratio to another analyte) - *3045427 / 33352-6 — Glucose/Creatinine [Mass Ratio] in Urine* - *3045505 / 34312-9 — Glucose/Creatinine [Molar ratio] in Urine* - *3040910 / 40488-9 — Glucose/Creatinine [Ratio] in Urine* - *40760123 / 57004-4 — Glucose/Creatinine [Mass Ratio] in 24 hour Urine* - *1989592 / 99602-5 — Glucose/Creatinine [Molar ratio] in 24 hour Urine* ### Qualitative — different measurand (presence, not a concentration) - *3020650 / 2349-9 — Glucose [Presence] in Urine* - *3007308 / 32174-5 — Glucose [Presence] in 24 hour Urine* ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports "urinary glucose", "urine glucose", "spot urine glucose", "glycosuria" without further specification: `3005570 / 15076-3 — Glucose [Moles/volume] in Urine`. name: Blood culture
description: Blood culture — microbiology test detecting bacteria or fungi in the bloodstream (aerobic, anaerobic, fungal, MAC); the test/specimen, not the organisms grown.

concept.conceptName: Blood culture for bacteria, including anaerobic screen

en.name: Blood culture
en.shortDescription: Blood culture — microbiology test detecting bacteria or fungi in the bloodstream (aerobic, anaerobic, fungal, MAC); the test/specimen, not the organisms grown.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

A blood culture is a microbiology test that detects micro-organisms (bacteria or fungi) circulating in the bloodstream. A sample of blood is drawn and incubated in culture bottles; if an organism grows, it is identified and antibiotic susceptibility is determined. Blood cultures are the key investigation for suspected bloodstream infection, sepsis and endocarditis, and are routinely drawn in the intensive care unit whenever a patient is febrile or deteriorating. A standard "set" comprises an aerobic and an anaerobic bottle, and two sets from separate sites are usually taken to distinguish true infection from skin-flora contamination.

This concept set captures the **blood-culture test / specimen-collection concepts** themselves (the fact that a blood culture was ordered or performed and of what type), not the organisms grown from them — those are the bacteria and fungi concept sets. It is the only specimen/test concept set in the Microbiology category; the rest define organisms.

## Included Concepts

This concept set is a curated list of blood-culture test concepts.

### Generic blood culture

- *4107893 / 30088009 — Blood culture (SNOMED)*: The generic blood-culture test, type unspecified. Default mapping target for a "blood culture" order or result with no further qualifier.

### By incubation atmosphere

- *4252846 / 409611004 — Aerobic blood culture (SNOMED)*: The aerobic bottle (organisms that grow with oxygen).
- *4252847 / 409612006 — Anaerobic blood culture (SNOMED)*: The anaerobic bottle (organisms that grow without oxygen).
- *4016944 / 104177005 — Blood culture for bacteria, including anaerobic screen (SNOMED)*: A bacterial blood culture explicitly including an anaerobic screen.

### Targeted cultures

- *4006847 / 121238005 — Fungal blood culture (SNOMED)* and *4015309 / 104188004 — Fungal culture, blood, with isolation (SNOMED)*: Blood culture targeting fungi (e.g., for suspected candidaemia), which may use a dedicated medium or prolonged incubation.
- *4014500 / 104183008 — Blood culture for MAC (SNOMED)*: Blood culture for Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC), using a specialised mycobacterial medium; relevant mainly in immunocompromised (e.g., advanced HIV) patients.

## Mapping Notes

- *Default concept*: When the source records a blood culture without specifying aerobic/anaerobic/fungal/MAC, map to Blood culture (4107893 / 30088009 — Blood culture, SNOMED). Do not infer the bottle type.
- *Aerobic/anaerobic bottles*: Map to the aerobic (4252846 / 409611004 — Aerobic blood culture) or anaerobic (4252847 / 409612006 — Anaerobic blood culture) concept only when the source distinguishes the bottle. A blood-culture "set" combining both, with no per-bottle breakdown, maps to the generic concept.
- *Targeted cultures*: Use the fungal (4006847 / 121238005 — Fungal blood culture) or MAC (4014500 / 104183008 — Blood culture for MAC) concept only when the source states the culture was specifically for fungi or mycobacteria.
- *Result vs. order*: This set represents the blood-culture test/specimen. The organism(s) isolated from a positive culture map to the corresponding bacteria or fungi concept sets, not here.
- *Common source labels*: "Blood culture", "BC", "Hemoculture", "Hémoculture", "Blood cx", "BACTEC"/"BacT-ALERT bottle" → Blood culture (4107893 / 30088009 — Blood culture, SNOMED) or the matching bottle-type concept.

name: Birth height
description: Birth length — body length measured at birth; in centimetres (cm).

en.name: Birth height
en.shortDescription: Birth length — body length measured at birth; in centimetres (cm).
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Birth length is the body length of a newborn measured at birth, head to heel, with the infant lying down. It produces a single numeric value timestamped at (or near) the time of birth, and is part of routine neonatal anthropometry alongside birth weight and head circumference. It is reported in centimetres (cm).

## Included Concepts

- *4014465 / 169886007 — Birth length (SNOMED)*: the newborn's length at birth.
- *36304231 / 89269-5 — Body height Measured --at birth (LOINC)*: the equivalent LOINC concept.

Both standard concepts represent the same variable; both are reported in cm.

## Mapping Notes

- Map any neonatal length/height recorded at birth here, using *4014465 / 169886007 — Birth length* (SNOMED) or *36304231 / 89269-5 — Body height Measured --at birth* (LOINC).
- Birth length is also a descendant of the *Body height* set; this set is the focused neonatal view of the same measurement.

fr.name: Taille à la naissance
fr.shortDescription: Taille de naissance — longueur du corps mesurée à la naissance ; en centimètres (cm).
fr.longDescription:
## Définition et contexte clinique

La taille de naissance est la longueur du corps d'un nouveau-né mesurée à la naissance, de la tête aux talons, l'enfant étant couché. Elle produit une valeur numérique unique horodatée au (ou près du) moment de la naissance, et fait partie de l'anthropométrie néonatale de routine avec le poids de naissance et le périmètre crânien. Elle est exprimée en centimètres (cm).

## Concepts inclus

- *4014465 / 169886007 — Birth length (SNOMED)* : la longueur du nouveau-né à la naissance.
- *36304231 / 89269-5 — Body height Measured --at birth (LOINC)* : le concept LOINC équivalent.

Les deux concepts standards représentent la même variable ; tous deux en cm.

## Notes de mapping

- Mapper ici toute taille/longueur néonatale relevée à la naissance, via *4014465 / 169886007 — Birth length* (SNOMED) ou *36304231 / 89269-5 — Body height Measured --at birth* (LOINC).
- La taille de naissance est aussi un descendant du jeu *Body height* ; ce jeu en est la vue néonatale ciblée.

en.name: Birth weight
en.shortDescription: Birth weight — body weight measured at birth; in grams (g) or kilograms (kg).
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Birth weight is the body weight of a newborn measured at birth. It produces a single numeric value timestamped at (or near) the time of birth, and is a core neonatal anthropometric measurement used to classify low/very-low birth weight. It is reported in grams (g) or kilograms (kg).

## Included Concepts

- *4264825 / 364589006 — Birth weight (SNOMED)*: the newborn's weight at birth.
- *3011043 / 8339-4 — Birth weight Measured (LOINC)*: the equivalent LOINC concept.

Both standard concepts represent the same variable.

## Mapping Notes

- Map any neonatal weight recorded at birth here, using *4264825 / 364589006 — Birth weight* (SNOMED) or *3011043 / 8339-4 — Birth weight Measured* (LOINC).
- Birth weight is also a descendant of the *Body weight* set; this set is the focused neonatal view of the same measurement.
- Watch the unit: neonatal scales often report grams, not kilograms — preserve the source unit.

fr.name: Poids à la naissance
fr.shortDescription: Poids de naissance — poids corporel mesuré à la naissance ; en grammes (g) ou kilogrammes (kg).
fr.longDescription:
## Définition et contexte clinique

Le poids de naissance est le poids corporel d'un nouveau-né mesuré à la naissance. Il produit une valeur numérique unique horodatée au (ou près du) moment de la naissance, et constitue une mesure anthropométrique néonatale fondamentale servant à classer les faibles/très faibles poids de naissance. Il est exprimé en grammes (g) ou kilogrammes (kg).

## Concepts inclus

- *4264825 / 364589006 — Birth weight (SNOMED)* : le poids du nouveau-né à la naissance.
- *3011043 / 8339-4 — Birth weight Measured (LOINC)* : le concept LOINC équivalent.

Les deux concepts standards représentent la même variable.

## Notes de mapping

- Mapper ici tout poids néonatal relevé à la naissance, via *4264825 / 364589006 — Birth weight* (SNOMED) ou *3011043 / 8339-4 — Birth weight Measured* (LOINC).
- Le poids de naissance est aussi un descendant du jeu *Body weight* ; ce jeu en est la vue néonatale ciblée.
- Attention à l'unité : les balances néonatales rapportent souvent des grammes, pas des kilogrammes — conserver l'unité source.

concept.conceptName: Self reported peak adult body height

en.name: Body height
en.shortDescription: Body height (stature) — how tall the patient is, standing or recumbent; in centimetres (cm).
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Body height produces a single numeric value per patient-timestamp, taken standing (stadiometer) or, for patients who cannot stand, lying down (recumbent length, typical for infants and bedridden ICU patients). It is recorded on admission and used for weight-for-height calculations, drug and ventilator settings, and nutritional assessment. It is reported in centimetres (cm).

## Included Concepts

The set is anchored on the SNOMED *Body height* concept with its descendants, plus the generic LOINC body-height concept (LOINC carries no hierarchy, so it is listed flat). They are grouped below by measurement posture for readability only — all belong to the same `body_height` variable, all in cm.

### Generic body height (default)

- *607590 / 1153637007 — Body height (SNOMED)* and *3036277 / 8302-2 — Body height (LOINC)*: the default, posture not specified.

### By posture

- *4093975 / 248333004 — Standing height (SNOMED)*: measured standing.
- *600652 / 1149101003 — Recumbent body height (SNOMED)*: measured lying down (infants, bedridden patients).

**Note on units**: reported in **centimetres** (`8582 / cm — centimeter`, UCUM), the recommended unit.

## Mapping Notes

- **Default concept** when the source records a height without specifying posture: *607590 / 1153637007 — Body height* (SNOMED) or *3036277 / 8302-2 — Body height* (LOINC).
- **Posture is an attribute, not a separate variable**: map to *Standing height* or *Recumbent body height* only when the source documents the posture; otherwise use the generic concept.
- **Excluded from the set** (do not map here): self-reported height, estimated height, and pre-amputation estimated/measured height — these are not directly measured current heights. Birth length is also excluded because it has its own dedicated *Birth height* set.
- This set is built symmetrically with the *Body weight* set (same anchoring strategy) so height and weight map consistently.

fr.name: Taille corporelle
fr.shortDescription: Taille corporelle (stature) — stature du patient, debout ou couchée ; en centimètres (cm).
fr.longDescription:
## Définition et contexte clinique

La taille corporelle produit une valeur numérique unique par patient-horodatage, prise debout (toise) ou, pour les patients ne pouvant se tenir debout, en position couchée (taille en décubitus, habituelle chez le nourrisson et le patient alité de réanimation). Elle est relevée à l'admission et sert aux calculs poids/taille, aux réglages médicamenteux et ventilatoires et à l'évaluation nutritionnelle. Elle est exprimée en centimètres (cm).

## Concepts inclus

Le jeu est ancré sur le concept SNOMED *Body height* et ses descendants, plus le concept LOINC générique de taille (LOINC n'a pas de hiérarchie, il est donc listé à plat). Ils sont regroupés ci-dessous par posture de mesure, à titre de lisibilité uniquement — tous relèvent de la même variable `body_height`, tous en cm.

### Taille générique (par défaut)

- *607590 / 1153637007 — Body height (SNOMED)* et *3036277 / 8302-2 — Body height (LOINC)* : par défaut, posture non précisée.

### Par posture

- *4093975 / 248333004 — Standing height (SNOMED)* : mesurée debout.
- *600652 / 1149101003 — Recumbent body height (SNOMED)* : mesurée couchée (nourrissons, patients alités).

**Note sur les unités** : exprimée en **centimètres** (`8582 / cm — centimeter`, UCUM), l'unité recommandée.

## Notes de mapping

- **Concept par défaut** quand la source enregistre une taille sans préciser la posture : *607590 / 1153637007 — Body height* (SNOMED) ou *3036277 / 8302-2 — Body height* (LOINC).
- **La posture est un attribut, pas une variable distincte** : ne mapper vers *Standing height* ou *Recumbent body height* que si la source documente la posture ; sinon utiliser le concept générique.
- **Exclus du jeu** (ne pas mapper ici) : taille auto-déclarée, taille estimée, taille pré-amputation estimée/mesurée — ce ne sont pas des tailles actuelles directement mesurées. La longueur de naissance est aussi exclue car elle dispose de son propre jeu *Birth height*.
- Ce jeu est construit symétriquement au jeu *Body weight* (même stratégie d'ancrage), pour un mapping cohérent taille/poids.

en.name: Body weight
en.shortDescription: Body weight — how much the patient weighs (any measured context, incl. dialysis and dry weight); in kilograms (kg).
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Body weight produces a single numeric value per patient-timestamp, read off a scale, bed scale, or hoist scale. It is recorded on admission and repeatedly during the stay, and underpins drug dosing, fluid balance, nutrition, and ventilator settings. It is reported in kilograms (kg).

## Included Concepts

The set is anchored on the SNOMED *Body weight* concept with its descendants, plus the generic LOINC body-weight concept (LOINC carries no hierarchy, so it is listed flat). They are grouped below by context for readability only — all belong to the same `body_weight` variable, all in kg.

### Generic body weight (default)

- *4099154 / 27113001 — Body weight (SNOMED)*, *4178502 / 363808001 — Body weight measure (SNOMED)* and *3025315 / 29463-7 — Body weight (LOINC)*: the default, context not specified.
- *42536495 / 735395000 — Current body weight (SNOMED)*: the patient's weight now.

### Dialysis / dry weight (ICU and renal)

- *37160447 / 1162421003 — Pre-dialysis body weight (SNOMED)* and *37160443 / 1162420002 — Post-dialysis body weight (SNOMED)*: weights measured around a dialysis session.
- *40484200 / 445541000 — Dry body weight (SNOMED)*: the target euvolaemic weight (no fluid overload).

**Note on units**: reported in **kilograms** (`9529 / kg — kilogram`, UCUM), the recommended unit, as listed by LOINC for 29463-7. For sources reporting pounds, the conversion table uses `[lb_us]` (OMOP concept 8739, factor 0.45359237). LOINC names the avoirdupois pound `[lb_av]`, the code defined by the UCUM specification, but the OMOP vocabulary has no concept for it; the only OMOP pound concepts left are `[lb_ap]` and `[lb_tr]` (apothecary and troy pound), which are about 0.82x the avoirdupois pound and would therefore be wrong by ~18%. `[lb_us]` is a standard concept of the UCUM vocabulary in OMOP carrying the correct mass (0.45359237 kg exactly, the international avoirdupois pound), so it is used here as the source unit. This gap is a known OHDSI issue (https://forums.ohdsi.org/t/ucum-concept-for-avoirdupois-pound/2808).

## Mapping Notes

- **Default concept** when the source records a weight without qualification: *4099154 / 27113001 — Body weight* (SNOMED) or *3025315 / 29463-7 — Body weight* (LOINC).
- **Context (dialysis, dry weight) is an attribute, not a separate variable**: map to a context-specific concept only when the source documents it; otherwise use the generic concept.
- **Excluded from the set** (do not map here): self-reported weight, estimated weight (incl. Broselow paediatric estimation), dosing weight (the weight used to compute drug doses, not a measured weight), baseline weight, previous well-weight, pre-amputation estimated/measured weight, and weight with/without shoes (ambulatory context, not relevant in the ICU) — these are derived, reported, or special-purpose values, not a directly measured current weight. Birth weight is also excluded because it has its own dedicated *Birth weight* set. Ideal/adjusted body weight is a separate set (*Ideal body weight*).
- This set is built symmetrically with the *Body height* set (same anchoring strategy) so height and weight map consistently.

fr.name: Poids corporel
fr.shortDescription: Poids corporel — masse du patient (tout contexte mesuré, y compris dialyse et poids sec) ; en kilogrammes (kg).
fr.longDescription:
## Définition et contexte clinique

Le poids corporel produit une valeur numérique unique par patient-horodatage, lu sur une balance, un lit-balance ou un lève-malade pesant. Il est relevé à l'admission et de façon répétée durant le séjour, et sous-tend les posologies, le bilan hydrique, la nutrition et les réglages ventilatoires. Il est exprimé en kilogrammes (kg).

## Concepts inclus

Le jeu est ancré sur le concept SNOMED *Body weight* et ses descendants, plus le concept LOINC générique de poids (LOINC n'a pas de hiérarchie, listé à plat). Regroupés ci-dessous par contexte à titre de lisibilité uniquement — tous relèvent de la même variable `body_weight`, tous en kg.

### Poids générique (par défaut)

- *4099154 / 27113001 — Body weight (SNOMED)*, *4178502 / 363808001 — Body weight measure (SNOMED)* et *3025315 / 29463-7 — Body weight (LOINC)* : par défaut, contexte non précisé.
- *42536495 / 735395000 — Current body weight (SNOMED)* : le poids actuel du patient.

### Dialyse / poids sec (réanimation et néphrologie)

- *37160447 / 1162421003 — Pre-dialysis body weight (SNOMED)* et *37160443 / 1162420002 — Post-dialysis body weight (SNOMED)* : poids mesurés autour d'une séance de dialyse.
- *40484200 / 445541000 — Dry body weight (SNOMED)* : le poids cible euvolémique (sans surcharge hydrique).

**Note sur les unités** : exprimé en **kilogrammes** (`9529 / kg — kilogram`, UCUM), l'unité recommandée.

## Notes de mapping

- **Concept par défaut** quand la source enregistre un poids sans précision : *4099154 / 27113001 — Body weight* (SNOMED) ou *3025315 / 29463-7 — Body weight* (LOINC).
- **Le contexte (dialyse, poids sec) est un attribut, pas une variable distincte** : ne mapper vers un concept contextuel que si la source le documente ; sinon utiliser le concept générique.
- **Exclus du jeu** (ne pas mapper ici) : poids auto-déclaré, poids estimé (y compris estimation pédiatrique de Broselow), poids de posologie (le poids servant à calculer les doses, pas un poids mesuré), poids de référence, poids antérieur en bonne santé, poids pré-amputation estimé/mesuré, et poids avec/sans chaussures (contexte ambulatoire, sans intérêt en réanimation) — valeurs dérivées, déclarées ou à finalité particulière, et non un poids actuel directement mesuré. Le poids de naissance est aussi exclu car il dispose de son propre jeu *Birth weight*. Le poids idéal/ajusté constitue un jeu distinct (*Ideal body weight*).
- Ce jeu est construit symétriquement au jeu *Body height* (même stratégie d'ancrage), pour un mapping cohérent taille/poids.

name: Gestational age
description: Gestational age — duration of the pregnancy at the moment of assessment; in weeks (or weeks + days).

en.name: Gestational age
en.shortDescription: Gestational age — duration of the pregnancy at the moment of assessment; in weeks (or weeks + days).
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Gestational age is how far along a pregnancy is, counted from the first day of the last menstrual period (or from an early ultrasound estimate). It produces a numeric value, usually expressed in completed weeks (sometimes weeks + days), and is assessed during pregnancy to date the pregnancy and guide care. This set is the *current* gestational age at the time of assessment; the duration at the moment of delivery is a separate set (*Gestational age at birth*).

## Included Concepts

- *3012266 / 18185-9 — Gestational age (LOINC)* and *1077378 / 598151000005105 — Gestational age (SNOMED)*: the same variable in both vocabularies.

## Mapping Notes

- Map any antenatal gestational-age assessment here, using *3012266 / 18185-9 — Gestational age* (LOINC) or *1077378 / 598151000005105 — Gestational age* (SNOMED).
- Do **not** map gestational age recorded specifically at birth here — use the *Gestational age at birth* set for that.
- Watch the unit: gestational age may be stored as decimal weeks, weeks + days, or total days — preserve the source representation.

fr.name: Âge gestationnel
fr.shortDescription: Âge gestationnel — durée de la grossesse au moment de l'évaluation ; en semaines (ou semaines + jours).
fr.longDescription:
## Définition et contexte clinique

L'âge gestationnel indique l'avancement de la grossesse, compté à partir du premier jour des dernières règles (ou d'une estimation échographique précoce). Il produit une valeur numérique, généralement exprimée en semaines révolues (parfois semaines + jours), évaluée pendant la grossesse pour la dater et orienter la prise en charge. Ce jeu correspond à l'âge gestationnel *courant* au moment de l'évaluation ; la durée au moment de l'accouchement constitue un jeu distinct (*Gestational age at birth*).

## Concepts inclus

- *3012266 / 18185-9 — Gestational age (LOINC)* et *1077378 / 598151000005105 — Gestational age (SNOMED)* : la même variable dans les deux vocabulaires.

## Notes de mapping

- Mapper ici toute évaluation anténatale de l'âge gestationnel, via *3012266 / 18185-9 — Gestational age* (LOINC) ou *1077378 / 598151000005105 — Gestational age* (SNOMED).
- Ne **pas** mapper ici l'âge gestationnel relevé spécifiquement à la naissance — utiliser le jeu *Gestational age at birth*.
- Attention à l'unité : l'âge gestationnel peut être stocké en semaines décimales, semaines + jours, ou en jours totaux — conserver la représentation source.

name: Gestational age at birth
description: Gestational age at birth — duration of the completed pregnancy at delivery; in weeks (or weeks + days).

en.name: Gestational age at birth
en.shortDescription: Gestational age at birth — duration of the completed pregnancy at delivery; in weeks (or weeks + days).
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Gestational age at birth is the length of the completed pregnancy at the moment of delivery — the value used to classify a newborn as preterm, term, or post-term. It produces a single numeric value, usually in completed weeks (sometimes weeks + days), timestamped at birth. It is distinct from the antenatal *Gestational age*, which is the current duration at any point during pregnancy.

## Included Concepts

- *4260747 / 412726003 — Length of gestation at birth (SNOMED)*: the gestational duration at delivery.

## Mapping Notes

- Map the gestational duration recorded at delivery here, using *4260747 / 412726003 — Length of gestation at birth* (SNOMED).
- For gestational age assessed *during* pregnancy (not at birth), use the *Gestational age* set instead.
- Watch the unit: may be stored as weeks, weeks + days, or total days — preserve the source representation.

fr.name: Âge gestationnel a la naissance
fr.shortDescription: Âge gestationnel à la naissance — durée de la grossesse menée à terme à l'accouchement ; en semaines (ou semaines + jours).
fr.longDescription:
## Définition et contexte clinique

L'âge gestationnel à la naissance est la durée de la grossesse menée à terme au moment de l'accouchement — la valeur servant à classer un nouveau-né comme prématuré, à terme ou post-terme. Il produit une valeur numérique unique, généralement en semaines révolues (parfois semaines + jours), horodatée à la naissance. Il se distingue de l'*âge gestationnel* anténatal, qui est la durée courante à un instant quelconque de la grossesse.

## Concepts inclus

- *4260747 / 412726003 — Length of gestation at birth (SNOMED)* : la durée de gestation à l'accouchement.

## Notes de mapping

- Mapper ici la durée de gestation relevée à l'accouchement, via *4260747 / 412726003 — Length of gestation at birth* (SNOMED).
- Pour l'âge gestationnel évalué *pendant* la grossesse (hors naissance), utiliser le jeu *Gestational age*.
- Attention à l'unité : peut être stockée en semaines, semaines + jours, ou jours totaux — conserver la représentation source.

name: Ideal body weight
description: Ideal body weight (IBW) — a height-based target weight used for dosing and ventilator settings; in kilograms (kg).

en.name: Ideal body weight
en.shortDescription: Ideal body weight (IBW) — a height-based target weight used for dosing and ventilator settings; in kilograms (kg).
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Ideal body weight (IBW) is a *calculated* target weight derived from a patient's height and sex, not a measured weight. It produces a single numeric value used to set drug doses and tidal-volume ventilator settings independently of the patient's actual (possibly oedematous or obese) weight. It is reported in kilograms (kg). Adjusted ideal body weight (AdjBW) is a related correction applied for obese patients.

## Included Concepts

- *4062985 / 170804003 — Ideal body weight (SNOMED)* and *3032445 / 50064-5 — Ideal body weight (LOINC)*: the standard height/sex-based target weight.
- *1073500 / 1304200008 — Adjusted ideal body weight (SNOMED)*: IBW corrected for obesity (lean-mass-adjusted).

Both are computed values; both in kg.

## Mapping Notes

- Map a calculated target weight here — **not** a measured weight (measured weight belongs in the *Body weight* set).
- Use *4062985 / 170804003 — Ideal body weight* (SNOMED) or *3032445 / 50064-5 — Ideal body weight* (LOINC) for the standard IBW; use *1073500 / 1304200008 — Adjusted ideal body weight* (SNOMED) only when the source explicitly records the adjusted (obesity-corrected) value.

fr.name: Poids idéal théorique
fr.shortDescription: Poids corporel idéal (IBW) — poids cible fondé sur la taille, utilisé pour les posologies et réglages ventilatoires ; en kilogrammes (kg).
fr.longDescription:
## Définition et contexte clinique

Le poids corporel idéal (IBW) est un poids cible *calculé* à partir de la taille et du sexe du patient, et non un poids mesuré. Il produit une valeur numérique unique servant à régler les posologies et le volume courant ventilatoire indépendamment du poids réel (parfois œdémateux ou obèse). Il est exprimé en kilogrammes (kg). Le poids idéal ajusté (AdjBW) est une correction apparentée appliquée chez le patient obèse.

## Concepts inclus

- *4062985 / 170804003 — Ideal body weight (SNOMED)* et *3032445 / 50064-5 — Ideal body weight (LOINC)* : le poids cible standard fondé sur taille/sexe.
- *1073500 / 1304200008 — Adjusted ideal body weight (SNOMED)* : IBW corrigé de l'obésité (ajusté à la masse maigre).

Deux valeurs calculées ; toutes deux en kg.

## Notes de mapping

- Mapper ici un poids cible calculé — **pas** un poids mesuré (le poids mesuré relève du jeu *Body weight*).
- Utiliser *4062985 / 170804003 — Ideal body weight* (SNOMED) ou *3032445 / 50064-5 — Ideal body weight* (LOINC) pour l'IBW standard ; utiliser *1073500 / 1304200008 — Adjusted ideal body weight* (SNOMED) uniquement quand la source enregistre explicitement la valeur ajustée (corrigée de l'obésité).

name: Contraindication to enteral feeding
description: Contraindication to enteral feeding — a documented reason enteral (tube) feeding must not be given; recorded as a flag.

en.name: Contraindication to enteral feeding
en.shortDescription: Contraindication to enteral feeding — a documented reason enteral (tube) feeding must not be given; recorded as a flag.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

This set captures the fact that, at a given time, enteral (tube) feeding is contraindicated for the patient — for example because of bowel obstruction, ischaemia, severe ileus, or an unprotected airway. It is a documented flag (present / recorded), not a numeric measurement, and is used to explain why a patient is on parenteral nutrition or is being kept nil-by-mouth.

There is **no standard SNOMED or LOINC concept** for "contraindication to enteral feeding" specifically (SNOMED only has the generic *Medical contraindication to procedure*). To represent this variable precisely without pulling in unrelated contraindications, the set uses a single **local INDICATE concept**.

## Included Concepts

- *2100000009 / contraindication-to-enteral-feeding — Contraindication to enteral feeding (INDICATE)*: a local concept created because no standard term exists. Custom concepts use the INDICATE vocabulary and are non-standard by definition.

## Mapping Notes

- Map any documented contraindication to enteral / tube feeding to *2100000009 / contraindication-to-enteral-feeding* (INDICATE).
- Treat it as a flag (recorded = contraindication present); the specific reason, if captured, is a separate observation.
- Do **not** map generic "contraindication to procedure" records here unless the source makes clear the procedure is enteral feeding.

fr.name: Contre-indication à la nutrition entérale
fr.shortDescription: Contre-indication à la nutrition entérale — raison documentée empêchant la nutrition entérale (par sonde) ; enregistrée comme indicateur.
fr.longDescription:
## Définition et contexte clinique

Ce jeu capture le fait qu'à un instant donné la nutrition entérale (par sonde) est contre-indiquée pour le patient — par exemple en cas d'occlusion intestinale, d'ischémie, d'iléus sévère ou de voie aérienne non protégée. Il s'agit d'un indicateur documenté (présent / enregistré), non d'une mesure numérique, servant à expliquer pourquoi un patient est sous nutrition parentérale ou maintenu à jeun.

Il n'existe **aucun concept standard SNOMED ou LOINC** spécifique pour « contre-indication à la nutrition entérale » (SNOMED ne propose que le générique *Medical contraindication to procedure*). Pour représenter précisément cette variable sans inclure de contre-indications sans rapport, le jeu utilise un unique **concept local INDICATE**.

## Concepts inclus

- *2100000009 / contraindication-to-enteral-feeding — Contraindication to enteral feeding (INDICATE)* : concept local créé faute de terme standard existant. Les concepts personnalisés utilisent le vocabulaire INDICATE et sont non standards par définition.

## Notes de mapping

name: Energy intake
description: Energy (calorie) intake actually delivered, in kcal; holds a 24h-total concept and a point-in-time concept that must be summed per day to compare.

en.name: Energy intake
en.shortDescription: Energy (calorie) intake actually delivered, in kcal; holds a 24h-total concept and a point-in-time concept that must be summed per day to compare.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Energy intake is the total amount of food energy a patient has actually taken in — orally, enterally, or parenterally — over a defined period (typically 24 hours). It produces a numeric value used to track nutritional delivery against the patient's requirement. It is reported in kilocalories (kcal).

## Included Concepts

This set deliberately holds two concepts with **different temporal semantics** — they are *not* directly interchangeable and must be interpreted differently when querying (see Mapping Notes).

- *3026267 / 9057-1 — Calorie intake total 24 hour (LOINC)*: a **daily total** (one value already aggregated over 24 hours). Stored in the Measurement table; one row per patient per day.
- *37206982 / 787787004 — Energy intake (SNOMED)*: a **point-in-time** energy-intake value at a given timestamp. Stored in the Observation table; there may be several rows per day, each a partial intake.

Both express energy actually consumed (delivered), in kcal.

## Mapping Notes

- Map a value that is already a 24-hour total to *3026267 / 9057-1 — Calorie intake total 24 hour* (LOINC); map a per-administration / point-in-time intake to *37206982 / 787787004 — Energy intake* (SNOMED).
- **To compare the two, the point-in-time values must be summed per patient per day** to reconstruct a daily total equivalent to the LOINC concept. Because the two concepts also live in different CDM tables (Measurement vs Observation), a daily energy-intake query has to read both and union them, for example:

```sql
-- Daily energy intake (kcal) per patient, harmonising both concepts.
-- LOINC 9057-1 is already a 24h total; SNOMED 787787004 is summed per day.
WITH daily_total AS (   -- already a 24h total (Measurement table)
    SELECT person_id,
           CAST(measurement_datetime AS DATE) AS intake_day,
           value_as_number AS kcal
    FROM   measurement
    WHERE  measurement_concept_id = 3026267        -- Calorie intake total 24 hour
),
pointwise AS (          -- point-in-time intakes (Observation table), summed per day
    SELECT person_id,
           CAST(observation_datetime AS DATE) AS intake_day,
           SUM(value_as_number) AS kcal
    FROM   observation
    WHERE  observation_concept_id = 37206982       -- Energy intake
    GROUP  BY person_id, CAST(observation_datetime AS DATE)
)
SELECT person_id, intake_day, kcal, 'total_24h' AS source FROM daily_total
UNION ALL
SELECT person_id, intake_day, kcal, 'summed'    AS source FROM pointwise;
```

  Prefer the pre-aggregated 24-hour total when both are available for the same day, to avoid double-counting.
- Do **not** map energy *requirement* (a target, not what was delivered) here — that is the *Energy requirement* set.

fr.name: Apport énergétique
fr.shortDescription: Apport énergétique (calorique) réellement délivré, en kcal ; contient un concept total 24 h et un concept ponctuel à sommer par jour pour comparer.
fr.longDescription:
## Définition et contexte clinique

L'apport énergétique est la quantité totale d'énergie alimentaire réellement ingérée par un patient — par voie orale, entérale ou parentérale — sur une période définie (typiquement 24 heures). Il produit une valeur numérique servant à suivre l'apport nutritionnel par rapport au besoin du patient. Il est exprimé en kilocalories (kcal).

## Concepts inclus

Ce jeu contient délibérément deux concepts aux **sémantiques temporelles différentes** — ils ne sont *pas* directement interchangeables et doivent être interprétés différemment lors des requêtes (voir Notes de mapping).

- *3026267 / 9057-1 — Calorie intake total 24 hour (LOINC)* : un **total journalier** (valeur déjà agrégée sur 24 heures). Stocké dans la table Measurement ; une ligne par patient et par jour.
- *37206982 / 787787004 — Energy intake (SNOMED)* : une valeur d'apport **ponctuelle** à un horodatage donné. Stockée dans la table Observation ; il peut y avoir plusieurs lignes par jour, chacune un apport partiel.

Tous deux expriment l'énergie réellement consommée (délivrée), en kcal.

## Notes de mapping

- Mapper une valeur déjà totalisée sur 24 h vers *3026267 / 9057-1 — Calorie intake total 24 hour* (LOINC) ; mapper un apport par administration / ponctuel vers *37206982 / 787787004 — Energy intake* (SNOMED).
- **Pour comparer les deux, les valeurs ponctuelles doivent être sommées par patient et par jour** afin de reconstituer un total journalier équivalent au concept LOINC. Comme les deux concepts vivent en outre dans des tables CDM différentes (Measurement vs Observation), une requête d'apport journalier doit lire les deux et les réunir, par exemple :

```sql
-- Apport énergétique journalier (kcal) par patient, harmonisant les deux concepts.
-- LOINC 9057-1 est déjà un total 24 h ; SNOMED 787787004 est sommé par jour.
WITH daily_total AS (   -- déjà un total 24 h (table Measurement)
    SELECT person_id,
           CAST(measurement_datetime AS DATE) AS intake_day,
           value_as_number AS kcal
    FROM   measurement
    WHERE  measurement_concept_id = 3026267        -- Calorie intake total 24 hour
),
pointwise AS (          -- apports ponctuels (table Observation), sommés par jour
    SELECT person_id,
           CAST(observation_datetime AS DATE) AS intake_day,
           SUM(value_as_number) AS kcal
    FROM   observation
    WHERE  observation_concept_id = 37206982       -- Energy intake
    GROUP  BY person_id, CAST(observation_datetime AS DATE)
)
SELECT person_id, intake_day, kcal, 'total_24h' AS source FROM daily_total
UNION ALL
SELECT person_id, intake_day, kcal, 'summed'    AS source FROM pointwise;
```

  Privilégier le total 24 h pré-agrégé quand les deux sont disponibles le même jour, pour éviter le double comptage.
- Ne **pas** mapper ici le *besoin* énergétique (une cible, pas ce qui a été délivré) — c'est le jeu *Energy requirement*.

name: Energy requirement
description: Energy requirement — the target amount of energy a patient needs over 24 hours; in kilocalories (kcal).

en.name: Energy requirement
en.shortDescription: Energy requirement — the target amount of energy a patient needs over 24 hours; in kilocalories (kcal).
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Energy requirement is the *target* amount of energy a patient needs (estimated or prescribed), against which actual intake is compared. It produces a numeric value, typically per 24 hours, used to set nutritional goals. It is reported in kilocalories (kcal). It is a goal/estimate — not a measurement of what was delivered (that is *Energy intake*).

## Included Concepts

The set is anchored on the SNOMED *Energy requirement* concept with its descendants, grouped below for readability — all are the same `energy_requirement` target variable.

### Generic energy requirement (default)

- *4022415 / 226244007 — Energy requirement (SNOMED)*: the default target.
- *604877 / 1003837001 — Estimated required quantity of energy in 24 hours (SNOMED)*: the estimated 24-hour requirement.

### Weight-indexed and population-specific

- *604878 / 1003838006 — Estimated required quantity of energy per kilogram body weight in 24 hours (SNOMED)*: requirement expressed **per kilogram of body weight** (kcal/kg/24 h) — a *different unit* from the absolute concepts above (kcal/24 h), see Mapping Notes.
- *45771253 / 702387006 — Pediatric energy requirement (SNOMED)*: paediatric target.

### Composition-specific

- *4027088 / 226245008 — Non-protein energy requirement (SNOMED)*: the energy target excluding protein-derived energy.

## Mapping Notes

- Map a nutritional energy *target/goal* here, using *4022415 / 226244007 — Energy requirement* (SNOMED) by default.
- **Per-kg, paediatric, and non-protein variants are attributes**: map to them only when the source explicitly records that form; otherwise use the generic concept.
- **Units are not comparable across the per-kg and absolute concepts**: *604878 / 1003838006 — Estimated required quantity of energy per kilogram body weight in 24 hours* is in **kcal/kg/24 h**, while *4022415 / 226244007 — Energy requirement* and *604877 / 1003837001 — Estimated required quantity of energy in 24 hours* are in **kcal/24 h**. To compare them you must multiply the per-kg value by the patient's body weight: `absolute_kcal_per_24h = per_kg_value × body_weight_kg` (body weight from the *Body weight* set). Do not pool the two units without this conversion.
- Do **not** map energy actually delivered/consumed here — that is the *Energy intake* set.

fr.name: Besoin énergétique
fr.shortDescription: Besoin énergétique — quantité d'énergie cible nécessaire au patient sur 24 heures ; en kilocalories (kcal).
fr.longDescription:
## Définition et contexte clinique

Le besoin énergétique est la quantité *cible* d'énergie dont un patient a besoin (estimée ou prescrite), à laquelle l'apport réel est comparé. Il produit une valeur numérique, typiquement par 24 heures, servant à fixer les objectifs nutritionnels. Il est exprimé en kilocalories (kcal). C'est un objectif/une estimation — pas une mesure de ce qui a été délivré (cela relève d'*Energy intake*).

## Concepts inclus

Le jeu est ancré sur le concept SNOMED *Energy requirement* et ses descendants, regroupés ci-dessous pour la lisibilité — tous constituent la même variable cible `energy_requirement`.

### Besoin énergétique générique (par défaut)

- *4022415 / 226244007 — Energy requirement (SNOMED)* : la cible par défaut.
- *604877 / 1003837001 — Estimated required quantity of energy in 24 hours (SNOMED)* : le besoin estimé sur 24 heures.

### Indexé sur le poids et spécifique à une population

- *604878 / 1003838006 — Estimated required quantity of energy per kilogram body weight in 24 hours (SNOMED)* : besoin exprimé **par kilogramme de poids corporel** (kcal/kg/24 h) — une *unité différente* des concepts absolus ci-dessus (kcal/24 h), voir Notes de mapping.
- *45771253 / 702387006 — Pediatric energy requirement (SNOMED)* : cible pédiatrique.

### Spécifique à la composition

- *4027088 / 226245008 — Non-protein energy requirement (SNOMED)* : la cible énergétique hors énergie d'origine protéique.

## Notes de mapping

- Mapper ici une *cible/objectif* énergétique nutritionnel, via *4022415 / 226244007 — Energy requirement* (SNOMED) par défaut.
- **Les variantes par kg, pédiatrique et non protéique sont des attributs** : ne mapper vers elles que si la source enregistre explicitement cette forme ; sinon utiliser le concept générique.
- **Les unités ne sont pas comparables entre le concept par kg et les concepts absolus** : *604878 / 1003838006 — Estimated required quantity of energy per kilogram body weight in 24 hours* est en **kcal/kg/24 h**, alors que *4022415 / 226244007 — Energy requirement* et *604877 / 1003837001 — Estimated required quantity of energy in 24 hours* sont en **kcal/24 h**. Pour les comparer, il faut multiplier la valeur par kg par le poids du patient : `kcal_absolu_par_24h = valeur_par_kg × poids_corporel_kg` (poids issu du jeu *Body weight*). Ne pas regrouper les deux unités sans cette conversion.
- Ne **pas** mapper ici l'énergie réellement délivrée/consommée — c'est le jeu *Energy intake*.

## Definition & Clinical Context

This set captures the fact that an advance care plan has been agreed with the patient — a documented record of the patient's wishes about future care (including limits on treatment). It is a flag (recorded = a plan has been agreed), not a numeric measurement, and is used in end-of-life and goals-of-care decision-making.

## Included Concepts

- *36685263 / 1095851000000100 — Advance care plan agreed (SNOMED)*: the agreed-plan flag.

## Mapping Notes

- Map a documented "advance care plan agreed" record here, using *36685263 / 1095851000000100 — Advance care plan agreed* (SNOMED).
- Treat it as a flag (presence = a plan has been agreed). The plan's content (e.g. resuscitation status, treatment limits) is captured by separate observations, not this set.

fr.name: Directives anticipées établies

Il s'agit d'un indicateur (enregistré = un plan a été convenu), non d'une mesure numérique, utilisé dans les décisions de fin de vie et d'objectifs de soins.

## Concepts inclus

## Notes de mapping

- Le traiter comme un indicateur (présence = un plan a été convenu). Le contenu du plan (statut de réanimation, limitations de traitement) est capturé par des observations distinctes, hors de ce jeu.

en.name: Consultation with patient
en.shortDescription: Consultation with patient — a clinical encounter between a clinician and the patient (any setting); recorded as an event.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

This set captures a clinical encounter between a clinician and the patient — a consultation event, regardless of setting (face-to-face, telemedicine, new vs follow-up). It is recorded as an event (it happened at a given time), not a numeric measurement, and is used to track patient contacts.

## Included Concepts

The set is anchored on the SNOMED *Consultation with patient* concept with its descendants, grouped below for readability — all are the same `consultation` event variable.

### Generic consultation (default)

- *37164964 / 1237136005 — Consultation with patient (SNOMED)*: the default consultation event.
- *4089048 / 185387006 — New patient consultation (SNOMED)* and *4027135 / 12843005 — Subsequent hospital visit by physician (SNOMED)*: new vs follow-up encounters.

### By modality

- *37168078 / 1269515004 — Face to face consultation with patient (SNOMED)*, *40489429 / 448337001 — Telemedicine consultation with patient (SNOMED)*, *1450350 / 2365641000000100 — Group face to face consultation (SNOMED)*.

### By context / purpose

- *4211804 / 416520008 — Consultation for unaccompanied minor (SNOMED)*, *37208165 / 461231000124109 — Consultation for suicide risk management (SNOMED)*, *764768 / 6051000124107 — Pharmacokinetic consultation (SNOMED)*, *764769 / 6061000124109 — Risk evaluation and mitigation strategy consultation (SNOMED)*.

## Mapping Notes

- Map a patient-consultation event here, using *37164964 / 1237136005 — Consultation with patient* (SNOMED) by default.
- **Modality, encounter type and purpose are attributes**: map to a specific variant only when the source documents it; otherwise use the generic concept.

fr.name: Consultation avec le patient
fr.shortDescription: Consultation avec le patient — rencontre clinique entre un soignant et le patient (tout contexte) ; enregistrée comme un événement.
fr.longDescription:
## Définition et contexte clinique

Ce jeu capture une rencontre clinique entre un soignant et le patient — un événement de consultation, quel que soit le contexte (présentiel, télémédecine, première fois vs suivi). Il est enregistré comme un événement (il a eu lieu à un instant donné), non comme une mesure numérique, et sert à suivre les contacts avec le patient.

## Concepts inclus

Le jeu est ancré sur le concept SNOMED *Consultation with patient* et ses descendants, regroupés ci-dessous pour la lisibilité — tous constituent la même variable d'événement `consultation`.

### Consultation générique (par défaut)

- *37164964 / 1237136005 — Consultation with patient (SNOMED)* : l'événement de consultation par défaut.
- *4089048 / 185387006 — New patient consultation (SNOMED)* et *4027135 / 12843005 — Subsequent hospital visit by physician (SNOMED)* : première rencontre vs suivi.

### Par modalité

- *37168078 / 1269515004 — Face to face consultation with patient (SNOMED)*, *40489429 / 448337001 — Telemedicine consultation with patient (SNOMED)*, *1450350 / 2365641000000100 — Group face to face consultation (SNOMED)*.

### Par contexte / finalité

- *4211804 / 416520008 — Consultation for unaccompanied minor (SNOMED)*, *37208165 / 461231000124109 — Consultation for suicide risk management (SNOMED)*, *764768 / 6051000124107 — Pharmacokinetic consultation (SNOMED)*, *764769 / 6061000124109 — Risk evaluation and mitigation strategy consultation (SNOMED)*.

## Notes de mapping

- Mapper ici un événement de consultation patient, via *37164964 / 1237136005 — Consultation with patient* (SNOMED) par défaut.
- **La modalité, le type de rencontre et la finalité sont des attributs** : ne mapper vers une variante spécifique que si la source la documente ; sinon utiliser le concept générique.

en.name: Surrogate decision maker documented
en.shortDescription: Surrogate decision maker documented — a flag that an active healthcare surrogate (proxy decision maker) is on record for the patient.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

This set captures the fact that the patient has an active healthcare surrogate on record — a person authorised to make care decisions on the patient's behalf when the patient cannot. It is a flag (recorded = a surrogate is in place), not a numeric measurement, and is relevant to consent and goals-of-care decisions, especially for incapacitated ICU patients.

## Included Concepts

- *762209 / 3021000175108 — Active healthcare surrogate (SNOMED)*: the surrogate-on-record flag.

## Mapping Notes

- Map a documented active surrogate / healthcare proxy here, using *762209 / 3021000175108 — Active healthcare surrogate* (SNOMED).
- Treat it as a flag (presence = a surrogate decision maker is documented). The surrogate's identity or relationship is captured separately, not in this set.

fr.shortDescription: Décideur substitut documenté — indicateur attestant qu'un mandataire de santé actif (décideur substitut) est enregistré pour le patient.
fr.longDescription:
## Définition et contexte clinique

Ce jeu capture le fait que le patient dispose d'un mandataire de santé actif enregistré — une personne autorisée à prendre des décisions de soins au nom du patient lorsque celui-ci ne le peut pas. Il s'agit d'un indicateur (enregistré = un substitut est en place), non d'une mesure numérique, pertinent pour le consentement et les décisions d'objectifs de soins, en particulier chez le patient de réanimation incapable de s'exprimer.

## Concepts inclus

- *762209 / 3021000175108 — Active healthcare surrogate (SNOMED)* : l'indicateur de substitut enregistré.

## Notes de mapping

- Mapper ici un mandataire de santé / substitut actif documenté, via *762209 / 3021000175108 — Active healthcare surrogate* (SNOMED).
- Le traiter comme un indicateur (présence = un décideur substitut est documenté). L'identité ou le lien du substitut est capturé séparément, hors de ce jeu.

name: Central venous catheter
description: Central venous catheter (CVC) device of any type (tunnelled, non-tunnelled, cuffed, PICC, umbilical…) — the presence of a CVC, not the insertion/removal procedure.

en.name: Central venous catheter
en.shortDescription: Central venous catheter (CVC) device of any type (tunnelled, non-tunnelled, cuffed, PICC, umbilical…) — the presence of a CVC, not the insertion/removal procedure.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

A central venous catheter (CVC) is a catheter whose tip sits in a large central vein (typically the superior or inferior vena cava), used to deliver drugs, fluids or parenteral nutrition, to measure central venous pressure, or for haemodialysis. In source data this set captures the **device** — i.e. the presence of a CVC — rather than the procedures of inserting, removing or replacing it. Each entry is a device record; there is no unit. It is recorded in intensive care, anaesthesia and oncology, across adult and neonatal patients. Representing the CVC as a device (rather than via insertion/removal procedures) makes it straightforward to determine whether a catheter is present over a given period [issue #15].

## Included Concepts

The set is anchored on the SNOMED device concept *Central venous catheter* with its descendants, so every CVC sub-type resolves automatically (and future SNOMED additions are captured). This currently resolves to the following devices.

- *4179206 / 52124006 — Central venous catheter (SNOMED)*: the general device concept; the default.
- *40482049 / 445085009 — Tunneled central venous catheter (SNOMED)*: tunnelled under the skin (e.g. for long-term use).
- *42709987 / 449859004 — Nontunneled central venous catheter (SNOMED)*: percutaneous, short-term.
- *42709989 / 449861008 — Cuffed central venous catheter (SNOMED)*.
- *4161814 / 398176008 — Peripherally inserted central catheter (SNOMED)*: PICC, inserted via a peripheral (usually arm) vein with the tip central.
- *37167946 / 1269192008 — Epicutaneo-caval catheter (SNOMED)*: a peripherally inserted central catheter used in neonates.
- *37167492 / 1268297002 — Umbilical venous catheter (SNOMED)*: inserted via the umbilical vein in neonates (kept — INDICATE includes neonatal patients).

## Mapping Notes

- **Default concept** when the source records a central venous catheter without a specific type: *4179206 / 52124006 — Central venous catheter*. Map to a specific type (tunnelled, non-tunnelled, cuffed, PICC, epicutaneo-caval, umbilical) only when documented.
- **Device, not procedure**: this set represents the presence of a CVC. The procedures of inserting, removing or replacing a CVC are intentionally not part of this set (removed per issue #15) — model CVC presence via this Device set, not via insertion/removal/replacement procedures.
- **Neonatal lines included**: umbilical venous catheters and epicutaneo-caval catheters are kept, as INDICATE includes neonatal patients.
- **Not a peripheral venous catheter**: a peripheral IV cannula (tip not central) is a different device and is not part of this set.

name: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO)
description: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) — extracorporeal life support; includes veno-venous (VV), veno-arterial (VA) and arterio-venous (AV) configurations.

en.name: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO)
en.shortDescription: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) — extracorporeal life support; includes veno-venous (VV), veno-arterial (VA) and arterio-venous (AV) configurations.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is a form of extracorporeal life support in which blood is pumped out of the body, oxygenated (and cleared of carbon dioxide) through a membrane oxygenator, and returned to the patient — used for severe, potentially reversible respiratory and/or cardiac failure. In source data this is a **procedure** record indicating that the patient was supported on ECMO; there is no unit. It is recorded in intensive care. The main configurations differ by where blood is drained and returned: veno-venous (VV, respiratory support) and veno-arterial (VA, respiratory + cardiac support).

## Included Concepts

The set is anchored on the SNOMED procedure *Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation* with its descendants, so the configuration sub-types resolve automatically.

- *4052536 / 233573008 — Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (SNOMED)*: the general concept; the default when the configuration is not specified.
- *37206603 / 786453001 — Venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (SNOMED)*: VV-ECMO — drains and returns venous blood; supports oxygenation/ventilation (respiratory failure).
- *37206601 / 786451004 — Venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (SNOMED)*: VA-ECMO — returns blood to an artery; supports both gas exchange and the circulation (cardiac or combined failure).
- *37206602 / 786452006 — Arteriovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (SNOMED)*: AV-ECMO — a pumpless configuration (pumpless extracorporeal lung assist) that draws from an artery and returns to a vein, driven by the patient's own arterial pressure rather than a pump; used mainly for carbon dioxide removal and requiring an adequately functioning heart.

## Mapping Notes

- **Default concept** when the source records ECMO without specifying the configuration: *4052536 / 233573008 — Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation*. Map to a specific configuration (VV, VA, AV) only when documented.
- **The ECMO procedure, not the equipment**: the ECMO circuit, membrane oxygenator and pump are devices captured elsewhere if needed; cannulation and blood sampling from the circuit are separate procedures and are not part of this set.

en.name: Enteral feeding
en.shortDescription: Enteral (tube) feeding — nutrition delivered into the GI tract via a feeding tube, by any route or method.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Enteral feeding (tube feeding) is the delivery of nutrition directly into the gastrointestinal tract through a feeding tube, used when a patient cannot eat safely or adequately by mouth. In source data this is a **procedure** record indicating that the patient received enteral nutrition; there is no unit. It is recorded in intensive care and across acute care. The variants differ by the route/site of the tube (nasogastric, orogastric, nasoduodenal, nasojejunal, gastrostomy, jejunostomy, etc.) and by the delivery method (continuous drip vs syringe/bolus).

## Included Concepts

The set is anchored on the SNOMED procedure *Enteral feeding* with all its descendants, so every route and method resolves automatically (and future SNOMED additions are captured). This currently resolves to the following concepts.

### Generic (default)

- *4042005 / 229912004 — Enteral feeding (SNOMED)*: the general concept; the default when the route is not specified.

### By tube route / site

- *4047288 / 229914003 — Nasogastric feeding (SNOMED)*: via a nasogastric tube (the most common ICU route).
- *4041331 / 229913009 — Orogastric feeding (SNOMED)*: via an orogastric tube.
- *4079763 / 183028005 — Nasal tube feeding (SNOMED)*: via a nasal tube (route into stomach/duodenum unspecified).
- *4041332 / 229915002 — Nasoduodenal feeding (SNOMED)* and *4151009 / 310244003 — Nasojejunal feeding (SNOMED)*: post-pyloric nasal routes.
- *4042006 / 229916001 — Esophagostomy feeding (SNOMED)*.
- *4041333 / 229917005 — Gastrostomy feeding (SNOMED)*, *4021170 / 225373002 — Percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy feeding (SNOMED)* (PEG), *4125454 / 289133003 — Button gastrostomy feeding (SNOMED)*.
- *4021171 / 225374008 — Jejunostomy feeding (SNOMED)* and *1244020 / 47441000087101 — Gastrojejunostomy tube feeding (SNOMED)*.

### By delivery method

- *4211519 / 56948003 — Tube feeding by drip method (SNOMED)*: continuous/gravity drip.
- *4306560 / 38903004 — Tube feeding by syringe method (SNOMED)*: bolus.

## Mapping Notes

- **Default concept** when the source records enteral/tube feeding without a specific route: *4042005 / 229912004 — Enteral feeding*. Map to a specific route (nasogastric, gastrostomy, jejunostomy…) only when documented.
- **Route vs method are independent**: a record may mention both (e.g. nasogastric continuous drip); map to the most specific single concept available, do not split one event across two concepts.
- **Not parenteral nutrition**: intravenous (parenteral) nutrition is a different route and is not part of this set.
- **The feeding act, not the tube device**: inserting the feeding tube and the tube itself are separate concepts; this set is the act of feeding via the enteral route.

en.name: Mobilization
en.shortDescription: Patient mobilization — getting the patient moving (in/out of bed, standing, walking, with or without assistance); the act, not joint/organ mobilization.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Mobilization here means **patient mobilization** — the physiotherapy/nursing activity of getting a critically ill patient moving: assisting with movement in bed, sitting up, getting out of bed, standing, and walking. Early mobilization is a core ICU rehabilitation intervention that counters the deconditioning of prolonged bed rest. In source data this is a **procedure** record indicating that the patient was mobilized; there is no unit. It is recorded in intensive care and rehabilitation. It is the counterpart of the *Order not to mobilize* concept set.

## Included Concepts

The set lists the SNOMED procedures for patient mobilization and ambulation (curated — SNOMED has no single anchor for patient mobilization, and the broad 'mobilization' hierarchy mixes in joint and surgical mobilizations that are out of scope).

- *46272565 / 710950005 — Progressive mobility (SNOMED)*: progressive (staged) patient mobilization — the core ICU early-mobility concept.
- *46271859 / 710122006 — Promotion of physical mobility (SNOMED)*.
- *46272439 / 710803000 — Assistance with mobility (SNOMED)* and *37016972 / 713138001 — Assistance with mobility in bed (SNOMED)*.
- *1242274 / 12101000202101 — Assistance with getting out of bed (SNOMED)*.
- *46272440 / 710804006 — Assistance with walking using device (SNOMED)* and *46271857 / 710120003 — Promotion of walking using mobility aid (SNOMED)*.
- *4040262 / 229595009 — Walking with patient - mobilization (SNOMED)*, *4204159 / 308931006 — Walking practice (SNOMED)*, *4158838 / 370871008 — Ambulation therapy (SNOMED)*.

## Mapping Notes

- Map records of the patient being mobilized / ambulated (in bed, out of bed, walking, with or without assistance/aids) to the matching concept here; use *46272565 / 710950005 — Progressive mobility* as the general early-mobility concept when not otherwise specified.
- **Patient mobilization, not joint/organ mobilization**: manual-therapy joint mobilizations (e.g. 'accessory mobilization of the shoulder') and surgical organ mobilizations (e.g. 'mobilization of intestine') are *not* part of this set — they were removed.
- **Counterpart of 'Order not to mobilize'**: this set is the act of mobilizing; the order not to mobilize (bed rest directive) is a separate concept set.

fr.shortDescription: Mobilisation du patient — mise en mouvement (au lit, hors du lit, debout, marche, avec ou sans aide) ; l’acte, non la mobilisation articulaire/chirurgicale.

name: Order not to mobilize
description: Clinical order that the patient must not be mobilized (bed rest); the directive itself, not the mobility status.

en.name: Order not to mobilize
en.shortDescription: Clinical order that the patient must not be mobilized (bed rest); the directive itself, not the mobility status.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

An order not to mobilize is a clinical directive indicating that a patient must not be mobilized — that is, must remain in bed or in a fixed position. This order is typically issued in the ICU or acute care setting when mobilization could be harmful, for example during hemodynamic instability, uncontrolled intracranial hypertension, unstable spinal fracture, active hemorrhage, or the immediate postoperative period following certain procedures [1].

This concept captures the clinical decision (the order itself), not the patient's mobility status. It is recorded as a binary observation: the order is either active or absent. It should not be confused with the patient's actual level of mobilization, which is captured by separate concept sets.

## Included Concepts

This concept set contains a single custom concept, as no equivalent exists in standard terminologies (SNOMED, LOINC).

## Mapping Notes

- **Source labels**: "No mobilization order", "Bed rest order", "Do not mobilize", "Strict bed rest" → map to this concept.
- **Distinguish from mobility status**: This concept captures the *order* (a directive), not the *observation* that the patient does not mobilize. "Patient does not mobilize" (a clinical finding) should not be mapped here.
- **Value**: This is typically a binary observation — the order is active or not. Use `value_as_concept_id` with appropriate Yes/No concepts if needed, or simply record the observation row when the order is active.

## References

[1] Hodgson CL, Stiller K, Needham DM, et al. Expert consensus and recommendations on safety criteria for active mobilization of mechanically ventilated critically ill adults. Crit Care. 2014;18(6):658. doi:10.1186/s13054-014-0658-y. PMID: 25475522

fr.name: Prescription de non-mobilisation
fr.shortDescription: Prescription indiquant que le patient ne doit pas être mobilisé (repos au lit) ; la directive elle-même, non le statut de mobilité.
fr.longDescription:
## Définition et contexte clinique

La prescription de non-mobilisation est une directive clinique indiquant qu'un patient ne doit pas être mobilisé — c'est-à-dire qu'il doit rester alité ou dans une position fixe. Cette prescription est typiquement émise en réanimation ou en soins aigus lorsque la mobilisation pourrait être délétère, par exemple en cas d'instabilité hémodynamique, d'hypertension intracrânienne non contrôlée, de fracture rachidienne instable, d'hémorragie active, ou en période postopératoire immédiate après certaines interventions [1].

Ce concept capture la décision clinique (la prescription elle-même), et non le statut de mobilité du patient. Il est enregistré comme une observation binaire : la prescription est active ou absente. Il ne doit pas être confondu avec le niveau de mobilisation effectif du patient, qui est capturé par des concept sets distincts.

## Concepts inclus

Ce concept set contient un seul concept custom, aucun équivalent n'existant dans les terminologies standard (SNOMED, LOINC).

## Notes de mapping

- **Libellés sources** : « Interdiction de lever », « Repos strict au lit », « Non-mobilisation », « Alitement strict » → mapper vers ce concept.
- **Distinguer du statut de mobilité** : Ce concept capture la *prescription* (une directive), et non l'*observation* que le patient ne se mobilise pas. « Le patient ne se mobilise pas » (un constat clinique) ne doit pas être mappé ici.
- **Valeur** : Il s'agit typiquement d'une observation binaire — la prescription est active ou non. Utiliser `value_as_concept_id` avec les concepts Oui/Non appropriés si nécessaire, ou simplement enregistrer la ligne d'observation lorsque la prescription est active.

## Références

[1] Hodgson CL, Stiller K, Needham DM, et al. Expert consensus and recommendations on safety criteria for active mobilization of mechanically ventilated critically ill adults. Crit Care. 2014;18(6):658. doi:10.1186/s13054-014-0658-y. PMID: 25475522

name: Prone position

en.name: Prone position
en.shortDescription: Prone (face-down) body position — the position state, not the act of placing the patient prone.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Prone position is the body position in which the patient lies face-down (on the stomach). In intensive care, placing a patient prone improves oxygenation in severe ARDS and is a standard intervention there. In source data this set captures the **position state** — that the patient is/was in the prone position — as an observation, rather than the action of turning the patient prone. There is no unit. It is recorded in intensive care and anaesthesia.

## Included Concepts

- *4050473 / 1240000 — Prone body position (SNOMED)*: the patient is in the prone (face-down) body position.

## Mapping Notes

- This concept captures the **state** (the patient is prone), not the act of placing the patient prone. Source records of the *procedure* 'placing subject in prone position' or 'assisted ventilation in prone position' describe the action/intervention; map the resulting position state here.
- **Not semi-prone / lateral**: the semi-prone and lateral positions are distinct body positions and are not part of this set.

en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Plasmapheresis is an extracorporeal procedure in which blood is separated and the plasma is removed (and replaced with a substitute fluid or returned after treatment), used to remove circulating antibodies, immune complexes or toxins — e.g. in autoimmune and certain neurological or haematological conditions. Therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE) is the form in which the removed plasma is replaced. In source data this is a **procedure** record; there is no unit. It is recorded in intensive care, nephrology and haematology.

## Included Concepts

The set is anchored on the SNOMED procedure *Plasmapheresis* with its descendants.

- *4049372 / 20720000 — Plasmapheresis (SNOMED)*: the general concept; the default.
- *4076662 / 225067007 — Therapeutic plasma exchange (SNOMED)*: plasmapheresis with replacement of the removed plasma (TPE).
- *4055766 / 19647005 — Therapeutic plasmapheresis using plasma as the major replacement fluid (SNOMED)*.

## Mapping Notes

- **Default concept** when the source records plasmapheresis or plasma exchange without detail: *4049372 / 20720000 — Plasmapheresis*. Map to *4076662 / 225067007 — Therapeutic plasma exchange* when the source specifies plasma exchange (TPE).
- **Not other apheresis / RRT**: cytapheresis and renal replacement therapy (haemodialysis/haemofiltration) are different extracorporeal procedures in their own concept sets.
