name: Renal replacement therapy (RRT)
description: Renal replacement therapy (RRT) — continuous, intermittent and hybrid dialysis/filtration for kidney failure.

en.name: Renal replacement therapy (RRT)
en.shortDescription: Renal replacement therapy (RRT) — continuous, intermittent and hybrid dialysis/filtration for kidney failure.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Renal replacement therapy (RRT) replaces kidney function in acute or chronic kidney failure by removing waste products and excess fluid from the blood. In the ICU it is delivered as continuous therapy (CRRT, run around the clock in haemodynamically unstable patients), intermittent haemodialysis (IHD), or hybrid/prolonged modalities (SLED/PIRRT). In source data this is a **procedure** record indicating that the patient received RRT; there is no unit. It is recorded in intensive care and nephrology. Modalities differ by continuity (continuous vs intermittent), the solute-removal principle (diffusion = dialysis, convection = filtration, or both = diafiltration), and the vascular access (veno-venous vs arterio-venous).

## Included Concepts

The set anchors on the SNOMED procedure *Continuous renal replacement therapy* with its descendants (covering all continuous modalities), plus the intermittent and hybrid modalities listed explicitly. Grouped here by continuity.

### Continuous (CRRT)

Anchored on *Continuous renal replacement therapy* with descendants — veno-venous and arterio-venous haemodialysis (CVVHD/CAVHD), haemofiltration (CVVHF/CAVHF) and haemodiafiltration (CVVHDF/CAVHDF).

- *37018292 / 714749008 — Continuous renal replacement therapy (SNOMED)*
- (descendants: continuous veno-venous and arterio-venous haemodialysis, haemofiltration and haemodiafiltration variants)

### Intermittent

- *4051326 / 233575001 — Intermittent hemodialysis (SNOMED)*
- *4050862 / 233577009 — Intermittent hemodialysis with continuous ultrafiltration (SNOMED)*
- *4051327 / 233576000 — Intermittent hemodialysis with sequential ultrafiltration (SNOMED)*
- *4050865 / 233582002 — Intermittent hemofiltration (SNOMED)*
- *4052538 / 233587008 — Intermittent hemodiafiltration (SNOMED)*

### Hybrid / prolonged

- *44783963 / 698074000 — Sustained low-efficiency dialysis (SNOMED)*
- *619390 / 895382009 — Prolonged intermittent renal replacement therapy (SNOMED)*

### Generic modalities

- *4120120 / 302497006 — Hemodialysis (SNOMED)*
- *4050864 / 233581009 — Hemofiltration (SNOMED)*
- *4049845 / 233586004 — Hemodiafiltration (SNOMED)*

## Mapping Notes

- **Default concepts** when the source records RRT without detail: map a generic 'dialysis/haemodialysis' to *4120120 / 302497006 — Hemodialysis*, generic continuous therapy to *37018292 / 714749008 — Continuous renal replacement therapy*. Map to a specific modality (CVVHDF, IHD, SLED…) when documented.
- **Diafiltration vs dialysis vs filtration**: diafiltration (HDF) combines diffusion and convection; map to the matching concept rather than collapsing to plain dialysis when the source distinguishes them.
- **This is the RRT procedure**, not chronic-care/home-dialysis administrative concepts (home, maintenance, nocturnal dialysis) — those are not part of this acute-care set — nor the vascular access (dialysis catheter), which is a separate device.
- **Peritoneal dialysis** is a different RRT route, rare in adult ICU; it is not included here.

name: Endotracheal tube

en.name: Endotracheal tube
en.shortDescription: Any type of endotracheal tube device (standard, preformed/RAE, armoured, and specialty tubes).
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

An endotracheal tube (ETT) is a flexible tube inserted through the mouth or nose into the trachea to secure the airway and connect the patient to a ventilator or anaesthesia circuit. In source data this is a **device** record, not a measurement: each entry identifies the type of tube placed in a patient, with no associated value or unit. It is most commonly recorded in intensive care, the operating theatre, and emergency settings, around intubation and mechanical ventilation. The variants in this set differ only by the tube's shape, reinforcement, or built-in features — clinically they are all endotracheal tubes.

## Included Concepts

The set is anchored on the single SNOMED device concept *Endotracheal tube* with all its descendants, so every more specific tube type resolves automatically (and future SNOMED additions are captured without editing the set). This currently resolves to 19 concepts, grouped here by what distinguishes them.

### Generic endotracheal tube (default)

Use this when the source records an endotracheal tube without specifying a type.

- *4097216 / 26412008 — Endotracheal tube (SNOMED)*: the general device concept; the default for any unspecified ETT.

### By shape / preformed design

Tubes pre-bent to route away from the surgical field, mostly used in head-and-neck or facial procedures.

- *4149923 / 309802003 — RAE endotracheal tube (SNOMED)*: a preformed (Ring–Adair–Elwyn) tube with a fixed bend.
- *4148969 / 309804002 — Oral RAE endotracheal tube (SNOMED)*: oral RAE variant.
- *4148970 / 309805001 — Nasal RAE endotracheal tube (SNOMED)*: nasal RAE variant.
- *4225181 / 420977008 — Preformed endotracheal tube (SNOMED)*: any pre-shaped tube.
- *4148025 / 309803008 — Oxford endotracheal tube (SNOMED)*: an L-shaped preformed tube.
- *4224877 / 420673005 — Magill type endotracheal tube (SNOMED)*: a standard-curve (Magill) tube.
- *4222389 / 420344001 — Magill type oral endotracheal tube (SNOMED)*: oral Magill variant.
- *4223308 / 420855005 — Magill type nasal endotracheal tube (SNOMED)*: nasal Magill variant.

### By construction / reinforcement

- *4149922 / 309801005 — Armored endotracheal tube (SNOMED)*: wire-reinforced ("armoured") tube resistant to kinking.
- *45763195 — Laser-resistant endotracheal tube (SNOMED)*: tube designed to withstand airway laser surgery.

### By built-in feature

Tubes with an additional integrated function beyond securing the airway.

- *4327418 / 430553000 — Endotracheal tube with bronchial blocker (SNOMED)*: incorporates a blocker for one-lung isolation.
- *40486643 / 449298004 — Endotracheal tube with directional tip (SNOMED)*: steerable tip.
- *37162306 / 1187321001 — Oxygen insufflation endotracheal tube (SNOMED)*: allows supplemental oxygen insufflation.
- *45761574 — Cuff-suction endotracheal tube (SNOMED)*: with a port for subglottic secretion suction above the cuff.
- *3661742 / 870581009 — Video intubation endotracheal tube (SNOMED)*: with an integrated camera for video-assisted intubation.
- *45767499 — Electromyographic endotracheal tube (SNOMED)*: with electrodes for nerve (EMG) monitoring.
- *45773232 — High-frequency ventilation endotracheal tube (SNOMED)*: designed for high-frequency ventilation.
- *45758564 — Antimicrobial endotracheal tube (SNOMED)*: coated to reduce microbial colonisation.

## Mapping Notes

- **Default concept** when the source records an endotracheal tube without a specific type: *4097216 / 26412008 — Endotracheal tube*. Do not infer a specific variant from indirect clues — if the type is not documented, map to the generic concept.
- **Tracheostomy tubes are a separate device** and do not belong here; they have their own concept set. An endotracheal tube passes through the larynx; a tracheostomy tube enters through a surgical neck stoma.
- **This set is about the device, not the act**: placing or removing the tube (intubation, extubation) are procedures captured in their own concept sets, not here.
- **Tube size / diameter is not part of the device identity**: the internal diameter is recorded separately (see the Endotracheal tube diameter concept set), not by choosing a different device concept.

reviews.comments: Reply to Maxim Moinat's review. Not to study the type of tube: the Mapping Notes already send an unqualified tube to the generic concept, and the variants only exist so that sources recording a type have somewhere to map. The purpose is reconstructing the real period of invasive ventilation. In clinical data warehouses the invasive-ventilation concept is often a prescription rather than an observation, entered late and left open because nobody discontinued it, so the period is wrong at both ends. We plan to derive it from converging signals: ventilation parameters (tidal volume, PEEP and the rest) and the presence of an airway device. That is also why this is not redundant with concept set 305: intubation is a brief act, and its duration, when recorded at all, is the duration of the gesture rather than of the ventilation, whereas the device exposure spans the whole time the tube is in place.

name: Tracheostomy tube
description: Any type of tracheostomy tube device, including fenestrated, cannula components and laryngectomy tubes.

en.name: Tracheostomy tube
en.shortDescription: Any type of tracheostomy tube device, including fenestrated, cannula components and laryngectomy tubes.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

A tracheostomy tube is a tube inserted through a surgical opening in the front of the neck (a stoma) directly into the trachea, bypassing the mouth and larynx to secure the airway. In source data this is a **device** record, not a measurement: each entry identifies the type of tube placed in a patient, with no associated value or unit. It is recorded in intensive care (for patients on prolonged ventilation or with weaning difficulties) and in patients with a long-term or permanent tracheostomy. The variants in this set differ by design (fenestrated vs not, reinforced), by component (inner/outer cannula), or by the specific stoma context (laryngectomy), but all are tracheostomy-route airway devices.

## Included Concepts

The set is anchored on the single SNOMED device concept *Tracheostomy tube* with all its descendants, so every more specific type resolves automatically (and future SNOMED additions are captured without editing the set). This currently resolves to 9 concepts, grouped here by what distinguishes them.

### Generic tracheostomy tube (default)

Use this when the source records a tracheostomy tube without specifying a type.

- *4044008 / 129121000 — Tracheostomy tube (SNOMED)*: the general device concept; the default for any unspecified tracheostomy tube.

### By design

- *1076472 / 1343696006 — Fenestrated tracheostomy tube (SNOMED)*: has an opening (fenestration) in the outer cannula to allow airflow through the upper airway (e.g. to support speech).
- *1076494 / 1344664005 — Non-fenestrated tracheostomy tube (SNOMED)*: no fenestration.
- *45760063 / 465608000 — Reinforced tracheostomy tube (SNOMED)*: wall-reinforced tube resistant to kinking or compression.

### By component (cannula)

A tracheostomy tube assembly has an outer and (often) a removable inner cannula. These concepts identify the cannula component specifically.

- *605799 / 1137710007 — Tracheostomy tube cannula (SNOMED)*: a tracheostomy tube cannula (outer/generic).
- *1076451 / 1343640004 — Tracheostomy tube inner cannula (SNOMED)*: the removable inner cannula.

### By stoma context / use

- *45758602 / 463384005 — Operative tracheostomy tube (SNOMED)*: tube used for a surgically created tracheostomy.
- *45772047 / 470610002 — Laryngectomy tube (SNOMED)*: tube for a patient whose larynx has been removed (permanent stoma).
- *36713922 / 718933007 — Laryngectomy tube, non-sterile (SNOMED)*: non-sterile laryngectomy tube variant.

## Excluded Concepts

- *45759423 / 464651008 — Oxygen administration transtracheal catheter (SNOMED)*: excluded. SNOMED files it under *Tracheostomy tube*, but its other parents are *Pulmonological catheter* and *Catheter*: it is a thin catheter delivering oxygen into the trachea through a stoma for long-term oxygen therapy, not a tracheostomy tube. It is also evidence of chronic oxygen therapy rather than of invasive ventilation, which this set helps establish.

## Mapping Notes

- **Default concept** when the source records a tracheostomy tube without a specific type: *4044008 / 129121000 — Tracheostomy tube*. Do not infer a specific variant from indirect clues — if the type is not documented, map to the generic concept.
- **Endotracheal tubes are a separate device** and do not belong here; they have their own concept set. A tracheostomy tube enters through a surgical neck stoma; an endotracheal tube passes through the mouth or nose and the larynx.
- **This set is about the device, not the act**: creating the tracheostomy, inserting, changing or removing the tube are procedures captured in their own concept sets, not here.
- **Cannula components**: *605799 / 1137710007 — Tracheostomy tube cannula* and *1076451 / 1343640004 — Tracheostomy tube inner cannula* identify a cannula part rather than a complete tube; map to these only when the source explicitly records the cannula component.

en.name: Fraction of inspired oxygen (FiO2)
en.shortDescription: Fraction of inspired oxygen (FiO2) — proportion of O2 in inspired gas, set or measured, in % or as a 0–1 fraction.
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context The fraction of inspired oxygen (FiO2) is the proportion of oxygen in the gas a patient breathes in. Room air is about 21% oxygen; supplemental oxygen and ventilators deliver higher concentrations, up to 100%. In source data this is a single numeric value per patient-timestamp — either a ventilator/oxygen-device *setting* or a *measured* inspired oxygen concentration. It is recorded continuously in intensive care and anaesthesia for any patient receiving oxygen therapy or mechanical ventilation. It is reported either as a percentage (**%**, e.g. 40) or as a fraction between 0 and 1 (e.g. 0.40); the two scales differ by a factor of 100 [1]. ## Included Concepts The set lists the LOINC and SNOMED concepts for inspired oxygen concentration. These are leaf terms with no descendants, so they are listed explicitly rather than via a hierarchy anchor. They differ mainly by source (generic vs ventilator vs analyser) and by the scale used. ### Generic inspired oxygen concentration (default) Use these when the source records FiO2 without tying it to a specific ventilator or analyser. - *4353936 / 250774007 — Inspired oxygen concentration (SNOMED)*: the general observable for FiO2. Synonyms: "FIO2 - Inspired fraction of oxygen", "Inspired fraction of oxygen". - *3020716 / 3150-0 — Inhaled oxygen concentration (LOINC)*: generic inhaled oxygen concentration (%). ### Measured on / set by the ventilator - *3024882 / 19994-3 — Oxygen/Total gas setting [Volume Fraction] Ventilator (LOINC)*: the FiO2 *setting* on the ventilator (%). - *3026238 / 19996-8 — Oxygen/Inspired gas Respiratory system --on ventilator (LOINC)*: inspired oxygen in the respiratory system while on a ventilator (%). - *3025408 / 19995-0 — Oxygen/Inspired gas Respiratory system by O2 Analyzer --on ventilator (LOINC)*: as above, specifically measured by an inline oxygen analyser (%). ### Reported as a fraction (0–1) - *42869590 / 71835-3 — Oxygen/Gas total [Pure volume fraction] Inhaled gas (LOINC)*: FiO2 expressed as a pure volume fraction (a number between 0 and 1) rather than a percentage. **Note on units.** The recommended unit is **percent (`8554 / % — percent`, UCUM)** for every concept except *42869590 / 71835-3 — Oxygen/Gas total [Pure volume fraction] Inhaled gas*, whose recommended unit is the dimensionless **fraction (`720868 / {fraction} — fraction`, UCUM)** — a number between 0 and 1 (LOINC created this term specifically for results reported as a decimal fraction without units [1]). A conversion is registered both ways: 1 fraction = 100 %, 1 % = 0.01 fraction. When harmonising, be explicit about the scale — a stored value of `0.4` on a `%` concept (meaning 0.4%) is almost certainly a fraction recorded under the wrong concept and should be 40%. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source records FiO2 without specifying the device: *4353936 / 250774007 — Inspired oxygen concentration*. - **Setting vs measured**: if the source distinguishes the FiO2 *set* on the ventilator from the *measured* inspired oxygen, map the setting to *3024882 / 19994-3 — Oxygen/Total gas setting [Volume Fraction] Ventilator* and the analyser-measured value to *3025408 / 19995-0 — Oxygen/Inspired gas Respiratory system by O2 Analyzer --on ventilator*. If the distinction is not documented, use the generic concept. - **Scale matters**: values may arrive as a percentage (21–100) or as a fraction (0.21–1.0). Map to *42869590 / 71835-3 — Oxygen/Gas total [Pure volume fraction] Inhaled gas* only when the source genuinely reports a 0–1 fraction; otherwise use a percent concept. Do not silently mix the two scales. - **Do not confuse FiO2 with related measurements**: inhaled oxygen *flow rate* (L/min) belongs to the Oxygen flow rate concept set; the PaO2/FiO2 ratio belongs to the Horowitz index concept set; arterial/blood oxygen content belongs to the blood-gas concept sets. ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 3150-0 — Inhaled oxygen concentration. Available: https://loinc.org/3150-0/

## Summary
**No verdict (comment).** Why use multiple concepts that mean the same (SNOMED/LOINC)? Also, are all the LOINC codes necessary, with different levels of detail but still meaning more or less the same?

## Use in our quality indicators
- Used in QI01 (Lung-protective ventilation in ARDS).
- CQL: 4 of 6 concepts are referenced in [`IndicateQi01Ventilation.cql`](https://github.com/umg-minai/cql-indicate-qi/blob/d63eb84a308d5586fcede0b7e3fa73abf6b6761c/cql/IndicateQi01Ventilation.cql?plain=1): [3024882](https://github.com/umg-minai/cql-indicate-qi/blob/d63eb84a308d5586fcede0b7e3fa73abf6b6761c/cql/IndicateQi01Ventilation.cql?plain=1#L48), [3025408](https://github.com/umg-minai/cql-indicate-qi/blob/d63eb84a308d5586fcede0b7e3fa73abf6b6761c/cql/IndicateQi01Ventilation.cql?plain=1#L47), [3026238](https://github.com/umg-minai/cql-indicate-qi/blob/d63eb84a308d5586fcede0b7e3fa73abf6b6761c/cql/IndicateQi01Ventilation.cql?plain=1#L46), [4353936](https://github.com/umg-minai/cql-indicate-qi/blob/d63eb84a308d5586fcede0b7e3fa73abf6b6761c/cql/IndicateQi01Ventilation.cql?plain=1#L45) (each ID links to its code definition).

en.name: Oxygen flow rate
en.shortDescription: Oxygen flow rate delivered to the patient, in L/min (distinct from FiO2 concentration).
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Oxygen flow rate is the volume of oxygen delivered to a patient per unit time — the "litres per minute" set on a flowmeter feeding a nasal cannula, mask, or oxygen-delivery system. In source data this is a single numeric value per patient-timestamp. It is recorded in intensive care, on the ward, in anaesthesia, and in emergency settings for any patient on supplemental oxygen. It is reported in **litres per minute (L/min)** [1]. This is distinct from the fraction of inspired oxygen (FiO2), which is the *concentration* of oxygen in the inspired gas, not its flow (see Mapping Notes). ## Included Concepts The set lists the LOINC and SNOMED concepts for oxygen flow rate, grouped by source. The SNOMED delivered-flow concept is anchored with its descendants; the LOINC concepts are leaf terms listed explicitly. ### Delivered / inhaled oxygen flow (default) Use these for the flow of oxygen delivered to the patient when the source does not tie it to a specific delivery system. - *4141684 / 427081008 — Delivered oxygen flow rate (SNOMED)*: the flow of oxygen delivered to the patient; descendants are included. Synonym: "Fresh gas flow rate". - *44782836 / 698833004 — Delivered oxygen flow rate to non ventilated lung (SNOMED)*: delivered oxygen flow to the non-ventilated lung, e.g. during one-lung ventilation (a descendant of the concept above). - *3005629 / 3151-8 — Inhaled oxygen flow rate (LOINC)*: litres per minute of oxygen inhaled, for delivery devices that supply a volume per minute [1]. ### Oxygen delivery system flow - *3014080 / 19941-4 — Oxygen gas flow Oxygen delivery system (LOINC)*: oxygen gas flow measured on an oxygen delivery system. **Note on units**: all concepts are reported in **`8698 / L/min — liter per minute` (UCUM)**, the recommended unit for this set [1]. ## Mapping Notes - **Flow rate vs FiO2 — do not confuse them**: this set is the *flow* of oxygen in **L/min** (e.g. 2, 6, 15). The *fraction/concentration* of inspired oxygen (FiO2, in % or as a 0–1 fraction, e.g. 40% / 0.40) belongs to the Fraction of inspired oxygen (FiO2) concept set. A value like `10` with unit L/min is a flow rate; a value like `40` with unit % is a FiO2. Map each to its own set. - **Default concept** when the source records an oxygen flow rate without specifying the delivery system: *4141684 / 427081008 — Delivered oxygen flow rate*. - **Delivery-system flow**: map to *3014080 / 19941-4 — Oxygen gas flow Oxygen delivery system* only when the source explicitly attributes the flow to an oxygen delivery system. If unspecified, use the generic delivered-flow concept. - **One-lung ventilation**: map to *44782836 / 698833004 — Delivered oxygen flow rate to non ventilated lung* only when the source explicitly records flow to the non-ventilated lung. ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 3151-8 — Inhaled oxygen flow rate. Available: https://loinc.org/3151-8/

name: Extubation
description: Removal of an airway tube (endotracheal or tracheostomy), including unplanned removal; tube changes are excluded.

en.name: Extubation
en.shortDescription: Removal of an airway tube (endotracheal or tracheostomy), including unplanned removal; tube changes are excluded.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Extubation is the removal of an artificial airway tube — an endotracheal tube (passed through the mouth or nose into the trachea) or a tracheostomy tube (inserted through a surgical opening in the neck) — that was in place to support breathing. The source data is an event record: a procedure (or a recorded clinical finding, in the case of an unplanned removal) marking the moment the tube was taken out, rather than a numeric measurement. It is recorded in intensive care, recovery, and ward settings, typically as part of weaning a patient off mechanical ventilation. There is no unit — each record represents one extubation event for a patient at a timestamp.

The clinically important distinction in this set is between **removing** a tube (extubation — the patient is left without an artificial airway) and **changing** a tube (the old tube is taken out and a new one inserted immediately, so the patient is never without an airway). A tube change is *not* an extubation and is excluded from this set (see Excluded Concepts).

## Included Concepts

The set is anchored on the SNOMED procedure *Extubation of trachea* with all its descendants, plus the separate clinical finding for unplanned extubation. Excluding the tube-change branch (below), this resolves to five concepts, grouped here by what they describe.

### Generic extubation (default)

Use this when the source records an extubation without specifying which device was removed or how.

- *4148972 / 309812005 — Extubation of trachea (SNOMED)*: the general concept for removing an airway tube from the trachea. Synonym: "Tracheal extubation".

### By airway device removed

Use these when the source explicitly identifies the device.

- *4150627 / 271280005 — Removal of endotracheal tube (SNOMED)*: removal of an endotracheal tube specifically. Synonym: "Endotracheal extubation".
- *4195943 / 44482009 — Ventilating tube removal by another physician (SNOMED)*: a tube removal carried out by a physician other than the one primarily responsible; a child of endotracheal tube removal in SNOMED. Map here only when the source explicitly records this circumstance.
- *4012607 / 113153002 — Removal of tracheostomy tube (SNOMED)*: removal of a tracheostomy tube (decannulation).

### Unplanned extubation

- *4231838 / 405639008 — Inadvertent tracheal extubation (SNOMED)*: an accidental or unintended removal of the airway tube (e.g. self-extubation by the patient, or dislodgement during care), as opposed to a planned, clinician-led extubation. This is a clinical *finding* (recorded as an observation), not a procedure. Synonyms: "Accidental tracheal extubation".

## Excluded Concepts

In SNOMED, "changing a tube" is modelled as a *child* of "removing a tube", so it would otherwise be pulled in as a descendant of *Extubation of trachea*. A tube change replaces the tube immediately and leaves the patient with a continuous airway, so it does not represent an extubation. The following are therefore excluded (per issue #13):

- *4026054 / 225719006 — Changing endotracheal tube (SNOMED)* — and its descendant *4026055 / 225720000 — Changing endotracheal tube headband (SNOMED)*, which concerns the tube's external fixation, not the tube itself.
- *4331311 / 2267008 — Changing tracheostomy tube (SNOMED)*. Synonyms: "Replacement of tracheostomy tube", "Change of tracheostomy tube".

## Mapping Notes

- **Default concept** when the source records an extubation but does not say which device was removed or under what circumstances: *4148972 / 309812005 — Extubation of trachea*.
- **By device**: map to *4150627 / 271280005 — Removal of endotracheal tube* for an endotracheal tube, or *4012607 / 113153002 — Removal of tracheostomy tube* for tracheostomy decannulation, only when the source explicitly identifies the device. If the device is not documented, use the generic *4148972 / 309812005 — Extubation of trachea*.
- **Planned vs unplanned**: map to *4231838 / 405639008 — Inadvertent tracheal extubation* only when the source explicitly flags the event as accidental, unplanned, or self-extubation. A plain "extubation" with no such flag is a planned extubation and maps to *4148972 / 309812005 — Extubation of trachea*.
- **Do not map tube changes here**: source events labelled "tube change", "tube replacement", "ETT change", "trach change", or "change of tracheostomy tube" are *not* extubations and must not be mapped to this set, even though SNOMED files them under the removal hierarchy.
- **Reintubation / weaning context**: this set captures the extubation event itself. It does not capture the decision to wean, spontaneous breathing trials, or reintubation — those belong to separate concept sets.

name: Humidification Therapy
description: Humidification of the breathing circuit: the humidification procedure and the humidifier device (incl. heat-and-moisture exchanger).

en.name: Humidification Therapy
en.shortDescription: Humidification of the breathing circuit: the humidification procedure and the humidifier device (incl. heat-and-moisture exchanger).
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Humidification therapy adds warmth and moisture to the gas a patient breathes. When a patient is intubated or on high-flow oxygen, the upper airway — which normally humidifies inhaled air — is bypassed, so the breathing circuit must humidify the gas to keep secretions thin and protect the airway lining. This concept set captures two kinds of records: the **procedure** (the patient received humidification) and the **device** used (a humidifier or a heat-and-moisture exchanger). It is recorded mainly in intensive care and anaesthesia for ventilated or high-flow-oxygen patients. These are event/device records, not numeric measurements, so there is no unit.

## Included Concepts

The set is built from two anchors plus the passive heat-and-moisture exchanger device, grouped here by what they represent.

### Humidification procedure

Anchored on *Humidification therapy* with its descendants (the traditional menthol/steam/fog/mist inhalation therapies are excluded — see Excluded Concepts).

- *4055258 / 243130008 — Humidification therapy (SNOMED)*: the general procedure; the default for "patient received humidification".
- *4116405 / 286814009 — Inspired gas humidification (SNOMED)*: humidification of the inspired gas in a breathing circuit.
- *4042359 / 229302002 — Ultrasonic humidification (SNOMED)*: humidification produced by an ultrasonic nebuliser.

### Humidifier device

Anchored on *Respiratory humidifier* with its descendants, covering the humidifier types used in breathing circuits, plus the passive heat-and-moisture exchanger.

- *45768203 / 706180003 — Respiratory humidifier (SNOMED)*: the general respiratory humidifier device.
- *45764021 / 700593005 — Heated respiratory humidifier (SNOMED)*: active heated humidifier.
- *45773241 / 700705005 — Non-heated respiratory humidifier (SNOMED)*: unheated humidifier.
- *45764272 / 700910000 — Ultrasonic respiratory humidifier (SNOMED)*: ultrasonic humidifier device.
- *45764051 / 700630004 — High-flow heated respiratory humidifier (SNOMED)*: heated humidifier for high-flow circuits.
- *1246607 / 48621000087108 — High-flow non-heated respiratory humidifier (SNOMED)*: unheated humidifier for high-flow circuits.
- *4178391 / 297117007 — Heat and moisture exchanger (SNOMED)*: a passive device ("artificial nose") placed in the circuit that traps the patient's exhaled heat and moisture and returns them on the next breath; an alternative to an active humidifier.

## Excluded Concepts

The traditional inhalation-therapy branch under *Humidification therapy* is excluded, as it covers home/ENT remedies rather than ventilation-circuit humidification:

- *4039397 / 229303007 — Mist inhalation therapy (SNOMED)* and its descendants *4039398 / 229304001 — Steam inhalations*, *4039921 / 229305000 — Menthol inhalations*, and *4215616 / 80677001 — Fog inhalation therapy* (all SNOMED).

## Mapping Notes

- **This set mixes procedures and devices.** Map a humidification *event* to the procedure concepts and a humidifier *device* to the device concepts. Do not mix the two kinds.
- **Default for an unspecified humidification procedure**: *4055258 / 243130008 — Humidification therapy*. Use *4116405 / 286814009 — Inspired gas humidification* when the source specifically describes humidifying the inspired gas of a breathing circuit.
- **Default for an unspecified humidifier device**: *45768203 / 706180003 — Respiratory humidifier*. Map to a specific type (heated, non-heated, ultrasonic, high-flow) only when the source states it.
- **Active humidifier vs HME**: map a passive heat-and-moisture exchanger ("artificial nose") to *4178391 / 297117007 — Heat and moisture exchanger*, not to a humidifier device — they are different pieces of equipment.
- **Humidifier temperature settings** (chamber temperature, target temperature, heated-wire differential) are numeric measurements and are intentionally not part of this set, which is limited to procedures and devices.
- **Traditional inhalation therapies** (steam, menthol, fog, mist) are not part of this set and should not be mapped here.

name: Endotracheal intubation
description: Endotracheal intubation by any route or technique (oral/nasal, fibreoptic, awake, emergency, double-lumen); surgical airways excluded.

en.name: Endotracheal intubation
en.shortDescription: Endotracheal intubation by any route or technique (oral/nasal, fibreoptic, awake, emergency, double-lumen); surgical airways excluded.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Endotracheal intubation is the act of placing a tube through the mouth or nose, past the larynx, into the trachea to secure the airway for mechanical ventilation, anaesthesia, or airway protection. In source data this is mostly a **procedure** event marking when a patient was intubated, recorded in intensive care, anaesthesia, and emergency settings. The set also keeps two non-procedure qualifiers about the intubation itself — whether it was unplanned and whether it was difficult (see Included Concepts). There is no unit. The various concepts differ by route (oral vs nasal), technique (direct laryngoscopy, fibreoptic, rigid bronchoscope, retrograde, digital, via a laryngeal mask), and circumstance (awake, emergency).

## Included Concepts

The procedures are anchored on the SNOMED concept *Intubation of respiratory tract* with its descendants, then the surgical-airway branch is removed (tracheostomy, cricothyroidotomy and related neck-stoma procedures live in a separate set — see Excluded Concepts). Two LOINC qualifier concepts are added explicitly.

### Generic intubation (default)

- *40487536 / 447996002 — Intubation of respiratory tract (SNOMED)*: the broadest intubation concept; the default when the source does not specify route or technique.
- *4013354 / 112798008 — Insertion of endotracheal tube (SNOMED)*: insertion of an endotracheal tube (the core endotracheal intubation concept).

### By route

- *4335481 / 232674004 — Orotracheal intubation (SNOMED)*: via the mouth.
- *4337616 / 232679009 — Nasotracheal intubation (SNOMED)*: via the nose.
- *4339623 / 232675003 — Oral intubation awake (SNOMED)*: oral, patient awake.
- *4335584 / 232680007 — Nasal intubation awake (SNOMED)*: nasal, patient awake.
- *4337045 / 232681006 — Blind nasal intubation (SNOMED)*: nasal, without direct visualisation.

### By technique

- *4179373 / 429161001 — Insertion of endotracheal tube using laryngoscope (SNOMED)*: direct laryngoscopy.
- *4337615 / 232678001 — Orotracheal fiberoptic intubation (SNOMED)* and *4337617 / 232682004 — Nasotracheal fiberoptic intubation (SNOMED)*: flexible fibreoptic-guided.
- *4335583 / 232677006 — Tracheal intubation using rigid bronchoscope (SNOMED)*: via a rigid bronchoscope.
- *4287921 / 397892004 — Retrograde intubation (SNOMED)*: tube placed over a retrograde guidewire.
- *4140765 / 427331009 — Digital assisted intubation (SNOMED)*: guided by the operator's fingers.
- *4303945 / 418613003 — Tracheal intubation through a laryngeal mask airway (SNOMED)*: tube passed through an in-situ laryngeal mask.

### By circumstance

- *4119642 / 304341005 — Awake intubation (SNOMED)*: performed with the patient awake.
- *4058031 / 16883004 — Endotracheal intubation, emergency procedure (SNOMED)*: emergency intubation.
- *4082243 / 182682004 — Emergency laryngeal intubation (SNOMED)*: emergency laryngeal intubation.
- *4283807 / 66861000 — Intubation of larynx (SNOMED)*: laryngeal intubation (general).
- *4056812 / 182709001 — Laryngeal intubation for inhalation (SNOMED)*: laryngeal intubation for inhalational anaesthesia.

### Bronchial / double-lumen

- *4335585 / 232687005 — Endobronchial intubation (SNOMED)*: tube advanced into a main bronchus.
- *37116698 / 733509002 — Insertion of double lumen tracheobronchial tube (SNOMED)*: a double-lumen endotracheal tube for one-lung ventilation.

### Qualifiers (non-procedure)

These describe a property of the intubation rather than the act, and are kept here for convenience.

- *36309319 / LA20580-9 — Unplanned intubation (LOINC)*: an answer value flagging that the intubation was unplanned.
- *36660691 / 95050-1 — Difficult intubation (LOINC)*: an observation that the intubation was difficult.

## Excluded Concepts

Surgical-airway procedures that reach the trachea through a neck incision rather than through the larynx are removed; they belong to the separate Tracheostomy and cricothyroidotomy concept set:

- *4337047 / 232685002 — Insertion of tracheostomy tube (SNOMED)*, *4337618 / 232683009 — Cricothyroidotomy tube insertion (SNOMED)* (and its descendant *4337046 / 232684003 — Minitrach insertion*), *4337048 / 232686001 — Insertion of tracheal T-tube (SNOMED)*, and *37206251 / 785906002 — Scalpel bougie cricothyroidotomy (SNOMED)*.

## Mapping Notes

- **Default concept** when the source records an intubation without route, technique, or circumstance: *40487536 / 447996002 — Intubation of respiratory tract*, or *4013354 / 112798008 — Insertion of endotracheal tube* when it is specifically an endotracheal tube. Do not infer route/technique from indirect clues — if not documented, use the generic concept.
- **Route and technique are independent**: a single source record may mention both (e.g. "nasotracheal fibreoptic"). Map to the most specific single concept available (*4337617 — Nasotracheal fiberoptic intubation*); do not split one event across two concepts.
- **Surgical airway is not intubation here**: tracheostomy, cricothyroidotomy, minitracheostomy and tracheal T-tube insertion go to the Tracheostomy and cricothyroidotomy concept set, not this one.
- **Qualifiers vs procedure**: "difficult intubation" and "unplanned intubation" describe the intubation, not the act of intubating; map a flag/observation to *36660691 / 95050-1 — Difficult intubation* or *36309319 / LA20580-9 — Unplanned intubation*, and the intubation event itself to the relevant procedure concept.

name: Invasive mechanical ventilation
description: Patient on invasive mechanical ventilation (via endotracheal or tracheostomy tube); the act only — ventilation modes are separate.

en.name: Invasive mechanical ventilation
en.shortDescription: Patient on invasive mechanical ventilation (via endotracheal or tracheostomy tube); the act only — ventilation modes are separate.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) is breathing support delivered by a ventilator through an artificial airway that enters the trachea directly — an endotracheal tube or a tracheostomy tube. "Invasive" refers to that airway (a tube inside the trachea), as opposed to non-invasive ventilation, which is delivered through a mask or similar interface over the face. In source data this is a **procedure** record indicating that the patient was on invasive ventilation; there is no unit. It is recorded in intensive care, anaesthesia, and emergency settings.

## Included Concepts

This set captures the act of invasive mechanical ventilation itself, as a single concept:

- *37158404 / 1258985005 — Invasive mechanical ventilation (SNOMED)*: the patient was mechanically ventilated through an endotracheal or tracheostomy tube.

The **ventilation mode** used (e.g. SIMV, assist-control, APRV, NAVA, high-frequency) is a separate dimension — modes apply to invasive and non-invasive ventilation alike — and is captured in the dedicated ventilation-mode concept sets, not here.

## Mapping Notes

- Map a record stating the patient was on invasive ventilation (via endotracheal or tracheostomy tube) to *37158404 / 1258985005 — Invasive mechanical ventilation*.
- **Mode is separate**: do not map a specific ventilation mode (SIMV, assist-control, pressure-control, volume-control, APRV, NAVA, high-frequency jet, etc.) to this set — those belong to the ventilation-mode concept sets. A patient can be on invasive ventilation *and* a specific mode at the same time; record each in its own set.
- **Invasive vs non-invasive**: ventilation delivered through a mask/interface (CPAP, BiPAP, non-invasive positive-pressure ventilation) is *not* invasive and belongs to the Non-invasive ventilation concept set.
- **The airway device itself** (the endotracheal or tracheostomy tube) and the act of placing it (intubation) are captured in their own concept sets; this set is only the ventilation act.

name: Non-invasive ventilation
description: Patient on non-invasive ventilation (via mask/interface, no tube); the act only — ventilation modes are separate.

en.name: Non-invasive ventilation
en.shortDescription: Patient on non-invasive ventilation (via mask/interface, no tube); the act only — ventilation modes are separate.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Non-invasive ventilation (NIV) is breathing support delivered through an external interface — a face or nasal mask, helmet, or similar — without an artificial airway inside the trachea. "Non-invasive" refers to that interface, as opposed to invasive ventilation, which is delivered through an endotracheal or tracheostomy tube. In source data this is a **procedure** record indicating that the patient was on non-invasive ventilation; there is no unit. It is recorded in intensive care, respiratory wards, and emergency settings.

## Included Concepts

This set captures the act of non-invasive ventilation itself:

- *4177224 / 428311008 — Non-invasive ventilation (SNOMED)*: the general concept; the default for "patient on NIV".
- *40486624 / 447837008 — Non-invasive positive pressure ventilation (SNOMED)*: NIV delivering positive pressure (the usual form).

The **ventilation mode** used non-invasively (CPAP, bilevel/BiPAP, pressure support, spontaneous-timed, etc.) is a separate dimension — modes apply to invasive and non-invasive ventilation alike — and is captured in the ventilation-mode concept sets (in particular the spontaneous/support modes set), not here.

## Mapping Notes

- Map a record stating the patient was on non-invasive ventilation (via mask/interface) to *4177224 / 428311008 — Non-invasive ventilation*, or *40486624 / 447837008 — Non-invasive positive pressure ventilation* when positive-pressure NIV is specified.
- **Mode is separate**: do not map a specific mode (CPAP, BiPAP/bilevel, pressure support, spontaneous-timed) to this set — those belong to the ventilation-mode concept sets. A patient can be on NIV *and* a specific mode at the same time; record each in its own set.
- **Invasive vs non-invasive**: ventilation delivered through an endotracheal or tracheostomy tube is *invasive* and belongs to the Invasive mechanical ventilation concept set, not here.
- **Weaning from NIV** is a distinct event (part of weaning) and is not the NIV act; it is not included in this set.

name: Oxygen therapy
description: Supplemental oxygen therapy and its delivery route (nasal cannula, mask, Venturi, non-rebreather, high-flow, etc.); not flow rate or FiO2.

en.name: Oxygen therapy
en.shortDescription: Supplemental oxygen therapy and its delivery route (nasal cannula, mask, Venturi, non-rebreather, high-flow, etc.); not flow rate or FiO2.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Oxygen therapy is the delivery of supplemental oxygen to a patient to raise the oxygen content of the gas they breathe. In source data this is a **procedure** record indicating that oxygen was administered, usually capturing the delivery interface (nasal cannula, face mask, Venturi mask, non-rebreather mask, high-flow nasal cannula, etc.). There is no unit. It is recorded across intensive care, emergency, anaesthesia and ward settings. The set covers the act and route of oxygen delivery — it is distinct from the oxygen *flow rate* (L/min) and the *fraction of inspired oxygen* (FiO2), which are numeric measurements in their own concept sets. It is scoped to acute, in-hospital oxygen administration (chronic/home oxygen-therapy contexts are excluded — see Excluded Concepts).

## Included Concepts

The set is anchored on the SNOMED procedure *Oxygen therapy* with its descendants, restricted to acute in-hospital oxygen delivery. Grouped here by what they describe.

### Generic oxygen therapy (default)

- *4239130 / 57485005 — Oxygen therapy (SNOMED)*: the general concept; the default when the source records oxygen administration without a specific route.
- *4074661 / 243136002 — Short-term oxygen therapy (SNOMED)*: acute, time-limited oxygen therapy.

### By delivery interface / route

- *4155151 / 371907003 — Oxygen administration by nasal cannula (SNOMED)*.
- *4216695 / 71786000 — Intranasal oxygen therapy (SNOMED)*.
- *4162736 / 371908008 — Oxygen administration by mask (SNOMED)*.
- *4323763 / 429253002 — Oxygen administration by Venturi mask (SNOMED)*: fixed-concentration (air-entrainment) mask.
- *44790731 / 240051000000102 — Oxygen administration by non rebreather mask (SNOMED)*: high-concentration reservoir mask.
- *44790798 / 243011000000108 — Oxygen administration by mask with bag and valve (SNOMED)*.
- *44806745 / 802801000000109 — Oxygen administration by mask at 60 percent concentration (SNOMED)*.
- *37155203 / 149761000000108 — Administration of oxygen using tracheostomy mask (SNOMED)*.

### High-flow / humidified

- *3655950 / 870533002 — Heated and humidified high flow oxygen therapy (SNOMED)* and *37158406 / 1259025002 — Heated and humidified high flow oxygen therapy using nasal cannula (SNOMED)*: high-flow nasal oxygen (HFNC/HFNO).
- *4119964 / 304577004 — Humidified oxygen therapy (SNOMED)*.

### By concentration / flow level

- *4201025 / 315041000 — High concentration oxygen therapy (SNOMED)*.
- *1074232 / 1336169000 — Low flow oxygen delivery (SNOMED)*.

## Excluded Concepts

Concepts pulled in by the SNOMED *Oxygen therapy* hierarchy that are out of scope for acute intensive-care oxygen administration are excluded:

- **Oxygen-delivery optimisation / oxygen dynamics** — *4189560 / 391893003 — Manipulation of oxygen dynamics* and *4136465 / 398077001 — Oxygen dynamic interventions* with their descendants (haemodynamic/metabolic interventions, not oxygen administration).
- **Oxygenator therapy** — *4082249 / 182714002 — Oxygenator therapy (SNOMED)*: an extracorporeal membrane oxygenator (ECMO), not interface-delivered oxygen.
- **Chronic / home-care contexts** — *4072513 / 243137006 — Long-term oxygen therapy*, *4140455 / 426990007 — Home oxygen therapy*, *44788930 / 201661000000106 — Ambulatory oxygen therapy*, *44788929 / 201651000000108 — SBOT - Short-burst oxygen therapy* (all SNOMED): outpatient/home oxygen contexts, not an acute in-hospital delivery.
- **Niche / non-ICU methods** — *4056814 / 182713008 — Catalytic oxygen therapy*, *37312322 / 788538002 — Alcohol-oxygen vapor therapy*, *603260 / 1363901000000105 — Oxygen administration using headbox* (neonatal hood), and *4173351 / 276732005 — Apneic oxygenation* (a peri-intubation technique rather than a continuous oxygen-delivery mode) (all SNOMED).

## Mapping Notes

- **Default concept** when the source records that oxygen was given without specifying the interface: *4239130 / 57485005 — Oxygen therapy*. Map to a specific interface concept only when the source documents it.
- **Therapy/route vs measurements**: this set is the *act and route* of oxygen delivery. The oxygen *flow rate* (L/min) belongs to the Oxygen flow rate concept set, and the inspired oxygen *fraction* (FiO2, %) to the Fraction of inspired oxygen (FiO2) concept set — do not map a numeric value here.
- **High-flow nasal oxygen**: map HFNC/HFNO to *37158406 / 1259025002 — Heated and humidified high flow oxygen therapy using nasal cannula*. The high-flow nasal cannula *device* itself is not part of this therapy set.
- **Out of scope**: chronic/home oxygen therapy, apneic oxygenation, ECMO/membrane oxygenation and oxygen-delivery optimisation are not mapped here.

name: Trial of spontaneous breathing
description: Spontaneous breathing trial (SBT) — test of ventilator-weaning readiness; the act of performing the trial.

en.name: Trial of spontaneous breathing
en.shortDescription: Spontaneous breathing trial (SBT) — test of ventilator-weaning readiness; the act of performing the trial.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

A spontaneous breathing trial (SBT) is a test in which a mechanically ventilated patient is allowed to breathe with little or no ventilator support for a short period, to assess whether they are ready to be weaned off the ventilator and extubated. In source data this is a **procedure** record marking that an SBT was performed; there is no unit. It is recorded in intensive care as part of the weaning process. The trial may be done on a T-piece, on low-level pressure support, or on CPAP, but the concept here captures the act of performing the trial regardless of how it is delivered.

## Included Concepts

This set contains the single SNOMED concept for a spontaneous breathing trial:

- *4308797 / 424139009 — Trial of spontaneous breathing (SNOMED)*: a spontaneous breathing trial. Synonym: "Spontaneous breathing trial".

## Mapping Notes

- Map a recorded spontaneous breathing trial (SBT) to *4308797 / 424139009 — Trial of spontaneous breathing*, regardless of the technique used to deliver it (T-piece, pressure support, CPAP).
- **SBT vs weaning**: this set is the trial itself, not the broader weaning process. The act of weaning from ventilation (reducing/withdrawing support) is a distinct concept and is not included here.
- **SBT vs extubation**: the trial assesses readiness; the actual removal of the tube is captured in the Extubation concept set.

name: Inspiratory time (Ti)
description: Inspiratory time (Ti) — duration of the inspiratory phase of a ventilator breath, in seconds.

en.name: Inspiratory time (Ti)
en.shortDescription: Inspiratory time (Ti) — duration of the inspiratory phase of a ventilator breath, in seconds.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Inspiratory time (Ti) is the duration of the inspiratory phase of a ventilator breath — the time during which gas is delivered to the patient. Together with expiratory time it sets the inspiratory:expiratory (I:E) ratio. In source data it is a single numeric value per patient-timestamp, set or measured by the ventilator. It is recorded in intensive care and anaesthesia for ventilated patients. It is reported in seconds (s).

## Included Concepts

The set lists the SNOMED and LOINC concepts for this duration. All are reported in seconds.

- *4353947 / 250819002 — Inspiratory time (SNOMED)*
- *3043415 / 33435-9 — Inspiratory breath [Time] --on ventilator (LOINC)*
- *36304672 / 76334-2 — Inspiratory time setting Ventilator (LOINC)*

**Note on units**: reported in **seconds** (`8555 / s — second`, UCUM), the recommended unit.

## Mapping Notes

- **Default concept** when not otherwise qualified: *4353947 / 250819002 — Inspiratory time*.
- **Setting vs measured**: map the set value to the LOINC 'setting' concept and the measured value to the measured concept; use the generic SNOMED concept when the source does not distinguish them.
- This is one specific breath-phase duration; inspiratory time, expiratory time and inspiratory pause time are separate concept sets (separate variables).

en.name: Carbon dioxide production (VCO2)
en.shortDescription: CO2 production (VCO2) — volume of CO2 exhaled per minute, in L/min (absolute, not body-indexed).
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Carbon dioxide production (VCO2) is the volume of carbon dioxide a patient's body produces and exhales per unit time, a marker of metabolic rate. It is measured by analysing the patient's exhaled gas, typically by a ventilator's volumetric capnography or a metabolic (indirect calorimetry) module. In source data it is a single numeric value per patient-timestamp, reported in litres per minute (**L/min**) [1]. It is recorded in intensive care and anaesthesia, mainly for ventilated patients and during indirect calorimetry.

## Included Concepts

This set contains the single LOINC concept for absolute carbon dioxide production:

- *21490580 / 60825-7 — Carbon dioxide production (VCO2) in Respiratory system (LOINC)*: VCO2 in L/min.

**Note on units**: reported in **`8698 / L/min — liter per minute` (UCUM)**, the recommended unit.

## Mapping Notes

- Map a recorded VCO2 value (in L/min, or mL/min after conversion) to *21490580 / 60825-7 — Carbon dioxide production (VCO2) in Respiratory system*.
- **Absolute vs indexed**: this set is the absolute VCO2 (L/min). Body-size–indexed variants (VCO2 per body surface area or per ideal body weight) have different units and are not part of this set.
- **Not the ventilatory equivalent**: the ventilatory equivalent for CO2 (minute volume divided by VCO2, used in exercise testing) is a different measurement and does not map here.

en.name: End tidal carbon dioxide (PetCO2)
en.shortDescription: End-tidal CO2 as a partial pressure (PetCO2), in mmHg/kPa. The % (fraction) form is a separate set.
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context End-tidal carbon dioxide (EtCO2) is the carbon dioxide in the gas a patient exhales at the very end of a breath, measured continuously by a capnograph on the breathing circuit. It is the standard non-invasive surrogate for arterial CO2 and is used to confirm tube placement, monitor ventilation, and detect changes in cardiac output. This set captures EtCO2 expressed as a **partial pressure (PetCO2)**, reported in **mmHg** (or kPa). In source data it is a single numeric value per patient-timestamp, recorded in intensive care, anaesthesia, and emergency settings for ventilated patients. (EtCO2 expressed as a volume fraction in % is a separate, non-inter-convertible measurement — see Mapping Notes.) ## Included Concepts - *4353938 / 250784008 — End tidal carbon dioxide concentration (SNOMED)*: the generic end-tidal CO2 concept; the default, recommended in mmHg (the usual ICU representation). - *3035357 / 19891-1 — Carbon dioxide [Partial pressure] in Exhaled gas --at end expiration (LOINC)*: measured PetCO2. - *3035115 / 19890-3 — Carbon dioxide [Partial pressure] in Exhaled gas by Calculated --at end expiration (LOINC)*: calculated PetCO2. **Note on units**: reported in **`8876 / mm[Hg] — millimeter mercury column`** (UCUM), the recommended unit, with a registered mmHg↔kPa conversion (1 mmHg = 0.133 kPa, 1 kPa = 7.50 mmHg). ## Mapping Notes - Map a PetCO2 value (mmHg, or kPa converted with ×7.50) to one of these concepts. Use the generic *4353938 / 250784008 — End tidal carbon dioxide concentration* when the source does not specify measured vs calculated. - **Partial pressure vs fraction are not inter-convertible**: EtCO2 expressed as a volume fraction (%) belongs to the separate **End tidal carbon dioxide fraction** concept set. The two are not related by a fixed factor — PetCO2 (mmHg) is the fraction multiplied by the barometric pressure [1] — so they are kept as separate, unit-homogeneous sets. - **Not arterial CO2**: arterial CO2 partial pressure (PaCO2, from a blood gas) is a different measurement in its own concept set. ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 19890-3 — Carbon dioxide [Partial pressure] in Exhaled gas by Calculated --at end expiration. Available: https://loinc.org/19890-3/

en.name: Horowitz index (PaO2/FiO2)
en.shortDescription: Horowitz index (PaO2/FiO2 ratio) — arterial oxygen partial pressure over inspired O2 fraction, in mmHg; ARDS/SOFA marker.
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context The Horowitz index (also written **P/F ratio** or **PaO2/FiO2**) is the ratio of the arterial oxygen partial pressure (PaO2) to the fraction of inspired oxygen (FiO2) — for example, PaO2 of 80 mmHg on FiO2 0.40 gives a Horowitz index of 200 [1]. It is a standard marker of how well the lungs oxygenate the blood, used to grade the severity of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and embedded in acuity scores such as SOFA, SAPS II and SAPS III [1]. In source data it is a single numeric value per patient-timestamp, derived from a blood-gas PaO2 and the concurrent FiO2. It is recorded in intensive care for ventilated and oxygen-treated patients. The numerator (PaO2) is in mmHg and the FiO2 is a unitless fraction, so the ratio is reported in **mmHg** [1]. ## Included Concepts The set lists the LOINC concepts for the Horowitz index, grouped by the blood specimen the oxygen partial pressure comes from. Within each specimen there are two variants: a plain index and one **adjusted to the patient's actual temperature** (blood-gas values can be temperature-corrected). ### Arterial blood (default) The Horowitz index is by definition an arterial measurement; these are the concepts to use in almost all cases. - *3029943 / 50984-4 — Horowitz index in Arterial blood (LOINC)*. - *3029268 / 50989-3 — Horowitz index adjusted to patients actual temperature in Arterial blood (LOINC)*. ### Blood (unspecified) Use when the source does not state the specimen. - *3029880 / 50982-8 — Horowitz index in Blood (LOINC)*. - *3029906 / 50987-7 — Horowitz index adjusted to patients actual temperature in Blood (LOINC)*. ### Venous blood - *3029316 / 50986-9 — Horowitz index in Venous blood (LOINC)*. - *3032443 / 50991-9 — Horowitz index adjusted to patients actual temperature in Venous blood (LOINC)*. ### Mixed venous blood - *3029599 / 50985-1 — Horowitz index in Mixed venous blood (LOINC)*. - *3029523 / 50990-1 — Horowitz index adjusted to patients actual temperature in Mixed venous blood (LOINC)*. ### Capillary blood - *3030774 / 50983-6 — Horowitz index in Capillary blood (LOINC)*. - *3032208 / 50988-5 — Horowitz index adjusted to patients actual temperature in Capillary blood (LOINC)*. **Note on units**: all concepts are reported in **`8876 / mm[Hg] — millimeter mercury column`** (UCUM), the recommended unit. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source records a Horowitz index / P/F ratio without specifying the specimen: *3029880 / 50982-8 — Horowitz index in Blood*. When the value is known to come from an arterial blood gas (the usual case), prefer *3029943 / 50984-4 — Horowitz index in Arterial blood*. - **Temperature-adjusted vs not**: map to an "adjusted to patient's actual temperature" concept only when the source explicitly states the blood-gas values were temperature-corrected; otherwise use the plain variant for that specimen. - **Units of the ratio**: the value is in mmHg because PaO2 is in mmHg and FiO2 is a 0–1 fraction. If a source computes the index from a PaO2 in kPa, the resulting ratio is in kPa; the kPa to mmHg conversion is registered. - **Do not confuse with its components**: PaO2 (arterial oxygen partial pressure) and FiO2 are separate measurements in their own concept sets; this set is only the ratio. - **Not the SpO2/FiO2 ratio**: the S/F ratio (peripheral oxygen saturation over FiO2) is a different surrogate and does not map here. ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 50984-4 — Horowitz index in Arterial blood. Available: https://loinc.org/50984-4/

description: Set inspiratory pressure on the ventilator (pressure-controlled breaths), in cmH2O; a setting, not a measured pressure.

en.name: Inspiratory pressure setting (Pinsp)
en.shortDescription: Set inspiratory pressure on the ventilator (pressure-controlled breaths), in cmH2O; a setting, not a measured pressure.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

The inspiratory pressure setting is the airway pressure the clinician sets on the ventilator to deliver each breath in a pressure-controlled mode — the target pressure the ventilator applies during inspiration. In source data it is a single numeric value per patient-timestamp, a ventilator setting rather than a measured airway pressure. It is recorded in intensive care and anaesthesia for ventilated patients. It is reported in centimetres of water (**cmH2O**); some ventilators display it in millibar (mbar), which is nearly equivalent (1 cmH2O ≈ 0.98 mbar).

## Included Concepts

This set contains the single SNOMED concept for the inspiratory pressure setting:

- *4215838 / 417071008 — Inspiratory pressure setting (SNOMED)*: the set inspiratory pressure on the ventilator.

**Note on units**: reported in **`44777590 / cm[H2O] — centimeter watercolumn`** (UCUM), the recommended unit; a cmH2O↔mbar conversion is registered (1 cmH2O = 0.98 mbar).

## Mapping Notes

- Map the set inspiratory pressure on a pressure-controlled ventilator to *4215838 / 417071008 — Inspiratory pressure setting*.
- **Setting, not a measured pressure**: this is the *set* target pressure, distinct from measured airway pressures. Peak inspiratory pressure, plateau pressure, mean airway pressure and PEEP are measured/derived pressures captured in their own concept sets.
- **Whether this is the pressure above PEEP or the absolute inspiratory pressure depends on the ventilator** and is not distinguished by this concept; preserve any such detail in the source value if needed, but map the value here regardless.
- **Pressure support level** (the inspiratory assist set in a spontaneous/support mode) is a distinct ventilator setting and is not part of this concept set.

name: Lung compliance
description: Lung (respiratory system) compliance — volume change per unit pressure, in mL/cmH2O (static and dynamic).

en.name: Lung compliance
en.shortDescription: Lung (respiratory system) compliance — volume change per unit pressure, in mL/cmH2O (static and dynamic).
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Lung (respiratory system) compliance is a measure of how easily the lungs distend — the change in lung volume per unit change in airway pressure. A low compliance means stiff lungs (e.g. in ARDS or fibrosis). In source data it is a single numeric value per patient-timestamp, derived by the ventilator or pulmonary-function equipment. It is recorded in intensive care and anaesthesia for ventilated patients. It is reported in millilitres per centimetre of water (mL/cmH2O).

## Included Concepts

The set lists the SNOMED and LOINC concepts for lung compliance, grouped by how it is measured.

### Generic lung compliance (default)

- *4298264 / 3863008 — Lung compliance (SNOMED)*: the general concept; the default when static vs dynamic is not specified.
- *21490581 / 60826-5 — Lung compliance (LOINC)*.

### Static compliance

Measured under no-flow conditions (e.g. during an inspiratory hold); reflects the elastic properties of the lung.

- *4090322 / 251886005 — Static lung compliance (SNOMED)*.
- *21490583 / 60828-1 — Compliance.static Lung (LOINC)*.

### Dynamic compliance

Measured during active breathing (with flow); influenced by both elastic and airway-resistance properties.

- *4090654 / 251885009 — Dynamic compliance (SNOMED)*.
- *4353624 / 250823005 — Total dynamic compliance (SNOMED)*.
- *21490582 / 60827-3 — Dynamic lung compliance (LOINC)*.

**Note on units**: reported in **mL/cmH2O** (`720866 / ml/cm [H2O] — milliliter per centimeter of water`, UCUM), the recommended unit.

## Excluded Concepts

- *4090655 / 251888006 — Specific compliance (lung) (SNOMED)*: specific compliance is lung compliance normalised to lung volume, so it is expressed per cmH2O (not mL/cmH2O) and is not inter-convertible with the concepts above; it is therefore not part of this unit-homogeneous set.

## Mapping Notes

- **Default concept** when the source records a lung/respiratory-system compliance without specifying static vs dynamic: *4298264 / 3863008 — Lung compliance*.
- **Static vs dynamic**: map to a static concept only when the value comes from a no-flow (inspiratory-hold) measurement, and to a dynamic concept when it is measured during active breathing. If not specified, use the generic concept.
- **Specific compliance** (normalised to lung volume, different unit) is not part of this set.

en.name: Mean airway pressure (Pmean)
en.shortDescription: Mean airway pressure (Pmean) over the respiratory cycle, in cmH2O; includes the inspiration-only mean variants.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Mean airway pressure (Pmean, MAP) is the average pressure applied to the airway over the whole respiratory cycle during mechanical ventilation. It reflects the overall pressure load on the lungs and correlates with oxygenation and with the risk of haemodynamic compromise. In source data it is a single numeric value per patient-timestamp, computed by the ventilator. It is recorded in intensive care and anaesthesia for ventilated patients. It is reported in centimetres of water (cmH2O); some ventilators display mbar, which is nearly equivalent (1 cmH2O ≈ 0.98 mbar).

## Included Concepts

The set lists the SNOMED and LOINC concepts for mean airway pressure.

### Mean airway pressure, whole cycle (default)

- *42527086 / 60949-5 — Mean airway pressure (LOINC)*: the average airway pressure over the full respiratory cycle; the default mean airway pressure value.

### Mean airway pressure during inspiration

The average taken over the inspiratory phase only — a narrower measure than the whole-cycle Pmean.

- *44782824 / 698821009 — Mean inspiratory airway pressure (SNOMED)*.
- *21490651 / 60952-9 — Mean airway pressure --during inspiration (LOINC)*.

**Note on units**: reported in **cmH2O** (`44777590 / cm[H2O] — centimeter watercolumn`, UCUM), the recommended unit, with a registered cmH2O↔mbar conversion (1 cmH2O = 0.98 mbar).

## Mapping Notes

- **Default concept** when the source records a mean airway pressure (Pmean / MAP) without qualification: *42527086 / 60949-5 — Mean airway pressure* (the whole-cycle average).
- **During inspiration**: map to *44782824 / 698821009 — Mean inspiratory airway pressure* or *21490651 / 60952-9 — Mean airway pressure --during inspiration* only when the source explicitly states the mean is over the inspiratory phase.
- **Not peak, plateau or PEEP**: peak inspiratory pressure, plateau pressure and PEEP are distinct airway pressures captured in their own concept sets.

en.name: Minute volume (MV)
en.shortDescription: Minute volume (minute ventilation) — gas volume moved per minute, in L/min (total, inspired/expired, spontaneous/mandatory, setting).
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Minute volume (minute ventilation) is the total volume of gas moved in or out of the lungs per minute — tidal volume multiplied by respiratory rate. It reflects how much the patient is being ventilated. In source data it is a single numeric value per patient-timestamp, measured or set by the ventilator. It is recorded in intensive care and anaesthesia for ventilated patients. It is reported in litres per minute (L/min).

## Included Concepts

The set lists the SNOMED and LOINC concepts for minute volume, grouped by what they qualify. All are reported in L/min.

### Generic minute volume (default)

- *4353621 / 250811004 — Minute volume (SNOMED)*: the general concept; the default.
- *4107999 / 250812006 — Total minute volume (SNOMED)*: total (spontaneous + mandatory) minute volume.

### By phase (inspired / expired)

- *4141207 / 426102006 — Inspiratory minute volume (SNOMED)*.
- *21490754 / 75960-5 — Inspired minute Volume (LOINC)*.
- *42527121 / 76009-0 — Inspired minute Volume during Mechanical ventilation (LOINC)*.
- *4144329 / 426168008 — Expiratory minute volume (SNOMED)*.
- *42527120 / 76008-2 — Expired minute Volume during Mechanical ventilation (LOINC)*.

### By breath origin

- *4108000 / 250813001 — Spontaneous minute volume (SNOMED)*: from the patient's own breaths.
- *4108447 / 250815008 — Mandatory minute volume (SNOMED)*: from ventilator-delivered breaths.
- *4353945 / 250814007 — Triggered minute volume (SNOMED)*.

### Setting

- *3045410 / 33425-0 — Minute volume setting Ventilator (LOINC)*: the set (target) minute volume, e.g. for mandatory-minute-ventilation modes.

**Note on units**: reported in **L/min** (`8698 / L/min — liter per minute`, UCUM), the recommended unit.

## Mapping Notes

- **Default concept** when the source records a minute volume without qualification: *4353621 / 250811004 — Minute volume*.
- **Expired is the usual measured value**: ventilators typically report expired minute volume; map to an expiratory/expired concept when the source specifies it, otherwise use the generic concept.
- **Setting vs measured**: map the set (target) minute volume to *3045410 / 33425-0 — Minute volume setting Ventilator*; measured values go to the measured concepts.
- **Spontaneous vs mandatory**: map to the spontaneous, mandatory or triggered concept only when the source distinguishes the breath origin.
- **Why setting and measured share one set**: they are not the same quantity — a mandatory-minute-ventilation target and a measured expired minute volume can differ — but they are one protocol variable. Depending on the centre, the ventilator and the mode, the same datum surfaces as a setting or as a measurement, often without a reliable label, so splitting them would force every ETL to choose arbitrarily and yield two half-empty columns. Keep both here and go down to the concept_id for an analysis that turns on the distinction.

en.name: Positive End-Expiratory Pressure (PEEP)
en.shortDescription: Positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) — airway pressure at end-expiration, in cmH2O (set, extrinsic, intrinsic/auto-PEEP, total).
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) is the airway pressure maintained above atmospheric at the end of expiration during mechanical ventilation, used to keep alveoli open and improve oxygenation. In source data it is a single numeric value per patient-timestamp, set or measured by the ventilator. It is recorded in intensive care and anaesthesia for ventilated patients. It is reported in centimetres of water (cmH2O); some ventilators display mbar, which is nearly equivalent (1 cmH2O ≈ 0.98 mbar). ## Included Concepts The set lists the SNOMED and LOINC concepts for PEEP. All are reported in cmH2O. ### PEEP — generic and setting (default) - *4353713 / 250854009 — Positive end expiratory pressure (SNOMED)*: the general concept; the default. - *4216746 / 416595007 — Positive end expiratory pressure setting (SNOMED)* and *3022875 / 20077-4 — Positive end expiratory pressure setting Ventilator (LOINC)*: the set PEEP on the ventilator (extrinsic/applied PEEP). - *4160171 / 398269008 — Best positive end expiratory pressure (SNOMED)*: the optimal PEEP identified by a titration/recruitment manoeuvre. ### Extrinsic / intrinsic / total - *42528515 / 83386-3 — Extrinsic PEEP Respiratory system (LOINC)*: the PEEP applied by the ventilator. - *3035822 / 38199-6 — Intrinsic PEEP Respiratory system (LOINC)*: auto-PEEP — gas trapped when expiratory time is too short to empty the delivered tidal volume [1]. - *42527140 / 76247-6 — Total PEEP Respiratory system (LOINC)*: the sum of extrinsic and intrinsic PEEP [2]. **Note on units**: reported in **cmH2O** (`44777590 / cm[H2O] — centimeter watercolumn`, UCUM), the recommended unit, with a registered cmH2O↔mbar conversion (1 cmH2O = 0.98 mbar). ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source records a PEEP without qualification: *4353713 / 250854009 — Positive end expiratory pressure*. The set/applied PEEP maps to *4216746 / 416595007 — Positive end expiratory pressure setting* (or its LOINC equivalent *3022875 / 20077-4 — Positive end expiratory pressure setting Ventilator*). - **Intrinsic / auto-PEEP vs extrinsic**: map to *3035822 / 38199-6 — Intrinsic PEEP* only for measured auto-PEEP, to *42528515 / 83386-3 — Extrinsic PEEP* for applied PEEP, and to *42527140 / 76247-6 — Total PEEP* for their sum. Use the generic concept if the source does not distinguish them. - **Not other airway pressures**: peak, plateau and mean airway pressures are distinct measurements in their own concept sets. - **Why setting and measured share one set**: they are not the same quantity — under auto-PEEP the measured total PEEP exceeds the set PEEP, and that gap is itself the clinical signal — but they are one protocol variable. Depending on the centre, the ventilator and the mode, the same datum surfaces as a setting or as a measurement, often without a reliable label, so splitting them would force every ETL to choose arbitrarily and yield two half-empty columns. Keep both here and go down to the concept_id for an analysis that turns on the distinction. ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 38199-6 — Intrinsic PEEP Respiratory system. Available: https://loinc.org/38199-6/ [2] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 76247-6 — Total PEEP Respiratory system. Available: https://loinc.org/76247-6/

name: Peak inspiratory pressure (PIP)
description: Peak inspiratory pressure (PIP) — highest airway pressure during a delivered breath, in cmH2O.

en.name: Peak inspiratory pressure (PIP)
en.shortDescription: Peak inspiratory pressure (PIP) — highest airway pressure during a delivered breath, in cmH2O.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Peak inspiratory pressure (PIP) is the highest airway pressure reached during the delivery of a breath by the ventilator. It reflects the combined pressure needed to overcome airway resistance and lung/chest-wall elastance; a rising PIP signals increased resistance (e.g. secretions, bronchospasm) or decreased compliance. In source data it is a single numeric value per patient-timestamp, measured by the ventilator. It is recorded in intensive care and anaesthesia for ventilated patients. It is reported in centimetres of water (cmH2O); some ventilators display mbar (1 cmH2O ≈ 0.98 mbar).

## Included Concepts

- *4101694 / 27913002 — Peak inspiratory pressure (SNOMED)*: the maximum airway pressure during a delivered breath.

**Note on units**: reported in **cmH2O** (`44777590 / cm[H2O] — centimeter watercolumn`, UCUM), the recommended unit, with a registered cmH2O↔mbar conversion (1 cmH2O = 0.98 mbar).

## Mapping Notes

en.name: Plateau pressure (Pplat)
en.shortDescription: Plateau pressure (Pplat) — airway pressure during an end-inspiratory hold, in cmH2O.
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Plateau pressure (Pplat) is the airway pressure at zero inspiratory flow, reflecting the pressure distending the alveoli — the elastic recoil of the lungs and chest wall. It is a key target in lung-protective ventilation (kept ≤ ~30 cmH2O). In source data it is a single numeric value per patient-timestamp. It is recorded in intensive care and anaesthesia for ventilated patients. It is reported in centimetres of water (cmH2O); some ventilators display mbar (1 cmH2O ≈ 0.98 mbar). The zero-flow condition is usually obtained with an end-inspiratory hold, but not always: in pressure-control modes where inspiratory flow decelerates to zero before the end of inspiration, the end-inspiratory pressure already is the plateau, and some ventilator pneumatics cannot perform a hold at all and derive the value instead. ## Included Concepts The set resolves to six concepts: five LOINC "Clinical Observation" codes and one SNOMED observable entity. - *36304439 / 60829-9 — Pressure.plateau Respiratory system airway (LOINC)*: the generic LOINC plateau pressure, context unspecified. The default. - *36303946 / 76259-1 — Pressure.plateau Respiratory system airway --on ventilator (LOINC)*: the same measurement, with the "on ventilator" context made explicit. - *44782825 / 698822002 — Airway plateau pressure (SNOMED)*: the SNOMED equivalent. - *3006369 / 20060-0 — Airway pressure --at zero inspiratory flow on ventilator (LOINC)*: named "airway pressure" rather than "plateau pressure", but zero inspiratory flow **is** the defining condition of the plateau — this is the same measurement, described by the manoeuvre instead of by its name. - *3012810 / 20059-2 — Airway pressure by Airway pressure monitor --at zero inspiratory flow on ventilator (LOINC)*: the same, with the measuring device made explicit. - *21490565 / 60802-6 — Dynamic plateau pressure (LOINC)*: a plateau pressure obtained without a dedicated hold manoeuvre — see below. The two `Pressure.plateau` LOINC codes are pulled in through their shared LOINC Hierarchy anchor, which covers exactly these two and nothing else. The other three LOINC codes sit on separate branches and are listed explicitly — in particular, the `Pressure.airway` anchor is deliberately **not** used, since it also covers peak and mean airway pressures, which are different measurands. **Note on the "dynamic" concept.** LOINC publishes no definition for *21490565 / 60802-6 — Dynamic plateau pressure*. The code is an import of the IEEE 11073 device term `MDC_PRESS_RESP_PLAT_DYNAMIC` [1], which denotes the pressure that would have been observed during an inspiratory hold — a plateau obtained without performing one. Valveless ventilators do this by necessity: the HAMILTON-C1/T1/MR1 derive it from expired tidal volume and static compliance [2]. All six concepts describe the same quantity in the same unit, which is why they are kept in one set; what differs is how the zero-flow condition was reached. **Note on units**: reported in **cmH2O** (`44777590 / cm[H2O] — centimeter watercolumn`, UCUM), the recommended unit, with a registered cmH2O↔mbar conversion (1 cmH2O = 0.98 mbar). ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source records a plateau pressure (Pplat): *36304439 / 60829-9 — Pressure.plateau Respiratory system airway*. This is the generic LOINC code. - **Source states the patient was on the ventilator**: *36303946 / 76259-1 — Pressure.plateau Respiratory system airway --on ventilator*. - **Source is coded in SNOMED**: *44782825 / 698822002 — Airway plateau pressure*. Otherwise prefer a LOINC concept above — a source without LOINC codes still maps to LOINC. - **Source names the value after the manoeuvre** ("airway pressure at zero inspiratory flow") rather than "plateau pressure": *3006369 / 20060-0 — Airway pressure --at zero inspiratory flow on ventilator*, or *3012810 / 20059-2 — Airway pressure by Airway pressure monitor --at zero inspiratory flow on ventilator* when the measuring device is stated. - **Use *21490565 / 60802-6 — Dynamic plateau pressure* only** when the source explicitly labels the value as obtained without a hold manoeuvre — a device field named for a dynamic or estimated plateau, or a ventilator model known not to perform holds. A plateau pressure of unknown provenance is **not** a reason to pick it: use the generic code above. - The six concepts belong in the same column. Where the distinction matters for an analysis — comparing a hold-derived value with a device-derived one — recover it from `measurement_concept_id`, not from the value. - **Not peak, mean or PEEP**: these are distinct pressures in their own concept sets. ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC/IEEE Medical Device Code Mapping Table, distributed with the LOINC release (`AccessoryFiles/LoincIeeeMedicalDeviceCodeMappingTable`). Maps LOINC 60802-6 to IEEE 11073-10101 `MDC_PRESS_RESP_PLAT_DYNAMIC` (152776) as `equivalent`. Available: https://loinc.org/downloads/ [2] Hamilton Medical. Calculating Pplateau with HAMILTON-C1/T1/MR1 ventilators. Available: https://www.hamilton-medical.com/en_US/Resource-center/Article-page\~knowledge-base\~14232908-6f10-47d0-abe1-2e5b9de333f1\~Calculating-Pplateau-with-HAMILTON-C1-T1-MR1-ventilators\~.html
