en.name: Tidal volume (Vt)
en.shortDescription: Tidal volume (Vt) — gas volume per breath, in mL (inspired/expired, spontaneous/mandatory, setting). Per-kg form is separate.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Tidal volume (Vt) is the volume of gas moved in or out of the lungs in a single breath. In ventilated patients it is set and/or measured by the ventilator and is central to lung-protective ventilation (commonly targeted by predicted body weight). In source data it is a single numeric value per patient-timestamp. It is recorded in intensive care and anaesthesia for ventilated patients. This set captures tidal volume as an absolute volume, reported in millilitres (mL); some sources use litres (L), which is inter-convertible (1 L = 1000 mL). Tidal volume normalised to body weight (mL/kg) is a different, non-inter-convertible measurement kept in a separate set — see Mapping Notes.

## Included Concepts

The set lists the SNOMED and LOINC tidal-volume concepts reported as an absolute volume (mL), grouped by what they qualify. Several LOINC concepts come in variants corrected or uncorrected for compressible gas volume in the circuit; both are included.

### Generic / total (default)

- *4029625 / 13621006 — Tidal volume (SNOMED)*
- *21490854 / 76222-9 — Tidal volume Ventilator --on ventilator (LOINC)*
- *3004732 / 20118-6 — Tidal volume.spontaneous+mechanical --on ventilator (LOINC)*
- *3017707 / 20121-0 — Tidal volume.spontaneous+mechanical uncorrected for compressible gas volume --on ventilator (LOINC)*

- *3007828 / 20119-4 — Tidal volume.spontaneous+mechanical corrected for compressible gas volume --on ventilator (LOINC)*

### Inspired

- *44782826 / 698823007 — Inspiratory tidal volume (SNOMED)*
- *36303816 / 76221-1 — Tidal volume.inspired (LOINC)*
- *3033780 / 20110-3 — Tidal volume inspired spontaneous+mechanical --on ventilator (LOINC)*
- *3016166 / 20109-5 — Tidal volume inspired spontaneous+mechanical Measured --on ventilator (LOINC)*
- *3021470 / 20111-1 — Tidal volume inspired spontaneous+mechanical corrected for compressible gas volume --on ventilator (LOINC)*

### Expired

- *44782827 / 698824001 — Expiratory tidal volume (SNOMED)*
- *21490752 / 75958-9 — Tidal volume expired Respiratory system airway (LOINC)*
- *21490789 / 76007-4 — Tidal volume expired Respiratory system airway --on ventilator (LOINC)*
- *3015016 / 20107-9 — Tidal volume expired spontaneous+mechanical Respiratory system airway --on ventilator (LOINC)*
- *3009097 / 20108-7 — Tidal volume expired spontaneous+mechanical corrected for compressible gas volume --on ventilator (LOINC)*
- *3011767 / 20106-1 — Tidal volume expired spontaneous corrected for compressible gas volume Respiratory system airway --on ventilator (LOINC)*

### Spontaneous

- *4108448 / 250816009 — Spontaneous tidal volume (SNOMED)*
- *3017594 / 20116-0 — Tidal volume.spontaneous --on ventilator (LOINC)*

### Mandatory

- *4353946 / 250817000 — Mandatory tidal volume (SNOMED)*

### Sigh

- *3008805 / 20114-5 — Tidal volume sigh spontaneous+mechanical --on ventilator (LOINC)*

### Setting

- *3012410 / 20112-9 — Tidal volume setting Ventilator (LOINC)*
- *3020572 / 20105-3 — Tidal volume expired spontaneous uncorrected for compressible gas volume setting Ventilator (LOINC)*

**Note on units**: reported in **mL** (`8587 / mL — milliliter`, UCUM), the recommended unit, with a registered mL↔L conversion (1 L = 1000 mL).

## Mapping Notes

- **Default concept** when the source records a tidal volume without qualification: *4029625 / 13621006 — Tidal volume*.
- **Expired is the usual measured value**: ventilators typically report expired tidal volume; map to an expired concept when specified, otherwise use the generic concept.
- **Setting vs measured**, **inspired vs expired**, **spontaneous vs mandatory**: map to the specific concept only when the source documents that distinction; otherwise use the generic concept.
- **Compressible-gas correction**: some LOINC concepts distinguish values corrected vs uncorrected for gas compressed in the circuit; map to the matching variant if the source states it, else use the plain concept.
- **Per body weight is separate**: tidal volume normalised to body weight (mL/kg) belongs to the separate Tidal volume per body weight concept set — mL and mL/kg are not inter-convertible without the patient's weight.

en.shortDescription: Cardiac output — the volume of blood the heart pumps per minute; measured by thermodilution, Fick, pulse-contour, Doppler/echo or imaging. Reported in L/min.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Cardiac output is the volume of blood the heart pumps each minute (heart rate × stroke volume), the central measure of how well the circulation is delivering blood to the body. Measuring it produces a flow value reported in litres per minute (L/min). There is no single way to measure it: in the intensive care unit it is most often obtained by thermodilution through a pulmonary-artery catheter, by pulse-contour analysis of an arterial waveform (e.g., PiCCO, FloTrac), or by the Fick method; in the echocardiography and cardiology laboratory it is derived from Doppler/2D/3D echocardiography, cardiac MR, CT, angiography or nuclear imaging. Each method appears as a distinct concept so the measurement technique is preserved.

This concept set captures **cardiac output values** across all measurement methods and across the chamber/vessel where flow is assessed (left ventricle, right ventricle, aortic root, pulmonary artery). Closely related but separate parameters — cardiac index (cardiac output normalised to body surface area), stroke volume, and central venous pressure — are not part of this set.

## Included Concepts

This concept set contains 45 standard concepts (43 LOINC + 2 SNOMED). Because most concepts are the same quantity (cardiac output) measured by a different technique, they are grouped below by **method** and by **anatomical site**; the many echocardiographic calculation variants are described collectively rather than enumerated. The default for an unqualified value is *4221102 / 82799009 — Cardiac output (SNOMED)* or, for a left-ventricular value, *3005555 / 8741-1 — Left ventricular Cardiac output (LOINC)*.

### Generic cardiac output

- *4221102 / 82799009 — Cardiac output (SNOMED)*: The generic cardiac output, no method or site specified. Default mapping target.
- *3005555 / 8741-1 — Left ventricular Cardiac output (LOINC)*: Left-ventricular cardiac output with no method specified (the left ventricle is the default chamber, as it drives systemic flow).
- *4326660 / 428628004 — Right ventricular cardiac output (SNOMED)*: Right-ventricular cardiac output, no method specified.

### By clinical (ICU / cath-lab) method

These are the methods most relevant to critical care and invasive haemodynamics.

- *3003487 / 8736-1 — Left ventricular Cardiac output by Fick method (LOINC)* and *3966088 / 101150-1 — Right ventricular Cardiac output by Fick method (LOINC)*: Fick method (from oxygen consumption and arteriovenous oxygen difference).
- *3002309 / 8737-9 — Left ventricular Cardiac output by Indicator dilution (LOINC)* and *3965272 / 101151-9 — Right ventricular Cardiac output by Indicator dilution (LOINC)*: Indicator/thermodilution (the pulmonary-artery-catheter and transpulmonary methods used in the ICU).
- *21492228 / 76519-8 — Left ventricular Cardiac output by Continuous (LOINC)* and *21490694 / 61014-7 — Left ventricular Cardiac output by Intermitent measure (LOINC)*: Continuous vs. intermittent cardiac-output monitoring (e.g., continuous-CO pulmonary-artery catheters vs. bolus thermodilution).

### By Doppler / echocardiography

- *3004582 / 8735-3 — Left ventricular Cardiac output by US.doppler (LOINC)*, *3013377 / 17992-9 — Aorta root Cardiac output by US.doppler (LOINC)*, *3016873 / 17994-5 — Pulmonary artery Cardiac output by US (LOINC)*: Doppler-ultrasound cardiac output at the LV, aortic root and pulmonary artery (the basis of non-invasive and oesophageal-Doppler CO).
- *3015207 / 24526-6 — Left ventricular Cardiac output by US (LOINC)*, *21493295 / 81390-7 — Left ventricular Cardiac output by US 3D (LOINC)*, *3013457 / 8731-2 — Ventricular Cardiac output by 2D echo (LOINC)*, *3028413 / 20214-3 — Right ventricular Cardiac output by US 2D tricuspid valve (LOINC)*: General 2D/3D echo cardiac output.
- **Echocardiographic calculation-method variants**: a large group of LOINC concepts records LV (and ventricular) cardiac output computed from 2D or M-mode echo by a specific geometric method — method of disks (Simpson), modified Simpson, Teichholz, Gibson, cube, bullet, single-/biplane area-length, single-/biplane ellipse, and apical 2-chamber (A2C) / 4-chamber (A4C) views. Examples: *3028063 / 20209-3 — Ventricular Cardiac output by US.2D+Calculated by modified Simpson method*, *3027576 / 20213-5 — Left ventricular Cardiac output by US+Calculated by Teichholz method*, *46234877 / 76571-9 — Left ventricular Cardiac output by US.2D+Calculated by Gibson method*, *3022693 / 20205-1 — Left ventricular Cardiac output by US.2D+Calculated by bullet method*. These all yield a cardiac-output value; they differ only in the geometric formula the echo machine uses. One variant — *3036561 / 20332-3 — Left ventricular Cardiac output/Heart rate 4 chamber by US 2D modified single-plane calculated* — is the per-beat value (cardiac output divided by heart rate, i.e., stroke volume) reported under this LOINC family.

### By cross-sectional / nuclear imaging

- *3002046 / 8738-7 — Left ventricular Cardiac output by MR (LOINC)*: Cardiac MR.
- *3019520 / 8734-6 — Left ventricular Cardiac output by Spiral CT (LOINC)*: CT.
- *3019293 / 8733-8 — Left ventricular Cardiac output by Angiography single plane (LOINC)* and *3022862 / 8732-0 — Left ventricular Cardiac output by Angiography biplane (LOINC)*: Contrast angiography.
- *3020967 / 8739-5 — Left ventricular Cardiac output by Nuclear blood pool (LOINC)*: Nuclear blood-pool imaging.

**Note on units.** Cardiac output is reported in L/min.

## Excluded Concepts

This set is kept as a comprehensive list of cardiac-output measurements; no concepts are excluded from the source list. Related parameters that are **not** part of this set: cardiac index (cardiac output per body surface area), stroke volume, cardiac-output-to-body-surface-area ratios, and other derived haemodynamic indices — these are separate variables. The SNOMED "Cardiac output" concept has no measurement descendants, so the set is a curated list rather than a hierarchy anchor.

## Mapping Notes

- *Default concept*: When the source records a cardiac-output value with no method or chamber, map to Cardiac output (4221102 / 82799009, SNOMED), or Left ventricular Cardiac output (3005555 / 8741-1 — Left ventricular Cardiac output, LOINC) if a left-ventricular value is implied. Do not infer a measurement method that is not documented.
- *ICU monitors*: A thermodilution or transpulmonary cardiac output (PA catheter, PiCCO) maps to Indicator dilution (3002309 / 8737-9 — Left ventricular Cardiac output by Indicator dilution, LOINC); a continuous-CO monitor maps to the Continuous concept (21492228 / 76519-8 — Left ventricular Cardiac output by Continuous, LOINC); a pulse-contour value with no stated method maps to the generic concept.
- *Echo calculation method*: Map to a specific echocardiographic calculation-method concept only when the source (typically a structured echo report) names that method; otherwise use the general 2D-echo or Doppler concept, or the generic cardiac output.
- *Cardiac output vs. cardiac index*: This set is cardiac output (L/min). If the source value is normalised to body surface area (L/min/m², "cardiac index"), it is a different parameter and does not map here.
- *Common source labels*: "CO", "DC" (débit cardiaque), "Cardiac output", "Thermodilution CO", "CCO" (continuous CO) → Cardiac output (4221102 / 82799009 — Cardiac output, SNOMED) or the matching method concept.

name: Central venous pressure
description: Central venous pressure (CVP) — blood pressure in the superior vena cava / right atrium, measured via a central venous catheter; includes mean, systolic and diastolic CVP.

en.name: Central venous pressure
en.shortDescription: Central venous pressure (CVP) — blood pressure in the superior vena cava / right atrium, measured via a central venous catheter; includes mean, systolic and diastolic CVP.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Central venous pressure (CVP) is the blood pressure in the large central veins close to the right atrium (typically the superior vena cava), reflecting the pressure of blood returning to the heart. It is measured by connecting a pressure transducer to a central venous catheter (a catheter whose tip sits in a central vein) and reading the resulting pressure trace. Measuring it produces a numeric pressure value, reported in millimetres of mercury (mmHg) or, in some units, centimetres of water (cmH2O) — 1 mmHg ≈ 1.36 cmH2O. CVP is a continuous haemodynamic parameter monitored almost exclusively in the intensive care unit and operating room, where a central line is already in place.

This concept set captures **numeric CVP values**: the standard (mean) CVP plus the systolic and diastolic components of the CVP waveform. It does not include the act of inserting the catheter, CVP waveform morphology, or qualitative findings (e.g., "raised CVP").

## Included Concepts

This concept set contains 5 standard concepts (4 LOINC + 1 SNOMED). The default concept for an unqualified CVP value is *21490675 / 60985-9 — Central venous pressure (CVP) (LOINC)* or its SNOMED equivalent *4323687 / 71420008 — Central venous pressure (SNOMED)*.

### Generic central venous pressure

- *21490675 / 60985-9 — Central venous pressure (CVP) (LOINC)*: The generic CVP value, with no systolic/diastolic qualifier. In practice a single "CVP" number reported by a bedside monitor is the mean pressure and maps here.

- *4323687 / 71420008 — Central venous pressure (SNOMED)*: The SNOMED equivalent of the generic CVP value. Use either this or the LOINC generic concept depending on which vocabulary the source system aligns to.

### Waveform components

These are used only when the source explicitly distinguishes a phase of the CVP waveform. A single monitor-displayed "CVP" value is not one of these — it is the mean.

- *3000333 / 8591-0 — Central venous pressure (CVP) Mean (LOINC)*: The mean CVP, explicitly labelled as the mean (as opposed to the generic CVP code). Maps here when the source distinguishes "mean CVP" from systolic/diastolic components.

- *21490677 / 60987-5 — Central venous pressure (CVP) Systolic (LOINC)*: The peak (systolic) pressure of the CVP waveform.

- *21490676 / 60986-7 — Central venous pressure (CVP) Diastolic (LOINC)*: The trough (diastolic) pressure of the CVP waveform.

**Note on units.** CVP is reported in mmHg or cmH2O depending on the unit's local convention; preserve the source unit and do not assume one over the other.

## Excluded Concepts

- *4182861 / 54654001 — Measurement of central venous pressure (SNOMED, Procedure)*: Removed from the set. This is the procedure (the act of measuring CVP), not the resulting value, and it is a non-standard concept that maps to the SNOMED observable *4323687 / 71420008 — Central venous pressure* already included here. Catheter insertion and CVP monitoring procedures are out of scope for this measurement set.

## Mapping Notes

- *Default concept*: When the source records a single "CVP" value with no systolic/diastolic qualifier, map to Central venous pressure (CVP) (21490675 / 60985-9 — Central venous pressure (CVP), LOINC), or its SNOMED equivalent (4323687 / 71420008 — Central venous pressure) if the source is SNOMED-aligned. A monitor-displayed CVP number is the mean pressure.

- *Mean vs. generic*: Only use Central venous pressure (CVP) Mean (3000333 / 8591-0 — Central venous pressure (CVP) Mean, LOINC) when the source explicitly labels the value "mean CVP" alongside separate systolic/diastolic readings. Otherwise use the generic CVP concept.

- *Waveform components*: Map to the systolic (21490677 / 60987-5 — Central venous pressure (CVP) Systolic, LOINC) or diastolic (21490676 / 60986-7 — Central venous pressure (CVP) Diastolic, LOINC) concepts only when the source separately records those phases of the CVP waveform, which is uncommon.

- *Common source labels*: "CVP", "PVC" (pression veineuse centrale), "Central venous pressure", "RA pressure (via CVC)" → Central venous pressure (CVP) (21490675 / 60985-9 — Central venous pressure (CVP), LOINC).

en.name: Diastolic arterial pressure
en.shortDescription: Diastolic arterial pressure — the arterial blood pressure during cardiac relaxation (the lower number of a blood-pressure reading); any site, method or position.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Diastolic arterial pressure is the pressure inside the arteries during the relaxation phase of the heartbeat (diastole), when the heart refills between contractions. It is the lower of the two numbers in a standard blood-pressure reading (e.g., the "80" in 120/80). Measuring it produces a numeric pressure value, reported in millimetres of mercury (mmHg), obtained either non-invasively (an automated or manual cuff) or invasively (an arterial catheter connected to a pressure transducer). It is one of the core vital signs, recorded in virtually every clinical setting and continuously in the intensive care unit and operating room.

This concept set captures **numeric diastolic arterial pressure values** across all measurement sites, methods, body positions and respiratory phases. Systolic and mean arterial pressure are covered by dedicated concept sets, as is central venous pressure.

## Included Concepts

This concept set contains 25 standard concepts (19 LOINC + 6 SNOMED) organised below by what the source documents about the measurement. A concept may appear in more than one group. The default for an unqualified diastolic reading is *3012888 / 8462-4 — Diastolic blood pressure (LOINC)* or its SNOMED equivalent *4154790 / 271650006 — Diastolic blood pressure (SNOMED)*.

### Generic diastolic pressure

- *3012888 / 8462-4 — Diastolic blood pressure (LOINC)*: The generic diastolic blood pressure, with no site, method or position specified. Default mapping target for an unqualified value.
- *4154790 / 271650006 — Diastolic blood pressure (SNOMED)*: SNOMED equivalent of the generic diastolic blood pressure.
- *35610320 / 1091811000000102 — Diastolic arterial pressure (SNOMED)*: SNOMED concept naming the diastolic component of arterial pressure; equivalent in meaning to the generic diastolic blood pressure.

### By measurement method

- *21492240 / 76535-4 — Diastolic blood pressure by Noninvasive (LOINC)*: Diastolic pressure measured non-invasively (e.g., automated oscillometric cuff), method stated.
- *4068414 / 174255007 — Non-invasive diastolic arterial pressure (SNOMED)*: SNOMED equivalent for a non-invasively measured diastolic pressure.
- *21490851 / 76213-8 — Invasive Diastolic blood pressure (LOINC)*: Diastolic pressure derived from an invasive arterial line. Standard in the ICU and operating room.
- *4354253 / 251073000 — Invasive diastolic arterial pressure (SNOMED)*: SNOMED equivalent for an invasively measured diastolic pressure.
- *21490777 / 75995-1 — Diastolic blood pressure by Continuous non-invasive monitoring (LOINC)*: Diastolic pressure from continuous non-invasive monitoring (e.g., finger-cuff volume-clamp devices).
- *37394653 / 1036571000000105 — Non-invasive central diastolic blood pressure (SNOMED)*: Non-invasively estimated central (aortic) diastolic pressure, as opposed to peripheral cuff pressure.

### By measurement site

- *3026099 / 8500-1 — Radial artery Diastolic blood pressure (LOINC)*: Diastolic pressure measured at the radial artery (the usual site for an arterial line).
- *3014005 / 8527-4 — Radial artery - right Diastolic blood pressure (LOINC)* and *3020255 / 8526-6 — Radial artery - left Diastolic blood pressure (LOINC)*: Side-specified radial measurements.
- *3020528 / 8498-8 — Femoral artery Diastolic blood pressure (LOINC)*: Diastolic pressure measured at the femoral artery (an alternative arterial-line site).
- *3034397 / 8519-1 — Femoral artery - right Diastolic blood pressure (LOINC)* and *3033568 / 8518-3 — Femoral artery - left Diastolic blood pressure (LOINC)*: Side-specified femoral measurements.

### By patient position

Use these only when the source explicitly records body position with the measurement; otherwise use the generic concept.

- *3013940 / 8455-8 — Diastolic blood pressure--supine (LOINC)*: Measured lying flat on the back.
- *4236281 / 407557002 — Lying diastolic blood pressure (SNOMED)*: Measured lying down (SNOMED).
- *36304130 / 89267-9 — Diastolic blood pressure--lying in L-lateral position (LOINC)*: Measured lying on the left side (used in obstetrics).
- *3034703 / 8453-3 — Diastolic blood pressure--sitting (LOINC)*: Measured sitting.
- *3019962 / 8454-1 — Diastolic blood pressure--standing (LOINC)*: Measured standing (part of orthostatic assessment).

### By respiratory phase

- *3034095 / 8447-5 — Diastolic blood pressure--inspiration (LOINC)* and *3038119 / 8446-7 — Diastolic blood pressure--expiration (LOINC)*: Measured at a specified phase of breathing; used when respiratory variation in blood pressure is documented.

### By clinical condition

- *36304326 / 87740-7 — Diastolic blood pressure--W exercise (LOINC)*: Measured during physical exercise (e.g., stress testing).
- *36305114 / 87736-5 — Diastolic blood pressure--post exercise (LOINC)*: Measured after exercise.
- *36306043 / 89281-0 — Diastolic blood pressure--during anesthesia (LOINC)*: Measured under anaesthesia (perioperative monitoring).

**Note on units.** Diastolic arterial pressure is reported in mmHg. Note: LOINC 2.81 lists `cm[H2O]` as the `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS` for the non-invasive code 76535-4 (21492240), unlike the generic code 8462-4 which lists `mm[Hg]`. Arterial pressure is universally measured in mmHg (cmH2O applies to airway and central venous pressures), and all three non-invasive blood pressure codes released together in LOINC 2.54 (76534-7, 76535-4, 76536-2) share this anomaly. The recommended unit here therefore deviates deliberately from the LOINC example and is set to `mm[Hg]`, consistent with every other concept in this set.

## Excluded Concepts

The set is a curated list of numeric diastolic arterial pressure measurements. Out-of-scope concepts from the surrounding blood-pressure hierarchies are intentionally not included: ambulatory and 24-hour blood-pressure summaries, percentile/centile values, self-reported pressures, neonatal-at-birth pressures, baseline and on-admission encodings, and any non-numeric findings (e.g., "low diastolic blood pressure"). Systolic, mean and central venous pressures are captured by their own dedicated concept sets.

## Mapping Notes

- *Default concept*: When the source records a diastolic value with no site, method or position, map to Diastolic blood pressure (3012888 / 8462-4 — Diastolic blood pressure, LOINC), or its SNOMED equivalent (4154790 / 271650006 — Diastolic blood pressure) if the source is SNOMED-aligned. Do not infer a method or site that is not documented.
- *Invasive vs. non-invasive*: Map to the invasive concept (21490851 / 76213-8 — Invasive Diastolic blood pressure, LOINC) only when the source identifies an arterial line / invasive measurement, and to the non-invasive concept (21492240 / 76535-4 — Diastolic blood pressure by Noninvasive, LOINC) only when a non-invasive method is stated. If the method is not documented, use the generic concept.
- *Cuff readings*: A routine automated cuff that does not state "non-invasive" explicitly should still map to the generic Diastolic blood pressure (3012888 / 8462-4 — Diastolic blood pressure, LOINC) unless the source labels the method.
- *Position*: Map to a positional concept only when body position is explicitly recorded with the reading.
- *Common source labels*: "DBP", "DAP", "PAD" (pression artérielle diastolique), "Diastolic", "NIBP diastolic" → Diastolic blood pressure (3012888 / 8462-4, LOINC). "ABP diastolic", "Art diastolic" (from an arterial line) → Invasive Diastolic blood pressure (21490851 / 76213-8 — Invasive Diastolic blood pressure, LOINC).

en.name: Heart rate
en.shortDescription: Heart rate — the number of heartbeats per minute (bpm); any measurement method or site. Excludes pulse waveform, rhythm and fetal heart rate.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Heart rate is the number of heartbeats per unit of time, expressed in beats per minute (bpm). It is a vital sign and hemodynamic parameter. Normal resting heart rate in adults is about 60–100 bpm. Measurement methods include palpation, auscultation, ECG, pulse oximetry, arterial line, Doppler ultrasound, and transthoracic impedance. All concepts in this set are expressed in per minute (UCUM: /min, 8541 / /min, UCUM).

This concept set captures **numeric heart rate values only**. It excludes pulse waveform morphology, pulse intensity, heart rhythm classification, calculated differences (e.g., orthostatic delta), measurement duration, and fetal heart rate (covered by a dedicated concept set).

## Included Concepts

This concept set contains 22 standard concepts (20 LOINC + 2 SNOMED) organised by clinical context. A concept may appear in more than one group when it combines attributes from multiple categories (e.g., method + condition). The most generic concept — *3027018 / 8867-4 — Heart rate (LOINC)* — should be used as the default when the source data does not specify a method, site, position, or clinical condition.

### General heart rate (unspecified method and site)

- *3027018 / 8867-4 — Heart rate (LOINC)*: The most generic heart rate concept, with no method, site, or condition specified. This is the default concept for mapping heart rate data when the source system does not provide additional detail. It is by far the most commonly used LOINC heart rate code.

- *21490736 / 76477-9 — Heart rate by Noninvasive (LOINC)*: Heart rate measured by an unspecified non-invasive method. Use this when the source explicitly states a non-invasive measurement but does not specify the exact technique (e.g., pulse oximetry vs. palpation).

### By measurement method

- *3023233 / 8890-6 — Heart rate Cardiac apex by Auscultation (LOINC)*: Heart rate counted by listening at the cardiac apex with a stethoscope.

- *3023766 / 8891-4 — Heart rate Cardiac apex by palpation (LOINC)*: Heart rate assessed by palpating the point of maximal impulse (PMI) at the cardiac apex. Less commonly documented than auscultation at the same site.

- *35610095 / 1089491000000108 — Heart rate measured at cardiac apex (SNOMED)*: SNOMED concept for heart rate measured at the cardiac apex, without specifying the method (auscultation or palpation). Synonyms include "Heart apex beat rate".

- *3003841 / 8893-0 — Heart rate Peripheral artery by palpation (LOINC)*: Heart rate measured by palpating a peripheral artery (typically radial). This corresponds to the traditional "pulse check" in routine clinical assessments.

- *3000276 / 8892-2 — Heart rate Peripheral artery by US.doppler (LOINC)*: Heart rate derived from Doppler ultrasound of a peripheral artery. Used when a pulse is difficult to palpate (e.g., hypotension, peripheral vascular disease, neonates).

- *3001376 / 8889-8 — Heart rate by Pulse oximetry (LOINC)*: Heart rate derived from the photoplethysmographic signal of a pulse oximeter (measured at the capillary bed). This is one of the most frequently recorded heart rate values in hospitalised patients, as pulse oximeters are near-ubiquitous at the bedside.

- *21490670 / 60978-4 — Heart rate Intra arterial line by Invasive (LOINC)*: Heart rate derived from an invasive intra-arterial pressure waveform. Standard in ICU and operating room settings where an arterial line is in place for continuous blood pressure monitoring.

- *42527141 / 76476-1 — Heart rate by Transthoracic impedance (LOINC)*: Heart rate derived from external transthoracic impedance measurements, where electrodes placed on the chest surface detect cardiac-related impedance changes. Used in some bedside cardiac monitors and wearable devices.

- *21490872 / 76282-3 — Heart rate.beat-to-beat by EKG (LOINC)*: Instantaneous (beat-to-beat) heart rate derived from the R-R interval on an electrocardiogram. Unlike averaged heart rate values, this represents the rate calculated from a single cardiac cycle and is relevant for heart rate variability analysis.

### By patient position

These concepts are used when the source explicitly documents the patient's body position at the time of measurement. If position is not documented, map to the generic concept Heart rate (3027018 / 8867-4, LOINC).

- *40771525 / 69000-8 — Heart rate --sitting (LOINC)*: Heart rate measured with the patient in a sitting position.

- *40771526 / 69001-6 — Heart rate --standing (LOINC)*: Heart rate measured with the patient standing. Often part of orthostatic vital signs assessment alongside blood pressure measurements in each position.

- *40771524 / 68999-2 — Heart rate --supine (LOINC)*: Heart rate measured with the patient lying supine. Commonly used in orthostatic assessment protocols and in critical care where the patient is supine by default.

### By clinical condition or context

- *3040891 / 40443-4 — Heart rate --resting (LOINC)*: Heart rate measured at rest, with no recent physical exertion. This is the standard baseline heart rate used in many clinical documentation systems.

- *40481601 / 444981005 — Resting heart rate (SNOMED)*: SNOMED concept equivalent to the LOINC resting heart rate, included as a standard concept in its own right.

- *36303943 / 89273-7 — Heart rate --W exercise (LOINC)*: Heart rate measured during active physical exercise, such as during a stress test or exercise tolerance test.

- *3042292 / 40442-6 — Heart rate --post exercise (LOINC)*: Heart rate measured after completion of physical exercise. Heart rate recovery (the rate of decline after exercise) is an important prognostic indicator.

- *36305351 / 89278-6 — Heart rate --during anesthesia (LOINC)*: Heart rate measured while the patient is under anaesthesia. Used in perioperative monitoring contexts.

- *36303801 / 89282-8 — Heart rate --post bronchodilation (LOINC)*: Heart rate measured after administration of a bronchodilator. Relevant in pulmonary function testing, as beta-agonist bronchodilators commonly increase heart rate.

- *40769763 / 67129-7 — Heart rate Peripheral artery by palpation --resting (LOINC)*: Heart rate measured at rest by palpating a peripheral artery. This concept combines both a method (palpation) and a condition (resting).

### Neonatal screening (pre- and postductal)

These two concepts are specific to neonatal critical congenital heart disease (CCHD) screening, where pulse oximetry readings are taken at pre- and postductal sites (typically right hand and a foot) to detect oxygen saturation differences suggestive of a ductus-dependent cardiac lesion.

- *43533822 / 73799-9 — Heart rate Blood Preductal Pulse oximetry (LOINC)*: Heart rate derived from pulse oximetry at a preductal site (typically the right hand, receiving blood from the aorta proximal to the ductus arteriosus).

- *43533818 / 73795-7 — Heart rate Blood Postductal Pulse oximetry (LOINC)*: Heart rate derived from pulse oximetry at a postductal site (typically a foot, receiving blood from the aorta distal to the ductus arteriosus).

## Excluded Concepts

The concept set expression starts from the LOINC hierarchy node "Heart rate" (1004025 / LP29713-2, LOINC) with descendants included, then excludes several branches and individual concepts to retain only the numeric heart rate measurements relevant to this data dictionary.

### Pulse waveform and pulse intensity

All concepts under the "Pulse wave form" and "Arterial pulse quality" hierarchy branches are excluded (1003061 / LP415754-3 — Arterial pulse quality | XXX | General heart rate, LOINC, and descendants, plus multiple site-specific pulse waveform nodes such as Dorsal pedal artery, Radial artery, Carotid artery, Brachial artery, Femoral artery, Popliteal artery, Posterior tibial artery, and Ulnar artery — both left and right). These capture the morphology or intensity of the arterial pulse waveform (an ordinal or narrative observation), not the numeric heart rate. The Pulse intensity assessment panel (21494979 / 80284-3 — Pulse intensity assessment panel, LOINC) is also excluded for the same reason.

### Heart rate measurement duration

The "Heart rate measure duration" branch (1002511 / LP415757-6, LOINC) is excluded. These concepts record the time duration over which heart rate was measured (e.g., 10-second strips), not the rate itself.

### Heart rate measurement site

The "Heart rate measurement site" branch (1002513 / LP415758-4, LOINC) is excluded. These concepts describe where on the body heart rate was assessed (a categorical qualifier), not the numeric result.

### Heart rate special circumstances

The "Heart rate special circumstances" branch (1003265 / LP415762-6, LOINC) is excluded. This includes concepts such as target heart rate and maximum heart rate, which are clinical goals or derived values rather than measured heart rates.

### Heart rate method and rhythm

The "Heart rate method" branches (1003333 / LP415759-2, LOINC; 1004019 / LP415760-0, LOINC) and "Heart rate rhythm" branch (1004152 / LP415761-8 — Heart rate rhythm | XXX | General heart rate, LOINC) are excluded. Method concepts describe the measurement technique (a categorical qualifier), and rhythm concepts characterise the regularity of the heartbeat (e.g., regular, irregular) rather than a numeric rate.

### Timed specific heart rate

The "Timed specific heart rate" branch (1002982 / LP415805-3, LOINC) is excluded. These concepts capture heart rate aggregated over fixed time windows (1h, 8h, 10h, 12h, 24h) from continuous monitoring (e.g., Holter, telemetry), including maximum, mean, and minimum values. They represent derived statistical summaries rather than point-in-time measurements and fall outside the scope of this general heart rate concept set.

### Arterial system sub-tree

The "Heart rate | Arterial system" branch (1003968 / LP415780-8, LOINC) is excluded. Its descendants include encounter-level maximum heart rate (40758551 / 55422-0 — Heart rate Encounter maximum, LOINC) and pedometer-derived aggregated values (maximum, mean, minimum over unspecified time periods). These are derived or device-aggregated summaries rather than point-in-time clinical measurements.

### Non-standard SNOMED concepts

- *4239408 / 364075005 — Heart rate (SNOMED)* and *3557049 / 511831000000106 — Resting heart rate (SNOMED)*: These two SNOMED concepts are non-standard and are explicitly excluded so they do not appear in the resolved list. Their standard equivalents are already covered — *3027018 / 8867-4 — Heart rate (LOINC)* and *40481601 / 444981005 — Resting heart rate (SNOMED)* respectively. Non-standard concepts should not be used directly for mapping.

### Fetal heart rate

- *40758412 / 55283-6 — Fetal Heart rate (LOINC)* and *4091643 / 249043002 — Fetal heart rate (SNOMED)*: The "Heart rate | Fetus" hierarchy branch (1003955 / LP415787-3, LOINC) and these two individual standard concepts are excluded because fetal heart rate is recorded at the maternal level (in the mother's obstetric record), which creates a risk of confusion with the mother's own heart rate. Separating it into a dedicated concept set prevents mixing fetal and maternal values during data alignment.

### Individual excluded standard concepts

- *3013883 / 11328-2 — Heart rate at First encounter (LOINC)*: Excluded because it encodes encounter timing as part of the observation. Encounter context should be captured as metadata, not within the measurement concept itself.

- *40771925 / 69408-3 — Orthostatic heart rate [Difference in rate] (LOINC)*: Excluded because it represents a calculated difference between heart rate measurements in different positions, not an absolute heart rate value.

- *4160327 / 399017001 — Heart rate on admission (SNOMED)*: Excluded because it encodes admission context as part of the observation. Like "Heart rate at First encounter", this timing information should be captured as encounter metadata.

## Mapping Notes

- *Default concept*: When the source data records "heart rate" or "pulse" without specifying method, site, position, or clinical context, map to Heart rate (3027018 / 8867-4, LOINC). Do not attempt to infer a more specific concept.

- *Pulse oximetry heart rate*: Many electronic health records automatically record both SpO2 and heart rate from the pulse oximeter. If the source explicitly identifies the heart rate as coming from pulse oximetry, map to Heart rate by Pulse oximetry (3001376 / 8889-8, LOINC). Otherwise, map to Heart rate (3027018 / 8867-4, LOINC).

- *ICU arterial line heart rate*: If the source identifies the heart rate as derived from an arterial line or invasive arterial waveform, map to Heart rate Intra arterial line by Invasive (21490670 / 60978-4, LOINC). If the source simply says "heart rate" even though an arterial line is present, use Heart rate (3027018 / 8867-4, LOINC) — do not assume the method.

- *EKG-derived heart rate*: If the source specifies beat-to-beat heart rate from ECG, use Heart rate.beat-to-beat by EKG (21490872 / 76282-3 — Heart rate.beat-to-beat by EKG, LOINC). Note this captures instantaneous (beat-to-beat) rate from the R-R interval.

- *Positional measurements*: Only map to the positional concepts — Heart rate --supine (40771524 / 68999-2, LOINC), Heart rate --sitting (40771525 / 69000-8, LOINC), Heart rate --standing (40771526 / 69001-6, LOINC) — when the source explicitly records the patient's body position as part of the heart rate observation. If position is not documented, use Heart rate (3027018 / 8867-4, LOINC).

- *Resting vs. generic heart rate*: Map to Heart rate --resting (3040891 / 40443-4, LOINC) when the source explicitly labels the measurement as "resting heart rate". A heart rate taken at the bedside without the "resting" label should use Heart rate (3027018 / 8867-4, LOINC).

- *Exercise-related heart rate*: Distinguish between Heart rate --W exercise (36303943 / 89273-7, LOINC) during active physical exercise and Heart rate --post exercise (3042292 / 40442-6, LOINC) after completion of exercise. Heart rate recovery is typically the post-exercise measurement.

- *Neonatal screening*: Heart rate Blood Postductal Pulse oximetry (43533818 / 73795-7, LOINC) and Heart rate Blood Preductal Pulse oximetry (43533822 / 73799-9 — Heart rate Blood Preductal Pulse oximetry, LOINC) are specifically for neonatal CCHD screening protocols. Do not use these for routine pulse oximetry in non-neonatal settings.

- *Common source labels*: "HR", "FC" (fréquence cardiaque), "Pulse", "Pols" → Heart rate (3027018 / 8867-4, LOINC). "SpO2 PR", "Pulse rate (SpO2)", "Pleth HR" → Heart rate by Pulse oximetry (3001376 / 8889-8, LOINC). "Apical HR", "Apical pulse" → Heart rate Cardiac apex by Auscultation (3023233 / 8890-6, LOINC) or Heart rate Cardiac apex by palpation (3023766 / 8891-4, LOINC) depending on method. "Art line HR" → Heart rate Intra arterial line by Invasive (21490670 / 60978-4 — Heart rate Intra arterial line by Invasive, LOINC).

en.name: Mean arterial pressure
en.shortDescription: Mean arterial pressure (MAP) — the average arterial pressure over one cardiac cycle; the key perfusion-pressure target in critical care. Any site, method or position.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Mean arterial pressure (MAP) is the average pressure in the arteries over one complete cardiac cycle. It is not the simple average of systolic and diastolic values: invasive monitors compute it as the area under the arterial pressure curve, and non-invasive monitors estimate it (approximately diastolic + one-third of the pulse pressure). Measuring it produces a numeric pressure value in millimetres of mercury (mmHg), obtained either invasively (arterial line and transducer) or non-invasively (automated cuff). MAP is the principal blood-pressure target in critical care because it best represents the pressure driving blood into the organs; ICU protocols are typically written around a MAP goal (commonly ≥ 65 mmHg).

This concept set captures **numeric mean arterial pressure values** across all measurement sites, methods, body positions and respiratory phases. Systolic and diastolic pressures are covered by dedicated concept sets, as is central venous pressure.

## Included Concepts

This concept set contains 23 standard concepts (20 LOINC + 3 SNOMED) organised below by what the source documents about the measurement. A concept may appear in more than one group. The default for an unqualified MAP value is *3027598 / 8478-0 — Mean blood pressure (LOINC)* or its SNOMED equivalents.

### Generic mean pressure

- *3027598 / 8478-0 — Mean blood pressure (LOINC)*: The generic mean blood pressure, no site/method/position specified. Default mapping target.
- *4239021 / 6797001 — Mean blood pressure (SNOMED)*: SNOMED equivalent of the generic mean blood pressure.
- *37168599 / 1285244000 — Mean arterial pressure (SNOMED)*: SNOMED concept explicitly named "mean arterial pressure"; equivalent in meaning to the generic mean blood pressure and the closest match to how clinicians refer to MAP.

### By measurement method

- *21492241 / 76536-2 — Mean blood pressure by Noninvasive (LOINC)*: MAP measured non-invasively, method stated.
- *4108289 / 251074006 — Non-invasive mean arterial pressure (SNOMED)*: SNOMED equivalent for a non-invasively measured MAP.
- *21490852 / 76214-6 — Invasive Mean blood pressure (LOINC)*: MAP derived from an invasive arterial line. Standard in the ICU and operating room.
- *4108290 / 251075007 — Invasive mean arterial pressure (SNOMED)*: SNOMED equivalent for an invasively measured MAP.
- *21490778 / 75996-9 — Mean blood pressure by Continuous non-invasive monitoring (LOINC)*: MAP from continuous non-invasive monitoring (e.g., finger-cuff volume-clamp devices).

### By measurement site

- *3005468 / 8506-8 — Radial artery Mean blood pressure (LOINC)*: MAP at the radial artery (usual arterial-line site).
- *3015847 / 8543-1 — Radial artery - right Mean blood pressure (LOINC)* and *3009075 / 8542-3 — Radial artery - left Mean blood pressure (LOINC)*: Side-specified radial measurements.
- *3019870 / 8504-3 — Femoral artery Mean blood pressure (LOINC)*: MAP at the femoral artery.
- *3018701 / 8535-7 — Femoral artery - right Mean blood pressure (LOINC)* and *3012895 / 8534-0 — Femoral artery - left Mean blood pressure (LOINC)*: Side-specified femoral measurements.
- *3015939 / 8418-6 — Renal artery - right Mean blood pressure (LOINC)* and *3010443 / 8417-8 — Renal artery - left Mean blood pressure (LOINC)*: MAP measured in a renal artery (specialised, e.g., during renal angiography).

### By patient position

Use only when the source explicitly records body position; otherwise use the generic concept.

- *3018336 / 8458-2 — Mean blood pressure--supine (LOINC)*: Measured lying flat.
- *3012526 / 8456-6 — Mean blood pressure--sitting (LOINC)*: Measured sitting.
- *3017490 / 8457-4 — Mean blood pressure--standing (LOINC)*: Measured standing.

### By respiratory phase

- *3013032 / 8449-1 — Mean blood pressure--inspiration (LOINC)* and *3022152 / 8448-3 — Mean blood pressure--expiration (LOINC)*: Measured at a specified phase of breathing.

### By clinical condition

- *36031915 / 95822-3 — Mean blood pressure--during anesthesia (LOINC)*: MAP measured under anaesthesia.
- *36031385 / 95821-5 — Mean blood pressure by Noninvasive--during anesthesia (LOINC)*: Non-invasive MAP measured under anaesthesia (method + condition).

**Note on units.** Mean arterial pressure is reported in mmHg. Note: LOINC 2.81 lists `cm[H2O]` as the `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS` for the non-invasive code 76536-2 (21492241), unlike the generic code 8478-0 which lists `mm[Hg]`. Arterial pressure is universally measured in mmHg (cmH2O applies to airway and central venous pressures), and all three non-invasive blood pressure codes released together in LOINC 2.54 (76534-7, 76535-4, 76536-2) share this anomaly. The recommended unit here therefore deviates deliberately from the LOINC example and is set to `mm[Hg]`, consistent with every other concept in this set.

## Excluded Concepts

The set is a curated list of numeric mean arterial pressure measurements. Out-of-scope concepts from the surrounding blood-pressure hierarchies are intentionally not included: ambulatory/24-hour summaries, percentile values, maximum/minimum/target derived values, self-reported pressures, and any non-numeric findings. Systolic, diastolic and central venous pressures are captured by their own dedicated concept sets.

## Mapping Notes

- *Default concept*: When the source records a MAP with no site, method or position, map to Mean blood pressure (3027598 / 8478-0 — Mean blood pressure, LOINC), or its SNOMED equivalent Mean arterial pressure (37168599 / 1285244000 — Mean arterial pressure) if the source is SNOMED-aligned. Do not infer an undocumented method or site.
- *Invasive vs. non-invasive*: Map to the invasive concept (21490852 / 76214-6 — Invasive Mean blood pressure, LOINC) only when the source identifies an arterial line, and to the non-invasive concept (21492241 / 76536-2 — Mean blood pressure by Noninvasive, LOINC) only when a non-invasive method is stated. Otherwise use the generic concept.
- *MAP from a monitor*: Bedside monitors usually display MAP alongside systolic/diastolic; an unlabelled MAP value maps to Mean blood pressure (3027598 / 8478-0, LOINC).
- *Common source labels*: "MAP", "MBP", "PAM" (pression artérielle moyenne), "Mean BP", "NIBP mean" → Mean blood pressure (3027598 / 8478-0, LOINC). "ABP mean", "Art MAP" (arterial line) → Invasive Mean blood pressure (21490852 / 76214-6 — Invasive Mean blood pressure, LOINC).

en.name: Systolic arterial pressure
en.shortDescription: Systolic arterial pressure — the peak arterial blood pressure during cardiac contraction (the upper number of a blood-pressure reading); any site, method or position.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Systolic arterial pressure is the peak pressure inside the arteries during the contraction phase of the heartbeat (systole), when the heart ejects blood. It is the higher of the two numbers in a standard blood-pressure reading (e.g., the "120" in 120/80). Measuring it produces a numeric pressure value in millimetres of mercury (mmHg), obtained non-invasively (automated or manual cuff, or by palpation) or invasively (an arterial catheter and pressure transducer). It is one of the core vital signs, recorded in virtually every clinical setting and continuously in the intensive care unit and operating room.

This concept set captures **numeric systolic arterial pressure values** across all measurement sites, methods, body positions and respiratory phases. Diastolic and mean arterial pressure are covered by dedicated concept sets, as is central venous pressure.

## Included Concepts

This concept set contains 25 standard concepts (17 LOINC + 4 SNOMED — plus position/site/condition variants) organised below by what the source documents about the measurement. A concept may appear in more than one group. The default for an unqualified systolic reading is *3004249 / 8480-6 — Systolic blood pressure (LOINC)* or its SNOMED equivalent *4152194 / 271649006 — Systolic blood pressure (SNOMED)*.

### Generic systolic pressure

- *3004249 / 8480-6 — Systolic blood pressure (LOINC)*: The generic systolic blood pressure, no site/method/position specified. Default mapping target.
- *4152194 / 271649006 — Systolic blood pressure (SNOMED)*: SNOMED equivalent of the generic systolic blood pressure.
- *4217013 / 72313002 — Systolic arterial pressure (SNOMED)*: SNOMED concept naming the systolic component of arterial pressure; equivalent in meaning to the generic systolic blood pressure.

### By measurement method

- *21492239 / 76534-7 — Systolic blood pressure by Noninvasive (LOINC)*: Systolic pressure measured non-invasively, method stated.
- *4354252 / 251070002 — Non-invasive systolic arterial pressure (SNOMED)*: SNOMED equivalent for a non-invasively measured systolic pressure.
- *21490853 / 76215-3 — Invasive Systolic blood pressure (LOINC)*: Systolic pressure from an invasive arterial line. Standard in the ICU and operating room.
- *4353843 / 251071003 — Invasive systolic arterial pressure (SNOMED)*: SNOMED equivalent for an invasively measured systolic pressure.
- *21490779 / 75997-7 — Systolic blood pressure by Continuous non-invasive monitoring (LOINC)*: Systolic pressure from continuous non-invasive monitoring (e.g., finger-cuff volume-clamp devices).
- *3028737 / 8479-8 — Systolic blood pressure by palpation (LOINC)*: Systolic pressure estimated by palpation (inflating a cuff and feeling for the return of the pulse). Gives a systolic value only; used when a stethoscope or monitor is unavailable, or to avoid an auscultatory-gap error.
- *37394652 / 1036551000000101 — Non-invasive central systolic blood pressure (SNOMED)*: Non-invasively estimated central (aortic) systolic pressure, as opposed to peripheral cuff pressure.

### By measurement site

- *3005659 / 8512-6 — Radial artery Systolic blood pressure (LOINC)*: Systolic pressure at the radial artery (usual arterial-line site).
- *3010693 / 8568-8 — Radial artery - right Systolic blood pressure (LOINC)* and *3012979 / 8567-0 — Radial artery - left Systolic blood pressure (LOINC)*: Side-specified radial measurements.
- *3020524 / 8510-0 — Femoral artery Systolic blood pressure (LOINC)*: Systolic pressure at the femoral artery.
- *3006633 / 8554-8 — Femoral artery - right Systolic blood pressure (LOINC)* and *3006962 / 8553-0 — Femoral artery - left Systolic blood pressure (LOINC)*: Side-specified femoral measurements.

### By patient position

Use only when the source explicitly records body position; otherwise use the generic concept.

- *3009395 / 8461-6 — Systolic blood pressure--supine (LOINC)*: Measured lying flat.
- *36303812 / 89268-7 — Systolic blood pressure--lying in L-lateral position (LOINC)*: Measured lying on the left side (used in obstetrics).
- *3018586 / 8459-0 — Systolic blood pressure--sitting (LOINC)*: Measured sitting.
- *3035856 / 8460-8 — Systolic blood pressure--standing (LOINC)*: Measured standing (part of orthostatic assessment).

### By respiratory phase

- *3033616 / 8451-7 — Systolic blood pressure--inspiration (LOINC)* and *3000605 / 8450-9 — Systolic blood pressure--expiration (LOINC)*: Measured at a specified phase of breathing; relevant where respiratory variation (e.g., pulsus paradoxus) is documented.

### By clinical condition

- *36305059 / 87739-9 — Systolic blood pressure--W exercise (LOINC)*: Measured during physical exercise (e.g., stress testing).
- *36303525 / 87741-5 — Systolic blood pressure--post exercise (LOINC)*: Measured after exercise.
- *36304016 / 89280-2 — Systolic blood pressure--during anesthesia (LOINC)*: Measured under anaesthesia (perioperative monitoring).

**Note on units.** Systolic arterial pressure is reported in mmHg. Note: LOINC 2.81 lists `cm[H2O]` as the `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS` for the non-invasive code 76534-7 (21492239), unlike the generic code 8480-6 which lists `mm[Hg]`. Arterial pressure is universally measured in mmHg (cmH2O applies to airway and central venous pressures), and all three non-invasive blood pressure codes released together in LOINC 2.54 (76534-7, 76535-4, 76536-2) share this anomaly. The recommended unit here therefore deviates deliberately from the LOINC example and is set to `mm[Hg]`, consistent with every other concept in this set.

## Excluded Concepts

The set is a curated list of numeric systolic arterial pressure measurements. Out-of-scope concepts from the surrounding blood-pressure hierarchies are intentionally not included: ambulatory and 24-hour summaries, percentile/centile values, self-reported pressures, neonatal-at-birth pressures, baseline and on-admission encodings, and any non-numeric findings. Diastolic, mean and central venous pressures are captured by their own dedicated concept sets.

## Mapping Notes

- *Default concept*: When the source records a systolic value with no site, method or position, map to Systolic blood pressure (3004249 / 8480-6 — Systolic blood pressure, LOINC), or its SNOMED equivalent (4152194 / 271649006 — Systolic blood pressure) if the source is SNOMED-aligned. Do not infer a method or site that is not documented.
- *Invasive vs. non-invasive*: Map to the invasive concept (21490853 / 76215-3 — Invasive Systolic blood pressure, LOINC) only when the source identifies an arterial line, and to the non-invasive concept (21492239 / 76534-7 — Systolic blood pressure by Noninvasive, LOINC) only when a non-invasive method is stated. Otherwise use the generic concept.
- *Palpated systolic*: Map to Systolic blood pressure by palpation (3028737 / 8479-8 — Systolic blood pressure by palpation, LOINC) only when the source states the value was obtained by palpation. A palpated reading has no diastolic counterpart.
- *Position*: Map to a positional concept only when body position is explicitly recorded with the reading.
- *Common source labels*: "SBP", "SAP", "PAS" (pression artérielle systolique), "Systolic", "NIBP systolic" → Systolic blood pressure (3004249 / 8480-6, LOINC). "ABP systolic", "Art systolic" (arterial line) → Invasive Systolic blood pressure (21490853 / 76215-3 — Invasive Systolic blood pressure, LOINC).

en.name: Body temperature
en.shortDescription: Body temperature — core body temperature and its accepted proxies, measured at any site used to estimate whole-body temperature (oesophageal, bladder, blood, rectal, tympanic, oral, axillary, etc.); reported in °C or °F.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Body temperature is the patient's central body temperature, the cardinal vital sign used to detect fever (pyrexia) and hypothermia. Measuring it produces a numeric value reported in degrees Celsius (°C) or degrees Fahrenheit (°F), obtained with a thermometer or temperature probe at one of many anatomical sites. Body temperature is recorded in every clinical setting and monitored continuously in the intensive care unit (e.g., bladder or oesophageal probes, and during targeted temperature management).

This concept set captures **core body temperature and its accepted proxies** — the sites where the measurement is taken in order to estimate the temperature of the body as a whole, the site being merely an access point. It deliberately **excludes local and peripheral measurements** (skin, extremity, finger, toe, foot, joint), which characterise *that site* rather than the patient: they are taken to assess local inflammation or peripheral perfusion, their distribution depends on the measurement site rather than on the patient, and pooling them with core measurements would produce a variable that cannot be interpreted. An oesophageal temperature of 38.5 °C and a foot-skin temperature of 38.5 °C do not describe the same thing.

**One variable, not one set per site.** Axillary and oral readings underestimate core temperature by roughly 0.3–0.5 °C, yet they remain a single variable here: a research protocol asks for the patient's temperature, not for an axillary temperature specifically. Splitting by site would also assume the site is known, which is often not the case — many source systems record an unqualified temperature. The site is preserved by the specific concept chosen, so a study that needs to stratify or adjust on it still can.

## Included Concepts

This concept set contains 33 standard concepts (LOINC + SNOMED), enumerated explicitly rather than expanded from a hierarchy: the SNOMED *Body temperature* branch mixes systemic and local measurements (joint, spine, skin, limb sites), so it cannot be used as an anchor with descendants. The default for an unqualified temperature is *3020891 / 8310-5 — Body temperature (LOINC)* or *4302666 / 386725007 — Body temperature (SNOMED)*.

### Generic body temperature

- *3020891 / 8310-5 — Body temperature (LOINC)* and *4302666 / 386725007 — Body temperature (SNOMED)*: The generic body temperature, no site specified. Default mapping target when the source does not state where the temperature was taken.
- *4174894 / 276885007 — Core body temperature (SNOMED)* and *3025926 / 8329-5 — Body temperature - Core (LOINC)*: Explicitly core temperature, site unspecified.

### Core sites

Sites that approximate true central body temperature directly.

- *21490588 / 60836-4 — Esophageal temperature (LOINC)* and *4333349 / 431598003 — Temperature of esophagus (SNOMED)*: Oesophageal probe (common under anaesthesia and in the ICU).
- *3025704 / 8334-5 — Body temperature - Urinary bladder (LOINC)*, *21490870 / 76278-1 — Bladder temperature via Foley (LOINC)* and *44782835 / 698832009 — Core body temperature measured at urinary bladder (SNOMED)*: Bladder (Foley-catheter thermistor) temperature.
- *21490586 / 60834-9 — Blood temperature (LOINC)*, *21490587 / 60835-6 — Arterial blood temperature (LOINC)*, *21490769 / 75987-8 — Venous blood temperature (LOINC)*, *3007416 / 8330-3 — Body temperature - Intravascular (LOINC)* and *37164002 / 1222808002 — Core body temperature measured in blood (SNOMED)*: Intravascular and blood temperature. Blood temperature is the reference standard for core temperature, measured by pulmonary-artery catheter or during extracorporeal circulation (CPB, ECMO, CRRT); the arterial and venous variants are included alongside the generic and intravascular codes.
- *37019573 / 91371-5 — Body temperature - Brain (LOINC)*: Brain temperature from an invasive neuro-ICU probe — a core temperature.
- *3022060 / 8332-9 — Rectal temperature (LOINC)* and *4143731 / 307047009 — Rectal temperature (SNOMED)*: Rectal probe, the classic bedside core site.

### Core proxies

Sites accepted as estimates of core temperature, with a known and modest offset.

- *4215364 / 415974002 — Tympanic temperature (SNOMED)*, *21490907 / 76011-6 — Ear temperature (LOINC)* and *4239770 / 363997004 — Temperature of pinna (SNOMED)*: Ear / tympanic (infrared aural thermometer).
- *3006322 / 8331-1 — Oral temperature (LOINC)* and *4218834 / 415945006 — Oral temperature (SNOMED)*: Mouth.
- *46235152 / 75539-7 — Body temperature - Temporal artery (LOINC)*: Temporal-artery (forehead-scanner) temperature.
- *21490590 / 60838-0 — Nasopharyngeal temperature (LOINC)*, *44782834 / 698831002 — Nasopharyngeal temperature (SNOMED)* and *21490906 / 76010-8 — Nasal temperature (LOINC)*: Nasal / nasopharyngeal probe.
- *3025085 / 8328-7 — Axillary temperature (LOINC)* and *4188706 / 415882003 — Axillary temperature (SNOMED)*: Armpit.
- *4212763 / 415922000 — Forehead temperature (SNOMED)*: Forehead (infrared thermometer).
- *1259509 / 104063-3 — Body temperature - Groin (LOINC)* and *4189949 / 415929009 — Groin temperature (SNOMED)*: Inguinal region. SNOMED 415929009 carries the synonym *"Estimated core body temperature measured in inguinal region"*, and the rectal-to-inguinal gap is of the same order as the rectal-to-axillary gap.

### Context and method variants

- *3032679 / 50400-1 — Body temperature --after transfusion reaction (LOINC)*: A body temperature whose LOINC code carries the transfusion-reaction context.
- *4329518 / 431807005 — Body temperature taken with digital thermometer (SNOMED)*: Generic temperature qualified only by the device, no site.

**Note on units.** The recommended unit is **`Cel`** (OMOP concept 586323 — degree Celsius), listed first by LOINC for these codes and the clinical standard outside the United States. Sources reporting Fahrenheit are converted with an **affine** conversion, not a multiplicative one: `°C = 0.555556 × °F − 17.777778` (and `°F = 1.8 × °C + 32`), which the conversion table stores using its `offset` field. LOINC lists `deg` (a plane angle) as the example unit for the nasal, ear and venous blood temperature codes 76010-8, 76011-6 and 75987-8, which is an error in the source table; all three are recommended in `Cel` here like every other concept of the set.

## Excluded Concepts

**Local and peripheral measurements** are excluded: they characterise the site rather than the patient, and mixing them into a whole-body temperature variable would make it uninterpretable.

- Skin and body surface: *3039856 / 39106-0 — Temperature of Skin (LOINC)*, *4265708 / 364537001 — Temperature of skin (SNOMED)*, *21490688 / 61008-9 — Body surface temperature (LOINC)*, *4215353 / 415921007 — Forehead skin strip temperature (SNOMED)*.
- Extremities: *21493955 / 81673-6 — Temperature of Extremity (LOINC)*, *1988377 / 98657-0 — Body temperature - Hand surface (LOINC)*, *1989404 / 98663-8 — Body temperature - Foot surface (LOINC)*, *21490584 / 60830-7 — Finger temperature (LOINC)*, *21490585 / 60833-1 — Toe temperature (LOINC)*, and the SNOMED foot, toe and digit sites.
- Joint temperatures (*4097461 — Joint temperature (SNOMED)* and its shoulder, elbow, wrist, thumb, finger, knee, ankle, foot and toe variants): rheumatology measurements of local inflammation, not a vital sign.
- Other local SNOMED sites reached only through the hierarchy: breast, vagina, and the cervical, thoracic and lumbar spine temperatures.

The centre-to-periphery temperature gradient is a real clinical signal (peripheral hypoperfusion), but no INDICATE use case currently requires it; a dedicated peripheral-temperature concept set may be created if one appears.

**Non-measurement concepts** from the SNOMED body-temperature hierarchy are likewise out of scope: *44809207 — Target body temperature* (a goal value, e.g. a targeted-temperature-management set point), *44809208 — Maximum body temperature* and *44813868 — Minimum body temperature* (derived summary statistics over a period), *45769775 — Temperature of neonate at birth* (encounter-specific encoding), *4113386 — Basal body temperature* (fertility-tracking measurement with a distinct protocol) and *4086670 — Comparative temperature in limbs* (a comparison between limbs, not an absolute value). Because the set no longer expands any hierarchy, these are simply not enumerated rather than explicitly excluded.

## Mapping Notes

- *Default concept*: When the source records a temperature with no site, map to Body temperature (3020891 / 8310-5 — Body temperature, LOINC) or its SNOMED equivalent (4302666 / 386725007 — Body temperature). Do not guess the site.
- *Site matters*: Map to the site-specific concept when the source states where the temperature was taken (e.g., "rectal temp", "tympanic", "bladder temp"). Core sites and proxy sites read differently (axillary and oral underestimate core temperature by roughly 0.3–0.5 °C), so preserving the site lets downstream analyses stratify or adjust.
- *Continuous ICU probes*: A continuously monitored temperature from a bladder or oesophageal probe maps to the corresponding bladder/oesophageal concept; a PA-catheter, arterial-line, CPB, ECMO or CRRT blood temperature maps to the blood/intravascular concepts (arterial or venous where the source specifies it).
- *Peripheral temperatures out of scope*: A skin, extremity, finger, toe or foot temperature does **not** belong to this variable, even when it is the only temperature the source records. Leave it unmapped here rather than treating it as the patient's body temperature.
- *Common source labels*: "Temp", "T°", "BT" → Body temperature (3020891 / 8310-5 — Body temperature, LOINC). "Tympanic", "Ear temp" → Ear/Tympanic temperature. "Rectal", "PR temp" → Rectal temperature (3022060 / 8332-9 — Rectal temperature, LOINC). "Axillary", "Axilla" → Axillary temperature (3025085 / 8328-7 — Axillary temperature, LOINC). "Core temp", "Bladder temp", "Oesophageal temp" → the matching core concept.

en.name: Urine output
en.shortDescription: Urine output — the volume of urine produced, as a rate or over a time window (hourly, daily) and by collection route (catheter, nephrostomy); reported in mL (or mL/h, mL/kg/h).
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Urine output is the volume of urine the patient produces, used to assess kidney function and fluid balance. It is one of the most closely watched parameters in the intensive care unit, where a falling urine output is an early sign of acute kidney injury or hypovolaemia. Measuring it produces a volume (in millilitres) collected over a defined period — most often hourly from an indwelling urinary catheter with a graduated collection chamber — and is frequently expressed as a rate (mL/h, or mL/kg/h normalised to body weight). Outside critical care it is also recorded as a 24-hour total or as the volume of individual voids.

This concept set captures **urine-volume measurements**: the generic urine output, fixed-window totals (1, 8, 10, 12, 24 hour), route-specific outputs (urethral catheter, nephrostomy), and the SNOMED urine-volume family (hourly, timed, voided, single-void volumes). The time window and collection route are preserved by the specific concept chosen.

## Included Concepts

This concept set contains 19 standard concepts (LOINC + SNOMED). The SNOMED side is anchored on *4264378 / 364202003 — Measure of urine output (SNOMED)* with descendants; the LOINC side is a curated list. The default for an unqualified urine-output value is *3014315 / 9187-6 — Urine output (LOINC)*.

### Generic urine output

- *3014315 / 9187-6 — Urine output (LOINC)*: The generic urine output, no time window or route specified. Default mapping target.
- *4264378 / 364202003 — Measure of urine output (SNOMED)*, *37397937 / 993701000000102 — Urine volume (SNOMED)*, *37394139 / 1027231000000106 — Other urine volume (SNOMED)*: SNOMED concepts for a urine-volume measurement without a specific window; equivalent to the generic LOINC concept.
- *4247279 / 60309003 — Diuresis (SNOMED)*: "Diuresis" is widely used (especially in French — *diurèse*) as a synonym for urine output; included as a generic mapping target.

### By time window

These record the urine volume accumulated over a fixed period. In the ICU the 1-hour value is the workhorse measurement.

- *3014835 / 9188-4 — Urine output 1 hour (LOINC)* and *4145209 / 426543000 — Hourly urine volume (SNOMED)*: Hourly urine output.
- *3008828 / 9189-2 — Urine output 8 hour (LOINC)*, *3013533 / 9190-0 — Urine output 10 hour (LOINC)*, *3018727 / 9191-8 — Urine output 12 hour (LOINC)*: Shift-length totals.
- *3008071 / 9192-6 — Urine output 24 hour (LOINC)*, *4191836 / 395060000 — 24 hour urine output (SNOMED)*, *4227851 / 404232001 — 24 hour voided urinary volume (SNOMED)*: Daily totals.
- *4227850 / 404231008 — Timed urine volume (SNOMED)*: Volume collected over an unspecified timed period.

### By void

- *4089953 / 251975009 — Voided urinary volume (SNOMED)* and *4090797 / 251977001 — Single voided urinary volume (SNOMED)*: Volume of urine passed in one (or a series of) void(s), as opposed to a continuous catheter collection.

### By collection route

- *3016267 / 9195-9 — Urine output by in and out urethral catheter (LOINC)*: Output measured via an in-and-out (intermittent) urethral catheter.
- *21491173 / 79549-2 — Urine output measured by nephrostomy (LOINC)*: Output drained through a nephrostomy tube (direct kidney drainage), which may be recorded separately from urethral output.

**Note on units.** Urine output is reported in mL, or as a rate in mL/h or mL/kg/h.

## Excluded Concepts

- *4065542 / 167578005 — Measurement of urine volume over 6 hours (SNOMED, Procedure)*: Removed. This is the procedure (the act of measuring), not the resulting value.
- Therapeutic diuresis interventions (e.g., *4347914 — Alkaline diuresis*, *4121323 — Forced alkaline diuresis*) are deliberately not pulled in: although they are descendants of "Diuresis", they are treatments, not urine-volume measurements. "Diuresis" is therefore included as a single leaf concept, without its descendants.

## Mapping Notes

- *Default concept*: When the source records a urine-output value with no time window or route, map to Urine output (3014315 / 9187-6 — Urine output, LOINC). Do not infer a window that is not stated.
- *Hourly ICU output*: An ICU catheter output recorded each hour maps to Urine output 1 hour (3014835 / 9188-4 — Urine output 1 hour, LOINC) or Hourly urine volume (4145209 / 426543000 — Hourly urine volume, SNOMED). If the source records a running total without a per-hour breakdown, use the matching window (8/12/24 hour) or the generic concept.
- *Rate vs. volume*: Some systems store urine output as a rate (mL/h or mL/kg/h) rather than a raw volume; the concept is the same — preserve the source unit and do not convert.
- *Route*: Map to the nephrostomy (21491173 / 79549-2 — Urine output measured by nephrostomy, LOINC) or in-and-out-catheter (3016267 / 9195-9 — Urine output by in and out urethral catheter, LOINC) concept only when the source identifies that collection route; a standard indwelling-catheter output maps to the generic or time-window concept.
- *Common source labels*: "UO", "Urine output", "Diuresis", "Diurèse", "Débit urinaire", "Hourly urine" → Urine output (3014315 / 9187-6 — Urine output, LOINC) or the matching time-window concept.

en.name: Respiratory rate (RR)
en.shortDescription: Respiratory rate (RR) — breaths per minute (/min); the measured rate (any method, incl. on the ventilator) and the ventilator set rate.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Respiratory rate (RR) is the number of breaths per minute — a core vital sign and ventilation parameter. In source data it is a single numeric value per patient-timestamp, measured by any means (bedside count, monitor impedance, capnography, pulse oximetry, the ventilator, etc.) or set on the ventilator. It is recorded across intensive care, anaesthesia, wards and emergency settings. It is reported in breaths per minute (UCUM unit /min). The measurement method and the set-vs-measured distinction are attributes of the value, not separate variables, so they are grouped in this single set.

## Included Concepts

The set groups the SNOMED and LOINC respiratory-rate concepts (a single `respiratory_rate` variable). They are organised below by source/context for readability only — all are part of the same set, all in /min.

### Generic respiratory rate (default)

- *3024171 / 9279-1 — Respiratory rate (LOINC)* and *4313591 / 86290005 — Respiratory rate (SNOMED)*: the default.
- *4108446 / 250810003 — Total breath rate (SNOMED)*: total respiratory rate, spontaneous and mechanical breaths combined.
- *4154772 / 271625008 — Rate of spontaneous respiration (SNOMED)*: spontaneous breaths only.
- *1175625 / 76528-9 — Breath rate spontaneous (LOINC)*: spontaneous breaths only, LOINC equivalent of the preceding concept.

### Measured on the ventilator

- *3007646 / 19840-8 — Breath rate spontaneous and mechanical --on ventilator (LOINC)*: total measured rate.
- *3026892 / 19839-0 — Breath rate spontaneous --on ventilator (LOINC)*: spontaneous component.

### Ventilator set rate

- *3007469 / 19834-1 — Breath rate setting Ventilator (LOINC)*: the rate set on the ventilator.

### By measurement method

- *21490867 / 76270-8 — Respiratory rate by Impedance.transthoracic (LOINC)*: derived from chest-impedance monitoring, the usual bedside monitor method.
- *42527123 / 76174-2 — Respiratory rate by Pulse oximetry.plethysmograph (LOINC)*: derived from the pulse-oximetry waveform.
- *21490847 / 76172-6 — Respiratory rate by Carbon dioxide measurement (LOINC)*: derived from capnography.
- *21490846 / 76171-8 — Respiratory rate by Airway flow measurement (LOINC)*: derived from airway flow, typically on a ventilator.
- *21490845 / 76170-0 — Respiratory rate by Acoustic measurement (LOINC)*: derived from an acoustic sensor.
- *36303374 / 76173-4 — Respiratory rate by Non-airway pressure measurement (LOINC)*: derived from a pressure sensor outside the airway.
- *3006396 / 19841-6 — Respiratory rate by Spirometry --at maximum voluntary ventilation (LOINC)*: measured during a spirometry manoeuvre.

### By context

- *3010647 / 9303-9 — Respiratory rate --resting (LOINC)*: measured at rest.
- *3038563 / 40441-8 — Respiratory rate --post exercise (LOINC)*: measured after exercise.
- *36305182 / 89274-5 — Respiratory rate --W exercise (LOINC)*: measured during exercise.
- *36305857 / 89279-4 — Respiratory rate --during anesthesia (LOINC)*: measured under anaesthesia.
- *3022705 / 19842-4 — Respiratory rate --at maximum voluntary ventilation (LOINC)*: measured during a maximum voluntary ventilation manoeuvre.
- Pre/post inhalation therapy, cardioversion, conscious sedation and bronchoscopy variants (LOINC), each following the same pattern.

**Note on units**: reported in **/min** (`8541 / /min — per minute`, UCUM), the recommended unit (breaths per minute).

## Mapping Notes

- **Default concept** when the source records a respiratory rate without qualification: *3024171 / 9279-1 — Respiratory rate* (or SNOMED *4313591 / 86290005 — Respiratory rate*).
- **Measurement method / context / setting are attributes, not separate variables**: map to a method/context/setting concept only when the source documents it; otherwise use the generic concept. The ventilator set rate maps to *3007469 / 19834-1 — Breath rate setting Ventilator*.
- This single set replaces the former separate ventilation-parameters respiratory-rate set (now deprecated).
