en.name: Oxygen saturation (SpO2)
en.shortDescription: Oxygen saturation (SpO2) — the percentage of haemoglobin carrying oxygen, measured non-invasively by pulse oximetry at the periphery; reported in %.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Oxygen saturation (SpO2) is the percentage of haemoglobin bound to oxygen, used to detect hypoxaemia. The "p" denotes a peripheral measurement obtained by pulse oximetry, which estimates arterial saturation non-invasively rather than measuring it on a blood sample. It is reported as a percentage, typically 95-100% on room air in a healthy adult. It is one of the core vital signs, recorded continuously on virtually every monitor.

This concept set captures **non-invasive pulse-oximetry oxygen saturation values (SpO2)**. It is distinct from blood-gas oxygen saturation (SaO2) measured by co-oximetry on an arterial blood sample, which is a laboratory measurement covered elsewhere. It excludes interpretive findings (e.g., "oxygen saturation decreased") and derived or goal values (baseline, maximum, minimum, target SpO2).

## Included Concepts

This concept set contains 20 standard concepts (LOINC + SNOMED). The SNOMED side is anchored on *4196147 / 431314004 — Peripheral oxygen saturation (SNOMED)* with descendants; the LOINC side is a curated list of pulse-oximetry concepts. The default for an unqualified SpO2 value is *40762499 / 59408-5 — Oxygen saturation in Arterial blood by Pulse oximetry (LOINC)* or *4196147 / 431314004 — Peripheral oxygen saturation (SNOMED)*.

Note: the LOINC concepts are named "Oxygen saturation in Arterial blood by Pulse oximetry" — the "Arterial blood" wording reflects that pulse oximetry *estimates* arterial saturation; these are SpO2 (pulse-oximeter) values, not blood-gas measurements.

### Generic SpO2

- *40762499 / 59408-5 — Oxygen saturation in Arterial blood by Pulse oximetry (LOINC)*: The generic SpO2 value, no context specified. Default mapping target.
- *4196147 / 431314004 — Peripheral oxygen saturation (SNOMED)*: SNOMED equivalent of the generic peripheral (pulse-oximetry) oxygen saturation.

### By oxygen / rest context

These specify whether the patient was on room air or supplemental oxygen, at rest or on exertion.

- *40762501 / 59410-1 — Oxygen saturation ... --on room air (LOINC)*: SpO2 breathing room air (no supplemental oxygen).
- *40762508 / 59417-6 — Oxygen saturation ... --resting (LOINC)*: SpO2 at rest.
- *44810014 / 866661000000106 — Peripheral blood oxygen saturation on room air at rest (SNOMED)*, *44810015 / 866681000000102 — Peripheral blood oxygen saturation on room air on exertion*, *44810016 / 866701000000100 — Peripheral blood oxygen saturation on supplemental oxygen at rest*, *44810017 / 866721000000109 — Peripheral blood oxygen saturation on supplemental oxygen on exertion*: SNOMED concepts combining oxygen source (room air vs. supplemental) with activity (rest vs. exertion); used in walk tests and respiratory assessments.

### Neonatal screening (pre- and postductal)

- *40762498 / 59407-7 — Oxygen saturation in Blood Preductal by Pulse oximetry (LOINC)* and *40762509 / 59418-4 — Oxygen saturation in Blood Postductal by Pulse oximetry (LOINC)*: Pre- and postductal SpO2, taken at a right-hand and a foot site respectively, for neonatal critical congenital heart disease screening (a difference between the two suggests a ductus-dependent lesion).

### By clinical condition / treatment phase

- *36305237 / 89276-0 — Oxygen saturation in Arterial blood by Pulse oximetry --W exercise* and *40762503 / 59412-7 — Oxygen saturation in Arterial blood by Pulse oximetry --post exercise*: SpO2 during and after exercise.
- *36304254 / 89277-8 — Oxygen saturation in Arterial blood by Pulse oximetry --during anesthesia*: SpO2 under anaesthesia.
- *40762500 / 59409-3 — Oxygen saturation in Arterial blood by Pulse oximetry --during treatment*, *40762504 / 59413-5 — Oxygen saturation in Arterial blood by Pulse oximetry --post treatment*, *40762507 / 59416-8 — Oxygen saturation in Arterial blood by Pulse oximetry --pre treatment*: SpO2 around a treatment.
- *40762502 / 59411-9 — Oxygen saturation in Arterial blood by Pulse oximetry --post bronchodilation* and *40762505 / 59414-3 — Oxygen saturation in Arterial blood by Pulse oximetry --pre bronchodilation*: SpO2 before/after a bronchodilator.
- *40762506 / 59415-0 — Oxygen saturation in Arterial blood by Pulse oximetry --pre physiotherapy*: SpO2 before chest physiotherapy.

**Note on units.** SpO2 is reported as a percentage (%).

## Excluded Concepts

- *4095045 / 250553009 — Capillary oxygen saturation measurement (SNOMED, Procedure)*: Removed — this is the procedure (the act), not the resulting value.
- *3661929 / 1321841000000106*, *3661930 / 1321861000000107*, *3661931 / 1321871000000100*, *3661932 / 1321881000000103 — Peripheral oxygen saturation ... on exertion decreased/unchanged (SNOMED, Clinical Finding)*: Removed — these are interpretive findings (the saturation went down / stayed the same), not numeric measurements.
- Derived and goal values among the SNOMED descendants are excluded: *45770406 / 927981000000106 — Baseline SpO2*, *44813869 / 852651000000100 — Maximum peripheral oxygen saturation*, *44809213 / 852661000000102 — Minimum peripheral oxygen saturation*, *44809212 / 852641000000103 — Target peripheral oxygen saturation*.
- Blood-gas oxygen saturation (SaO2) measured by co-oximetry on an arterial sample is not part of this set; it is a separate laboratory measurement.

## Mapping Notes

- *Default concept*: When the source records an SpO2 / pulse-oximetry value with no context, map to Oxygen saturation in Arterial blood by Pulse oximetry (40762499 / 59408-5 — Oxygen saturation in Arterial blood by Pulse oximetry, LOINC), or its SNOMED equivalent (4196147 / 431314004 — Peripheral oxygen saturation). Do not infer the oxygen source or activity level.
- *SpO2 vs. SaO2*: This set is for the non-invasive pulse-oximeter value. If the source value comes from an arterial blood-gas analyser (co-oximetry), it is SaO2 and belongs to the blood-gas laboratory measurement, not here.
- *Room air vs. supplemental oxygen*: Map to the room-air concept (40762501 / 59410-1 — Oxygen saturation in Arterial blood by Pulse oximetry --on room air, LOINC) only when the source states the patient was on room air. If oxygen status is not documented, use the generic concept.
- *Neonatal screening*: Use the pre-/postductal concepts (40762498 / 59407-7 — Oxygen saturation in Blood Preductal by Pulse oximetry and 40762509 / 59418-4 — Oxygen saturation in Blood Postductal by Pulse oximetry, LOINC) only in neonatal congenital-heart-disease screening, not for routine SpO2.
- *Common source labels*: "SpO2", "SatO2", "Sat", "Pulse ox", "O2 sat", "Saturation" → Oxygen saturation in Arterial blood by Pulse oximetry (40762499 / 59408-5 — Oxygen saturation in Arterial blood by Pulse oximetry, LOINC).

en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context This concept captures the diameter of the endotracheal tube (ETT) in place — by convention the tube's internal diameter, the number used to size and label ETTs (e.g. 7.0, 7.5, 8.0). In source data it is a single numeric measurement per patient-timestamp, recording which tube size was used rather than a physiological measurement of the patient. It is documented in intensive care, anaesthesia, and emergency settings whenever a patient is intubated. It is reported in millimetres (**mm**) [1]. ## Included Concepts The set contains the single LOINC concept for endotracheal tube diameter: - *21491186 / 79562-5 — Endotracheal tube Diameter (LOINC)*: the internal diameter of the endotracheal tube, in millimetres. This is a leaf LOINC term with no descendants. **Note on units**: reported in **mm**, following the LOINC example unit for this term [1]. Standard adult ETT internal diameters fall roughly in the 7.0–8.0 mm range; paediatric and neonatal tubes are smaller. Tube sizes are commonly recorded in half-millimetre steps. ## Mapping Notes - This is the **tube's diameter**, not the tube device itself: the type of endotracheal tube is recorded separately (see the Endotracheal tube concept set). Map a recorded tube size here, and the device type (if any) to that other set. - **Internal diameter** is the conventional sizing figure for an ETT; if a source distinguishes internal from external diameter, only the internal diameter maps to this concept. - Tracheostomy tube sizing is a different device and is not captured by this concept. ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 79562-5 — Endotracheal tube Diameter. Available: https://loinc.org/79562-5/

en.name: Airway device change
en.shortDescription: Replacing an in-place airway device (endotracheal, tracheostomy or cricothyroidotomy tube), keeping the airway; not an extubation.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Airway device change is the act of replacing an in-place artificial airway with a new one — swapping an endotracheal tube, a tracheostomy tube, or a cricothyroidotomy tube. The distinguishing feature is that the airway is *maintained*: the old device is removed and a new one inserted immediately, so the patient is never left without an artificial airway (unlike extubation, where no tube is reinserted). In source data this is an event record (a procedure) marking the moment a tube was exchanged, not a numeric measurement. It is recorded mainly in intensive care and anaesthesia, e.g. when a tube is damaged, blocked, the wrong size, or routinely changed.

## Included Concepts

The set lists the SNOMED procedures for changing an airway device, grouped by route. There is no single SNOMED ancestor covering all of them (the only common parent, "Replacement of device", is far too broad), so the concepts are listed explicitly.

### Endotracheal tube change

- *4026054 / 225719006 — Changing endotracheal tube (SNOMED)*: changing an endotracheal tube.
- *4161799 / 398118003 — Change of endotracheal or endobronchial tube (SNOMED)*: a more general change concept also covering endobronchial tubes; its descendants are included.
- *4216776 / 397874007 — Airway exchange catheter procedure (SNOMED)*: exchanging the tube over an airway exchange catheter (a guide passed through the old tube to railroad the new one), a specific technique for changing an endotracheal/endobronchial tube.

### Tracheostomy tube change

- *4331311 / 2267008 — Changing tracheostomy tube (SNOMED)*: changing a tracheostomy tube. Synonyms: "Replacement of tracheostomy tube", "Change of tracheostomy tube".

### Cricothyroidotomy tube change

- *4339602 / 232576007 — Change of cricothyroidotomy tube (SNOMED)*: changing the tube of an emergency surgical (cricothyroidotomy) airway.

## Excluded Concepts

Concepts that change the tube's **fixation** rather than the airway device itself are intentionally not included, following the same reasoning applied to the Extubation concept set (issue #13): re-securing a tube does not change the airway device.

- *4026055 / 225720000 — Changing endotracheal tube headband (SNOMED)* — fixation band, not the device.
- *4021519 / 225721001 — Changing endotracheal tube tapes (SNOMED)* — fixation tapes, not the device.

## Mapping Notes

- **A device change is not an extubation**: these events keep the patient's airway in place. Do not map them to the Extubation concept set, which captures genuine tube *removals* (where no tube is reinserted).
- **Default for an unspecified endotracheal tube change**: *4026054 / 225719006 — Changing endotracheal tube*. Use *4161799 / 398118003 — Change of endotracheal or endobronchial tube* when the source uses the broader wording or the change involves an endobronchial tube.
- **Match the route**: map a tracheostomy tube change to *4331311 / 2267008 — Changing tracheostomy tube* and a cricothyroidotomy tube change to *4339602 / 232576007 — Change of cricothyroidotomy tube* — do not collapse different airway routes onto the endotracheal concept.
- **Fixation events** (changing the headband, tapes or dressing securing the tube) do not belong here and should not be mapped to this set.

en.name: Ventilation mode
en.shortDescription: Ventilation mode in use (PCV, VCV, SIMV, pressure support, CPAP/BiPAP, APRV, NAVA, high-frequency, CMV…) — one variable, all modes.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

The ventilation mode is the control strategy a mechanical ventilator uses to deliver breaths — how it triggers, targets and cycles each breath (for example volume-controlled, pressure-controlled, pressure support, CPAP, or high-frequency). In source data this is a single categorical variable per patient-timestamp whose value is the mode in use; it is a **procedure** record with no unit. It is recorded in intensive care and anaesthesia for ventilated patients. The mode is independent of whether ventilation is invasive (via a tube) or non-invasive (via a mask) — that distinction is captured in the Invasive mechanical ventilation and Non-invasive ventilation concept sets.

## Included Concepts

This set groups all SNOMED ventilation-mode concepts in one place (a single `ventilation_mode` variable). They are organised below by mode family for readability only — all are part of the same set.

### Pressure-controlled (and volume-targeted pressure-control)

- *37152410 / 1186746005 — Assist control ventilation pressure control inflation-type (SNOMED)*
- *37152412 / 1186748006 — Assist control ventilation pressure-control inflation-type and assured constant airway pressure adjunct (SNOMED)*
- *37152411 / 1186747001 — Assist control ventilation volume-targeted pressure-control inflation-type (SNOMED)*
- *37152408 / 1186744008 — Assist control ventilation volume-targeted pressure-control inflation-type and assured constant airway pressure adjunct (SNOMED)*
- *37152364 / 1186622005 — Synchronized intermittent mandatory ventilation - pressure-control pressure-support inflation (SNOMED)*
- *37152384 / 1186679003 — Synchronized intermittent mandatory ventilation - volume targeted pressure-control and pressure-support inflation (SNOMED)*
- *37152386 / 1186681001 — Synchronized intermittent mandatory ventilation with pressure-control, two levels of pressure-support and an assured constant airway pressure adjunct (SNOMED)*
- *37152387 / 1186682008 — Synchronized intermittent mandatory ventilation with pressure-control, one level of pressure-support active during both phases and an assured constant airway pressure adjunct (SNOMED)*
- *37152388 / 1186683003 — Synchronized intermittent mandatory ventilation with pressure-control, an assured constant airway pressure adjunct and pressure-support at the higher pressure level only (SNOMED)*
- *37152389 / 1186684009 — Synchronized intermittent mandatory ventilation with synchronized termination pressure-control, pressure-support and an assured constant airway pressure adjunct (SNOMED)*
- *37152390 / 1186685005 — Synchronized intermittent mandatory ventilation with volume targeted pressure-control, pressure-support and an assured constant airway pressure adjunct (SNOMED)*

### Volume-controlled

- *37152409 / 1186745009 — Assist control ventilation volume-control inflation-type (SNOMED)*
- *4055375 / 243150007 — Assisted controlled mandatory ventilation (SNOMED)*
- *4245036 / 59427005 — Synchronized intermittent mandatory ventilation (SNOMED)*
- *37152363 / 1186621003 — Synchronized intermittent mandatory ventilation - volume control pressure-support inflation (SNOMED)*
- *37152385 / 1186680000 — Synchronized intermittent mandatory ventilation volume control inflation and an assured constant airway pressure adjunct during expiratory phase (SNOMED)*

### Spontaneous / support

- *37154096 / 1259864003 — Pressure support ventilation (SNOMED)*
- *4165535 / 47545007 — Continuous positive airway pressure ventilation treatment (SNOMED)*
- *4055262 / 243142003 — Dual pressure spontaneous ventilation support (SNOMED)*
- *3661883 / 34291000175108 — Nocturnal dual pressure spontaneous ventilation support (SNOMED)*
- *37152400 / 1186731003 — Continuous spontaneous ventilation with pressure support (SNOMED)*
- *37152401 / 1186732005 — Continuous spontaneous ventilation with volume targeted pressure-support (SNOMED)*
- *37152402 / 1186733000 — Continuous spontaneous ventilation with effort support (SNOMED)*
- *40491848 / 447243000 — Bilevel positive airway pressure titration (SNOMED)*
- *37152378 / 1186658003 — Spontaneous timed ventilation with pressure-support for spontaneous breaths and volume-control ventilator initiated inflation (SNOMED)*
- *37152379 / 1186672007 — Spontaneous timed ventilation with pressure-support for spontaneous breaths and pressure-control with flow termination for ventilator initiated inflation (SNOMED)*
- *37152380 / 1186674008 — Spontaneous timed ventilation with volume targeted pressure-support for spontaneous breaths and volume targeted pressure-control for ventilator initiated inflations (SNOMED)*
- *37152383 / 1186678006 — Continuous positive airway pressure with an assured constant airway pressure adjunct (SNOMED)*
- *37152791 / 1197780003 — Spontaneous and/or timed ventilation (SNOMED)*
- *3661882 / 34281000175105 — Nocturnal continuous positive airway pressure (SNOMED)*

### High-frequency, NAVA, APRV, CMV and other advanced modes

- *4072515 / 243143008 — Airway pressure release ventilation (SNOMED)*
- *37153603 / 1222606000 — Continuous mandatory ventilation (SNOMED)*
- *37153604 / 1222607009 — Continuous mandatory ventilation with sigh (SNOMED)*
- *37151336 / 1187022003 — Continuous mandatory ventilation volume-control inflation-type and assured constant airway pressure adjunct in the expiratory phase (SNOMED)*
- *37151337 / 1187023008 — Continuous mandatory ventilation pressure-control inflation-type (SNOMED)*
- *37151338 / 1187024002 — Continuous mandatory ventilation pressure-control inflation-type and assured constant airway pressure adjunct (SNOMED)*
- *37151339 / 1187025001 — Continuous mandatory ventilation volume-targeted pressure-control inflation-type (SNOMED)*
- *37152413 / 1186749003 — Continuous mandatory ventilation volume-control inflation-type (SNOMED)*
- *37152407 / 1186742007 — Intermittent mandatory ventilation with synchronized-termination pressure-control and assured constant airway pressure adjunct (SNOMED)*
- *37157430 / 1217390002 — Intermittent mandatory ventilation with synchronized-termination pressure control and assured constant airway pressure adjunct during the inflation phase (SNOMED)*
- *37157167 / 1197612007 — Intermittent mandatory ventilation (SNOMED)*
- *37158487 / 1260411001 — Continuous flow apneic ventilation (SNOMED)*
- *4074666 / 243155002 — High frequency oscillatory ventilation (SNOMED)*
- *4055377 / 243154003 — High frequency jet ventilation (SNOMED)*
- *4055376 / 243153009 — High frequency positive pressure ventilation (SNOMED)*
- *1243692 / 1297240007 — Neurally adjusted ventilatory assist (SNOMED)*

## Mapping Notes

- Map a recorded ventilation mode to the matching concept here, whatever its family. The mode families above are descriptive groupings, not separate sets.
- **Mode vs ventilation act**: this set is the *mode*; whether the patient is on invasive or non-invasive ventilation is recorded separately (Invasive mechanical ventilation / Non-invasive ventilation concept sets). A patient has both a ventilation act and a mode at the same time.
- **Dual / volume-targeted pressure-control** modes (e.g. PRVC) are grouped with the pressure-controlled family, since pressure is the controlled variable.
- **No unit**: the value is the mode itself, not a measurement.

en.name: Coagulation factor V antigen
en.shortDescription: Immunological quantity of factor V protein ; distinct from factor V activity (functional)
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Factor V antigen is the **immunological measurement of the factor V protein concentration** in plasma — what this concept set measures. It quantifies how much factor V protein is present, irrespective of whether the molecule is functionally active [1]. The result is a single numeric value per patient-timestamp, produced on platelet-poor plasma by immunoassay [1, 2]. Results are reported as a percentage of normal plasma concentration — the representation this concept set covers. A separate LOINC code expresses the same assay in IU/mL; it is excluded here because that unit is not convertible to a percentage [3]. **Note: activity vs antigen.** This concept set covers **antigen** only — the immunological mass of the factor V protein. The functional capacity of the protein in the clotting cascade is captured by a separate concept set, "Coagulation factor V activity". The two values can diverge in qualitative deficits where antigen is normal but activity is reduced [1] — they are different study variables and must not be merged. ## Included Concepts The set contains a single LOINC "Lab Test" concept, measuring factor V antigenic concentration in platelet-poor plasma by immunoassay: - *3023945 / 3195-5 — Coagulation factor V Ag actual/normal in Platelet poor plasma by Immunoassay (LOINC)*: result expressed as a **percentage** of pooled normal plasma antigenic concentration. **Note on units.** The recommended unit is **`%`** (OMOP concept 8554 — percent), the proportion of pooled normal plasma antigenic concentration, as listed by LOINC for `3195-5`. Sources reporting factor V antigen in `U/mL` or `IU/mL` are measuring the concentration variant excluded from this set — see *Excluded Concepts* below. ## Excluded Concepts One concept is explicitly excluded by name (see the note on units below). The following LOINC concepts that exist for factor V are also not part of this set: - **Factor V activity** (`3005757 / 3193-0 — Coagulation factor V activity actual/normal in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay`): captured by the separate concept set "Coagulation factor V activity". - **Factor V inhibitor** (`3004057 / 3191-4 — Coagulation factor V inhibitor [Units/volume] in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay`, `21494686 / 81124-0 — Coagulation factor V inhibitor [Presence] in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay`): rare bleeding disorder workup, separate scope. - **Factor V activity and inhibitor panel** (`36031832 / 96458-5 — Coagulation factor V activity and inhibitor panel - Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay`): panel grouping concept, not a measurement result. **Note on excluded units.** Concept 3027396 / 3194-8 — Coagulation factor V Ag [Units/volume] in Platelet poor plasma by Immunoassay (LOINC) is excluded from this set. It reports an *activity concentration* in arbitrary units (`[arb'U]/mL`) rather than a proportion of normal plasma, and the two are not interchangeable: UCUM defines arbitrary units as non-dimensional and non-convertible, while IUPAC/IFCC call the same thing a *procedure-defined unit* — a unit whose reference is set by the individual laboratory or measuring device. No conversion factor to `%` can therefore be stated with confidence. In practice laboratories report factor V as a percentage of normal (typically 50–200 % in adults [2]), and no published source documents reference values in `[arb'U]/mL`. Should a data provider actually report this concept, it warrants its own concept set rather than being merged here. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source explicitly reports "factor V antigen", "factor V Ag", "facteur V antigène" with the result expressed as a percentage of normal: `3023945 / 3195-5 — Coagulation factor V Ag actual/normal in Platelet poor plasma by Immunoassay`. - **Source reports IU/mL or U/mL for factor V antigen**: do **not** map here. That representation corresponds to `3027396 / 3194-8 — Coagulation factor V Ag [Units/volume] in Platelet poor plasma by Immunoassay`, which is excluded from this set because its arbitrary unit cannot be converted to a percentage of normal. - **Source reports a single "factor V" without specifying activity vs antigen**: by default, map to the "Coagulation factor V activity" concept set — the activity assay is the routine clinical measurement; antigen is a specialty test. Only map to this antigen concept set when the source unambiguously labels the result as "Ag" / "antigen" / "antigène". - **Do not confuse with**: factor V activity (different concept set), factor V Leiden genotype (genetic test, not immunoassay), factor V inhibitor titre. ## References [1] Asselta R, Tenchini ML, Duga S. Inherited defects of coagulation factor V: the hemorrhagic side. *J Thromb Haemost*. 2006;4(1):26-34. Available: https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1538-7836.2005.01590.x [2] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 3194-8 — Coagulation factor V Ag [Units/volume] in Platelet poor plasma by Immunoassay. Available: https://loinc.org/3194-8/ [3] Nomenclature for Properties and Units (NPU). IFCC/IUPAC. NPU codes (current release). Available: https://npu-terminology.org/npu-database/

en.name: Fibrinogen antigen
en.shortDescription: Immunoassay-measured fibrinogen ; distinct from functional (clottable) fibrinogen (Clauss)
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Fibrinogen antigen is the **immunological measurement of the fibrinogen protein concentration** in plasma — what this concept set measures. It quantifies how much fibrinogen protein is present, irrespective of whether the molecule is functionally clottable by thrombin [1]. The result is a single numeric value per patient-timestamp, produced on platelet poor plasma (PPP) by immunoassay [2]. Results are reported as a mass concentration in g/L or mg/dL [3]. Clinically, fibrinogen antigen aids in the diagnosis of fibrinogen deficiencies (acquired or congenital) and is used for monitoring the severity and treatment of disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) and fibrinolysis [2]. **Note: "fibrinogen" vs "fibrinogen antigen".** This concept set covers **fibrinogen antigen** only — the immunological mass of the fibrinogen protein. The functionally clottable fibrinogen, measured by clot-based or viscoelastic assays, is captured by a separate concept set, "Fibrinogen in blood". The two values can diverge in dysfibrinogenaemia, where antigen is normal but the clot-based result is reduced — they are different study variables and must not be merged. ## Included Concepts The set contains two LOINC "Lab Test" concepts, both measuring fibrinogen antigenic concentration in platelet poor plasma, differing only by the assay method: - *3016628 / 3256-5 — Fibrinogen Ag [Mass/volume] in Platelet poor plasma by Immunoassay*: generic immunoassay code. Most widely used. - *3037950 / 42772-4 — Fibrinogen Ag [Mass/volume] in Platelet poor plasma by Nephelometry*: same quantity, with the nephelometry method explicit. **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS`: **`mg/dL`** for both codes. Source systems may also report in `g/L`; conversion `1 g/L = 100 mg/dL`. ## Excluded Concepts No concepts are explicitly excluded by name. The following LOINC concepts that exist for fibrinogen are deliberately not part of this set (they belong to other concept sets): - **Fibrinogen by clot-based or viscoelastic assay**: captured by "Fibrinogen in blood". - **Fibrinogen Ag/Fibrinogen [Mass Ratio]** (`3026131 / 31158-9 — Fibrinogen Ag/Fibrinogen [Mass Ratio] in Platelet poor plasma`): a derived ratio used to detect dysfibrinogenaemia, computed downstream from the activity and antigen values — not a primary measurement. - **Fibrinogen [Presence]** / **Fibrinogen [Interpretation]**: qualitative concepts. - **Cryofibrinogen, Fibrinogen fragments, Fibrin+Fibrinogen fragments**: different measurands. - **Tissue and Smears specimens**: out of scope. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source explicitly reports "fibrinogen antigen", "fibrinogen Ag": `3016628 / 3256-5 — Fibrinogen Ag [Mass/volume] in Platelet poor plasma by Immunoassay`. - **Source explicitly states nephelometry method**: map to `3037950 / 42772-4 — Fibrinogen Ag [Mass/volume] in Platelet poor plasma by Nephelometry`. - **Source reports a single "fibrinogen" without specifying activity vs antigen**: by default, map to the "Fibrinogen in blood" concept set — the clot-based assay is the routine clinical measurement; antigen is a specialty test. Only map to this antigen concept set when the source unambiguously labels the result as "Ag" / "antigen". - **Do not confuse with**: fibrinogen by clot-based assay (separate concept set), fibrinogen fragments (degradation products), D-dimer, cryofibrinogen. ## References [1] Mosesson MW. Fibrinogen and fibrin structure and functions. *J Thromb Haemost*. 2005;3(8):1894-904. Available: https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1538-7836.2005.01365.x [2] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 3256-5 — Fibrinogen Ag [Mass/volume] in Platelet poor plasma by Immunoassay. Available: https://loinc.org/3256-5/ [3] Nomenclature for Properties and Units (NPU). IFCC/IUPAC. NPU codes (current release). Available: https://npu-terminology.org/npu-database/

en.name: Prothrombin ratio in blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context The prothrombin ratio is a transformation of the prothrombin time (PT) expressed as a percentage of the activity of pooled normal plasma. It is one of the standard outputs of a coagulation analyser, alongside the PT in seconds. A healthy patient has a prothrombin ratio of ~100 %; lower values indicate longer clotting times. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a coagulation analyser on platelet poor plasma (PPP). Results are reported in **%** [2]. **Note: prothrombin ratio vs PT vs INR.** The prothrombin ratio (this concept set), the PT in seconds, and the INR are three different representations of the same underlying physical measurement, with different normalisations: - **Prothrombin ratio** — percentage of pooled normal plasma activity (this concept set). - **PT (seconds)** — raw measurement; depends on the laboratory's thromboplastin reagent. Captured by a separate concept set, "Prothrombin time in blood". - **INR** — dimensionless, reagent-independent transformation. Used for vitamin K antagonist (VKA) monitoring. Captured by a separate concept set, "INR in blood". The three representations are **not interconvertible** without the laboratory's local calibration curve. The data dictionary keeps them addressable independently — analyses needing a homogeneous variable should pick one representation rather than merging across. ## Included Concepts The set contains one LOINC "Lab Test" concept: - *3033658 / 5894-1 — Prothrombin time (PT) actual/Normal*: result expressed as a percentage of pooled normal plasma activity. **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows LOINC: **`%`** (concept 8554 — percent). ## Excluded Concepts No concepts are explicitly excluded by name. The following LOINC concepts that exist for PT actual/Normal variants are deliberately not part of this set: - **PIVKA-sensitive / PIVKA-insensitive variants** (`3039709 / 52753-1 — Prothrombin time (PT) PIVKA insensitive actual/normal in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay`, `3042131 / 52761-4 — Prothrombin time (PT) PIVKA sensitive actual/normal in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay`, `3042392 / 52752-3 — Prothrombin time (PT) PIVKA insensitive actual/normal in Capillary blood by Coagulation assay`, `3041830 / 52760-6 — Prothrombin time (PT) PIVKA sensitive actual/normal in Capillary blood by Coagulation assay`): specialised assays for vitamin K antagonist monitoring, not the routine prothrombin ratio. - **Factor substitution / control / mixing study** variants (e.g. `1091858 / 105049-1 — Prothrombin time (PT) factor substitution [Time Ratio] in Control Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay --2H post incubation with 1:1 normal plasma`): research context, not routine measurement. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports "prothrombin ratio" or "prothrombin index" with the value as a percentage of normal: `3033658 / 5894-1 — Prothrombin time (PT) actual/Normal`. - **Source reports PT in seconds**: do **not** map to this concept set. PT in seconds has its own concept set, "Prothrombin time in blood". - **Source reports INR**: do **not** map to this concept set. INR has its own concept set, "INR in blood". - **Do not confuse with**: PT in seconds, INR, aPTT, thrombin time, Reptilase time. ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 5894-1 — Prothrombin time (PT) actual/Normal. Available: https://loinc.org/5894-1/ [2] Nomenclature for Properties and Units (NPU). IFCC/IUPAC. NPU codes (current release). Available: https://npu-terminology.org/npu-database/

en.name: aPTT ratio in blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context The aPTT ratio is a transformation of the activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) expressed as the patient's time divided by the laboratory's normal control time. It is one of the standard outputs of a coagulation analyser, alongside the aPTT in seconds. A healthy patient has an aPTT ratio of ~1. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a coagulation analyser on platelet poor plasma (PPP). Results are reported as a dimensionless ratio [1]. **Note: aPTT ratio vs aPTT.** The aPTT ratio (this concept set) and the aPTT in seconds are two different representations of the same underlying physical measurement, with different normalisations: - **aPTT ratio** — patient time divided by the laboratory's normal control time (this concept set). - **aPTT (seconds)** — raw measurement; depends on the laboratory's reagent. Captured by a separate concept set, "aPTT in blood". The two representations are **not interconvertible** without the laboratory's local normal control. The data dictionary keeps them addressable independently — analyses needing a homogeneous variable should pick one representation rather than merging across. ## Included Concepts The set contains one LOINC "Lab Test" concept: - *40766287 / 63561-5 — aPTT actual/normal in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay*: dimensionless ratio (patient/normal control). **Note on units.** The aPTT ratio is dimensionless. LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS` lists no unit; some source systems report no unit, others report `1` or `{ratio}`. All represent the same dimensionless quantity. ## Excluded Concepts No concepts are explicitly excluded by name. The aPTT-derived ratios related to protein C / APC resistance assays (e.g. `48590-4`, `52766-3`, `52767-1`) are deliberately not part of this set — they are specialised tests with a different clinical question. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports "aPTT ratio" (patient/control, dimensionless): `40766287 / 63561-5 — aPTT actual/normal in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay`. - **Source reports aPTT in seconds**: do **not** map to this concept set. The aPTT in seconds has its own concept set, "aPTT in blood". - **Do not confuse with**: aPTT in seconds, prothrombin ratio, INR, activated clotting time (ACT), APC resistance test, thrombin time, or anti-Xa heparin level. ## References [1] Nomenclature for Properties and Units (NPU). IFCC/IUPAC. NPU codes (current release). Available: https://npu-terminology.org/npu-database/ [2] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 63561-5 — aPTT actual/normal in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay. Available: https://loinc.org/63561-5/

en.name: Glasgow coma scale eye opening
en.shortDescription: GCS eye opening sub-score (1–4): spontaneous, to sound, to pressure, none
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context The eye opening component (E) of the Glasgow Coma Scale assesses arousal by observing under what stimulus the patient opens their eyes. It is scored on a 4-point scale [1]: - 4 spontaneous — eyes open without any prompt - 3 to sound — eyes open in response to verbal command - 2 to pressure — eyes open only to a noxious stimulus (e.g. trapezius pinch, supraorbital pressure) - 1 none — no eye opening to any stimulus The eye opening score reflects the integrity of the brainstem arousal systems. When eye opening cannot be assessed (e.g. severe periorbital oedema, eyelid laceration, recent ophthalmic surgery), the component should be recorded as not testable (NT) rather than scored 1. This concept set captures only the recorded eye opening sub-score; the global GCS total and the verbal and motor components are captured in separate concept sets. ## Included Concepts This concept set contains the single LOINC concept representing the recorded GCS eye opening sub-score: - `3016335` — Glasgow coma score eye opening (`9267-6`, Clinical Observation) ## References [1] Teasdale G, Jennett B. Assessment of coma and impaired consciousness: a practical scale. *Lancet*. 1974;2(7872):81-84. doi:10.1016/s0140-6736(74)91639-0. PMID: 4136544

fr.name: Glasgow coma scale eye opening
fr.shortDescription: Sous-score GCS d'ouverture des yeux (1–4) : spontanée, au bruit, à la pression, aucune
fr.longDescription: ## Définition et contexte clinique Le sous-score d'ouverture des yeux (E) du Glasgow Coma Scale évalue l'éveil en observant à quel stimulus le patient ouvre les yeux. Il est coté sur une échelle de 4 points [1] : - 4 spontanée — yeux ouverts sans sollicitation - 3 au bruit — yeux ouverts en réponse à un ordre verbal - 2 à la pression — yeux ouverts uniquement à un stimulus nociceptif (par ex. pincement du trapèze, pression sus-orbitaire) - 1 aucune — aucune ouverture des yeux à aucun stimulus Le sous-score d'ouverture des yeux reflète l'intégrité des systèmes d'éveil du tronc cérébral. Lorsque l'ouverture des yeux ne peut pas être évaluée (par ex. œdème périorbitaire sévère, plaie palpébrale, chirurgie ophtalmique récente), la composante doit être enregistrée comme non testable (NT) plutôt que cotée 1. Ce concept set ne couvre que le sous-score d'ouverture des yeux enregistré ; le score total GCS et les sous-scores verbal et moteur sont capturés dans des concept sets séparés. ## Concepts inclus Ce concept set contient l'unique concept LOINC représentant le sous-score d'ouverture des yeux GCS enregistré : - `3016335` — Glasgow coma score eye opening (`9267-6`, Clinical Observation) ## Références [1] Teasdale G, Jennett B. Assessment of coma and impaired consciousness: a practical scale. *Lancet*. 1974;2(7872):81-84. doi:10.1016/s0140-6736(74)91639-0. PMID: 4136544

en.name: Glasgow coma scale verbal response
en.shortDescription: GCS verbal sub-score (1–5): oriented, confused, words, sounds, none
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context The verbal response component (V) of the Glasgow Coma Scale assesses the content and coherence of the patient's spoken response. It is scored on a 5-point scale [1]: - 5 oriented — correctly states name, place and time - 4 confused — converses but disoriented or confused - 3 words — articulates intelligible words but no coherent conversation - 2 sounds — produces only moans, groans or unintelligible sounds - 1 none — no verbal response The verbal sub-score depends on intact higher cortical function, language and respiratory tract patency. In intubated or tracheostomised patients the verbal component cannot be assessed; the convention is to record it as not testable (NT, sometimes notated "T") rather than score 1, since a score of 1 would otherwise spuriously suggest deeper impairment than is actually documented. This concept set captures only the recorded verbal sub-score; the global GCS total and the eye opening and motor components are captured in separate concept sets. ## Included Concepts This concept set contains the single LOINC concept representing the recorded GCS verbal sub-score: - `3009094` — Glasgow coma score verbal (`9270-0`, Clinical Observation) ## References [1] Teasdale G, Jennett B. Assessment of coma and impaired consciousness: a practical scale. *Lancet*. 1974;2(7872):81-84. doi:10.1016/s0140-6736(74)91639-0. PMID: 4136544

fr.name: Glasgow coma scale verbal response
fr.shortDescription: Sous-score GCS verbal (1–5) : orientée, confuse, mots, sons, aucune
fr.longDescription: ## Définition et contexte clinique Le sous-score de réponse verbale (V) du Glasgow Coma Scale évalue le contenu et la cohérence de la parole du patient. Il est coté sur une échelle de 5 points [1] : - 5 orientée — donne correctement son nom, le lieu et la date - 4 confuse — converse mais est désorienté ou confus - 3 mots — articule des mots intelligibles sans conversation cohérente - 2 sons — émet uniquement des gémissements, plaintes ou sons inintelligibles - 1 aucune — aucune réponse verbale Le sous-score verbal dépend d'une fonction corticale supérieure intacte, du langage et de la perméabilité des voies aériennes. Chez les patients intubés ou trachéotomisés, la composante verbale ne peut pas être évaluée ; la convention est de l'enregistrer comme non testable (NT, parfois notée « T ») plutôt que de la coter 1, car un score de 1 suggérerait à tort une atteinte plus profonde que celle réellement documentée. Ce concept set ne couvre que le sous-score verbal enregistré ; le score total GCS et les sous-scores d'ouverture des yeux et moteur sont capturés dans des concept sets séparés. ## Concepts inclus Ce concept set contient l'unique concept LOINC représentant le sous-score verbal GCS enregistré : - `3009094` — Glasgow coma score verbal (`9270-0`, Clinical Observation) ## Références [1] Teasdale G, Jennett B. Assessment of coma and impaired consciousness: a practical scale. *Lancet*. 1974;2(7872):81-84. doi:10.1016/s0140-6736(74)91639-0. PMID: 4136544

en.name: Glasgow coma scale motor response
en.shortDescription: GCS motor sub-score (1–6): obeys, localising, normal flexion, abnormal flexion, extension, none
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context The motor response component (M) of the Glasgow Coma Scale assesses the best motor response obtained, by observing spontaneous movement and the response to verbal command and to a noxious stimulus. It is scored on a 6-point scale [1]: - 6 obeys commands — performs the requested action (e.g. raise two fingers) - 5 localising — purposeful movement towards the source of a noxious stimulus - 4 normal flexion — withdraws limb from the noxious stimulus - 3 abnormal flexion — decorticate posturing (flexion of upper limbs, extension of lower limbs) - 2 extension — decerebrate posturing (extension of all four limbs) - 1 none — no motor response The motor sub-score is the strongest single predictor of outcome among the three GCS components and is often used in isolation in field triage scales (e.g. as the M-score in the Simplified Motor Score). Always record the best response observed across the four limbs, not the worst. This concept set captures only the recorded motor sub-score; the global GCS total and the eye opening and verbal components are captured in separate concept sets. ## Included Concepts This concept set contains the single LOINC concept representing the recorded GCS motor sub-score: - `3008223` — Glasgow coma score motor (`9268-4`, Clinical Observation) ## References [1] Teasdale G, Jennett B. Assessment of coma and impaired consciousness: a practical scale. *Lancet*. 1974;2(7872):81-84. doi:10.1016/s0140-6736(74)91639-0. PMID: 4136544

fr.name: Glasgow coma scale motor response
fr.shortDescription: Sous-score GCS moteur (1–6) : obéit, localisée, flexion normale, flexion anormale, extension, aucune
fr.longDescription: ## Définition et contexte clinique Le sous-score de réponse motrice (M) du Glasgow Coma Scale évalue la meilleure réponse motrice obtenue, en observant les mouvements spontanés et la réponse à un ordre verbal et à un stimulus nociceptif. Il est coté sur une échelle de 6 points [1] : - 6 obéit aux ordres — effectue l'action demandée (par ex. lever deux doigts) - 5 localisée — mouvement orienté vers la source du stimulus nociceptif - 4 flexion normale — retrait du membre face au stimulus nociceptif - 3 flexion anormale — posture de décortication (flexion des membres supérieurs, extension des membres inférieurs) - 2 extension — posture de décérébration (extension des quatre membres) - 1 aucune — aucune réponse motrice Le sous-score moteur est le meilleur prédicteur isolé du pronostic parmi les trois composantes du GCS et il est souvent utilisé seul dans les échelles de tri préhospitalier (par ex. comme M-score dans le Simplified Motor Score). Il faut toujours enregistrer la meilleure réponse observée sur les quatre membres, pas la pire. Ce concept set ne couvre que le sous-score moteur enregistré ; le score total GCS et les sous-scores d'ouverture des yeux et verbal sont capturés dans des concept sets séparés. ## Concepts inclus Ce concept set contient l'unique concept LOINC représentant le sous-score moteur GCS enregistré : - `3008223` — Glasgow coma score motor (`9268-4`, Clinical Observation) ## Références [1] Teasdale G, Jennett B. Assessment of coma and impaired consciousness: a practical scale. *Lancet*. 1974;2(7872):81-84. doi:10.1016/s0140-6736(74)91639-0. PMID: 4136544

description: Bedside categorical assessment of pupillary light reactivity (brisk / sluggish / absent), recorded separately for each eye

en.name: Pupillary response
en.shortDescription: Bedside categorical assessment of pupillary light reactivity (brisk / sluggish / absent), recorded separately for each eye
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

The pupillary response (also called pupillary light reflex) describes the constriction of the pupil in response to a directly applied light stimulus. It is recorded at the bedside as a categorical variable for each eye, conventionally classified as [1]:
- brisk — prompt, full constriction (the normal response)
- sluggish — delayed or incomplete constriction
- absent / non-reactive / fixed — no constriction

The pupillary response tests the integrity of the afferent (cranial nerve II) and efferent (cranial nerve III, parasympathetic) limbs of the light reflex and the connecting brainstem nuclei. A unilateral non-reactive pupil in a comatose patient is a red flag for ipsilateral mass effect or uncal herniation; bilaterally fixed and dilated pupils signal severe brainstem dysfunction.

The two pupils are always recorded independently. This concept set captures the manual bedside assessment; automated infrared pupillometry yielding quantitative metrics (constriction velocity, percentage change, NPi) is a distinct concept and is not included here.

## Included Concepts

This concept set contains the two LOINC concepts representing the manually recorded pupillary response, separately for each eye:
- `21490963` — Right pupil Pupillary response (`79815-7`, Clinical Observation)
- `21491763` — Left pupil Pupillary response (`79899-1`, Clinical Observation)

## Related Concept Sets

Pupil size is captured in a separate concept set (Pupil diameter), since the two measurements have different scales and units and cannot be combined or compared.

## References

[1] Posner JB, Saper CB, Schiff ND, Claassen J. *Plum and Posner's Diagnosis and Treatment of Stupor and Coma*. 5th ed. Oxford University Press; 2019. Chapter 2: Examination of the comatose patient.

fr.name: Réponse pupillaire
fr.shortDescription: Évaluation catégorielle au lit du patient de la réactivité pupillaire à la lumière (vive / paresseuse / abolie), séparément pour chaque œil
fr.longDescription:
## Définition et contexte clinique

La réponse pupillaire (également appelée réflexe photomoteur) décrit la constriction de la pupille en réponse à un stimulus lumineux directement appliqué. Elle est enregistrée au lit du patient comme une variable catégorielle pour chaque œil, conventionnellement classée en [1] :
- vive — constriction immédiate et complète (réponse normale)
- paresseuse — constriction retardée ou incomplète
- abolie / non réactive / fixée — aucune constriction

La réponse pupillaire teste l'intégrité des voies afférente (nerf crânien II) et efférente (nerf crânien III, parasympathique) du réflexe photomoteur et des noyaux du tronc cérébral qui les connectent. Une pupille unilatérale non réactive chez un patient comateux est un signe d'alerte évoquant un effet de masse ipsilatéral ou un engagement uncal ; des pupilles bilatéralement fixées et dilatées signent une dysfonction sévère du tronc cérébral.

Les deux pupilles sont toujours enregistrées indépendamment. Ce concept set couvre l'évaluation manuelle au lit ; la pupillométrie infrarouge automatisée fournissant des métriques quantitatives (vitesse de constriction, pourcentage de variation, NPi) est un concept distinct et n'est pas incluse ici.

## Concepts inclus

Ce concept set contient les deux concepts LOINC représentant la réponse pupillaire enregistrée manuellement, séparément pour chaque œil :
- `21490963` — Right pupil Pupillary response (`79815-7`, Clinical Observation)
- `21491763` — Left pupil Pupillary response (`79899-1`, Clinical Observation)

## Concept sets associés

La taille des pupilles est capturée dans un concept set séparé (Pupil diameter), les deux mesures ayant des échelles et des unités différentes et ne pouvant pas être combinées ou comparées.

## Références

[1] Posner JB, Saper CB, Schiff ND, Claassen J. *Plum and Posner's Diagnosis and Treatment of Stupor and Coma*. 5e éd. Oxford University Press ; 2019. Chapitre 2 : Examen du patient comateux.

en.name: Corrected calcium in blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Corrected calcium is the total calcium concentration mathematically adjusted to compensate for variations in plasma albumin (or total protein). In hypoalbuminaemia, total calcium falls because the protein-bound fraction decreases, even though the biologically active ionized fraction may be normal — the correction is meant to estimate the calcium concentration the patient would have had with a normal albumin [1, 2]. It is used when ionized calcium is not directly available. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp. Results are reported as a substance concentration in mmol/L (SI unit) or as a mass concentration in mg/dL [3]. **Note: this concept set covers corrected calcium only.** Total calcium (uncorrected) is captured by a separate concept set, "Calcium in blood"; ionized (free) calcium is captured by "Ionized calcium in blood". The three are different measurands and must not be merged. **Note: different correction formulas.** LOINC distinguishes corrections **for albumin** from corrections **for total protein**. The most widely cited albumin-based formula is Payne's (1973) [1]: - US (mg/dL): `Adjusted calcium = calcium − albumin (g/dL) + 4.0` - SI (mmol/L, g/L): `Adjusted calcium = calcium + 0.025 × (40 − albumin g/L)` For correction by total protein, LOINC does not specify a single canonical formula; preserve the source method when known. All forms (albumin-corrected, protein-corrected) are included in this concept set because most clinical sources aggregate them under "corrected calcium", but they are not numerically equivalent. Study designs that explicitly compare formulas should preserve the distinction at the source value level. ## Included Concepts The set lists five LOINC "Lab Test" concepts, grouped here by correction formula. ### Corrected for albumin (Payne's formula) - *3020059 / 29265-6 — Calcium [Moles/volume] corrected for albumin in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: SI form. Most widely used corrected calcium code. - *3047107 / 46099-8 — Calcium [Mass/volume] corrected for albumin in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: same measurand expressed as mass concentration. ### Corrected for total protein - *3004064 / 18281-6 — Calcium [Moles/volume] corrected for total protein in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)* - *3030597 / 34907-6 — Calcium [Mass/volume] corrected for total protein in Serum or Plasma (LOINC)*: same measurand expressed as mass concentration. - *3049461 / 47597-0 — Calcium [Moles/volume] corrected for total protein in Blood (LOINC)* **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS`: **`mmol/L`** (concept 8753 — millimole per litre) for `[Moles/volume]` codes and **`mg/dL`** (concept 8840) for `[Mass/volume]` codes. Conversion: `1 mmol/L ≈ 4.01 mg/dL`. ## Excluded Concepts No concepts are explicitly excluded by name. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports "corrected calcium", "calcium corrigé", "Ca corrected" with the corrected-for-albumin formula: `3020059 / 29265-6 — Calcium [Moles/volume] corrected for albumin in Serum or Plasma`. - **Source explicitly mentions correction for total protein** (rather than albumin): map to the corresponding `corrected for total protein` LOINC code. Do **not** merge with `corrected for albumin` without checking — the two formulas yield different values. - **Source reports total calcium without correction**: do **not** map. Use "Calcium in blood" instead. - **Source reports ionized calcium**: do **not** map. Use "Ionized calcium in blood" instead. - **Do not confuse with**: total calcium (uncorrected, separate concept set), ionized (free) calcium (separate concept set). ## References [1] Payne RB, Little AJ, Williams RB, Milner JR. Interpretation of serum calcium in patients with abnormal serum proteins. *Br Med J*. 1973;4(5893):643-6. Available: https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.4.5893.643 [2] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 29265-6 — Calcium [Moles/volume] corrected for albumin in Serum or Plasma. Available: https://loinc.org/29265-6/ [3] Nomenclature for Properties and Units (NPU). IFCC/IUPAC. NPU codes (current release). Available: https://npu-terminology.org/npu-database/

en.name: Carbon dioxide partial pressure in venous blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context The venous partial pressure of carbon dioxide (PvCO2) is the pressure of CO2 dissolved in venous blood. It is typically 4-6 mmHg higher than arterial PCO2 in stable patients (reflecting tissue CO2 production), but the gradient widens substantially in low-flow states (shock, severe heart failure) [1]. The venous-arterial gradient (`PvCO2 − PaCO2`, also called Pv-aCO2) is used in intensive care as a marker of tissue perfusion: a wide gradient (> 6 mmHg) suggests inadequate cardiac output relative to tissue CO2 production [1]. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a blood gas analyser on a venous sample. Results are reported in mmHg (US convention) or kPa (SI / European convention) [2]. **Note: arterial vs venous.** This concept set covers **venous PCO2 only** (peripheral venous, central venous, mixed venous, capillary blood). Arterial PCO2 is captured by the separate concept set "Carbon dioxide partial pressure in arterial blood". **Note: venous specimens.** Central venous PCO2 (CVC) reflects upper-body return, mixed venous PCO2 (pulmonary artery catheter) reflects whole-body return, peripheral venous PCO2 reflects the drained tissue bed. The user should preserve the specimen distinction in analyses where the source-of-blood matters. **Note: temperature-corrected variant.** Modern blood gas analysers measure at 37 °C. A separate LOINC code exists for PCO2 corrected to the patient's actual temperature (relevant in hypothermia). Both forms are included here; analyses that need to distinguish them must use the LOINC code, not the value. **Note: do not confuse with total CO2.** LOINC distinguishes `Carbon dioxide [Partial pressure]` (PvCO2, dissolved gas, mmHg or kPa) from `Carbon dioxide, total [Moles/volume]` (total CO2 content, mmol/L). The latter is essentially the bicarbonate plus dissolved CO2 and belongs with the separate concept set "Bicarbonate in blood". Only `[Partial pressure]` codes are included here. ## Included Concepts The set is anchored on four LOINC Hierarchy concepts (scoped to `Chemistry - non-challenge`), each expanded to include all their descendants, with total-CO2 codes excluded by name. The set resolves to eight LOINC "Lab Test" concepts, grouped here by specimen. ### Venous blood - *3021447 / 2021-4 — Carbon dioxide [Partial pressure] in Venous blood (LOINC)* - *3041290 / 40619-9 — Carbon dioxide [Partial pressure] adjusted to patient's actual temperature in Venous blood (LOINC)* ### Mixed venous blood - *3021513 / 19212-0 — Carbon dioxide [Partial pressure] in Mixed venous blood (LOINC)* - *3029306 / 50981-0 — Carbon dioxide [Partial pressure] adjusted to patient's actual temperature in Mixed venous blood (LOINC)* ### Central venous blood - *1616989 / 97538-3 — Carbon dioxide [Partial pressure] in Central venous blood (LOINC)* - *1616289 / 97539-1 — Carbon dioxide [Partial pressure] adjusted to patient's actual temperature in Central venous blood (LOINC)* ### Capillary blood - *3023024 / 2020-6 — Carbon dioxide [Partial pressure] in Capillary blood (LOINC)* - *3042462 / 40620-7 — Carbon dioxide [Partial pressure] adjusted to patient's actual temperature in Capillary blood (LOINC)* **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS`: **`mm[Hg]`** (concept 8876 — millimetre of mercury). Conversion: `1 kPa ≈ 7.50 mmHg`. ## Excluded Concepts The following LOINC concepts that exist for CO2 in non-arterial blood are deliberately not part of this set, grouped by reason for exclusion. ### Total CO2 — different measurand (bicarbonate equivalent) - *3010140 / 2027-1 — Carbon dioxide, total [Moles/volume] in Venous blood* - *3049133 / 48391-7 — Carbon dioxide, total [Moles/volume] in Venous blood by calculation* - *1617274 / 97545-8 — Carbon dioxide, total [Moles/volume] in Central venous blood* - *3018225 / 19223-7 — Carbon dioxide, total [Moles/volume] in Mixed venous blood* - *40761029 / 57920-1 — Carbon dioxide, total [Moles/volume] in Mixed venous blood by calculation* - *3009293 / 16551-4 — Carbon dioxide, total [Moles/volume] in Capillary blood* - *3038734 / 51781-3 — Carbon dioxide, total [Moles/volume] in Capillary blood by calculation* ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports a venous PCO2 without further specification: `3021447 / 2021-4 — Carbon dioxide [Partial pressure] in Venous blood`. - **Source explicitly mentions central venous or mixed venous**: map to the matching LOINC code rather than the generic venous one. - **Source reports PCO2 from arterial blood**: do **not** map. Use "Carbon dioxide partial pressure in arterial blood" instead. - **Source reports "total CO2" or "TCO2" (mmol/L)**: do **not** map. Use the "Bicarbonate in blood" concept set. - **Do not confuse with**: arterial PCO2 (separate concept set), bicarbonate (separate concept set), end-tidal CO2. ## References [1] Vallet B, Pinsky MR, Cecconi M. Resuscitation of patients with septic shock: please "mind the gap"! *Intensive Care Med*. 2013;39(9):1653-5. Available: https://doi.org/10.1007/s00134-013-2998-5 [2] Nomenclature for Properties and Units (NPU). IFCC/IUPAC. NPU codes (current release). Available: https://npu-terminology.org/npu-database/

en.name: Oxygen partial pressure in venous blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context The venous partial pressure of oxygen (PvO2) is the pressure of O2 dissolved in venous blood, after tissue oxygen extraction. In healthy adults, mixed venous PO2 is ~ 40 mmHg, much lower than arterial PO2 (~ 80-100 mmHg under room air) [1]. PvO2 is used in intensive care to assess the adequacy of oxygen delivery relative to consumption, mainly via the venous oxygen saturation derived from it. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a blood gas analyser on a venous sample. Results are reported in mmHg (US convention) or kPa (SI / European convention) [2]. **Note: arterial vs venous.** This concept set covers **venous PO2 only** (peripheral venous, central venous, mixed venous, capillary blood). Arterial PO2 is captured by the separate concept set "Oxygen partial pressure in arterial blood". **Note: venous specimens.** Central and mixed venous PO2 are most clinically relevant in critical care; peripheral venous PO2 is highly dependent on tourniquet, local perfusion and metabolism. The user should preserve the specimen distinction in analyses where the source-of-blood matters. **Note: temperature-corrected variant.** Modern blood gas analysers measure at 37 °C. A separate LOINC code exists for PO2 corrected to the patient's actual temperature (relevant in hypothermia). Both forms are included here; analyses that need to distinguish them must use the LOINC code, not the value. **Note: do not confuse with P50.** LOINC has separate codes `Oxygen [Partial pressure] saturation adjusted to 0.5` (P50, marker of haemoglobin oxygen affinity, not routine PO2). They are excluded from this concept set. ## Included Concepts The set is anchored on four LOINC Hierarchy concepts (scoped to `Chemistry - non-challenge`), each expanded to include all their descendants, with P50 codes excluded by name. The set resolves to eight LOINC "Lab Test" concepts, grouped here by specimen. ### Venous blood - *3024354 / 2705-2 — Oxygen [Partial pressure] in Venous blood (LOINC)* - *3004529 / 19258-3 — Oxygen [Partial pressure] adjusted to patient's actual temperature in Venous blood (LOINC)* ### Mixed venous blood - *3038071 / 19211-2 — Oxygen [Partial pressure] in Mixed venous blood (LOINC)* - *3019464 / 19257-5 — Oxygen [Partial pressure] adjusted to patient's actual temperature in Mixed venous blood (LOINC)* ### Central venous blood - *1616654 / 97540-9 — Oxygen [Partial pressure] in Central venous blood (LOINC)* - *1617238 / 97541-7 — Oxygen [Partial pressure] adjusted to patient's actual temperature in Central venous blood (LOINC)* ### Capillary blood - *3028626 / 2704-5 — Oxygen [Partial pressure] in Capillary blood (LOINC)* - *3019240 / 19256-7 — Oxygen [Partial pressure] adjusted to patient's actual temperature in Capillary blood (LOINC)* **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS`: **`mm[Hg]`** (concept 8876 — millimetre of mercury). Conversion: `1 kPa ≈ 7.50 mmHg`. ## Excluded Concepts The following LOINC concepts that exist for O2 in venous blood are deliberately not part of this set, grouped by reason for exclusion. ### P50 — different measurand - *3016798 / 19216-1 — Oxygen [Partial pressure] saturation adjusted to 0.5 in Venous blood* - *3017333 / 19217-9 — Oxygen [Partial pressure] saturation adjusted to 0.5 in Mixed venous blood* - *3008707 / 19215-3 — Oxygen [Partial pressure] saturation adjusted to 0.5 in Capillary blood* ### Oxygen saturation — different measurand - All `Oxygen saturation` codes: covered by the separate "Oxygen saturation in venous blood" concept set. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports a venous PO2 without further specification: `3024354 / 2705-2 — Oxygen [Partial pressure] in Venous blood`. - **Source explicitly mentions central venous or mixed venous**: map to the matching LOINC code rather than the generic venous one. - **Source reports PO2 from arterial blood**: do **not** map. Use "Oxygen partial pressure in arterial blood" instead. - **Source reports venous oxygen saturation**: do **not** map. Use "Oxygen saturation in venous blood" (different measurand). - **Source reports P50** (haemoglobin oxygen affinity): out of scope of this concept set. - **Do not confuse with**: arterial PO2 (separate concept set), oxygen saturation (separate concept set), P50. ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. en.name: Oxygen saturation in venous blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Venous oxygen saturation is the fraction of haemoglobin in venous blood bound to oxygen, expressed as a percentage. It is measured by CO-oximetry on a venous blood sample. In critical care, it is used to assess the balance between oxygen delivery and consumption: a low venous saturation suggests inadequate oxygen delivery relative to demand (low cardiac output, anaemia, hypoxaemia) or increased extraction. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, reported as a percentage (0-100%). **Note: SvO2 vs ScvO2 vs peripheral SvO2.** Three distinct venous saturation measurements exist, with different sampling sites and clinical interpretations [1, 2]: - **SvO2 (mixed venous saturation)** — sampled from the pulmonary artery via a pulmonary artery catheter. It is the true average venous saturation of the whole body and the gold standard for oxygen delivery/consumption balance. In adults, residual mixed venous oxygen saturation is approximately 60-80% [1]. - **ScvO2 (central venous saturation)** — sampled from a central venous catheter, typically in the superior vena cava. It reflects upper-body return only, not the whole body, but is much less invasive than SvO2 and used as a surrogate. In healthy adults, ScvO2 is slightly **lower** than SvO2 [2]. In circulatory failure (heart failure, cardiogenic shock, septic shock), blood flow is redirected away from the splanchnic bed; this reverses the relationship and ScvO2 becomes **higher** than SvO2 — differences of 5-18% have been reported [2]. The Rivers early goal-directed therapy protocol for severe sepsis used ScvO2 ≥ 70% as a resuscitation target [3]; the clinical benefit of EGDT is now controversial, but ScvO2 monitoring remains widely used. - **Peripheral venous saturation** — sampled from a peripheral vein. Highly dependent on tourniquet, local perfusion and local metabolism. Of limited clinical value as a marker of systemic oxygen balance. This concept set covers all venous specimens (peripheral, mixed venous, central venous, capillary). The user must preserve the LOINC code in downstream analyses where the source-of-blood matters — values are **not interchangeable** across specimens. **Note: directly measured vs calculated.** LOINC distinguishes `Oxygen saturation in X blood` (direct CO-oximetry) from `Oxygen saturation Calculated from oxygen partial pressure` (computed from PO2 via the haemoglobin dissociation curve). Both forms are included; calculated values are less reliable when dyshaemoglobinaemias are present. ## Included Concepts The set lists 12 LOINC "Lab Test" concepts for venous oxygen saturation (cord blood excluded), grouped by specimen. ### Venous blood - *3024928 / 2711-0 — Oxygen saturation in Venous blood (LOINC)* - *3041253 / 51731-8 — Oxygen saturation Calculated from oxygen partial pressure in Venous blood (LOINC)* - *42869600 / 71845-2 — Oxygen saturation [Pure mass fraction] in Venous blood (LOINC)* - *42869596 / 71841-1 — Oxygen saturation [Pure mass fraction] Calculated from oxygen partial pressure in Venous blood (LOINC)* ### Mixed venous blood (SvO2) - *3018465 / 19224-5 — Oxygen saturation in Mixed venous blood (LOINC)* - *44786762 / 74105-8 — Oxygen saturation Calculated from oxygen partial pressure in Mixed venous blood (LOINC)* - *42869601 / 71846-0 — Oxygen saturation [Pure mass fraction] in Mixed venous blood (LOINC)* ### Central venous blood (ScvO2) - *1616373 / 97549-0 — Oxygen saturation in Central venous blood (LOINC)* ### Capillary blood - *3021901 / 2709-4 — Oxygen saturation in Capillary blood (LOINC)* - *3039986 / 51732-6 — Oxygen saturation Calculated from oxygen partial pressure in Capillary blood (LOINC)* - *42869606 / 71851-0 — Oxygen saturation [Pure mass fraction] in Capillary blood (LOINC)* - *42869597 / 71842-9 — Oxygen saturation [Pure mass fraction] Calculated from oxygen partial pressure in Capillary blood (LOINC)* **Note on units.** Recommended unit follows LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS`: **`%`** (concept 8554 — percent). The `[Pure mass fraction]` variants are dimensionless ratios between 0 and 1. ## Excluded Concepts No concepts are explicitly excluded by name. The set deliberately omits: - **Arterial blood specimens**: covered by the separate "Oxygen saturation in arterial blood" concept set. - **Cord blood specimens**: physiologically distinct from post-natal blood. - **Pulse oximetry codes**: pulse oximetry produces an SpO2 estimate that, by sensor placement, is intended to approximate arterial saturation, not venous. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports a venous saturation without further specification: `3024928 / 2711-0 — Oxygen saturation in Venous blood`. - **Source explicitly says SvO2 (mixed venous, pulmonary artery catheter)**: map to `3018465 / 19224-5 — Oxygen saturation in Mixed venous blood`. - **Source explicitly says ScvO2 (central venous catheter)**: map to `1616373 / 97549-0 — Oxygen saturation in Central venous blood`. - **Source reports arterial saturation (SaO2, SpO2)**: do **not** map. Use "Oxygen saturation in arterial blood" or the pulse oximetry concept set. - **Do not confuse with**: arterial saturation (separate concept set), oxygen partial pressure (separate concept set). ## References [1] Lee CP, Bora V. Anesthesia Monitoring of Mixed Venous Saturation. In: *StatPearls*. Treasure Island (FL): StatPearls Publishing. Available: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK539835/ [2] Reinhart K, Kuhn HJ, Hartog C, Bredle DL. Continuous central venous and pulmonary artery oxygen saturation monitoring in the critically ill. *Intensive Care Med*. 2004;30(8):1572-8. en.name: pH in venous blood
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Venous pH is the negative log of the hydrogen ion activity in venous blood, typically slightly lower than arterial pH (acidic shift from tissue CO2 production) [1]. Although arterial pH remains the reference for acid-base management, venous pH is widely used as a less invasive surrogate in the emergency department for the initial evaluation of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), where it shows close agreement with arterial pH (mean arterio-venous difference ~ 0.03 pH units) [2]. In low-flow states (shock, hypoperfusion) and respiratory failure, the gradient widens and venous pH may underestimate the degree of acidaemia or fail to reflect the respiratory component; arterial sampling remains preferable in those settings [2]. The source data will typically be a single numeric result per patient-timestamp, produced by a blood gas analyser on a venous sample. pH is dimensionless. **Note: venous specimens.** This concept set covers peripheral venous, central venous (central venous catheter), mixed venous (pulmonary artery catheter) and capillary blood. The user should preserve the specimen distinction in analyses where the source-of-blood matters. **Note: temperature-corrected variant.** Modern blood gas analysers measure at 37 °C. A separate LOINC code exists for pH corrected to the patient's actual temperature (relevant in hypothermia). Both forms are included; downstream analyses that need to distinguish them must use the LOINC code, not the value. ## Included Concepts The set lists eight LOINC "Lab Test" concepts for pH in non-arterial blood (cord blood excluded), grouped by specimen. ### Venous blood - *3012544 / 2746-6 — pH of Venous blood (LOINC)* - *3038999 / 39486-6 — pH of Venous blood adjusted to patient's actual temperature (LOINC)* ### Mixed venous blood - *3012388 / 19213-8 — pH of Mixed venous blood (LOINC)* - *3030238 / 50980-2 — pH of Mixed venous blood adjusted to patient's actual temperature (LOINC)* ### Central venous blood - *1616438 / 97536-7 — pH of Central venous blood (LOINC)* - *1617447 / 97537-5 — pH of Central venous blood adjusted to patient's actual temperature (LOINC)* ### Capillary blood - *3009343 / 2745-8 — pH of Capillary blood (LOINC)* - *3040135 / 39485-8 — pH of Capillary blood adjusted to patient's actual temperature (LOINC)* **Note on units.** pH is dimensionless. LOINC's `EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS` is **`[pH]`**; the OMOP vocabulary spells the same unit **`pH`** (OMOP concept 8482), which is the code used in this dictionary. ## Excluded Concepts No concepts are explicitly excluded by name. The set deliberately omits: - **Arterial blood specimens**: covered by the separate "pH in arterial blood" concept set. - **Cord blood specimens**: physiologically distinct from post-natal blood. - **Generic blood (`pH of Blood`)**: ambiguous specimen, not used in routine clinical practice; out of scope. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source reports a venous pH without further specification: `3012544 / 2746-6 — pH of Venous blood`. - **Source explicitly mentions central venous or mixed venous**: map to the matching LOINC code rather than the generic venous one. - **Source reports pH from arterial blood**: do **not** map. Use "pH in arterial blood" instead. - **Do not confuse with**: arterial pH (separate concept set), urinary pH, gastric pH. ## References [1] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 2746-6 — pH of Venous blood. Available: https://loinc.org/2746-6/ [2] Brandenburg MA, Dire DJ. Comparison of arterial and venous blood gas values in the initial emergency department evaluation of patients with diabetic ketoacidosis. *Ann Emerg Med*. 1998;31(4):459-65. Available: https://doi.org/10.1016/S0196-0644(98)70254-9

en.name: Tracheostomy and cricothyroidotomy
en.shortDescription: Procedures creating a neck (transtracheal) airway: tracheostomy and cricothyroidotomy (surgical or percutaneous).
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

This set covers the procedures that create a tracheal airway through the front of the neck — a **tracheostomy** (an opening into the trachea, surgical or percutaneous) or a **cricothyroidotomy** (an opening through the cricothyroid membrane, typically an emergency rescue airway). Both bypass the upper airway and larynx, unlike endotracheal intubation. In source data this is a **procedure** record marking that the airway was created (or the tube inserted); there is no unit. It is recorded in intensive care, anaesthesia, and emergency settings. The procedures differ by site (cricothyroidotomy vs tracheostomy), technique (surgical/open vs percutaneous/Seldinger), and context (elective vs emergency).

## Included Concepts

The set is anchored on the SNOMED procedure hierarchies for cricothyroidotomy and tracheostomy creation (with descendants), plus the tube-insertion procedures. Grouped here by site.

### Cricothyroidotomy

Anchored on *Cricothyroidotomy* and *Cricothyroidotomy tube insertion* with their descendants.

- *4068680 / 173067007 — Cricothyroidotomy (SNOMED)*: the general concept.
- *4134560 / 398142004 — Emergency cricothyroidotomy (SNOMED)*.
- *4335586 / 232692007 — Open cricothyroidotomy (SNOMED)*: surgical.
- *4337731 / 232689008 — Percutaneous cricothyroidotomy (SNOMED)* and *4339624 / 232690004 — Percutaneous dilatational cricothyroidotomy (SNOMED)*.
- *37205949 / 785905003 — Cannula cricothyroidotomy (SNOMED)*, *37206251 / 785906002 — Scalpel bougie cricothyroidotomy (SNOMED)*, *37206252 / 785907006 — Wire guided cricothyroidotomy (SNOMED)*.
- *4337618 / 232683009 — Cricothyroidotomy tube insertion (SNOMED)* and its descendant *4337046 / 232684003 — Minitrach insertion (SNOMED)* (a small-bore cricothyroidotomy/minitracheostomy).

### Tracheostomy

Anchored on *Construction of tracheostomy* with its descendants, plus the tube-insertion concepts.

- *1073322 / 1303805000 — Construction of tracheostomy (SNOMED)*: the general concept.
- *4143728 / 307007002 — Percutaneous tracheostomy (SNOMED)* and *4134745 / 397930006 — Percutaneous dilational tracheostomy (SNOMED)*.
- *4166281 / 274969000 — Anterior tracheostomy (SNOMED)*, *4168864 / 274970004 — Lateral tracheostomy (SNOMED)*, *4199580 / 52536006 — Mediastinal tracheostomy (SNOMED)*.
- *4065590 / 21619009 — Permanent tracheostomy (SNOMED)*, *4195473 / 43988005 — Temporary tracheostomy (SNOMED)*, *4208093 / 55622001 — Tracheostomy, emergency procedure by transtracheal approach (SNOMED)*.
- *4337047 / 232685002 — Insertion of tracheostomy tube (SNOMED)*.
- *4337048 / 232686001 — Insertion of tracheal T-tube (SNOMED)*: placement of a tracheal T-tube (e.g. Montgomery) through a tracheostomy stoma.

## Excluded Concepts

Major head-and-neck cancer operations that include a synchronous tracheostomy are excluded, as they are laryngectomy procedures rather than airway-creation procedures:

- *4175285 / 50339005 — Complete laryngectomy with radical neck dissection, synchronous thyroidectomy and synchronous tracheostomy (SNOMED)*.
- *4216541 / 7240008 — Total laryngectomy with partial pharyngectomy and synchronous tracheostomy (SNOMED)*.

## Mapping Notes

- **Default concepts** when the source does not specify the technique: *4068680 / 173067007 — Cricothyroidotomy* for a cricothyroidotomy, *1073322 / 1303805000 — Construction of tracheostomy* for a tracheostomy. Map to a specific technique (percutaneous, open, emergency…) only when documented.
- **Cricothyroidotomy vs tracheostomy**: cricothyroidotomy is through the cricothyroid membrane (higher, usually an emergency rescue airway); tracheostomy is lower, through the tracheal rings. Map to the matching site.
- **Not endotracheal intubation**: placing a tube through the mouth/nose and larynx is a different procedure, captured in the Endotracheal intubation concept set.
- **Procedure, not device**: this set is the creation/insertion procedure. The tracheostomy *tube* (the device) is captured in the Tracheostomy tube concept set; tube *removal* (decannulation) and *changes* are in their own sets.
- **Laryngectomy with synchronous tracheostomy** is not mapped here (it is a laryngectomy procedure).

en.name: End tidal carbon dioxide fraction (FetCO2)
en.shortDescription: End-tidal CO2 as a volume fraction / concentration, in %. The partial-pressure (mmHg) form is a separate set.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

End-tidal carbon dioxide (EtCO2) is the carbon dioxide in the gas a patient exhales at the very end of a breath, measured by a capnograph. This set captures EtCO2 expressed as a **volume fraction / concentration**, reported in **%** (e.g. 5%). In source data it is a single numeric value per patient-timestamp, recorded in intensive care and anaesthesia for ventilated patients. (EtCO2 expressed as a partial pressure in mmHg/kPa is a separate, non-inter-convertible measurement — see Mapping Notes.)

## Included Concepts

- *3012287 / 19888-7 — Carbon dioxide/Gas.total.at end expiration in Exhaled gas by Infrared absorption (LOINC)*: by infrared capnography (the standard method).
- *3017485 / 19889-5 — Carbon dioxide/Gas.total.at end expiration in Exhaled gas (LOINC)*: method not specified.

**Note on units**: reported in **`8554 / % — percent`** (UCUM), the recommended unit.

## Mapping Notes

- Map an EtCO2 value reported as a percentage to one of these concepts.
- **Fraction vs partial pressure are not inter-convertible**: EtCO2 expressed as a partial pressure (PetCO2, mmHg/kPa) belongs to the separate **End tidal carbon dioxide (PetCO2)** concept set. The two are not related by a fixed factor (the partial pressure depends on barometric pressure), so they are kept as separate, unit-homogeneous sets.
- **Not arterial CO2**: arterial CO2 is a different measurement in its own concept set.
